• A baseline needs a result. baseline_flag takes a record only when its result is not null or blank and --STAT is not NOT DONE. The result is --STRESC when present, else --ORRES, or the new result_col=. When --ORRES is present and is not the result, it must hold a value too, unless --DRVFL is Y (CG0553). With no result column the verb stops. SDTMIG 3.4 defines --LOBXFL as the last non-missing value prior to RFXSTDTC.
  • One record on a tie, as SAS LAST. (Mahdi, Q1 A). A tie on the last date and time goes to the last record by the new order_by=, default --SEQ, then input order, with a warning when order_by= is not given. This is the admiral ad_advs.R order and the result a SAS QC program with PROC SORT and LAST. gives. CORE FB2603 and FB2604 expect one flag per group.
  • where filters first. In flag(criteria="first"/"last") a record that fails where takes no part, even on a tie. On a tie among candidates, last takes the last input record and first the first, as SAS PROC SORT with EQUALS and admiral. flag_all=True takes the extreme over candidates only.
  • QTc reads RR in ms by default (Mahdi, Q2 A), as admiral compute_qtc. rr_unit= takes ms, msec, s or sec. The verb stops when a value cannot be in its unit: an RR under 10 in ms, an RR of 10 or more in seconds, or a QT under 10 ms.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Flag every record on the tied date (sdtm.oak). Rejected: CORE fires on each tie, and a QC program with LAST. shows a difference on each.
  • Stop on a tie until order_by= is given. Rejected: a study with triplicate ECGs stops at the first run.
  • Keep RR in seconds as the default. Rejected: most calls would need rr_unit="ms", and the call would not look like the admiral or SAS code QC compares it with.
  • No default RR unit. Rejected: every define.yaml qtc entry would need an edit before it runs.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• baseline_flag on a frame with no --STRESC or --ORRES stops: give result_col=.
  • Date-only data with replicates on the last date get one flag, not one per replicate, and a warning.
  • qtc on RR in seconds stops until the call gives rr_unit="s".

docs.title: Grading criteria are generated from admiral, with their provenance
docs.text: The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (package D) found that the bundled CTCAE and DAIDS criteria gave wrong grades with no message: a null BNRIND gave grade 0 for ALT at 22 x ULN, a unit in lower case gave null, a term with several subgroups or units took the cut-offs of the last entry, CTCAE v5 INR had no absolute cut-offs, and v4 Hemoglobin increased raised an error. Only 4 of 399 entries had a test. The cause was the format: grade-level rules, written by hand, that could not state an AND, a null arm or an addition. We decided that the criteria files are generated from the admiral metadata by a kept script, keep the admiral text of each term, and are tested against a frozen admiral grid.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• One source, generated (Mahdi, Q2 A). scripts/regen_grading_criteria.R parses each admiral GRADE_CRITERIA_CODE and FILTER with R's own parser and writes them as expression trees (schema version 2). Each term is the ordered arms of the R case_when: the first arm that holds gives the grade, a null condition counts as false, and no arm gives null. Nobody edits the JSON by hand; a Fleet rule that must differ from admiral goes in the script's OVERRIDES, with its reason.
  • Provenance in the file. Each file names the admiral version, the dataset and the generator. Each term keeps the admiral GRADE_1 to GRADE_5 text, COMMENT and the R code, so a reviewer compares an arm with its source without R.
  • admiral rules for the dataset. The term and the unit match without case. Of a term's entries, the first population filter that holds is used (a null filter gives a null grade), then the entry of the row's unit. A row with another unit, a null unit or no entry gets null, and every row stays in its order (admiral drops a row whose filter is NA; Fleet keeps it with null). With several units for a term, unit_var= is required.
  • INR takes the worst case (Mahdi, Q1 A). CTCAE v5 and v6 INR increased apply the absolute cut-offs and the baseline multiples, and the higher grade wins, as the admiral COMMENT says ("assume on anticoagulation"). A SAP with another rule uses a custom criteria file.
  • signif_dig defaults to 15, as admiral signif_digits.
  • The old format is dropped (Mahdi, Q3 A). A file without schema_version stops with a message that says how to rewrite it. Fleet has no release yet.
  • The oracle is a frozen admiral grid. scripts/regen_admiral_grading_grid.R grades 34,146 seeded rows (every entry, every cut-off, BNRIND, SEX, age band and unit spelling) with admiral 1.4.1 into tests/fixtures/goldens/grading/admiral_grid.parquet. CI compares Fleet with it and needs no R.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep the grade-level format and correct the known terms by hand (Q2 B). Rejected: the other entries stay hand-made, and the next admiral change is found only by chance.
  • Store the admiral R code and translate it at load. Rejected: Fleet would need an R parser at run time. R's own parser, run once by the script, is exact.
  • Convert old-format files at load (Q3 B). Rejected: that format cannot state AND or null arms, so a converted file can still grade wrongly.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Grades change for null BNRIND, unit case, DAIDS subgroups, multi-unit terms, CTCAE v5/v6 INR and the terms the old files had wrong.
  • A custom criteria file must be rewritten in schema version 2.
  • Updating to a new admiral version is: run the two scripts, read the JSON diff with its source text, run the tests.

docs.title: BLQ comes from the SDTM text
docs.text: The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (package E) found that blq_flag, blqfn and blq_impute read only the number in PCSTRESN. SDTM keeps a BLQ result only as text in PCSTRESC, with PCSTRESN null, so each SDTM-coded BLQ record was skipped with no message: not flagged, not imputed. avalcat did the opposite and called every record with no number BLQ, a missed sample and an above-range result included. We decided that the four verbs share one BLQ rule, on positive evidence only.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• One rule. A record is BLQ when its number is below the LLOQ, or it has no number and its text matches a BLQ text. PCSTAT is not read: NOT DONE means no result, not a low one.
  • The text list is a default (Mahdi, Q2 A). A text that starts with <, or is BLQ, BQL, BLOQ or LLOQ (any case). ALQ and >1000 never match. blq_text= replaces the list, because the data transfer agreement decides it.
  • A number below the LLOQ is BLQ (Mahdi, Q3 A), as the ADaM popPK 1.0 BLQFL text supports. numeric_below_lloq=False lets only the text decide, as admiral does, for a SAP that wants it.
  • The text column is expected (Mahdi, Q4 A). text_col="PCSTRESC" by default; a frame without it stops, and text_col=None states that the frame holds numeric results only, as evid_col and dtype_col do in the same namespace.
  • AVALCAT1 keeps the source text (Mahdi, Q1 A). A record with no number that is not BLQ gets its PCSTRESC text (>1000), or null for a missed sample.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• AVALCAT1 always null for such records (Q1 B). Rejected: the listing shows the same blank for an above-range result and a missed sample.
  • A short text list, or no default (Q2 B, C). Rejected: BQL and BLOQ would pass with no sign, or every call would need the list.
  • Only the text decides (Q3 B) as the default. Rejected: a value below the LLOQ would enter the analysis as a measured number.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Existing calls on a frame without PCSTRESC must add text_col=None once.
  • adnca_example.py now flags and imputes its 4 BLQ records, and its popPK DV comes from PCSTRESN, so a BLQ record keeps DV null and MDV 1.

docs.title: The population filter selects the subjects of every count
docs.text:
The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (package G) found five TLG rules that gave a wrong number with no message:

  • adsl_filter changed only the big N. A record of a subject outside the population still counted in n, so a percentage could pass 100.
  • On a continuous table, n counted distinct subjects, also those with a missing value and twice for a subject with two records. Q1 and Q3 used the Polars default, not the SAS one.
  • worst_case ranked an unknown value below every listed value. With the default relationship_order ['N', 'Y'], a POSSIBLY RELATED event lost to N.
  • The shift and abnormality tables guessed the post-baseline rule: ONTRTFL when present, else ABLFL. Without both, screening records counted as post-baseline.
  • The QTc table pooled every parameter and visit, and the VS summary pooled every visit.

We decided that a table counts only what the programmer states, and stops when a rule is missing.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• The population filter selects subjects (Mahdi, Q1 A). The filter selects the ADSL subjects for N, and the engine keeps only the analysis records of those subjects for n. A subject in ADSL but outside the filter is left out with an INFO note on the fleet logger. A subject not in ADSL at all is left out with a warning, because that is a data issue. This is the SAS idiom where saffl = 'Y' on both datasets. An adsl_filter with no ADSL stops.
  • Continuous n is PROC MEANS N (Mahdi, Q2 A). On a table with continuous statistics, n is the count of non-missing values in the cell. A null value never counts. There is no warning: the programmer selects the analysis records (for example with ANL01FL). Q1 and Q3 follow SAS QNTLDEF=5 (R type 2).
  • An unknown value stops the worst-case table (Mahdi, Q3 A). relationship_order keeps its default ['N', 'Y'], and a value outside the order stops the table with the name of the spec field to set. A null or blank value still ranks below every listed value.
  • The post-baseline rule is a stated prefilter (Mahdi, Q4 A). LBShiftSpec and LBAbnormalSpec default to ONTRTFL = 'Y' and not the ABLFL record. Without these columns the table stops and proposes a SAP rule, for example pl.col("ADY") > 1. prefilter=None survives a YAML round trip.
  • QTc percentages use the visit base (Mahdi, Q5 A). One block per parameter and visit, with an n row: the subjects with a non-missing AVALCAT1 in the arm, parameter and visit. percent_base="adsl" selects the big N instead. Two records of one subject in one block stop the table.
  • VS summary per visit. VSSummarySpec rows default to PARAMCD and AVISIT, as LB and EG do.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep the filter on ADSL only (Q1 B). Rejected: n and N come from two populations.
  • Count subjects for continuous n, with a warning on duplicates (Q2 B). Rejected: a hidden rule behind the scene. The programmer owns the record selection.
  • Change the relationship default to the sponsor terms (Q3 B). Rejected: AEREL has no CDISC codelist, so no default fits every study.
  • Keep the ONTRTFL or ABLFL guess (Q4 B). Rejected: the rule changes with the columns present, with no sign in the output.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A table with adsl_filter and analysis records outside the population now gives lower n and lower percentages.
  • Continuous n can change where a cell has null values or several records per subject. Q1 and Q3 can change.
  • Shift and abnormality calls on data without ONTRTFL must state a prefilter.
  • Studies with sponsor AEREL terms must set relationship_order.
  • The egt05 and vst01 goldens changed.

docs.title: Every CORE finding blocks until the study accepts it
docs.text: The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (package H) found that fleet validate said Status: PASS and exited 0 on a DM without COUNTRY. Fleet read a Severity key that no CORE report has, so every finding became a warning, and on_fail="raise" never raised. Engine problems read as data failures: a timeout, a crash or a half-written report gave FAIL with an invented rule ID (TIMEOUT-001, ENGINE-001, ERROR-001), and the engine workers kept running after a timeout. We decided that Fleet invents no severity, that every finding blocks until the study accepts it with a reason, and that an engine problem is its own outcome.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• Every finding blocks (Mahdi, Q1 A). A finding stops blocking only when validation.accepted in study_config.yaml lists its rule ID and its dataset with a reason, as an SDRG explanation does. An accepted finding stays in the report with its reason.
  • Status words. PASS: at least one rule executed and no finding. FINDINGS (n): every finding accepted. NOT ASSESSED: the Rules_Report shows no executed rule (SUCCESS or ISSUE_REPORTED). FAIL: a finding blocks. COULD NOT RUN: the engine crashed, timed out, wrote no report or wrote a report Fleet cannot read. Exit codes: 0, 0, 0, 1, 2.
  • Study-level findings. In a sweep they get their own STUDY block, which is not counted as a dataset. In a single-dataset run (the verb, the MCP tool) they are information only: one dataset cannot show what the study lacks.
  • The engine run. Fleet reads the return code before the report, runs the engine in its own process group and stops the whole group on timeout. The limit comes from --timeout, else validation.timeout, else 300 s. Fleet no longer passes -rr: the standard JSON report has the same keys, and CORE 0.17 crashed in the raw-report writer.
  • Tested engine versions. fleet.validation.engine.TESTED_ENGINE_VERSIONS lists the CORE versions Fleet runs on. fleet install-engine installs the default tag from that table; the report header and fleet doctor name any other version. A weekly workflow (core-canary.yml) runs Fleet on the newest CORE release; a version joins the table only after it passes.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• No finding blocks by default (Q1 B). Rejected: a CI job stays green on a DM without COUNTRY.
  • A fixed list of blocking rules (Q1 C). Rejected: no CDISC document states such a list, and the QC programmer would have to defend it.
  • The executability field decides (Q1 D). Rejected: it says how reliable a rule is, not how serious its finding is.
  • Keep the engine errors as findings. Rejected: a timeout on a large LB is not a data problem, and exit 1 sent the programmer to fix data that was correct.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The first run of a study fails on findings that the study must fix or explain (for example CORE-000767 when there is no FA domain). Each explanation is written once, in the study config, with its reason.
  • fleet validate exits 2 more often: every engine problem is "could not run".
  • CORE v1.0.0 (released 3 November 2026) adds rules: on the same DM and AE it gives 13 findings where 0.15.0 gives 8, among them CORE-000510 on non-split datasets. It ships no ADaM rules and stops with "No rules were selected"; Fleet reads that as NOT ASSESSED, as 0.15.0 already gave for ADSL (0 rules executed).

docs.title: Define-XML gaps are named, and strict refuses
docs.text: The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (package H) found three defects in the Define-XML path. A Derived variable with no method text got no MethodOID, with no message (c1-557). Numeric items had no Length and float items no SignificantDigits, and the spec had no key for SignificantDigits (c1-776). DefineXMLGenerator and DefineValidator read a retired YAML dialect: every documented call failed, and fleet check used that validator, so it passed specs that the real generator refused (c1-774). We decided that the generator names each gap, that a strict mode refuses, and that fleet check runs that strict mode.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A gap is named, not hidden (Mahdi, Q2 B). Define-XML 2.1 requires a MethodOID on each Derived ItemRef, a Length on text, integer and float items, and SignificantDigits on float items. The generator lists each item that misses one, as DM.SAFFL: no method text (add a comment: or a derivation: block), or VS.AVAL (PARAMCD = SYSBP): no SignificantDigits (required on float) for a value-level entry.
  • The default writes and warns. fleet define-xml and DefineSpecGenerator(spec) write the file and give one warning with the list. A draft define for a review is still possible.
  • Strict refuses. fleet define-xml --strict and DefineSpecGenerator(spec, strict=True) raise SpecError, exit with code 1 and write nothing.
  • fleet check is strict. It runs the real generator with strict=True and writes no file. A new study can be red there; each message names the fields to fill (as decided for c1-533).
  • Methods are on by default. enrich_methods=True is the default; --enrich-methods is kept and does nothing. A method from a comment: only has no FormalExpression.
  • significant_digits: is a new key on a variable and on a value-level entry. The schema refuses it on a type other than float, and refuses length: on date and datetime.
  • The retired classes are removed: DefineXMLGenerator, DefineValidator, StudyContext.define_schema() and define_xml_2_1_schema.json.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Refuse by default (Q2 A). Rejected: a programmer who wants a draft define for a spec review gets nothing until every method is written.
  • Warn only, with no strict mode (Q2 C). Rejected: CI cannot stop a define with a Derived variable and no method.
  • Keep DefineValidator and port it to the current dialect. Rejected: two validators of one spec drift again. The generator already validates the schema, the codelist references, the CDISC XSDs and the semantic lint.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The CDISC pilot specs now hold a length: on each numeric variable, significant_digits: on each float, a comment: with the method text for the seven derivations made inline (SAFFL, ITTFL, TRTEMFL, ANL01FL, the two ASEQ, EXDURD), and origin: Predecessor for the ADSL variables copied into ADVS, ADAE and ADEX. Four variables that the pipeline does not make (ADSL.DTHFL, ADVS.DTHFL, ADVS.DTYPE, ADVS.ANL01FL) are removed from the ADaM spec.
  • Code that imported DefineXMLGenerator or DefineValidator must use DefineSpecGenerator(spec).generate(out) and fleet check.

docs.title: The bootstrap pins two CT packages and invents no text
docs.text: The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (package H, part 3) found that a study made by the documented bootstrap could not pass fleet check when it had ADaM datasets (c1-297). CDISC publishes ADaM CT on its own dates, and some codelists are only in ADaM CT: DTYPE (C81224) is not in any SDTM CT package. fleet init ct asked only the SDTM package, dropped the ADaM-only codelists with no message, and fleet check then advised a command that could not help. The scaffold also wrote an empty study.description and study.originator, and fleet define-xml ended in a traceback (c1-533). We decided that a study pins an SDTM and an ADaM CT package, and that the bootstrap never invents metadata text.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• Two pins. study_config.yaml holds ct.package (SDTM CT) and ct.adam_package (ADaM CT). fleet init cfg and fleet new with ADaM datasets pin adamct-2023-06-30, the latest ADaM package on or before the default sdtmct-2023-12-15 (Mahdi, c1-297 A). With another --package, they need --adam-package, because fleet init cfg has no network to find the date.
  • One resolver. fleet init ct takes each codelist from the first pinned package that holds it, SDTM CT first. Only a 404 moves to the next package; a 401 or a network error stops the command.
  • A missing codelist stops. When no pinned package holds a codelist, fleet init ct names its ID, writes no file and exits with code 1.
  • Two-package marker. A codelists.py with codelists from both pins has __ct_packages__. The stale checks compare it with both pins. Two dates of one product (two SDTM CT packages) still fail.
  • Terms in define.yaml. fleet init ct writes the terms and decodes (NCI preferred term) into each codelists: entry of the define.yaml files that has no terms; with --force, into every entry. The generator names each codelist that has no terms.
  • Both CT standards in an ADaM define. The ADaM define.yaml has ct_version (SDTM CT) and adam_ct_version (ADaM CT). Its Define-XML lists two CT standards, with the publishing sets SDTM and ADaM.
  • No invented text (Mahdi, c1-533 C). The scaffold leaves study.description and study.originator empty when the user gave none. One clean message names the empty fields; --description and --company fill them at creation.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• The first ADaM package after the SDTM date (c1-297 B). Rejected: the define.xml then states an ADaM CT newer than the SDTM CT.
  • fleet init ct finds the ADaM package and writes it into the config. Rejected: a later command changes the config, so a reviewer can miss the pin.
  • Write the codelists found and name the rest. Rejected: a partial codelists.py stays in the study.
  • The generator reads the terms from codelists.py. Rejected: the define.xml then depends on a second file that a reviewer of define.yaml does not see.
  • A placeholder description (c1-533 A, B). Rejected: placeholder text can reach a define.xml as if it were real metadata.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A study made before this change has no ct.adam_package. fleet check names the missing pin for each ADaM-only codelist.
  • fleet init ct --force rewrites the define.yaml files through YAML, so only their header comment stays.
  • The committed CDISC pilot ADaM define now states its ct_version with the publishing set SDTM.
  • The first fleet check after fleet new is red until the user fills the description, the company and the Define-XML gaps of ADR-0018. Each row names what to fill.

docs.title: A missing sort key sorts last, as admiral
docs.text: The admiral oracle of alpha audit 5.3 found that flag(criteria="last") differs from admiral derive_var_extreme_flag(mode = "last") when an order_by value is missing. Fleet left out every record with a missing key, so an AE with no AESEVN or no ASTDT never got ANL01FL, and a group whose records all missed the key got no flag at all. admiral sorts with dplyr::arrange, which puts a missing value last in each key. We decided to follow admiral (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A missing value sorts last in each key, then the next key, then input order. "last" takes the last record of that order, so a record with a missing key wins over the others. "first" takes a record with a missing key only when every candidate of the group misses that key, and the next key then decides.
  • flag_all=True flags every candidate equal to the winner on the order keys, where a missing value equals a missing value.
  • where still filters first: a record that fails it takes no part (ADR-0013).

admiral 1.4.1, run on the rows of test_a_missing_order_value_sorts_last_as_admiral, gives the values that test holds. scripts/admiral_oracle.py compares the same rule weekly.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Leave the record out, as before. Rejected: an admiral double program flags a record that Fleet does not, and a group with only missing keys gets no flag.
  • A missing value first, as SAS PROC SORT. Rejected by the decision to match admiral. A QC program with PROC SORT and LAST. differs on a group with a missing key: it takes the last non-missing record.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• ANL01FL, ABLFL and other first/last flags can now fall on a record with a missing order value. When the SAP wants the last non-missing record, give where= (for example where="AESEVN.is_not_null()").
  • Polars 1.x ignores nulls_last in a window order_by with more than one key. The verb sorts on is_null() before each key, so the rule holds on Polars 1.x and 2.x.

docs.title: Date imputation reads the form of the value and follows admiral highest_imputation
docs.text:
Status: partly superseded by ADR-0045. A *DTM target now takes highest= (except "Y"), and a partial date with time= is imputed. The rest stands.

The alpha audit of 4 November 2026 (findings c1-67, c1-69, c1-74, c1-119) found that .date(highest=) was one level stricter than admiral highest_imputation: highest="M" gave null for 2021, highest="D" gave null for 2021-03, and "h" nulled even a complete date. The imputation and the *DTF flag read the length of the text, so 2021---15 gave null and 202103 carried a flag on a null date. On a *DTM target, highest= and time= of .adam.date() had no effect and gave no message.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• The form decides, not the length. The date engine reads year, month and day, a hyphen standing for a missing part (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4.2). A missing day imputes the day (2021-03, 2021-03--T08:30). A missing month imputes the month and the day, and a collected day is not used (2021---15 gives 2021-01-01 with flag M), as admiral impute_dtc_dt does. Any other form gives null.
  • highest= has the admiral meaning. It names the highest part that may be imputed: "n" none, "D" the day, "M" the month and the day. A date that needs more is null. No highest= keeps the Fleet default: month and day may be imputed.
  • "Y" and the time levels raise on a *DT target. Fleet does not impute a missing year; admiral needs min_dates or max_dates for it. "h", "m" and "s" have no meaning on a date.
  • A *DTM target refuses highest=, as it refuses min_date= and max_date=, in both namespaces, until a tested date-time rule exists.
  • A flag is null where the date is null. The *DTF and *TMF flags describe an imputed value; a null value has nothing to describe.
  • .adam.date() honours time= on a *DTM target with the same code as .sdtm.date(). A partial date with time= gives null in both namespaces.
  • value= with date-only text on a *DTM target gives midnight (2024-01-15 gives 2024-01-15T00:00:00).

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Rename highest= and keep the old meaning. Rejected: the name is the admiral name, and a programmer who knows admiral reads it with the admiral meaning.
  • Impute highest="Y" with a fixed year. Rejected: admiral refuses it without bounds, and a guessed year changes TRTEMFL.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• .date("ASTDT", highest="M") now imputes 2021 to 2021-01-01; a spec that relied on the stricter meaning gets more imputed dates. Check the *DTF flag.
  • highest="Y", "h", "m" and "s" now raise on a *DT target, and any highest= raises on a *DTM target.
  • Values such as 2021---15 and 2021-03--T08:30 now give an imputed date with a flag, not null.

docs.title: A date verb reads the type of each column
docs.text: The alpha audit of 4 November 2026 (findings c1-4, c1-5, c1-7, c1-78, c1-117, c1-141, c1-143, c1-371) found date verbs that cast every input to a date. A SAS date stored as a number became a date counted from 1970, 10 years off, with no message. A pl.Date source to .date("ADT") stopped with a raw Polars error. on_treatment dropped the time, so a pre-dose record on the first dose day was on treatment. duration() read a pl.Expr as 24-hour periods and wrote ISO 8601 durations with no sign.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A number raises. Every verb that reads a date (.date(), duration, study_day, on_treatment, treatment_emergent, onset_recovery, age_from_dates, the peds ages, aval) checks the dtype in the lazy schema. A numeric column raises DerivationError with the column name and the conversion: pl.date(1960, 1, 1) + pl.duration(days=pl.col(...)) for a SAS date, pl.datetime(1960, 1, 1) + pl.duration(seconds=...) for a SAS date-time. Fleet does not guess the origin. The check lives in fleet.core.dtc.to_day, so each date verb gets it.
  • A date or a date-time converts. .date() reads a pl.Date or pl.Datetime source as its ISO 8601 text and sends it through the one engine, so the flags follow the same rules.
  • --DTC text is read by its date portion in every day count (ADR-0011). A partial value gives null.
  • A pl.Expr input is read by its type, as a column name is.
  • on_treatment keeps the time of the start comparison when the analysis date and the treatment start are both date-times; the end comparison stays at date level, as admiral derive_var_ontrtfl does by default. Date, text and mixed inputs stay at date level, because a date read as midnight would fall before a 09:00 dose.
  • aval() takes each row from its own columns: the end is the date of ADTM, else ADT; the start the date of STARTDTM, else STARTDT.
  • A sub-day duration on text with no time gives null and one warning with the column and the count, and a hint to .date() for an imputed time with a flag (finding c1-5).
  • An ISO 8601 duration keeps the sign and adds one only on request (Mahdi, c1-7 A). -PT15M for a pre-dose sample; PT1H30M for 90 minutes; P9D from 1 to 10 January, an elapsed time; add_one=True gives P10D. Months and years raise, because they have no fixed length; weeks that are not whole give null with a warning.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• A sas_epoch= option on each verb. Rejected: one more argument on every verb, and a default origin is still a guess.
  • Add one day by default to an ISO 8601 day duration, as the numeric output does (option B). Rejected by Mahdi: --ELTM and --DUR are elapsed times, and a QC programmer would see every PK value one unit too large.
  • Raise unless add_one is explicit (option C). Rejected: every existing call would change.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A frame with a numeric SAS date column now stops at the verb call. Convert the column at the IO boundary.
  • on_treatment on two date-time columns can now give null for a record on the first dose day, before the dose.
  • duration(out="iso8601") now writes - for a negative span and hours with minutes, and refuses months and years.

docs.title: nodup sorts a missing key as SAS
docs.text: The alpha audit (finding c1-18) found that nodup(sort_by=["AESEVN"], keep="first", descending=True) kept the record with no severity, not the worst one. Polars puts a missing value first in both directions, so a descending sort put it on top. SAS PROC SORT BY DESCENDING puts it last, and admiral filter_extreme(order = exprs(desc(AESEVN)), mode = "first") keeps the worst value too. We decided that nodup follows the SAS rule (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A missing value is the lowest value: it sorts first when ascending and last when descending, per key.
  • Records that tie on sort_by keep their input order, as PROC SORT EQUALS (c1-21). keep="first" takes the first input record of a tie and keep="last" the last.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• A missing value last in both directions, as admiral and ADR-0020. Rejected for nodup: nodup translates PROC SORT NODUPKEY, so a QC program with PROC SORT is its reference. On a descending sort both rules agree. They differ only on an ascending sort, where SAS keeps the missing record first.
  • Leave the Polars default. Rejected: a keep-worst selection kept a missing value, with no warning.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Fleet has two null rules for sorts. The flag verbs follow admiral (ADR-0020). nodup follows SAS. Each docstring states its rule.
  • Only a descending nodup changes its result. The ascending result is the same as before.

docs.title: pick needs an order and takes the last tied record
docs.text: The alpha audit (findings c1-125 and c1-207) found two defects in the record that pick selects inside an event. With no order, pick took the first input record, in both modes, so DTHCAUS for a subject with two fatal AEs depended on row order. With order and a tie, mode="last" took the first tied record, where SAS LAST. and admiral filter_extreme(mode = "last") take the last one. No warning appeared. We decided to raise on the first case and to follow SAS on the second (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• An event with more than one matching record in a group needs an order, its own or the top-level one. Without it, pick raises DerivationError and names the event and the first group. admiral derive_vars_extreme_event makes order a required argument.
  • A tie on the order keeps input order. mode="first" takes the first tied record and mode="last" the last, as SAS FIRST. and LAST. after PROC SORT EQUALS.
  • A tie whose records set different values gives a warning, as admiral does with its duplicate check.
  • A missing order value loses in both modes, as before: it is taken only when every record of the group misses it.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Warn on no order and keep the first record. Rejected: a row-order result has no safe reading, and the docstring already called the order required.
  • A missing order value last in both modes, as ADR-0020 for the flag verbs. Rejected for this change: tests/unit/test_pick_verb.py pins the present rule (a fatal AE with an end date wins over one with no end date under mode="last"), and the audit asked to keep it.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A pick call with no order whose source has two records for one subject now raises. Add the order, for example "order": ["AESTDTC", "AESEQ"].
  • mode="last" can now give a different record on a tie. Add a sequence variable to the order to remove the dependence on input order.
  • The rule across events does not change: with a top-level order, a tie between events goes to the first listed event.

docs.title: A derived value keeps full precision, and age is completed years
docs.text: The alpha audit (c1-76, c1-138, c1-77) found that bmi, bsa, map, qtc and adsl.age_years rounded the stored value with a fixed half-to-even rule that no docstring stated and no argument turned off. WEIGHT 86.6 kg and HEIGHT 170 cm gave BMI 30.0, so the subject fell into an SAP group BMI >= 30 that the unrounded value 29.9654 does not reach. age_from_dates and peds.age_years returned days / 365.25 rounded to 1 or 2 decimals, so a subject born 1956-06-01 was 65.0 on 2021-05-31, one day before the 65th birthday, and went into AGEGR1 '>=65'. nrind compared raw floats, so 1.3 x 88.4 = 114.92000000000002 against ANRHI 114.92 was HIGH. We decided to follow admiral and SAS on all three points (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• Full precision by default. bmi, bsa, map, qtc and adsl.age_years store the unrounded value, as admiral compute_bmi, compute_bsa, compute_map, compute_qtc and compute_age_years. A new round_digits= argument rounds with the SAS ROUND rule: half away from zero, after a first rounding of the scaled value to 8 decimals so that 24.25 gives 24.3. The helper is fleet.adam.utils.sas_round.
  • Age from dates is completed years. adsl.age_from_dates and peds.age_years return Int64 completed years by default, as admiral derive_vars_aage and SAS FLOOR(YRDIF(b, r, 'AGE')). A 29 February birthday is reached on 1 March in a non-leap year. unit="decimal" gives days / 365.25 at full precision, and only that form takes round_digits=. Both verbs use one helper, fleet.adam.utils.age_between.
  • nrind compares at 15 significant digits, as admiral derive_var_anrind (signif(x, 15) on AVAL, ANRLO and ANRHI), and gives null for a NaN value. The new signif_dig= argument changes the number of digits.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep one decimal by default and state it. Rejected: PROC COMPARE against an admiral or unrounded SAS program differs on nearly every row, and subjects near a cut-off change group.
  • Unrounded decimal age by default. Rejected: PROC COMPARE against an integer age differs on almost all rows, and AAGE >= 65 is false on the 65th birthday for some birth dates.
  • Keep the rounded decimal age and add an integer option. Rejected: about 1 subject in 20 still reads one year too old with the default.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A SAP that says "round to one decimal, then classify" needs round_digits=1 in the call.
  • A SAP that defines a decimal age (a PK covariate) needs unit="decimal".
  • Outputs of existing pipelines change: BMI, BSA, MAP, QTc and AAGE gain decimals, and AAGE from dates becomes an integer that can be one year lower.

docs.title: Pediatric BMI uses the CDC 2000 or WHO 2007 reference, and the adult rule moves to metabolic
docs.text: The alpha audit (c1-161, issue #178) found that peds.bmi_category applied the WHO adult cut-offs (18.5, 25, 30 kg/m2) from the pediatrics namespace. A boy aged 5 years with BMI 18.0 got Underweight, while the CDC 2000 charts put him at or above the 95th percentile (17.94), so obese. We decided on option C (Mahdi, 4 November 2026): move the adult rule out of peds and add a pediatric verb with the two reference tables an SAP names.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• metabolic.bmi_category_adult holds the WHO adult rule. peds.bmi_category is removed with no VERB_RENAMES entry, because a rename would carry an adult rule into pediatric code without a warning. A null, NaN or infinite BMI, or a value not below the last bound, gets null (c1-158).
  • peds.bmi_percentile_category classifies BMI by age in months and sex. reference has no default: the SAP names "CDC2000" or "WHO2007".
  • CDC 2000 (24 to < 240 months): the row of the completed month (60.5 stands for 60.0 to 60.99 months, as CDC states), compared with the published P5, P85 and P95. Classes: Underweight, Healthy weight, Overweight, Obesity (CDC "Child and Teen BMI Categories").
  • WHO 2007 (61 to 228 months): L, M and S interpolated linearly between the two whole months around the age, the z-score rounded to 2 decimals, as the WHO anthroplus R package. Classes: Severe thinness (< -3), Thinness (< -2), Normal, Overweight (> +1), Obesity (> +2).
  • The tables are package data under src/fleet/adam/data/growth/, from the official files: CDC bmiagerev.csv byte for byte, and the WHO expanded LMS workbooks converted to CSV. scripts/regen_growth_references.py downloads them again; the README in that folder gives the URLs, versions and SHA-256 values.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Option A, move the rule with no pediatric verb. Rejected by the decision: the programmer would have to copy the CDC or WHO table and the lookup rule himself.
  • Option B, keep the adult rule in peds as bmi_category_adult. Rejected: a reviewer can still accept an adult class for a child.
  • A default reference. Rejected: CDC and WHO give different classes for the same child, and the SAP names one.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• QC must check the reference and the age rule (completed months or exact age) against the SAP. A wrong reference gives a plausible class that differs from the SAS result.
  • The CDC 2022 extended BMI-for-age charts change z-scores above the 95th percentile only; the four classes do not use them. Severe obesity (>= 120 % of P95 or >= 35 kg/m2) is not a class of this verb.
  • Ages under 24 months (CDC) or under 61 months (WHO 2007) get null. The WHO 2006 child growth standards for 0 to 5 years are not included.

docs.title: Vaccine flags follow their cited definitions, and the call states the SAP rule
docs.text: The alpha audit found three vaccine verbs that did not do what their citations say. fever_flag flagged only values strictly above 38.0 °C, although the FDA 2007 toxicity grading scale and the Brighton Collaboration start fever at 38.0 °C (c1-417). seroconversion_flag applied only AVAL / BASE, so a subject below the LLOQ at baseline (HI '<10', BASE 5) and 20 after vaccination was seroconverted, while the FDA CBER 2007 influenza rule needs a post-vaccination titre of at least 1:40 (c1-416). event_flag ignored AVALC unless told, missed the AVALC value Y, spread one event to every FAOBJ of a subject through its default by=["USUBJID"], and gave N to a diary with no data (c1-418). Mahdi decided on 4 November 2026: c1-417 option B, c1-416 option A, c1-418 option A.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• fever_flag is inclusive by default (>=), and a new inclusive=False gives > for a strict SAP limit such as FDA grade 4 (> 40 °C).
  • seroconversion_flag has a required lloq_col. lloq_col="ISLLOQ" applies the two-arm rule: BASE below the LLOQ needs AVAL >= seronegative_fold x LLOQ (default fold_rise), BASE at or above the LLOQ needs AVAL >= fold_rise x BASE. lloq_col=None keeps the plain ratio for a SAP that states it. The flag stays Y or null.
  • event_flag follows admiralvaccine derive_vars_event_flag. by is required. severity_col defaults to "AVALC" (None opts out), and the default severity values add Y; [] means no value counts. A group with an event gives Y on every record. In a group with no event, a record that shows no event (AVAL <= cutoff or AVALC = "N") gives N, and a record with missing AVAL and AVALC gives null.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• c1-417 A, plain >= with no argument. Not chosen: a strict limit would need case_when.
  • c1-417 C, keep > by default. Rejected: each default call misses 38.0 °C.
  • c1-416 B or C, a default for lloq_col. Rejected: either default hides a SAP choice that differs between sponsors (FDA 2007 against an AstraZeneca-type plain ratio).
  • c1-418 B or C, N for a group with no assessable data. Rejected: a missing diary counts as no event and the event rate is under-stated.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A call of seroconversion_flag or event_flag without the new required argument stops with a TypeError. The programmer adds the rule of the SAP.
  • With inclusive=False at 38.0 °C, the 38.0 miss comes back with no warning. QC checks the argument against the SAP.
  • A plan with a third seroconversion rule (MET44, pre < 1:8 and post >= 1:8) may fit neither form. The programmer then writes the rule with case_when.
  • event_flag can now give null; every denominator states how null is counted.

docs.title: Toxicity grading states its unit and description columns
docs.text: The alpha audit found three ways in which a grading call gave a wrong grade with no warning. atoxgr without unit_var compared a hemoglobin of 13.5 g/dL with the SI cut-offs of ctcae_v5 (80 g/L) and gave grade 3 (c1-329). combine_grades gave ATOXGR '0' when one direction had no grade, also when the description of that direction was present, so a potassium with a missing ANRHI read as normal (c1-386). atoxgr(direction="LOW") and aval_adis(lloq_rule="HALF") accepted any text and gave all-null grades or the full LLOQ (c1-420). Mahdi decided on 4 November 2026: c1-329 the recommendation, c1-386 option B, c1-420 the fix as described.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• unit_var is a required keyword of atoxgr, as get_unit_expr in admiral 1.4.1 derive_var_atoxgr_dir. A row whose unit is not a unit of the term's criteria gets null, and the verb warns once per term with the count of such rows. The docstring states that ctcae_* and daids hold SI cut-offs and *_uscv hold US conventional units.
  • combine_grades needs the description columns, with the defaults low_desc_var="ATOXDSCL" and high_desc_var="ATOXDSCH", and raises when a column is absent. It gives '0' only when each side is '0' or its description is null, as admiral derive_var_atoxgr.
  • Closed values are checked. grade_dataset (so atoxgr) raises DerivationError for a direction other than "L" or "H", before the criteria lookup. aval_adis raises for a lloq_rule other than "half" or "lloq". An empty lookup (a custom file with only H terms and direction="L") is still a valid all-null result.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep unit_var optional and warn. Rejected: a warning in a batch log is easy to miss, and admiral refuses the call.
  • c1-386 A, keep '0' and document it. Rejected: the row reads as normal and differs from an admiral double program.
  • c1-386 C, null when one side is null and no description is named. Rejected: every normal anemia row with no high criteria becomes null and leaves the shift table denominators.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Old calls of atoxgr without unit_var stop with a TypeError; old calls of combine_grades on data without ATOXDSCL or ATOXDSCH stop with a DerivationError. A one-direction study adds the other description as a null column.
  • The define.yaml schema marks unit_var as required for algorithm: atoxgr, and direction as L or H.

docs.title: LOCF adds records with DTYPE, as admiral
docs.text: Alpha audit finding c1-317 found that derive_locf_records filled a null AVAL in place, set no DTYPE, and added no record for a missed visit. ADaMIG v1.3 requires DTYPE on a record whose AVAL is imputed, and a LOCF analysis at WEEK 24 needs a WEEK 24 record for each subject. Finding c1-318 found that the default order_by="ADT" sorted undated missed visits first and filled nothing. We decided to port admiral derive_locf_records, with imputation="add" as the default (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• dataset_ref is required. It holds the expected visits (for example AVISIT and AVISITN). For each by group, a visit of dataset_ref with no record with a non-null value gets a new record.
  • Each imputed record has DTYPE "LOCF". An existing DTYPE on other records is kept.
  • The default is imputation="add", as admiral. A record with a null value is kept, and a second record with the carried value and DTYPE "LOCF" is added. "update" puts the value on that record. "update_add" does both.
  • order_by is required. Its first column must be in dataset_ref, so that a new record has a sort value. A null value in an order_by column raises.

admiral 1.4.1, run on the rows of tests/unit/test_bds_record_verbs.py, gives the values that the test holds for the three modes.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• imputation="update" as the default. Rejected: the updated record keeps the collected ADT, so the value looks collected on that date, and a QC program with the admiral default has more rows.
  • No default for imputation. Rejected: each admiral call ported without imputation= stops with a TypeError, and the admiral default is a published convention.
  • Keep the in-place fill and add DTYPE only. Rejected: a subject with no WEEK 24 record still has no WEEK 24 value.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• PROC COMPARE with ID USUBJID PARAMCD AVISITN reports duplicate keys in add mode: put DTYPE in the ID statement.
  • Old calls (by= and order_by="ADT" only) stop with a TypeError until dataset_ref= and order_by= are given.
  • A group with no earlier value keeps a null value on the new record, as admiral.

docs.title: Response confirmation follows admiralonco by default
docs.text: Alpha audit finding c1-406 found that confirmed_response_flag only checked that two CR or PR records were 28 days apart. A PR after the first PD confirmed a response, and SD or NE between the two records had no limit. RECIST 1.1 Table 3 has two time points only, so no standard fixes the rule for SD and NE in between. We decided on the strict admiralonco default (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• The window. For each CR or PR record, the window holds the later records up to and including the first that confirms it: a CR at least confirmation_days later for a CR, a CR or PR for a PR.
  • The default is max_nr_ne=1, max_nr_sd=0, as the admiralonco crsp_y_cr and crsp_y_pr events. For a CR the window holds only CR and NE. For a PR it holds CR, PR and NE (and SD when max_nr_sd is not 0), and no PR follows a CR. None removes a limit.
  • The verb stops at the first PD of a group. Records after it confirm nothing and are not confirmed.
  • Only the confirmed record is flagged.
  • The verb warns on a null response, on two assessments on one date, and on a CR followed by a PR or SD, with the group values.
  • responses is CR, PR or a subset. Another value raises.

admiralonco 1.4.1, run on the rows of tests/unit/test_onco_response_rules.py, gives the subjects that the test holds, for the default and for accept_sd=TRUE of the deprecated derive_param_confirmed_resp (max_nr_sd=1).

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Lenient default, as SWOG S0819 section 10.3 (no SD or NE limit, stop at first PD). Rejected: on a strict SAP the response rate is above the QC value, and if QC also uses the Fleet default, nobody sees the overstated endpoint.
  • No default, both arguments required. Rejected: each existing call stops until two values are added, and a wrong reading of the SAP still passes.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• On a SWOG-type SAP the response rate is below the SAS QC value until the programmer sets max_nr_ne=None, max_nr_sd=None. The first PROC COMPARE shows it.
  • The verb now materialises the pipeline, because it joins the records of a group to each other.
  • A subject with PR, SD, PR (C07) or PR, NE, NE, PR (C09) is no longer flagged by default.

docs.title: Best overall response needs the protocol SD minimum
docs.text: Alpha audit finding c1-407 found that best_overall_response applied no minimum time for SD or NON-CR/NON-PD: a subject with SD on day 14 and PD on day 56 got BOR SD, where RECIST 1.1 gives PD. Finding c1-408 found that the documented chain took the best response over all records, so a response after the first PD set BOR. We decided that the SD minimum is a required argument, and that the verb stays a plain minimum over the records it gets, with filter_pd documented first (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• date_col, reference_date and min_sd_days are required, with no default. RECIST 1.1 section 4.4.3 says the minimum is protocol specified, so no value is safe as a default.
  • An SD or NON-CR/NON-PD before reference_date + min_sd_days, or with a null date, counts as NE before the rank, as admiralonco derive_param_bor (ADT >= reference + minimum). CR and PR have no minimum.
  • min_sd_days=0 switches the rule off. The two date columns are then not read.
  • The verb does not cut at the first PD. The docstrings and the module example run filter_pd on a copy, then join BOR back to the full ADRS.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Optional arguments with a warning. Rejected: a programmer who misses the warning still gets SD for B05.
  • A 42-day default from RANDDT, as the admiralonco bor_sd event. Rejected: with a 35-day protocol minimum, SD on day 38 gives NE instead of SD.
  • No rule, a docstring note and a hand recode per study. Rejected: each study needs a new reviewed recode.
  • Cut at the first PD by default (c1-408 option B). Rejected: under iRECIST or a SAP that counts post-PD response the result changes, and existing calls break.
  • Warn when a better response follows a PD (c1-408 option C). Rejected: the number stays wrong, and QC must read the log.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Every old call stops with a TypeError until the programmer adds the three arguments. A study with no protocol minimum writes min_sd_days=0.
  • A QC programmer who follows RECIST and a production program that calls the verb without filter_pd still differ on a response after PD: the docstring states it.

docs.title: Merge reads as SAS MERGE and stops on a clash
docs.text: The alpha audit found that the join verbs of Fleet changed data with no message. merge(keep=) kept only the key and the listed columns, so every other pipeline column was lost (c1-17). A non-key column on both sides gave an X_right column and kept the old left value (c1-12, c1-131). A repeated subject in ADSL multiplied the AE records in merge_adsl, and join_adsl and study_day took one row by input order (c1-14). how="full" lost the key of a subject on the right only (c1-15). We decided to make the join verbs read as SAS MERGE and stop as admiral derive_vars_merged stops (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• keep limits the right dataset. ae.sdtm.merge(dm, on="USUBJID", keep=["AGE"]) reads as merge ae dm(keep=USUBJID AGE): every AE column stays. A keep name that is not in the right dataset raises with a did-you-mean. where filters the right dataset first, so it may use a column that keep leaves out. A spec merge block raises when its variable is not in the frame after the block.
  • A non-key column on both sides raises in merge, merge_adsl, join_adsl, first_date, last_date and count_events, and the message names the columns. There is no overwrite= option: drop or rename the column first. This is the admiral rule; SAS keeps the right value with no message, which a QC program can miss.
  • ADSL holds one record per subject (ADaMIG 1.3). merge_adsl, join_adsl, study_day and baseline_flag with a reference frame, and the carry-through join of fleet run, raise and name the first 5 repeated keys. Identical rows count as one row.
  • Generic merge decides nothing about the key, because one-to-many is a normal join (DM onto AE). It warns at to_frame() when a key repeats on both sides (many-to-many), as the SAS NOTE on repeats of BY values. validate="m:1", "1:m" or "1:1" makes the rule strict; the error at to_frame() names the repeated keys. The check waits for to_frame(), so merge stays lazy.
  • how="full" gives one key column, as SAS MERGE with no IN= and dplyr full_join.
  • Keys match exactly. "S1 " and "S1" are two keys, in merge as in SAS.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep the old keep meaning and document it. Rejected: a SAS programmer reads keep as a data set option, and the old meaning dropped columns with no message.
  • An overwrite= argument on a clash. Rejected: it adds a choice for a case that a drop or a select states more clearly.
  • Warn on any repeated key in merge. Rejected: one-to-many joins are normal and would warn on every DM to AE merge.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A program that merged a frame with shared columns (STUDYID, DOMAIN) now raises. Give keep=, or select the right columns.
  • A spec merge block with no keep: brings every column of its dataset and raises on a shared column. Give keep: [VAR].
  • The many-to-many warning reads the left plan once more at to_frame().

docs.title: A criterion on a missing value is missing, as admiral
docs.text: The alpha audit (finding c1-204) found that criterion() gave CRITyFL N and CRITyFN 0 when the condition could not be evaluated. A record with a missing AVAL then counted as "criterion not met", and a responder table with the denominator Y + N held a subject with no value. admiral derive_vars_crit_flag(values_yn = TRUE, create_numeric_flag = TRUE) gives a missing flag on that record. We decided to follow admiral (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A null condition gives a null CRITyFL and a null CRITyFN. A true condition gives Y and 1, a false condition gives N and 0.
  • CRITy keeps the description on every record, also on a record with a null condition.
  • A SAP rule "missing is not met" is written in the condition: condition=(pl.col("AVAL") >= 10).fill_null(False).

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text: • Keep N and 0 and document it. Rejected: an admiral QC program differs, and AVAL < 5 gives N on a missing AVAL where a plain SAS IF/ELSE gives Y.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A SAS QC program with IF AVAL >= 10 THEN ... ELSE ... gives N on a missing AVAL. It differs from Fleet until it handles the missing value explicitly.
  • flag() is not changed: its false_value still applies to every record that does not meet the criteria.

docs.title: Record filters live in a dataset-level row_steps list
docs.text: The alpha audit (finding c1-39) found that to_spec_yaml() saw only verbs that add a lineage node. A chain with whereclauses, nodup(keep=...) or merge froze to a define.yaml that kept every row, or lost a merged column, with no stub and no warning. A spec block sits under a variable name, and a record filter has no variable. We decided where a frozen filter lives (Mahdi, 4 November 2026, option B).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A dataset holds an ordered row_steps: list. Each step is a verb call: algorithm: whereclauses with where:, or algorithm: nodup with subset:, sort_by:, keep: and descending:.
  • Each step is anchored after: a variable of the dataset (null: before the first variable). from_spec runs the variables in file order and runs a step right after its anchor. The anchor keeps the two ordered lists in one order: ASEQ derived after the filter is numbered on the filtered records, in the chain and in the file.
  • to_spec_yaml() writes the steps. A step it cannot write (a pl.Expr filter, derive_param, derive_summary_records, derive_locf_records, filter_pd) is written as algorithm: TODO with the verb name, and a warning names it. from_spec refuses a TODO step, an unknown algorithm and an unknown anchor before it derives anything.
  • Define-XML shows the steps as the dataset comment: a def:CommentDef (COM.<DATASET>.ROWS) referenced from the ItemGroupDef, in derivation order.
  • A column that a verb added with no lineage node (merge) gets a TODO stub and the warning, never a Predecessor (c1-40).

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• A block under an invented variable name (- name: FILT1). Rejected: the QC programmer reads a variable that the dataset does not have, and one path that forgets to skip it writes a phantom ItemDef.
  • No block; a stub that makes from_spec fail until a programmer writes the filter. Rejected by the decision: the filter could not round-trip, and no tool checks that the hand-written filter equals the inline one.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A variable-level algorithm: whereclauses block still runs; to_spec_yaml() no longer writes one.
  • A step anchor moves back to the nearest earlier written variable when its own anchor is not written (a dropped scratch column).
  • merge and the other row-adding verbs remain TODO steps or stubs until they record their own node (issue #98).

docs.title: visit_map numbers an unscheduled visit and counts study days
docs.text: Alpha audit findings c1-222 and c2-950 found two gaps in visit_map. The window arithmetic subtracted study-day numbers across the missing Day 0, and the docstring said calendar days. A dated record outside every window got a null VISITNUM with no warning, and SV.VISITNUM is Req. We decided both rules with Mahdi (4 November 2026): c1-222 option B, c2-950 option C.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• The distance is the difference of study-day numbers. It is abs(SVSTDY - VISITDY), as a SAS QC program computes it. Across the missing Day 0, Day -1 is 2 days from VISITDY 1. The docstring and the TVSTRL text of TrialVisits.from_schedule() now say "study days, no Day 0".
  • A dated record outside every window is an unscheduled visit. It gets the VISITNUM of the last planned visit whose VISITDY is on or before its study day, plus .1, .2, ... in study-day order within the subject. VISIT is UNSCHEDULED <VISITNUM>, for example UNSCHEDULED 5.1. A record before the first planned visit counts from 0.
  • The verb refuses a number it cannot give. A tenth unscheduled visit after one planned visit, or a number that repeats a planned VISITNUM, raises a DerivationError: map these visits by hand.
  • A record with no study day keeps a null. One UserWarning gives the count of null records and of unscheduled records. For DOMAIN SV, a second UserWarning gives the USUBJID + VISITNUM keys that repeat.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Calendar days across Day 0 (c1-222 option A). Rejected: a SAS QC program that computes abs(SVSTDY - VISITDY) gets a different window and reports a false mismatch.
  • Keep the null and warn only (c2-950 option A). Rejected: VISITNUM stays null until someone fixes it by hand.
  • An unmatched= flag column (c2-950 option B). Rejected: the extra column is not SDTM and must be dropped before export.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The decimal numbering is a sponsor convention (the CDISC pilot uses UNSCHEDULED 5.1). The number can differ from the collected data and from an independent program: state the rule in the SDRG.
  • With no tolerance=, every dated record takes the nearest planned visit, so no record is unscheduled. Give a window to use the rule.
  • VISITNUM becomes Float64 when a record is unscheduled. With no unscheduled record it keeps the TV type.

docs.title: An arm path entry is an element or a step
docs.text: Alpha audit findings c1-247 and c1-781 found that StudyDesign derived every TA value of a position from the element alone. An element had one EPOCH, so a crossover arm (BA: SCRN, B, WO, A) wrote TREATMENT 2 for its first treatment period. TABRANCH was always Randomized to <arm> at the branch point, also when the branch was a responder extension, and no input reached TATRANS. We decided the input shape with Mahdi (4 November 2026): the engineering recommendation for c1-247, and option A for c1-781.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A path entry is an ETCD string or a step. A step is {"etcd": ..., "epoch": ..., "tabranch": ..., "tatrans": ...}. Every key but etcd is optional, and an unknown key raises. A plain string keeps the element's own epoch and the default TABRANCH.
  • EPOCH is the epoch of the position. A step's epoch replaces the element's epoch for that row of TA (SDTMIG 3.4 TA.EPOCH: the epoch of "this element of the arm"). from_usdm writes a step when the epoch of a study cell differs from the element's first epoch.
  • TABRANCH keeps its default (c1-781 option A). It is Randomized to <arm> on the last element that every arm shares, or on the randomized_at element when it is given. A step's tabranch replaces the text, and its tatrans gives TATRANS.
  • The audit warns, it does not refuse. design.audit() reports FLEETTD04 when two arms have the same path and FLEETTD05 when an element repeats in an arm with no per-position epoch. A repeated cycle with one epoch stays possible.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• A ValueError on a repeated element. Rejected: repeated treatment cycles in one epoch are a valid design.
  • TABRANCH blank with a warning (c1-781 option B), or an error until randomized_at is given (option C). Rejected by the decision: every existing randomized design would need a new input.
  • A separate per-arm epoch map. Rejected: the epoch belongs to a position, and an element can appear twice in one arm.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A non-randomized branch still gets Randomized to <arm> until the author writes the rule on the step. The QC programmer must check TABRANCH against the protocol for each non-randomized study.
  • to_mermaid cannot draw a per-position epoch, and it warns.
  • The YAML round trip keeps the steps.

docs.title: A printed tie rounds half away from zero
docs.text: The audit found that apply_fmt_fn printed the stored value with a Python f-string. An f-string rounds the exact binary value, so a printed tie went down or up by chance: 5/16 = 31.25 % printed 31.2, and 1.005 at xx.xx printed 1.00. SAS ROUND and the {cards} default print 31.3 and 1.01, so a SAS QC program failed PROC COMPARE on these cells. Fleet did not state its rule. We decided to round half away from zero as the only rule (Mahdi, 4 November 2026).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A tie rounds half away from zero: 31.25 at xx.x prints 31.3, 2.5 at xx prints 3, -2.25 prints -2.3.
  • The value is read at 15 significant digits first, so a binary artefact such as 31.249999999999996 still counts as the tie 31.25.
  • A value that rounds to zero prints 0.0, never -0.0.
  • The ARD keeps the unrounded value. Only stat_fmt and the rendered cells change.

The rule is in apply_fmt_fn, format_ard and docs/api/tlg.md.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep the f-string rule and document it. Rejected: a SAS QC program fails PROC COMPARE on the tie cells, and neither ROUND nor ROUNDE gives the same cells.
  • Half away from zero by default, with a spec field for the other rule. Rejected: two tables of one study could use different rules, and the cell does not show it.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A QC programmer who uses tern with default settings sees 31.2 where Fleet prints 31.3. Set round_type = "sas" in the QC program.
  • No golden table changed: the pilot fixture has no tie at the printed precision.

docs.title: A missing value is counted, not dropped
docs.text:
The audit found three places where a table drops a null without a sign, so the rows do not add up to N:

  • A subject in the population with a null arm (a screen failure with TRT01A null) stopped the DM table with a raw TypeError (c1-430), and a "*" Total pool counted analysis records that have no arm, so Total was larger than the sum of the arms (c1-431).
  • A null category value (RACE null, AESEV null) had no row and no message (c1-442).

We decided to exclude a null arm with a warning, and to count a null category in a "Missing" row (Mahdi, 4 November 2026, answers A and A).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A null arm is in no column. compute_big_n leaves the subjects out of every N, a "*" pool included, and raises one UserWarning that names the arm column, the count and up to five USUBJIDs. This is the nearest to SAS: PROC FREQ leaves out a missing class level and prints a frequency-missing count. A "*" pool pools every arm present; a null is not an arm.
  • A null category counts in a "Missing" row, last in its block, only when a null exists. The percent base is big N. A blank string counts as null, so an XPT file and a Parquet file give the same table.
  • The rule is a spec field, missing: MissingLevel(columns, label), with a default per template, not per row: DM (SEX, AGEGR1, RACE, ETHNIC), AET03, AET04 and the relationship table (the ranked level), DST01 (EOSSTT), ENT01 (SITEID), PDT01 (DVDECOD). DCSREAS (completers), DTHCAT (it has "Unknown"), PARAMCD and AVISIT get no Missing row. The builder verb is .missing().
  • missing: null switches the rule off. label: null adds no row: the count goes to the ARD warning column of that variable, with one UserWarning.
  • In a worst-case table a ranked value beats a null. A subject with MILD and a null intensity counts under MILD; a subject with only a null counts under Missing.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Stop with a SchemaError for a null arm. Rejected: every normal ADSL with screen failures would need a population filter, and the zero-config call stops.
  • A "Missing" arm column. Rejected: the column is not in the mock shell.
  • No Missing row, only a warning. Kept as label: null, not the default: the rendered table does not add up to N.
  • Percentages on non-missing values (tern, PROC FREQ default). Rejected: every percentage of the block differs from a double program that divides by big N.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A QC programmer can miss the null-arm warning when a randomized subject lost the arm by a data error; N is then low by one. Read the log, or set a population filter.
  • A SAP that counts a missing severity as severe sees an extra row in PROC COMPARE until it sets missing: null or derives ASEV.
  • No golden table changed: the pilot fixture has no null in those columns.

References: FDA CDER Standard Safety Tables and Figures IG v2.0, section 2.1.2; SAS PROC FREQ, missing values.

docs.title: A count cell shows every number the table needs
docs.text:
The audit found three rendered cells that hide a number the ARD holds:

  • In a SOC/PT table the SOC row had empty cells, so the SOC subject count never reached the table, and the PT rows (3 records for 2 subjects) cannot give it (c1-451).
  • When a spec asked for n_events, the table dropped the event count, so the explorer choice "+ events" changed nothing (c1-452).
  • The LBT04 cells printed n (%) with a percent of a per-cell N that the table did not show (c1-453).

We decided on the common SAS shell forms (Mahdi, 4 November 2026, answers A and A; c1-453 without a decision).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• The SOC row prints its subject count: NERVOUS 2 (50.0%), the common SAS shell and the gtsummary form. A parent of continuous rows (PARAMCD in a lab summary) stays blank. A page never ends on a SOC row: the stub test reads the row type.
  • An event count prints in the same cell: 2 (50.0%) 3, the SAS "n (%) E" form, also with n alone (2 3). A footnote explains the form: "n (%) E: n = number of subjects, E = number of events."
  • A cell with a per-cell N prints n/N (%), and n/N when n or N is 0: 1/2 (50.0%), 0/3, 0/0. This is the NEST LBT04 form and the ARD stat label "n / N (%)".

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• tern form for the SOC count: a blank SOC stub, then "Total number of patients with at least one AE". Rejected: one more row per SOC, and a SAS shell with counts on the SOC row no longer matches line by line.
  • Keep the SOC row blank. Rejected: the SOC count can be checked only in the ARD.
  • A second row "Number of events" under each level, as tern. Rejected: the table doubles in length and no longer matches a one-row-per-PT shell.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A QC programmer who validates against a NEST or tern program maps the SOC count to another row.
  • A parser or a PROC REPORT compare must split three values in an "n (%) E" cell.
  • The ARD does not change; only the rendered cells and the footnotes do.

docs.title: RTF pages carry their own title, footnotes and page number
docs.text:
The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (findings c1-820 and c1-456) found two page faults in the TLG renderers:

  • render_rtf broke a logical page every 40 rows and wrote "Page X of Y" as body text. With a two-line column header, footnotes or wrapped rows, 40 rows did not fit one landscape Letter page. Word then made an overflow page with no title, and the counter sat on the wrong physical page.
  • paginate cut a page by row count only. A page could start at a statistic row (Median) or a preferred term, with its parameter, visit or SOC on the page before.

We decided that every physical page shows what it is: its title, its parents and its own page number.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• Title and footnotes in the Word header and footer by default, BODYTITLE on request (Mahdi, c1-820 C). render_rtf and render_listing_rtf write the title and subtitle in one {\header} group and the footnotes in one {\footer} group, as the SAS ODS RTF default. body_title=True writes them in the body at each page break, as ODS RTF BODYTITLE and r2rtf.
  • The page number is a Word field. The footer always holds Page {PAGE} of {NUMPAGES}, so each physical page has a correct number in both layouts.
  • The page budget is in points. A page holds the rows that fit 468 pt (landscape Letter, 1 inch margins). The title, the column-header lines, the footnotes (in the body, or when the header or footer is taller than its margin) and the wrapped lines of each row count. A line is 1.2 times the font size, and a cell wraps at the Courier New width. rows_per_page (default 40) stays as a cap.
  • A continued page repeats its parents. paginate finds the parents of the first row from TableRow.indent and repeats them with the suffix " (continued)" and empty cells. These rows count in the page. The statistic rows of one level stay on one page when they fit; a larger block is split. The first page of a page_by block has no continued row. render_pdf uses the RTF default of 40 rows per page, so its pages also come from the model layer.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Header and footer only (c1-820 A). Rejected as the only layout: a body-only text check does not see the title, and a writer who copies the table into a CSR loses it.
  • Body only, with a line budget (c1-820 B). Rejected as the only layout: when the budget is too high (a long verbatim term, another font), an overflow page has a number but no title.
  • A new pagination argument for continued rows. Rejected: one default is simpler, and a page without its parents is never correct.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Text viewers that drop RTF header and footer groups (TextEdit, textutil) do not show the default title, footnotes or page number. Word does. Use body_title=True when a QC script reads the RTF text.
  • A QC script that searches the RTF for the literal "Page 1 of" no longer matches.
  • RTF and PPTX pages, and PDF pages, can hold fewer rows than before and can start with "(continued)" rows.
  • The two layouts need their own visual check.

docs.title: The define follows the IG for dataset defaults and qualifiers
docs.text: The alpha audit of 2 November 2026 (package define) found two dataset-level defaults in the Define-XML path that disagree with the CDISC examples. Every dataset was IsReferenceData="No", so TS was described as subject data, and a dataset with no repeating: key was Repeating="Yes", also DM and ADSL (c1-561). In an SDTMIG 3.4 spec, a role: qualifier variable was described as a variable of its parent domain, with no SUPP-- dataset and no message (c1-562). We decided that the defaults follow the official Define-XML 2.1 SDTM example, and that the generator refuses a qualifier in its parent domain up to SDTMIG 3.4.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• Repeating. With no repeating: key, DM, ADSL and the trial design datasets (TA, TE, TV, TI, TS, TD, TM) are Repeating="No". Every other dataset is Repeating="Yes". fleet init define writes the same rule.
  • IsReferenceData. With no is_reference_data: key (a new dataset key), TA, TE, TV, TI, TS, TD, TM and a dataset of class TRIAL DESIGN are IsReferenceData="Yes". Every other dataset is No.
  • An explicit key wins over both defaults.
  • A qualifier in its parent domain is refused (Mahdi, c1-562 B). For standard: SDTMIG and standard_version 3.4 or earlier, a variable with role: qualifier (or algorithm: nsv) in a dataset that is not SUPP-- gives a SpecError that names AE.AETRTEM and SUPPAE. The author declares SUPPAE and moves the variable there. Changed by ADR-0044: the generator now moves such a variable to a generated SUPPAE, and refuses only a qualifier that cannot move.
  • A SUPP-- dataset describes its parent. A dataset named SUPPAE gets Domain="AE", as in the official example.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Build SUPP-- automatically with QVAL value-level items (c1-562 A). Rejected: generated metadata with an IDVAR that the spec does not state can pass review with a wrong IDVAR.
  • Keep the qualifier in its parent and warn (c1-562 C). Rejected: the warning can be missed, and the define still shows a non-standard variable in its parent for IG 3.4.
  • Keep Repeating="Yes" as the default. Rejected: DM and ADSL have one record per subject; a reviewer reads Yes as a wrong structure.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A spec that runs export_supp(spec=...) from role: qualifier variables in the parent dataset could not give an SDTMIG 3.4 define from the same file. ADR-0044 removes this conflict: the define describes the qualifier in a generated SUPP<domain> ItemGroupDef, so one define.yaml serves fleet run, fleet define-xml and fleet check. The refusal stays for a qualifier that cannot move (for example a parent with no --SEQ, or a declared SUPP<domain> as well). No qualifier is described as a parent-domain variable.
  • Specs that relied on the old Repeating="Yes" default for DM, ADSL or a trial design dataset now give No. Set repeating: true to keep the old value.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• CDISC Define-XML 2.1, example defineV21-SDTM.xml (TS: Repeating="No" IsReferenceData="Yes"; SUPPAE: Domain="AE").
  • SDTMIG 3.4, section 8.4 (Relating Non-Standard Variable Values to a Parent Domain).

docs.title: The SDTM define states the ItemRef Role, and CORE checks a define only on request
docs.text: The alpha audit of November 2026 (c1-268) found that Fleet cannot give a Define-XML to CORE, and that the define YAML has no key for the SDTM role of a variable. When the audit ran CORE with -dxp and Fleet's pilot define, rule CG0010 (CORE-001081) reported "define role null" 19 times on DM alone. We decided that fleet init define fills the role of each SDTM variable from the CDISC Library, that the Define-XML writes it as the ItemRef Role, and that fleet validate passes a define to CORE only when the user names it.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• Role from the CDISC Library (Mahdi, option A). fleet init define writes sdtm_role: on each SDTM variable from the role of the SDTMIG variable in the CDISC Library (Identifier, Topic, Timing, Grouping Qualifier, Result Qualifier, Synonym Qualifier, Record Qualifier, Variable Qualifier, Rule). The key is new: the existing role: qualifier keeps its one meaning (a Non-Standard Variable for supp()) and never reaches the Define-XML.
  • ItemRef Role. DefineSpecGenerator writes Role="<sdtm_role>" on the ItemRef of each variable that has the key. A variable without the key gets no Role, as before.
  • CORE checks a define on request only. fleet validate --define PATH (and ValidationService.validate_datasets(..., define_xml=PATH)) passes -dxp PATH to each engine run. The path goes through the run setup, is resolved against the working directory and is printed in the report header. A path that does not exist refuses the run (exit 2). Without the flag, no define is passed.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• B: leave Role out and do not pass the define by default. Rejected: an agency or sponsor checker that runs CG0010 reports the same warnings there first, on each variable.
  • C: leave Role out and pass the define by default. Rejected: about 19 CG0010 warnings on DM alone hide the real findings in each report.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The role in a define is a value nobody typed: a sponsor-specific role can differ from the Library fill, so QC must check sdtm_role: like any other define value.
  • Defines written before this change have no sdtm_role:. Rerun fleet init define --force, or add the key by hand, before passing the define to CORE.
  • References: CDISC Define-XML 2.1 specification (ItemRef, attribute Role); SDTM variable roles in the SDTMIG; CORE rule CG0010.

docs.title: TTE censors at the last record before the stop date
docs.text: The alpha audit of November 2026 (c1-355) found that df.adam.tte.param() censored a subject without an event at the end date, not at the last censor record on or before it. Example: subject A, TRTSDT 2024-01-01, last assessment 2024-03-01, new anticancer therapy 2024-04-01, no progression. Fleet gave ADT 2024-04-01, AVAL 92. admiral 1.5 derive_param_tte (end_dates, event_type = "negative") gives ADT 2024-03-01, AVAL 61. The unassessed 31 days counted as progression-free. The event_type argument changed nothing, and the doc page claimed "admiral 1.5 parity". We decided to follow the admiral rule, and to replace the source objects with plain frames (Mahdi, option A and the API below).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
adtte = adsl.adam.tte.param(
    "PFS",
    "Progression-Free Survival",
    start="TRTSDT",
    events={"PROGRESSIVE DISEASE": adrs.filter(pl.col("AVALC") == "PD")},
    censors={
        1: last_assessment.with_columns(CNSDTDSC=pl.lit("LAST ADEQUATE TUMOR ASSESSMENT")),
        3: no_baseline,
    },
    stop_at={
        "EOSDT": (4, "END OF STUDY"),
        "NACTDT": (2, "NEW ANTICANCER THERAPY"),
        "DCUTDT": (5, "DATA CUT-OFF"),
    },
    keep_reason=[3],
)
  • Sources are plain frames. Each event or censor value is a Polars frame with the subject keys and ADT. The key of events= is the EVNTDESC. The key of censors= is the CNSR (an integer >= 1). A frame may carry SRCDOM, SRCVAR, SRCSEQ, CNSDTDSC and, for a censor, EVNTDESC; a censor without EVNTDESC gets null and a warning (see "EVNTDESC of a censor"). SRCSEQ breaks a tie on one date.
