  • Stop date. stop_at= maps an ADSL date column to (CNSR, EVNTDESC). The stop date of a subject is the earliest non-null stop_at date. Event and censor records after it are dropped; a record on the stop date stays. This is the admiral rule for both event types.
  • Selection. The first event left wins: CNSR 0, EVNTDESC its key. Without an event, the last censor record left gives the date (ADT, CNSDTDSC). On a censor date tie, the frame given last wins (admiral: the last source in censor_conditions). CNSR and EVNTDESC follow "Reason of the censoring" below. A date before start is set to start (admiral: ADT = max(ADT, STARTDT)). This applies to events and censors; the CNSR does not change (Mahdi: keep the admiral rule).
  • No record left. The subject drops, with a warning that names the count and the first USUBJIDs. A censor frame on the start date (CNSR 3 above) keeps such a subject; retain="censor_at_start" is the other way.
  • Positive events. No event_type argument. For a favorable event (time to response), add a censor frame on the stop date, for example {1: adsl.select("USUBJID", ADT=pl.min_horizontal("EOSDT", "NACTDT"))}. It is the last record in the window, so a subject without the event is censored at the stop date, as admiral event_type = "positive". The stop gives the CNSR and EVNTDESC of that row.
  • AVAL is unchanged: .aval() gives ADT − STARTDT + 1 days. Subject A: 61.
  • The old EventSource / CensorSource objects, the prebuilt library (DEATH_EVENT, ...), sources_frame() and the start_date=, end_dates= and event_type= arguments are removed. No example, define.yaml or spec registry entry used them. When the base frame is ADSL and no ADSL is pinned, param() pins it, so a later param(), join_adsl() and km_data() read it.

docs.title: Reason of the censoring
docs.text:
A follow-up of c1-355 (Mahdi, option B, November 2026). The first version took the CNSR from the key of the censor frame, and the stop columns carried no CNSR. To tell "censored before new therapy" from "censored at end of study", a programmer had to build one censor frame per stop. A forgotten frame gave a wrong CNSR on every such subject.

Rationale. RECIST 1.1 defines progression, not censoring. The FDA guidance "Clinical Trial Endpoints for the Approval of Cancer Drugs and Biologics" (2018) and the EMA appendix on PFS (Guideline on the evaluation of anticancer medicinal products, Appendix 1) separate two facts for a censored subject:

  • The date: the last adequate tumour assessment before the stop.
  • The reason: why the observation stopped (new anticancer therapy, end of study, data cut-off, no baseline assessment).

ADaM BDS-TTE puts the reason in CNSR and EVNTDESC, and the description of the date in CNSDTDSC. So the stop carries CNSR and EVNTDESC; the censor frame carries the date and CNSDTDSC. This is also the admiral rule for end_dates: a censor record takes the censor and set_values_to of the first end date, and consider_end_dates = FALSE on a censor_source is the opt-out.

The rule. For a subject with no event in the window, CNSR and EVNTDESC come from, in this order:

  1. A censor frame whose key is in keep_reason=: its own key and its own EVNTDESC (admiral consider_end_dates = FALSE). Example: no baseline assessment, censored on TRTSDT with CNSR 3, although the data cut-off applies.
  2. Else, when the subject has a stop date: the stop. If two stop columns share the earliest date, the first column in the stop_at dict wins.
  3. Else (no stop date): the key of the censor frame, and EVNTDESC from the frame (or null with the warning).

CNSDTDSC from the censor frame is kept in all cases. ADT and AVAL do not change. An event keeps CNSR 0 and its EVNTDESC; events after the stop date stay dropped. retain="censor_at_start" keeps its own CNSR 1 and NO EVENT OBSERVED: it is a fallback for subjects with no record, not a censor frame.

Validation.

  • stop_at must be a dict. A list raises, and the message shows the dict form. The package is pre-alpha, so there is no shim; a list form "stop with no reason" was rejected because two forms of one argument hide which rule gave the CNSR.
  • Each value is (CNSR, EVNTDESC): an integer >= 1 and a non-empty text.
  • The stop codes are distinct, and they differ from the censors= keys. One CNSR value then names one reason, and a reviewer can read the reason from CNSR alone. admiral allows two end dates with the same censor (its default is 1); Fleet does not. To give two columns one reason, combine them first, for example adsl.with_columns(STOPDT=pl.min_horizontal("EOSDT", "LSTCONDT")).
  • keep_reason keys must be keys of censors=.

Trace. explain=True (and the trace of select_tte()) has a cnsr_from column on the selected row: event, keep_reason, stop_at <column>, censors key or retain.

docs.title: EVNTDESC of a censor
docs.text:
Mahdi: use the guidance first, then the admiral default, else make a call.

  • Guidance. ADaM BDS-TTE v1.0 (CDISC, published 2016-02-12) defines EVNTDESC (Event or Censoring Description) as a permissible free-text variable with no codelist; its examples give a study text on each row (for example DEATH, COMPLETED STUDY). CDISC ADaM CT on NCI EVS (checked November 2026) has no EVNTDESC codelist. So the guidance gives no default value.
  • admiral. censor_source() has no default EVNTDESC: it is NA unless set_values_to gives it.
  • The call. A censor frame without an EVNTDESC column gives a null EVNTDESC, as admiral, and param() warns once per call. The warning names the CNSR keys and shows the fix (EVNTDESC=pl.lit("ALIVE") on the frame). A fixed text such as "CENSORED" was rejected: the reason of the censoring is study text from the SAP, and a text that Fleet invents differs from an admiral or SAS double program on every censored row. A silent null was rejected: BDS-TTE expects a description on censored rows, and the reviewer cannot tell why a subject was censored.
  • retain="censor_at_start" keeps its own text, NO EVENT OBSERVED.

docs.title: PARAM label
docs.text:
Mahdi: when param is not given, use the controlled terminology. param() takes PARAM from, in this order:

  1. param=, or PARAM in set_values_to.
  2. The study CT: the decode of PARAMCD in the codelist that a PARAMCD variable of the ADaM define.yaml references (the ADTTE dataset first, then the other datasets). The study is the first study_config.yaml in the working directory or above it, as import_codelists() finds it. fleet init ct writes the CDISC CT preferred terms as these decodes, so a PARAMCD from a pinned CDISC CT codelist resolves here too.
  3. CDISC CT itself: no lookup. CDISC ADaM CT (NCI EVS, November 2026) has no time-to-event PARAMCD codelist; its parameter code codelists (for example GAD02PC, HAMD1PC) are questionnaire and scale codes. The generated codelists.py holds submission values only, not decodes. Fleet makes no network call.

If no source gives a label, param() raises. The message names PARAMCD, the places searched and the fix (param=, or a decode in the define.yaml codelist). When PARAMCD comes from set_values_to (strata), PARAM must come from there too, because the static PARAMCD does not name the stratum. Before this change, a missing label gave rows without PARAM; ADaMIG requires PARAM with a one-to-one map to PARAMCD.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• B: keep censoring at the end date. Rejected: an admiral or SAS double program that censors at the last assessment differs for each such subject (31 days for subject A), and the FDA guidance on oncology endpoints censors at the last adequate assessment before new anticancer therapy.
  • C: keep the source objects and add consider_end_dates. Rejected: the objects repeat what filter and select already say, and the pin nickname hid which frame a source read.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Differences from admiral: the stop codes must be distinct (admiral allows the same censor on two end dates). The stop EVNTDESC replaces the EVNTDESC of the censor frame; in admiral, a set_values_to of the censor source overwrites the end date value unless it uses coalesce(). Fleet takes the guidance order: the reason of the stop wins, and keep_reason is the explicit opt-out.
  • Code that used the old API must change to frames. The package is pre-alpha, so there is no shim. Code that passed stop_at as a list must give the dict form.
  • References: admiral 1.5.0 derive_param_tte (end_dates, event_type, censor_source(consider_end_dates)), its examples "End of the observation period" and "Differentiating censoring reasons"; FDA Guidance for Industry, Clinical Trial Endpoints for the Approval of Cancer Drugs and Biologics (2018), PFS censoring; EMA Guideline on the evaluation of anticancer medicinal products in man, Appendix 1 (methodological considerations for PFS); RECIST 1.1; CDISC ADaM BDS-TTE v1.0 (CNSR, EVNTDESC, CNSDTDSC); ADaMIG v1.3 (PARAM, PARAMCD); CDISC ADaM CT, NCI EVS ADaM Terminology.txt.

docs.title: The define moves a parent qualifier to a generated SUPP-- dataset
docs.text: The alpha audit found that the spec path makes no SUPP-- dataset (c1-105). Step A of the fix made fleet run write SUPP<domain> for each SDTM variable with role: qualifier or algorithm: nsv. ADR-0041 (c1-562 B) made fleet define-xml and fleet check refuse the same variable in its parent domain up to SDTMIG 3.4. So one define.yaml could not drive fleet run and also pass fleet define-xml. We decided that the parent dataset of the spec keeps the qualifier for the derivation, and that the generator describes it in a generated SUPP<domain> dataset.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• The spec form. The qualifier stays a variable of its parent dataset in define.yaml (role: qualifier or algorithm: nsv), with its label, type, length, origin and derivation. fleet run derives it there and writes it to SUPP<domain> (step A).
  • The Define-XML form. For standard: SDTMIG and standard_version 3.4 or earlier, the generator leaves the qualifier out of the parent ItemGroupDef and adds an ItemGroupDef SUPP<domain> after it:
  • Domain is the parent, def:Class is RELATIONSHIP, the structure is "One record per IDVAR, IDVARVAL, and QNAM value per subject".
  • The variables are STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, QNAM, QLABEL, QVAL, QORIG, QEVAL. The keys are STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, QNAM.
  • STUDYID and USUBJID are Predecessor of the parent variables.
  • QVAL has one ValueListDef. Each qualifier gives one WhereClauseDef QNAM EQ <name> and one value-level ItemDef with the label, type, length, codelist, origin and method of the qualifier.
  • The leaf is supp<domain> with the format of the parent, the file that fleet run writes.
  • IDVAR is stated. IDVAR is <DOMAIN>SEQ, the rule of fleet run. The IDVAR ItemDef names it in its origin text, and IDVARVAL has a method. For DM, IDVAR and IDVARVAL are null, and the origin text says so.
  • The refusal of ADR-0041 stays for a qualifier that cannot move. The generator and fleet check refuse the define and name SUPP<domain> when the parent has no STUDYID or USUBJID, a parent other than DM has no <DOMAIN>SEQ, the spec also declares SUPP<domain>, a qualifier name has more than 8 characters (QNAM), its label has more than 40 characters (QLABEL), or a qualifier is a key of the parent.
  • A spec may still declare SUPP<domain> itself, with no qualifier in the parent. The generator writes it as declared.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Declare SUPP<domain> in define.yaml and move the qualifier there (the ADR-0041 form). Rejected: fleet run builds the qualifier in the parent derivation, so the variable must be in the parent dataset. Two declarations of one variable can disagree.
  • Keep the qualifier in the parent ItemGroupDef. Rejected: SDTMIG 3.2 to 3.4 do not allow a non-standard variable in the parent domain (c1-562 B).
  • IDVAR from a new spec key. Rejected for now: fleet run uses <DOMAIN>SEQ, and the define states it. A sponsor that needs another IDVAR (for example --GRPID) declares SUPP<domain> by hand.

The concern of ADR-0041 against generated SUPP-- metadata (an IDVAR that the spec does not state) is answered: the IDVAR rule is fixed and shared with fleet run, and the define names it.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One define.yaml serves fleet run, fleet define-xml and fleet check.
  • A page map key AE.AETRTEM of the external page map does not reach the moved qualifier. Put the pages under crf_pages: of the variable; they go to the value-level item.
  • The value-level ItemDef is named QVAL. Its description is the label of the qualifier.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• SDTMIG 3.4, section 8.4 (Relating Non-Standard Variable Values to a Parent Domain).
  • CDISC Define-XML 2.1, example defineV21-SDTM.xml (SUPPAE with value-level metadata on QVAL by QNAM).
  • ADR-0041 (the define follows the IG for dataset defaults and qualifiers).

docs.title: One date-time path follows admiral derive_vars_dtm
docs.text:
The alpha audit of November 2026 (c1-119, with c1-67 and c1-74) found that .adam.date() and .sdtm.date() gave two results for one *DTM call. .adam imputed 2024-03 to 2024-03-01T00:00:00; .sdtm gave null. With time=, both gave null for a partial date, and highest= raised (ADR-0021, step 1). The time= path set TMF to null, even for a time it imputed.

We checked admiral 1.4.1 derive_vars_dtm on a grid of 15 --DTC forms, six highest_imputation levels and the first and last imputation (scripts/regen_admiral_dtm_grid.R, frozen in tests/fixtures/goldens/dates/admiral_dtm_grid.csv).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• One path. impute_dtc_to_datetime in fleet.adam.utils gives the *DTM value, its DTF and its TMF for both namespaces.
  • time= comes first. The date and the time become one --DTC value by SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4.2 (2024-03 and 08:15 give 2024-03--T08:15). The value then takes the imputation and highest=, as a --DTC source does. A time in another layout (0815) is left out, with one warning.
  • highest= has the admiral meaning on a *DTM target: "M", "D", "h", "m", "s" or "n" names the highest part that may be imputed. A value that needs more is null. No highest= is "M", as on a *DT target (ADR-0021). This is not the admiral default ("h"), which gives null for every partial date.
  • The first missing part decides (admiral preserve = FALSE, the default). A part below it is not used: 2021-03--T08:30 gives 2021-03-01T00:00:00 with DTF D and TMF H; 2021-03-15T08:-:45 gives 08:00:00 with TMF M. This is the same rule as 2021---15 on a *DT target.
  • TMF follows the imputed parts, also with time=: 08:30 gives TMF S, a null time gives H.
  • "Y" still raises. admiral imputes a year only with min_dates or max_dates, and a *DTM target refuses min_date= and max_date= (ADR-0021).

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep a collected time below a missing day (admiral preserve = TRUE). Rejected for the default: admiral does not do it by default, and *DT drops a collected day below a missing month. A preserve= argument can come later if a SAP asks for it.
  • The admiral default highest = "h". Rejected: a *DT target imputes the month and the day by default, and the two targets of one --DTC value would disagree.
  • Null for a partial date in .sdtm.date(), with a docstring note. Rejected: one verb name would still give two results.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• .sdtm.date("ASTDTM", ...) on a partial date now gives an imputed value with its flags, not null.
  • With time=, a partial date now gives an imputed value; the collected time is not kept. An hh:mm time takes seconds 00, or 59 with impute_time="last", and TMF S.
  • A null time with time= takes impute_time, else impute (it took "first" before).
  • impute="mid" on a missing month gives June 15, and admiral gives June 30. That is a separate defect and is out of the grid.
  • An hh:mm time (2021-03-15T10:30) gives TMF S. admiral derive_vars_dtm gives NA by default, because ignore_seconds_flag = TRUE. The date docstring says so; a SAP that follows admiral drops or nulls the TMF column (c1-73).

docs.title: A subject-level table takes the ADSL arm
docs.text: The alpha audit of November 2026 (c1-432) found that the TLG templates asked for TRTA on ADSL. ADaMIG 1.3 puts the arm on ADSL as TRTxxP and TRTxxA, and TRTA on BDS and OCCDS datasets. A conformant ADSL has no TRTA, so the demographics and disposition tables stopped ("requires columns [..., 'TRTA', ...]"), and the examples added the planned arm under the actual-arm name: adsl.with_columns(pl.col("TRT01P").alias("TRTA")). For an AE table, ADAE holds TRTA and ADSL holds TRT01A: the CLI gave no route and no hint. We decided (Mahdi, option A) that the CLI stops with an error that names --adsl-groupby TRT01A, and that the user states the ADSL arm column. No column is mapped automatically.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
# Subject-level table: the arm is TRT01A, else TRT01P.
ard = adsl.tlg.dm.t_summary()

# Event-level table: ADAE by TRTA, big N from ADSL by TRT01A.
ard = adae.tlg.ae.population(adsl, group_col="TRT01A").by("TRTA").template("aet02").to_ard()

fleet tlg run aet01.yaml --data ADAE=adae.parquet --adsl adsl.parquet --adsl-groupby TRT01A
  • Subject-level templates (dmt01, dst01, dtht01, ent01: one record per subject, ADSL) default to TRT01A. When ADSL has no TRT01A, they take TRT01P. The spec declares columns: [TRT01A] and arm_fallback = ("TRT01A", "TRT01P").
  • The fallback applies only when columns is not set. A spec or call that names the arm (columns: [TRT01A], groupby=, .by(), --groupby) gets that column or an error, never the planned arm in its place.
  • Event-level templates (AE, CM, MH, VS, LB, EG, EX, the deviations table on ADDV) keep TRTA. Their big N reads ADSL by the same name, or by adsl_group_col (population(adsl, group_col=), --adsl-groupby, MCP adsl_groupby) when ADSL has the arm under another name.
  • The CLI and the MCP tool do not auto-detect the arm of a subject-level spec: the template does it, with the same rule as run_spec.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• B: map TRTA to TRT01A for the big N automatically, with a note. Rejected: in a crossover the N is then the period 1 count, the table looks valid, and a PROC FREQ by period does not match.
  • C: auto-pick a column that is in both frames. Rejected: the numerators then stop using TRTA, so a period 2 AE is counted under the period 1 arm.
  • Default the subject-level templates to TRT01P. Rejected: the safety tables count subjects by the treatment they received. TRT01P is the fallback for an ADSL without TRT01A (a study before first dose, or a planned-arm analysis set).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A table on ADSL now shows TRT01A as group1, not TRTA. The golden ARDs of dmt01, dst01, dtht01 and ent01 changed in that column only.
  • Code that passed groupby="TRTA" on an ADSL with a TRTA alias still runs. The alias is no longer needed.
  • In a crossover, adsl_group_col: TRT01A gives the period 1 N. The SAP must support it; for a by-period N, derive a period-level denominator.
  • References: CDISC ADaMIG 1.3, section 3.1.4 (ADSL treatment variables TRTxxP, TRTxxA) and section 3.3.2 (BDS TRTP, TRTA); CDISC ADaM OCCDS 1.1 (TRTA on OCCDS).

docs.title: derive_param adds no record with a null AVAL
docs.text: The alpha audit of November 2026 found two gaps in derive_param against admiral derive_param_computed. First (c1-321), a by group with a null component (for example WEIGHT not done at BASELINE) got a new BMI record with a null AVAL. admiral adds no record by default (keep_nas = FALSE). Second (c1-320), Fleet had no constant_by_vars: a per-visit BMI with the height of the screening visit only gave one BMI record, at SCREENING.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
advs = vs.adam.derive_param(
    by=["USUBJID", "AVISIT"],
    constant_by=["USUBJID"],
    constant_parameters={"H": "HEIGHT"},
    parameter_filter={"W": "WEIGHT"},
    set_values_to={"PARAMCD": "BMI", "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"},
    analysis_value=pl.col("W") / (pl.col("H") / 100) ** 2,
).to_frame()
  • keep_nas=False is the default. A new record whose AVAL is null is not added. This includes an AVAL that is infinite or NaN (a division by zero): it becomes null with a warning, and the record is not added. keep_nas=True keeps the record with a null AVAL, as before.
  • constant_parameters join on constant_by. The parts of parameter_filter join on by; the parts of constant_parameters then join on constant_by, which must be a subset of by. Each part must be unique on its own key.
  • A PARAMCD with no record warns with a did-you-mean hint (admiral warns that no observation fulfils the filter).
  • set_values_to holds constants only. An expression raises. In derive_summary_records, an expression is evaluated per group (admiral set_values_to = exprs(ADT = min(ADT))).

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep the null record by default. Rejected: a BMI record with a null AVAL at a visit where the weight was not done adds a row that a QC programmer with admiral or SAS does not have, and the counts of a by-visit table differ.
  • A separate verb for constant parameters. Rejected: the rule is one join more; two arguments on derive_param keep one verb, as admiral.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A pipeline that relied on the null records gets fewer records. Give keep_nas=True to keep them.
  • References: admiral derive_param_computed (keep_nas, constant_by_vars, constant_parameters); admiral ADVS template (derive_param_bmi(constant_by_vars = exprs(USUBJID))).

docs.title: Age in years uses the admiral year for weeks and hours
docs.text: The alpha audit of November 2026 (c1-83) found that adsl.age_years() divided an age in WEEKS by 52.1775 and gave null for an age in HOURS. admiral compute_age_years divides weeks by 365.25/7 (52.17857) and hours by 8766. AGE 587 WEEKS gave 11.250060 in Fleet and 11.249829 in admiral; with round_digits=1 the values were 11.3 and 11.2. The docstring said that admiral uses 52.1775 weeks, which is not true. HOURS is a value of the CDISC CT codelist AGEU (C66781).

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• One year is 12 months, 365.25/7 weeks, 365.25 days or 8766 hours, as admiral compute_age_years. age_in_years computes AGE * 7 / 365.25 for WEEKS and AGE / 8766 for HOURS.
  • An unknown unit gives null and a warning. adsl.age_years() counts the rows whose AGEU is not YEARS, MONTHS, WEEKS, DAYS or HOURS (for example YEAR) and names some of the values. The expression in fleet.adam.utils stays a pure expression and does not warn.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep 52.1775 weeks per year (365.2425/7, the Gregorian mean year). Rejected: the days branch already uses 365.25, so the two branches disagreed, and admiral parity is the stated aim of the verb.
  • Raise on an unknown unit. Rejected: a DM with one bad AGEU row would stop the whole ADSL; a null with a warning keeps the other subjects and points at the row.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• An age in weeks changes in the sixth significant digit. A rounded value can change by one unit in the last digit.
  • tests/unit/test_admiral_parity.py::TestAgeInYears::test_weeks now holds the admiral values.

docs.title: A table orders its rows and columns as the shell
docs.text: The alpha audit of November 2026 found that a Fleet table sorted its levels and its columns as text. Week 12 printed before Week 2 (c1-439), the age group <65 printed after 65-80, a Total pool printed between two arms, and an Enum arm lost its order (c1-438). A typo in column_order was silently ignored. The demographics table showed Mean and SD for age with no n row, so the reader could not see that a subject had no age (c1-804). A SAS programmer gets the shell order from a numeric code (BY AVISITN), from a format with ORDER=DATA, or from PROC REPORT ORDER=INTERNAL.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
# Levels sort by AVISITN when ADLB has it: Baseline, Week 2, Week 4, Week 12.
ard = adlb.tlg.lb.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)

# An explicit key for a field without a <field>N column.
spec = LBSummarySpec(rows=[Row(field="PARAMCD", order_by="PARAMN"), Row(field="AVISIT")])
  • Row levels. A row field sorts on Row.order_by. When it is not set, the engine takes <field>N when the dataset has it (AVISIT by AVISITN, AGEGR1 by AGEGR1N, RACE by RACEN). Each level sorts on the minimum of the order column within its parent level; a null key sorts last, and a tie sorts as text. A field without an order column sorts as text, as before. PARAMCD has no default: PARAMCDN is not an ADaM variable, so set order_by="PARAMN". The missing level stays last in its block (ADR-0038).
  • Columns. The arms come first, then the pools in their definition order. The arms follow the categories of an Enum arm column (ADSL first, else the analysis dataset), and a category with no subject keeps its column with N=0. Without an Enum, the arms sort as text. column_order moves its entries to the front; an entry that is not an arm or a pool raises.
  • Arm type. The arm column must be text (String, Categorical or Enum). A numeric arm (TRTAN) stops with a message that names TRTA and column_order. It is not cast: a Float64 code from an XPT file would print as 1.0.
  • Continuous blocks of the demographics table start with n, the count of subjects with a value, as PROC MEANS N and tern analyze_vars.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• An arms: field that lists the columns. Rejected for now: column_order and an Enum give the order, and a second field would have to agree with both.
  • Sort every level as text and let the user sort the ARD. Rejected: the rendered table follows the ARD order, so a user who does not know the rule prints Week 12 before Week 2.
  • Dispatch on the dtype of the row field (sort a numeric field numerically). Rejected: AVISIT is text; only its N companion carries the order.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The order of a table with a <field>N column, a pool, or an Enum arm changes. The values do not change.
  • The golden dmt01 ARD gains one n row per arm.
  • A spec with a column_order typo, or a numeric groupby, now stops.
  • References: CDISC ADaMIG v1.3, BDS timing variables (AVISITN is the numeric version of AVISIT and gives its sort order; a *N variable is the numeric version of its character variable); SAS PROC REPORT ORDER= and PROC MEANS N; tern analyze_vars.

docs.title: A table refuses values that SAS cannot hold
docs.text: The alpha audit of November 2026 found two inputs that a SAS table program cannot meet and that Fleet summarised without a message. A NaN analysis value was counted in n and blanked the mean and SD, and an infinite value printed inf and then crashed the renderer (c1-434). A duplicate ADSL record weighted the mean age by records, and a subject in two arms counted twice (c1-443). SAS has no NaN or infinite value, and ADaMIG requires one ADSL record per subject.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
# NaN counts as missing, with one UserWarning: "AVAL has 1 NaN value(s); ..."
ard = adlb.tlg.lb.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)
  • NaN in the analysis-value column (or a continuous_vars column of the demographics table) becomes null before any statistic, with one UserWarning that gives the count. n, mean, SD and the quantiles then match PROC MEANS and R mean(na.rm = TRUE).
  • An infinite value (inf, -inf) raises SchemaError with the column and the count.
  • A duplicate ADSL record (the same USUBJID and arm twice, after the population filter) raises SchemaError with the count and the first USUBJIDs. The demographics check() reports it too.
  • One USUBJID in two arms (a crossover ADSL read by period) counts in each arm, with one UserWarning.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Raise on NaN. Rejected: NaN comes from a Polars division by zero in a derivation; a missing value is the SAS reading of it, and the warning makes it visible.
  • Drop duplicate ADSL records silently, or keep the first. Rejected: the two records can differ, and the choice would decide the numbers.
  • Raise on a subject in two arms. Rejected: a crossover study can read ADSL by period on purpose. The warning names the subjects.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A table on a dataset with NaN now warns and gives the PROC MEANS values.
  • A table on an ADSL with duplicate records now stops.
  • References: CDISC ADaMIG v1.3, section 3.1 (ADSL has one record per subject); SAS PROC MEANS (missing values are left out); R mean(na.rm = TRUE).

docs.title: baseline_flag names its reference date and its test code
docs.text: Alpha audit finding c1-107 found two silent defaults in the SDTM baseline_flag. The reference date was RFSTDTC by default, but SDTMIG 3.4 defines --LOBXFL as "the last non-missing value prior to RFXSTDTC". With no testcd_col, the verb flagged one record per subject across all tests, so WEIGHT got no flag when SYSBP had a later record. Neither choice was visible in the call, so a QC programmer could not see it.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• ref_col is required. The call names the reference date, for example ref_col="RFXSTDTC" for --LOBXFL or ref_col="RFSTDTC" for a sponsor --BLFL. sdtm.oak derive_blfl has no default for ref_var either.
  • testcd_col is required. The call names the test code column, for example testcd_col="VSTESTCD". testcd_col=None is still legal for a frame with one test, but the programmer must write it.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Change the default to RFXSTDTC. Rejected: a --BLFL program that relied on RFSTDTC would change its flags with no message.
  • Keep the defaults and warn when the frame holds more than one test code. Rejected: it fixes the test code only, and the reference stays hidden.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Each existing call without ref_col= or testcd_col= raises a TypeError that names the missing argument. Add the two arguments; the flags do not change when the old defaults were right.
  • The ADaM baseline_flag is a different verb and does not change.

docs.title: A trial design arm needs its protocol name
docs.text: Alpha audit finding c1-786 found that StudyDesign made TA.ARM from the ARMCD when arm_names had no entry for an arm: ARMCD XAN_HI gave ARM Xan Hi. SDTMIG 3.4 defines TA.ARM as the name of the arm in the protocol, and CDISC CORE-000047 requires each DM.ARM to be a TA.ARM. An invented name passes every Fleet check and then fails against DM.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• Each arm needs an entry in arm_names. StudyDesign raises a ValueError that names the arms with no name. There is no fallback.
  • The audit compares DM with TA. When DM has ARM, each DM (ARMCD, ARM) pair must be a TA pair. A pair that TA does not hold gives the warning FLEETTD07. The reserved codes (SCRNFAIL, NOTASSGN) and an ARMCD that TA does not hold (already FLEETTD02) are not checked again.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• Keep the fallback and warn. Rejected: the dataset is still written with a name that no protocol holds.
  • Make the DM check an error. Rejected: in a multistage design DM.ARM can name a path that TA builds from more than one ARMCD, so a warning is safer.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A trial_design.yaml or a Python design with no arm_names raises: add the protocol names.
  • from_mermaid and from_usdm give names (the diagram label or the USDM arm label), so they do not change.

docs.title: A study run stops on a declared variable that no input has
docs.text: fleet run on the CDISCPILOT01 example wrote ADSL without SAFFL and ITTFL, and exited 0. The define declared both with no derivation, because the example script derived them inline, and no input had them. select(spec=) skipped the absent columns with a UserWarning only. A QC programmer then gets an ADSL with no safety population flag from a run that reports success.

docs.title: The decision
docs.text:
• A carry-through column that no input has stops the run. After a step is built, run_study checks each declared variable with no derivation. When the built dataset does not have it, a StudyRunError names the dataset, the variables and the inputs, and says how to fix it. Nothing is written for the step: fleet run keeps the old file.
  • optional: true on a variable is the permanent exception. It is in the define, so a reviewer sees it. It applies only to a variable with no derivation. An optional variable is still carried when an input has it.
  • --no-strict (strict=False) is the run-wide exception. It already turned an unknown algorithm into a warning; it now does the same for an absent variable. It is for a draft run, not for a study that is final.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• A per-dataset list (allow_absent: [RFXSTDTC]). Rejected: the list is far from the variable, so a renamed variable leaves a stale entry.
  • A run-level list (--allow-absent ADSL.SAFFL). Rejected: the exception is in the command line, so two programmers who run the same study get different datasets.
  • An error only for mandatory: true. Rejected: the pilot marks SAFFL mandatory: false, so it would still be lost with exit 0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The pilot ADSL now derives SAFFL and ITTFL in its define (algorithm: flag, criteria: exists on the pinned EX). Its DM marks RFXSTDTC and RFXENDTC optional: true: no input has them.
  • examples/minipilot is a small study that fleet run builds end to end, from raw CSV files to ADSL, ADVS, ADAE and ADEX (finding c1-347).

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Fleet's public API is reachable from a single import:

import fleet

Documentation generated from source — never out of sync

Every module page below is rendered live from the Python docstrings in the package. The Verb Cheat Sheet cross-links each verb name to its source-of-truth docstring via autorefs. When a verb's signature, parameters, or examples change in code, the docs update automatically on the next build — there is no parallel reference to maintain or fall behind.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Module Description sdtm SDTM namespace — derivation verbs + Trial Design domains (call .verbs()) adam ADaM BDS namespace — derivation verbs + shared-verb mixin (call .verbs()) adsl ADSL namespace (df.adam.adsl) — patient-level verbs occds OCCDS namespace (df.adam.occds) — occurrence verbs ta Therapeutic-area extensions (df.adam.<ta>, including pk) define_xml Define-XML generation, validation, spec generation ct Controlled terminology — CDISC Library API, code generation, validation tlg TLG namespace (df.tlg) — summary tables, listings, ARD generation, HTML/PDF export comparison fleet.compare — PROC COMPARE analogue: keyed matching, comparison report, flags core StudyContext, PipelineDAG, exceptions

docs.title: Namespace registration
docs.text:
Importing fleet registers two core namespace extensions on every polars.DataFrame. All ADaM sub-structures and TA extensions are accessed as nested properties of df.adam:

import fleet  # registers df.sdtm, df.adam, df.tlg
import polars as pl

pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).sdtm  # SDTM verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam  # ADaM BDS verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.adsl  # ADSL verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.occds  # OCCDS verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.onco  # TA extensions via df.adam.<ta>
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.pk  # PK (pharmacokinetics) verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).tlg.ae  # AE summary tables and listings
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).tlg.vs  # Vital-signs summary tables

docs.title: Discovering what's available
docs.text:
Every namespace answers for itself — no cheat sheet required:

import fleet
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]})
df.sdtm.verbs()  # DataFrame: every SDTM verb + one-line summary + origin
df.adam.adsl.verbs()  # same for any (sub-)namespace
df.adam.onco.verbs().filter(pl.col("origin") == "adam.onco")  # only the oncology verbs

fleet.spec_algorithms("sdtm")  # define.yaml algorithm ids per standard
fleet.spec_coverage()  # algorithm ↔ verb ↔ required-fields matrix

verbs() returns a sorted Polars DataFrame (verb, summary, origin) built live from the class docstrings, so it can never lag behind the installed version. origin is the path you type to reach the namespace that defines the verb: sdtm, adam, adam.onco, or core for the verbs every namespace shares. A sub-namespace inherits every shared verb, so autocomplete lists about 45 names; filter on origin to see the handful it adds.

docs.title: ADaM Namespace
docs.text: The df.adam namespace builds ADaM BDS datasets (ADVS, ADLB, …).

docs.title: fleet.adam.AdamNamespace
docs.text:
Bases: SharedADaMVerbsMixin

Immutable pipeline builder for ADaM derivations.

Each verb adds one step to the plan of one LazyFrame; to_frame() collects the plan once (a verb that needs data earlier says so). Accepts both pl.DataFrame and pl.LazyFrame inputs, so scanned sources stay lazy end-to-end.

Inherits shared verbs from SharedADaMVerbsMixin (assign, case_when, merge, source, derivation, whereclauses, ...). Discover the full set with df.adam.verbs().

Source code in src/fleet/adam/namespace.py 
@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("adam")
@pl.api.register_lazyframe_namespace("adam")
class AdamNamespace(SharedADaMVerbsMixin):
    """
    Immutable pipeline builder for ADaM derivations.

    Each verb adds one step to the plan of one LazyFrame; ``to_frame()``
    collects the plan once (a verb that needs data earlier says so).
    Accepts both ``pl.DataFrame`` and ``pl.LazyFrame`` inputs, so scanned
    sources stay lazy end-to-end.

    Inherits shared verbs from ``SharedADaMVerbsMixin`` (``assign``,
    ``case_when``, ``merge``, ``source``, ``derivation``, ``whereclauses``,
    ...).  Discover the full set with ``df.adam.verbs()``.
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 9.  baseline — propagate baseline value to all group records        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def baseline(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        aval: str = "AVAL",
        baseline_flag: str = "ABLFL",
        by: str | list[str] | None = None,
        strict: bool = True,
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive BASE as the AVAL where the baseline flag equals ``"Y"``.

        Uses a window function so all records in the same group receive the
        same baseline value.  A group with **more than one** flagged
        record has an ambiguous baseline: with ``strict=True`` (default)
        this raises a ``DerivationError`` naming the offending groups
        (admiral semantics); ``strict=False`` keeps the legacy behaviour
        (silently taking the maximum flagged value) but emits a
        ``UserWarning``.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"BASE"``).
            aval: Analysis value column (default ``"AVAL"``).
            baseline_flag: Flag column indicating the baseline record.
            by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"]``).
            strict: Raise when a group has multiple baseline-flagged
                records (default ``True``).

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Raises:
            DerivationError: When ``strict=True`` and at least one group
                carries more than one baseline-flagged record.

        Examples:
            Propagate baseline AVAL to all records::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL",
                              by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        import warnings

        grps = [by] if isinstance(by, str) else list(by or ["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
        schema_names = self._lazy.collect_schema().names()
        if baseline_flag not in schema_names or any(g not in schema_names for g in grps):
            # Missing columns — defer to _chain's verb-attributed error.
            return self._chain(
                baseline(aval=aval, baseline_flag_col=baseline_flag, group_by=grps, target=target),
                verb="baseline",
            )
        dup_groups = (
            self._lazy.filter(pl.col(baseline_flag) == "Y")
            .group_by(grps)
            .agg(pl.len().alias("__n_baseline__"))
            .filter(pl.col("__n_baseline__") > 1)
            .collect()
        )
        if dup_groups.height:
            sample = dup_groups.select(grps).head(5).rows()
            keys = "; ".join(", ".join(f"{k}={v!r}" for k, v in zip(grps, row)) for row in sample)
            more = f" (+{dup_groups.height - 5} more)" if dup_groups.height > 5 else ""
            detail = (
                f"baseline('{target}'): {dup_groups.height} group(s) have more than one "
                f"record flagged {baseline_flag}='Y' — the baseline is ambiguous. "
                f"Offending groups: {keys}{more}."
            )
            if strict:
                raise DerivationError(
                    f"{detail} Deduplicate the baseline flag (e.g. via "
                    ".flag(..., criteria='last') or .nodup(...)) or pass strict=False "
                    "to keep the legacy max() behaviour."
                )
            warnings.warn(
                f"{detail} Taking the maximum flagged value per group (strict=False).",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        return self._chain(
            baseline(aval=aval, baseline_flag_col=baseline_flag, group_by=grps, target=target),
            verb="baseline",
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 10. chg — change from baseline                                      #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def chg(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        aval: str = "AVAL",
        base: str = "BASE",
        post_baseline: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Compute change from baseline: ``CHG = AVAL - BASE``.

        Without *post_baseline*, every record gets a value, also the baseline
        record (0) and the records before it.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"CHG"``).
            aval: Analysis value column.
            base: Baseline value column.
            post_baseline: Condition that marks the post-baseline records,
                as an expression or a string parsed as ``where=`` is.  The
                other records get null.  Default ``None``: every record.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        References:
            ADaMIG 1.3, section 3.3.4: CHG is populated for post-baseline
            records.  admiral template ``ad_advs.R`` restricts
            ``derive_var_chg`` with ``restrict_derivation(filter = AVISITN > 0)``.

        Examples:
            Derive CHG on the records after the first dose::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE",
                         post_baseline="pl.col('ADT') > pl.col('TRTSDT')")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(
            _post_baseline_only(
                f"chg('{target}')",
                chg(aval=aval, base=base, target=target),
                post_baseline,
                self._lazy.collect_schema(),
            ),
            verb="chg",
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 11. pchg — percent change from baseline                             #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def pchg(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        aval: str = "AVAL",
        base: str = "BASE",
        post_baseline: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Compute percent change from baseline.

        ``PCHG = (AVAL - BASE) / BASE * 100``.  Returns null when BASE is
        null or zero.  ADaMIG formula. admiral ``derive_var_pchg`` divides
        by abs(BASE), so the sign differs on a negative baseline: AVAL -2,
        BASE -2.5 gives PCHG -20 here and 20 in admiral.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"PCHG"``).
            aval: Analysis value column.
            base: Baseline value column.
            post_baseline: Condition that marks the post-baseline records,
                as an expression or a string parsed as ``where=`` is.  The
                other records get null.  Default ``None``: every record.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        References:
            ADaMIG 1.3, section 3.3.4: PCHG is populated for post-baseline
            records.  admiral template ``ad_advs.R`` restricts
            ``derive_var_pchg`` with ``restrict_derivation(filter = AVISITN > 0)``.

        Examples:
            Derive PCHG on the records after the first dose::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE",
                          post_baseline="pl.col('ADT') > pl.col('TRTSDT')")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(
            _post_baseline_only(
                f"pchg('{target}')",
                pchg(aval=aval, base=base, target=target),
                post_baseline,
                self._lazy.collect_schema(),
            ),
            verb="pchg",
        )

                advs = (

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 14. nrind — normal range indicator                                   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def nrind(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        value: str,
        low: str,
        high: str,
        signif_dig: int = 15,
    ) -> Self:
        """Categorise *value* relative to normal range: LOW / NORMAL / HIGH.

        The value and the limits are compared at *signif_dig* significant
        digits, so float noise (1.3 x 88.4 = 114.92000000000002) does not
        move a value at the limit out of the range.  A null or NaN value gives
        null.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"NRIND"``).
            value: Column containing the numeric result.
            low: Column containing the lower limit of normal.
            high: Column containing the upper limit of normal.
            signif_dig: Significant digits for the comparison (default 15).

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        References:
            admiral ``derive_var_anrind`` (pharmaverse): ``signif(x, 15)`` on AVAL,
            ANRLO and ANRHI before the comparison.

        Examples:
            Derive normal range indicator for lab results::

                adlb = (
                    lb_raw.adam
                    .nrind("NRIND", value="LBSTRESN",
                           low="LBSTNRLO", high="LBSTNRHI")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(
            _nrind_expr(value=value, low=low, high=high, target=target, signif_dig=signif_dig),
            verb="nrind",
        )

    # 15. on_treatment — derive ONTRTFL                                    #

    def on_treatment(
        self,
        target: str = "ONTRTFL",
        *,
        adt: str,
        trtsdt: str,
        trtedt: str,
        open_ended: bool = True,
    ) -> Self:
        """Set *target* to ``"Y"`` when *adt* is within [trtsdt, trtedt].

        When *open_ended* is ``True`` (default) and *trtedt* is null, the

        value gives null); a number raises.  When *adt* and *trtsdt* are
        both ``pl.Datetime``, the start comparison keeps the time, so a
        pre-dose record on the first dose day is not on treatment; the end
        comparison is at date level.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"ONTRTFL"``).
            adt: Analysis date column.
            trtsdt: Treatment start date column.
            trtedt: Treatment end date column.
            open_ended: Treat null *trtedt* as open-ended (default ``True``).

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        References:
            admiral ``derive_var_ontrtfl`` (start compared with time when
            both are date-times); ADR-0011 and ADR-0022.

        Examples:
            Derive on-treatment flag::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .on_treatment("ONTRTFL", adt="ADT",
                                  trtsdt="TRTSDT", trtedt="TRTEDT")
                    .to_frame()

        """
        return self._chain(
            _on_treatment_expr(
                adt=adt,
                trtsdt=trtsdt,
                trtedt=trtedt,
                target=target,
                open_ended=open_ended,
                dtypes=self._lazy.collect_schema(),
            ),
            verb="on_treatment",
        )
