class DatasetChecker:
    """Validate a ``pl.DataFrame`` against a simplified Fleet define YAML.

    Parameters
    ----------
    define_yaml_path:
        Path to a ``define.yaml`` conforming to ``define_spec_schema.json``.
    enabled:
        Master switch.  When *False* all checks are skipped and ``check()``
        returns an empty ``CheckResult`` immediately.
    check_columns:
        When *True* (default), verify column completeness (missing / extra).
    check_types:
        When *True* (default), verify Polars dtype compatibility.
    check_ct:
        When *True* (default), verify values of variables declaring a
        ``codelist:`` against the spec's inline ``codelists:`` items.
        Out-of-codelist values are errors.
    check_values:
        When *True* (default), verify the define ``length`` of text values,
        no null in a ``mandatory`` variable, and no two records with the
        same ``keys`` (a null key value counts as one value, as in
        ``PROC SORT NODUPKEY``).
    validate_schema:
        When *True* (default), validate the YAML against the JSON schema on
        load.  Set to *False* to skip during tight inner loops.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        define_yaml_path: str | Path,
        *,
        enabled: bool = True,
        check_columns: bool = True,
        check_types: bool = True,
        check_ct: bool = True,
        check_values: bool = True,
        validate_schema: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self._enabled = enabled
        self._check_columns = check_columns
        self._check_types = check_types
        self._check_ct = check_ct
        self._check_values = check_values

        self._data: dict[str, Any] = read_define_yaml(
            define_yaml_path, validate_schema=validate_schema and enabled
        )

        # Build a lookup: dataset_name (upper) → dataset dict
        self._datasets: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
            ds["name"].upper(): ds for ds in self._data.get("datasets", [])
        }
        # Inline codelists: oid → codelist dict (used by the CT check)
        self._codelists: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
            cl["oid"]: cl for cl in self._data.get("codelists", [])
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Public API                                                           #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def check(
        self,
        df: pl.DataFrame | pl.LazyFrame,
        dataset: str,
        *,
        strict: bool = True,
    ) -> CheckResult:
        """Check *df* against the define for *dataset*.

        Args:
            df: The ``pl.DataFrame`` to check.  A ``pl.LazyFrame`` is
                collected.
            dataset: Dataset name to look up in the define (e.g. ``"DM"``).
                Case-insensitive.
            strict: When ``True`` (default), ``core="Req"`` issues are
                errors.  When ``False``, ``Req`` issues are downgraded to
                warnings so the pipeline can proceed despite missing
                required variables (e.g. during development or when source
                data is incomplete).

        Returns:
            CheckResult: Always returns a result — never raises unless you
                call ``result.raise_on_errors()``.

        Examples:
            Check DM against the pilot define::

                checker = DatasetChecker("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml")
                checker.check(dm, "DM").print_report()
        """
        result = CheckResult(dataset=dataset.upper())

        if not self._enabled:
            return result
        if isinstance(df, pl.LazyFrame):
            df = df.collect()

        ds_def = self._datasets.get(dataset.upper())
        if ds_def is None:
            result.errors.append(
                f"Dataset '{dataset}' not found in define. Available: {sorted(self._datasets)}"
            )
            return result

        # Build variable index (exclude private _-prefix names)
        vars_by_name: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
            v["name"]: v for v in ds_def["variables"] if not v["name"].startswith("_")
        }

        # Labels always populated regardless of other flags
        result.labels = {name: v.get("label", "") for name, v in vars_by_name.items()}

        # Actual DataFrame columns excluding private _-prefix columns
        actual_cols: set[str] = {c for c in df.columns if not c.startswith("_")}

        if self._check_columns:
            self._run_column_checks(result, vars_by_name, actual_cols, strict=strict)

        if self._check_types:
            self._run_type_checks(result, df, vars_by_name, actual_cols, strict=strict)

        if self._check_ct:
            self._run_ct_checks(result, df, vars_by_name, actual_cols)

        if self._check_values:
            self._run_value_checks(result, df, ds_def, vars_by_name, actual_cols, strict=strict)

        return result

    def datasets(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the list of dataset names declared in the define."""
        return list(self._datasets)

    def labels(self, dataset: str) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Return the variable → label mapping for *dataset* without running full checks."""
        ds_def = self._datasets.get(dataset.upper())
        if ds_def is None:
            return {}
        return {
            v["name"]: v.get("label", "")
            for v in ds_def["variables"]
            if not v["name"].startswith("_")
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Check runners                                                        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    @staticmethod
    def _run_column_checks(
        result: CheckResult,
        vars_by_name: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
        actual_cols: set[str],
        *,
        strict: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        define_cols = set(vars_by_name)

        missing = define_cols - actual_cols
        for col in sorted(missing):
            var_def = vars_by_name[col]
            core = var_def.get("core", "")
            msg = f"Column '{col}' declared in define is missing from the DataFrame."
            result.missing_columns.append(col)
            _classify(
                result, msg, core=core, mandatory=var_def.get("mandatory", False), strict=strict
            )

        extra = actual_cols - define_cols
        for col in sorted(extra):
            msg = f"Column '{col}' is present in the DataFrame but not declared in the define."
            result.extra_columns.append(col)
            result.warnings.append(msg)

    @staticmethod
    def _run_type_checks(
        result: CheckResult,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        vars_by_name: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
        actual_cols: set[str],
        *,
        strict: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        schema = df.schema
        for col_name, var_def in vars_by_name.items():
            if col_name not in actual_cols:
                continue  # already reported as missing
            define_type = var_def.get("type")
            if define_type is None:
                continue  # the schema check reports a variable with no type
            actual_dtype = schema[col_name]
            # --DTC is ISO 8601 text whatever the define type says (SDTMIG 3.4 4.4)
            is_dtc = col_name.upper().endswith("DTC")
            compat_types = (pl.String,) if is_dtc else _POLARS_COMPAT.get(define_type, ())

            ok = isinstance(actual_dtype, compat_types)
            if not ok and define_type == "integer" and actual_dtype in (pl.Float32, pl.Float64):
                # SAS transport has only Char and Num: an XPT code reads as a float.
                values = df[col_name].drop_nulls()
                ok = bool((values == values.round(0)).all())
            if not ok:
                mm = TypeMismatch(
                    variable=col_name,
                    define_type=define_type,
                    actual_dtype=str(actual_dtype),
                )
                result.type_mismatches.append(mm)
                expected_label = (
                    "String (ISO 8601 text)"
                    if is_dtc
                    else _TYPE_LABEL.get(define_type, define_type)
                )
                msg = (
                    f"Column '{col_name}': define type '{define_type}' "
                    f"(expects {expected_label}) but actual dtype is '{actual_dtype}'."
                )
                core = var_def.get("core", "")
                _classify(
                    result, msg, core=core, mandatory=var_def.get("mandatory", False), strict=strict
                )

    def _run_ct_checks(
        self,
        result: CheckResult,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        vars_by_name: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
        actual_cols: set[str],
    ) -> None:
        """Verify variable values against the spec's inline codelists.

        The define.yaml already declares each codelist's submission values
        (``codelists[].items[].coded_value``) — a dataset asserting
        conformance to them must actually contain them.  Out-of-codelist
        values are **errors**.  When an offending value matches a decode
        (or a raw ``ct_map`` key from the variable's derivation), the
        message says so — those are almost always unapplied mappings.
        """
        for col_name, var_def in vars_by_name.items():
            oid = var_def.get("codelist")
            if not oid or col_name not in actual_cols:
                continue
            codelist = self._codelists.get(oid)
            if codelist is None:
                result.warnings.append(
                    f"Column '{col_name}' references codelist '{oid}' which is not "
                    f"declared in this define. Declared codelist OIDs: "
                    f"{sorted(self._codelists)}"
                )
                continue
            items = codelist.get("items") or []
            if not items:
                result.warnings.append(
                    f"Column '{col_name}': codelist {oid} has no items, so its values "
                    "are not checked; run fleet init ct."
                )
                continue
            coded: set[str] = {str(item["coded_value"]) for item in items}
            decode_of: dict[str, str] = {
                str(item["decode"]): str(item["coded_value"])
                for item in items
                if item.get("decode")
            }
            ct_mapping: dict[str, Any] = (var_def.get("derivation") or {}).get("ct_map") or {}

            values = [_code_text(v) for v in df[col_name].drop_nulls().unique().to_list()]
            values = [v for v in values if v != ""]
            invalid = sorted(v for v in values if v not in coded)
            if not invalid:
                continue

            hints: list[str] = []
            for v in invalid:
                if v in decode_of:
                    hints.append(f"'{v}' is the decode of submission value '{decode_of[v]}'")
                elif v in ct_mapping:
                    hints.append(f"'{v}' is a raw ct_map key — the mapping was not applied")
            hint = f" ({'; '.join(hints)})" if hints else ""
            msg = (
                f"Column '{col_name}': value(s) {invalid} not in codelist "
                f"'{oid}' ({codelist.get('name', oid)}). "
                f"Valid values: {sorted(coded)}.{hint}"
            )
            result.ct_violations.append(msg)
            result.errors.append(msg)

    @staticmethod
    def _run_value_checks(
        result: CheckResult,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        ds_def: dict[str, Any],
        vars_by_name: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
        actual_cols: set[str],
        *,
        strict: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Check the define Length, the Mandatory variables and the key of *df*."""
        found: list[str] = []
        for col_name, var_def in vars_by_name.items():
            if col_name not in actual_cols:
                continue
            column = df[col_name]
            length = var_def.get("length")
            if length is not None and column.dtype == pl.String:
                too_long = column.str.len_bytes() > int(length)
                if too_long.any():
                    longest = int(column.str.len_bytes().max() or 0)
                    found.append(
                        f"Column '{col_name}': {int(too_long.sum())} value(s) longer than the "
                        f"define Length {length} (longest {longest} bytes)."
                    )
            if var_def.get("mandatory"):
                empty = column.is_null()
                if column.dtype == pl.String:
                    empty = empty | (column.str.strip_chars() == "")
                if empty.any():
                    found.append(
                        f"Column '{col_name}': {int(empty.sum())} null value(s), but the "
                        "define marks it Mandatory."
                    )
        keys = list(ds_def.get("keys") or [])
        absent = [k for k in keys if k not in actual_cols]
        if keys and absent:
            found.append(
                f"Key variable(s) {absent} are missing, so duplicate keys are not checked."
            )
        elif keys:
            dupes = df.select(keys).is_duplicated()
            if dupes.any():
                example = df.filter(dupes).select(keys).row(0)
                found.append(
                    f"{int(dupes.sum())} record(s) share their key {keys} with another "
                    f"record (first: {dict(zip(keys, example, strict=True))})."
                )
        for msg in found:
            if strict:
                result.errors.append(msg)
            else:
                result.warnings.append(msg + " [strict=False: downgraded from error]")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # CDISC Core validation                                                #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def validate_core(
        self,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        dataset: str,
        *,
        standard: str | None = None,
        version: str | None = None,
    ) -> ValidationResult:
        """Run the official CDISC Rules Engine against *df*.

        Standard (``"SDTMIG"`` / ``"ADAMIG"``) and version are auto-detected
        from the ``study`` block in the define YAML.  Override either with the
        *standard* / *version* keyword arguments.

        Requires the CDISC Rules Engine to be installed and discoverable.  See
        ``OfficialCDISCValidator`` for setup instructions.

        Args:
            df: The materialised ``pl.DataFrame`` to validate.
            dataset: Dataset / domain name (e.g. ``"DM"``, ``"ADVS"``).
            standard: Override — e.g. ``"SDTMIG"`` or ``"ADAMIG"``.
            version: Override — e.g. ``"3.4"`` or ``"1.1"``.

        Returns:
            ValidationResult: The engine findings.

        Raises:
            ValidationSetupError: The run setup is refused (an IG version
                Fleet does not support), or no engine is found.  The
                engine, custom rules, timeout and accepted findings come
                from the study config, as for ``fleet validate``.

        Examples:
            Run CORE on DM with the define's standard::

                checker = DatasetChecker("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml")
                result = checker.validate(dm, "DM")
        """
        from fleet.core.exceptions import ValidationSetupError
        from fleet.validation.run_setup import build_run_setup, missing_engine_reason
        from fleet.validation.service import ValidationService

        study = self._data.get("study", {})
        detected_standard = (standard or study.get("standard", "SDTMIG")).upper()
        declared = study.get("standard_version")
        setup = build_run_setup(
            name=dataset,
            standard="adam" if "ADAM" in detected_standard else "sdtm",
            version=version or (str(declared) if declared is not None else None),
        )
        if setup.engine.value is None:
            raise ValidationSetupError(missing_engine_reason(setup))

        svc = ValidationService(rules_engine_path=setup.engine.value)
        ig, rules, timeout = (
            setup.ig_version.value,
            setup.custom_rules.value,
            setup.timeout.value,
        )
        if setup.standard.value == "adam":
            result = svc.validate_adam(
                df, dataset=dataset, version=ig, custom_rules=rules, timeout=timeout
            )
        else:
            result = svc.validate_sdtm(
                df, domain=dataset, version=ig, custom_rules=rules, timeout=timeout
            )
        result.apply_setup(setup)
        return result

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # XPT export                                                           #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def write_xpt(
        self,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        dataset: str,
        path: str | Path,
        *,
        reorder: bool = True,
    ) -> Path:
        """Write *df* as a SAS transport file, version 5, with the define labels.

        When *reorder* is ``True`` (default) the DataFrame columns are
        rearranged to match the variable order declared in the define before
        writing.  Columns not declared in the define (e.g. private ``_``-prefix
        columns) are silently dropped so the XPT only contains define-declared
        variables.  The dataset and variable labels come from the define;
        the rules of the file are those of :func:`fleet.io.save_xpt`.

        Requires ``pyreadstat``.  Install with ``uv add "fleet-cdisc[io]"``.

        Args:
            df: The materialised ``pl.DataFrame`` to write.
            dataset: Dataset name used to look up the variable order in the
                define.  It must equal the file name (FDA TCG 3.1.1).
            path: Destination file path (e.g. ``"outputs/dm.xpt"``).
            reorder: Whether to reorder / filter columns to match define
                order.

        Returns:
            Path: Resolved path of the written file.

        Raises:
            FleetIOError: When the file name is not the dataset name.

        Examples:
            Write DM with the define labels::

                checker = DatasetChecker("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml")
                checker.write_xpt(dm, "DM", "outputs/dm.xpt")
        """
        from fleet.core.exceptions import FleetIOError
        from fleet.io import save_xpt

        out = Path(path)
        if out.stem.upper() != dataset.upper():
            raise FleetIOError(
                f"{out.name} would hold dataset {dataset.upper()}; name the file "
                f"{dataset.lower()}.xpt, because the member is named as the file (FDA TCG 3.1.1)."
            )

        ds_def = self._datasets.get(dataset.upper())
        if reorder and ds_def is not None:
            define_names = [v["name"] for v in ds_def["variables"]]
            # Keep only columns that are both in define and in df; preserve define order
            ordered = [c for c in define_names if c in df.columns]
            df = df.select(ordered)

        return save_xpt(
            df,
            out,
            label=ds_def.get("label") if ds_def is not None else None,
            column_labels=self.labels(dataset),
        )

    reorder: bool = True,
) -> Path:
    """Write *df* as a SAS transport file, version 5, with the define labels.

    When *reorder* is ``True`` (default) the DataFrame columns are
    rearranged to match the variable order declared in the define before
    writing.  Columns not declared in the define (e.g. private ``_``-prefix
    columns) are silently dropped so the XPT only contains define-declared
    variables.  The dataset and variable labels come from the define;
    the rules of the file are those of :func:`fleet.io.save_xpt`.

    Requires ``pyreadstat``.  Install with ``uv add "fleet-cdisc[io]"``.

    Args:
        df: The materialised ``pl.DataFrame`` to write.
        dataset: Dataset name used to look up the variable order in the
            define.  It must equal the file name (FDA TCG 3.1.1).
        path: Destination file path (e.g. ``"outputs/dm.xpt"``).
        reorder: Whether to reorder / filter columns to match define
            order.

    Returns:
        Path: Resolved path of the written file.

    Raises:
        FleetIOError: When the file name is not the dataset name.

    Examples:
        Write DM with the define labels::

            checker = DatasetChecker("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml")
            checker.write_xpt(dm, "DM", "outputs/dm.xpt")
    """
    from fleet.core.exceptions import FleetIOError
    from fleet.io import save_xpt

    out = Path(path)
    if out.stem.upper() != dataset.upper():
        raise FleetIOError(
            f"{out.name} would hold dataset {dataset.upper()}; name the file "
            f"{dataset.lower()}.xpt, because the member is named as the file (FDA TCG 3.1.1)."
        )

    ds_def = self._datasets.get(dataset.upper())
    if reorder and ds_def is not None:
        define_names = [v["name"] for v in ds_def["variables"]]
        # Keep only columns that are both in define and in df; preserve define order
        ordered = [c for c in define_names if c in df.columns]
        df = df.select(ordered)

    return save_xpt(
        df,
        out,
        label=ds_def.get("label") if ds_def is not None else None,
        column_labels=self.labels(dataset),
    )

docs.title: Tooling Introspection
docs.text:
fleet.introspect is the surface for editor and tooling integrations — a language server offering algorithm: completions, a hover card, a define.yaml linter. If you are writing derivations rather than tooling, you want the SDTM and ADaM namespaces instead.

The module is additive-only within a major version: names and return fields may be added, but nothing is removed or renamed except on a major. A client therefore declares a minimum Fleet version — read from serverInfo.version in the language-server handshake — and never a maximum. See ADR-0001 for the reasoning.

from fleet import introspect

items = [
    {"label": algo.name, "documentation": algo.description}
    for algo in introspect.algorithms("adam")
]

If standard is not a known CDISC standard.

Examples:

Put a red line on a misspelled key::

from fleet import introspect

problems = introspect.check_derivation(
    "sdtm", {"algorithm": "assign", "sorce": "sex"}
)
assert problems[0].key == "sorce"
Source code in src/fleet/introspect.py 
def check_derivation(
    standard: Standard,
    block: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    target: str = "VAR",
    codelist: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[DerivationProblem, ...]:
    """Return why ``from_spec()`` would refuse one ``derivation:`` block.

    The block is checked by the same per-algorithm model ``from_spec()``
    uses, after the variable's ``codelist:`` fills ``ct`` (ADR-0008).  An
    unknown algorithm gives one problem; use :func:`suggest_algorithm` for
    a better message.

    Args:
        standard: ``"sdtm"`` or ``"adam"``.
        block: The ``derivation:`` block, with its ``algorithm`` key.
        target: The variable the block derives.
        codelist: The ``codelist:`` of the variable, if any.

    Returns:
        tuple[DerivationProblem, ...]: Empty when the block is valid.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *standard* is not a known CDISC standard.

    Examples:
        Put a red line on a misspelled key::

            from fleet import introspect

            problems = introspect.check_derivation(
                "sdtm", {"algorithm": "assign", "sorce": "sex"}
            )
            assert problems[0].key == "sorce"
    """
    _check_standard(standard)

    from pydantic import ValidationError

    from fleet.core import spec_registry

    try:
        data = spec_registry.with_codelist(standard, block, codelist)
    except ValueError as exc:
        return (DerivationProblem(None, str(exc)),)
    try:
        spec_registry.parse_variable_spec(standard, {"target": target, **data})
    except ValidationError as exc:
        problems = []
        for error in exc.errors():
            location = error["loc"]
            message = str(error["msg"]).removeprefix("Value error, ")
            key = str(location[1]) if len(location) > 1 else None
            problems.append(DerivationProblem(key, f"{key}: {message}" if key else message))
        return tuple(problems)
    return ()

def algorithm_doc(name: str, standard: Standard | None = None) -> AlgorithmDoc | None:
    """Return the docstring summary of the verb *name* dispatches to.

    Kept separate from :class:`AlgorithmInfo` on purpose: resolving a
    docstring imports and scans the verb-bearing namespace modules, which
    is too expensive for the per-keystroke completion path.

    Args:
        name: Canonical algorithm name.
        standard: ``"sdtm"`` or ``"adam"``: resolve the verb of that
            standard only. ``seq`` and ``date`` exist in both, with
            different verbs. ``None`` takes the SDTM verb first.

    Returns:
        AlgorithmDoc | None: Summary and dotted verb path, or ``None``
            when the algorithm has no resolvable verb.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *standard* is not a known CDISC standard.

    Examples:
        Add the verb's own words to a hover card::

            from fleet import introspect

            doc = introspect.algorithm_doc("baseline", standard="adam")
            markdown = f"{doc.summary}\\n\\nVerb: `{doc.verb_path}`" if doc else ""
    """
    from fleet.core.algorithm_resolver import resolve_algorithm_docstring

    if standard is not None:
        _check_standard(standard)
    summary, verb_path = resolve_algorithm_docstring(name, standard)
    if summary is None or verb_path is None:
        return None
    return AlgorithmDoc(summary=summary, verb_path=verb_path)

def load_spec_yaml(text: str) -> Any:
    """Parse define.yaml text the way ``from_spec`` does.

    The spec dialect reads booleans the YAML 1.2 way (``true`` and ``false``
    only), so the ``on:`` join key of ``merge`` stays a string.  A tool that
    parses a define.yaml itself must use this loader, or it sees the key
    ``True`` where Fleet sees ``on``.

    Args:
        text: The YAML document.

    Returns:
        The parsed document, or ``None`` for an empty one.

    Raises:
        yaml.YAMLError: On invalid YAML.

    Examples:
        Read the blocks of a file the editor holds::

            from fleet import introspect

            data = introspect.load_spec_yaml(editor_text) or {}
    """
    from fleet.core.define_spec import load_spec_yaml as _load

    return _load(text)

Immutable pipeline builder for OCCDS (one-row-per-event) derivations.

Covers occurrence datasets: ADAE, ADCM, ADMH, ADEX, etc. Also registered as the occds LazyFrame namespace, so pl.scan_parquet(...).occds starts a fully lazy OCCDS pipeline.

Inherits shared verbs from SharedADaMVerbsMixin (assign, case_when, merge, source, derivation, whereclauses, ...) and adds OCCDS-specific verbs for event sequencing, worst-record flagging, and treatment-emergent classification. Discover the full set with .verbs().

Source code in src/fleet/adam/occds_namespace.py 
@pl.api.register_lazyframe_namespace("occds")
class OCCDSNamespace(SharedADaMVerbsMixin):
    """
    Immutable pipeline builder for OCCDS (one-row-per-event) derivations.

    Covers occurrence datasets: ADAE, ADCM, ADMH, ADEX, etc.  Also
    registered as the ``occds`` LazyFrame namespace, so
    ``pl.scan_parquet(...).occds`` starts a fully lazy OCCDS pipeline.

    Inherits shared verbs from ``SharedADaMVerbsMixin``
    (assign, case_when, merge, source, derivation, whereclauses, ...)
    and adds OCCDS-specific verbs for event sequencing, worst-record
    flagging, and treatment-emergent classification.  Discover the full
    set with ``.verbs()``.
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # OCCDS-specific verbs                                                 #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def treatment_emergent(
        self,
        target: str = "TRTEMFL",
        *,
        start_date: str,
        end_date: str | None,
        trtsdt: str,
        trtedt: str | None = None,
        end_window: int | None = None,
        offset_days: int = 0,
    ) -> Self:
        """Set *target* to ``"Y"`` for treatment-emergent events, as admiral ``derive_var_trtemfl``.

        The cases are taken in this order; the first that applies decides:

        1. *trtsdt* missing: null (the subject is not treated).
        2. *end_date* before *trtsdt*: null (the event ended before treatment).
        3. *start_date* missing: ``"Y"`` (a missing start cannot show the
           event began before treatment).
        4. *start_date* on or after *trtsdt* (+ *offset_days*), and, when
           *end_window* is given, on or before *trtedt* + *end_window* days,
           with a missing *trtedt* read as still on treatment: ``"Y"``.
        5. Otherwise: null.

        ``--DTC`` text is read by its date portion.  Pass ``end_date=None``
        when the data hold no event end date; the SAP decides the window.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column (default ``"TRTEMFL"``).
            start_date: Event start date column (``ASTDT``).
            end_date: Event end date column (``AENDT``), or ``None``.
            trtsdt: Treatment start date column.
            trtedt: Treatment end date column; given with *end_window*.
            end_window: Days after *trtedt* in which an event still counts;
                given with *trtedt*.  ``0`` stops at the last dose date.
            offset_days: Days added to *trtsdt* before the start-date
                comparison of case 4 (a Fleet extension; admiral has none).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Raises:
            DerivationError: When only one of *trtedt* and *end_window* is
                given, or *end_window* is negative.

        References:
            admiral ``derive_var_trtemfl`` (pharmaverse), Details. CDISC gives
            no rule for missing dates; check the SAP.

        Examples:
            TEAE up to 30 days after the last dose::

                adae = (
                    ae_raw.adam.occds
                    .treatment_emergent("TRTEMFL", start_date="ASTDT", end_date="AENDT",
                                        trtsdt="TRTSDT", trtedt="TRTEDT", end_window=30)
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        if (trtedt is None) != (end_window is None):
            raise DerivationError(
                f"treatment_emergent('{target}'): give trtedt= and end_window= together "
                "(admiral end_window). end_window=0 stops at the last dose date; without "
                "both, an event after the last dose still counts."
            )
        if end_window is not None and end_window < 0:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"treatment_emergent('{target}'): end_window={end_window} must be 0 or more days."
            )
        schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()

        def day(name: str) -> pl.Expr:
            return to_day(pl.col(name), schema.get(name), verb="treatment_emergent").cast(pl.Date)

        start, trt_start = day(start_date), day(trtsdt)
        ref = trt_start + pl.duration(days=offset_days) if offset_days else trt_start
        in_window = start >= ref
        if trtedt is not None:
            last = day(trtedt) + pl.duration(days=end_window)
            in_window = in_window & (last.is_null() | (start <= last))
        ended_before = day(end_date) < trt_start if end_date is not None else pl.lit(False)
        flag = (
            pl.when(trt_start.is_null())
            .then(None)
            .when(ended_before.fill_null(False))
            .then(None)
            .when(start.is_null())
            .then(pl.lit("Y"))
            .when(in_window)
            .then(pl.lit("Y"))
            .otherwise(None)
        )
        return self._chain(flag.cast(pl.String).alias(target))

    def onset_recovery(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        start_date: str,
        end_date: str,
        ref_date: str,
    ) -> Self:
        """Flag events that started on/after the reference date and have recovered.

        Sets *target* to ``"Y"`` when *start_date* >= *ref_date* and
        *end_date* is not null.  ``--DTC`` text is read by its date portion
        (a partial or blank start gives no flag); a number raises.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            start_date: Event start date column.
            end_date: Event end date column.
            ref_date: Reference date column (e.g. ``"TRTSDT"``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive recovery flag for adverse events::

                adae = (
                    ae_raw.adam.occds
                    .onset_recovery("RCVRYFL", start_date="AESTDTC",
                                    end_date="AEENDTC", ref_date="TRTSDT")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()

        def day(name: str) -> pl.Expr:
            return to_day(pl.col(name), schema.get(name), verb="onset_recovery").cast(pl.Date)

        cond = (day(start_date) >= day(ref_date)) & pl.col(end_date).is_not_null()
        return self._chain(pl.when(cond).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit(None)).alias(target))

flag(
    target,
    *,
    criteria,
    by=None,
    order_by=None,
    value_col=None,
    where=None,
    from_dataset=None,
    on=None,
    source_filter=None,
    condition=None,
    inclusive=True,
    flag_no_ref_groups=True,
    flag_all=False,
    flag_value="Y",
    false_value=None
)

Set target to flag_value for records matching criteria.

Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

  • "first" / "last" — rank-based edge detection within groups.
  • "max" / "min" — value-based extreme within groups.
  • "exists" — set-membership from external dataset(s).
  • "before" / "after" — relative to a landmark condition.
  • "exists_after" / "exists_before" — temporal/self-join flag.

Parameters that are irrelevant to the selected criteria mode raise :class:~fleet.core.exceptions.VerbUsageError instead of being silently ignored. The flag_first / flag_last / flag_extreme / flag_exists / flag_relative wrappers expose each mode with only its own parameters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output flag column.

required criteria str | Expr

A Polars expression, or one of "first", "last", "max", "min", "exists", "before", "after", "exists_after", "exists_before".

required by list[str] | None

Partition columns (default ["USUBJID"]) for "first"/"last", "max"/"min" and "before"/"after". An expression flags each row on its own, so by raises there and in the exists modes.

None order_by str | list[str] | None

Sort column(s) required for "first"/"last" and "before"/"after". On a tie among candidates, "last" takes the last input record and "first" the first (SAS LAST./FIRST.); add a sequence variable to remove the dependence on input order. For "first"/"last" a missing value sorts last in each key, as admiral (ADR-0020): "last" takes a record with a missing key, and "first" takes one only when every candidate misses it. SAS sorts a missing value first, so a QC program with PROC SORT differs on such a group. "exists_after"/"exists_before" take one column only; build one ordered key (ADTM) for date and time.

None value_col str | None

Value column required for "max"/"min".

None where str | Expr | None

Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates; rows that fail it take no part, even on a tie.

None from_dataset DataFrame | list[DataFrame] | None

External dataset(s) for "exists" and "exists_after"/"exists_before" criteria.

None on list[str] | None

Join key columns for "exists" criteria.

None source_filter str | Expr | None

Filter applied to from_dataset before key extraction or join; an expression string is parsed as where is.

None condition str | Expr | None

Boolean expression (or expression string) identifying landmark rows for "before"/"after" or the current-row condition for "exists_after"/"exists_before".

None inclusive bool

Whether the landmark row itself is included in the flag (for "before"/"after"). Default True.

True flag_no_ref_groups bool

If False, groups without a landmark condition match get None instead of being flagged (for "before"/"after"). Default True.

True flag_all bool

If True, all tied extreme values receive the flag (for "first"/"last"). Default False.

False flag_value str

Value to assign when condition is met (default "Y").

'Y' false_value str | None

Value to assign when condition is not met. Default None (null).

None

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target appended; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Raises:

Type Description VerbUsageError

When a parameter irrelevant to the selected criteria mode is passed.

DerivationError

When a mode-required parameter is missing, or a bare-identifier criteria matches neither a keyword nor a column.

References

admiral derive_var_extreme_flag (pharmaverse): the order of "first"/"last", a missing value last in each key (ADR-0020).

Examples:

First observation per group::

advs = (
    vs_raw.adam
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
          by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .to_frame()
)

Existence flag from external dataset::

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl
    .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
          from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
          source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
    .to_frame()
)

Relative flag — before first PD::

result = (
    response.adam
    .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
          condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
          order_by="AVISITN", by=["USUBJID"],
          inclusive=True)
    .to_frame()
)

Population flag from the treatment start date (a population flag is never blank, so non-members get "N")::

adsl = (
    adsl.adam.adsl
    .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null(),
          false_value="N")
    .to_frame()
)

def flag(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    criteria: str | pl.Expr,
    by: list[str] | None = None,
    order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
    value_col: str | None = None,
    where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    from_dataset: pl.DataFrame | list[pl.DataFrame] | None = None,
    on: list[str] | None = None,
    source_filter: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    condition: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    inclusive: bool = True,
    flag_no_ref_groups: bool = True,
    flag_all: bool = False,
    flag_value: str = "Y",
    false_value: str | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Set *target* to *flag_value* for records matching *criteria*.

    Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

    - ``"first"`` / ``"last"`` — rank-based edge detection within groups.
    - ``"max"`` / ``"min"`` — value-based extreme within groups.
    - ``"exists"`` — set-membership from external dataset(s).
    - ``"before"`` / ``"after"`` — relative to a landmark condition.
    - ``"exists_after"`` / ``"exists_before"`` — temporal/self-join flag.

    Parameters that are irrelevant to the selected criteria mode
    raise :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.VerbUsageError` instead of
    being silently ignored.  The ``flag_first`` / ``flag_last`` /
    ``flag_extreme`` / ``flag_exists`` / ``flag_relative`` wrappers
    expose each mode with only its own parameters.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output flag column.
        criteria: A Polars expression, or one of ``"first"``,
            ``"last"``, ``"max"``, ``"min"``, ``"exists"``,
            ``"before"``, ``"after"``, ``"exists_after"``,
            ``"exists_before"``.
        by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``) for
            ``"first"``/``"last"``, ``"max"``/``"min"`` and
            ``"before"``/``"after"``.  An expression flags each row
            on its own, so *by* raises there and in the exists modes.
        order_by: Sort column(s) required for ``"first"``/``"last"``
            and ``"before"``/``"after"``.  On a tie among candidates,
            ``"last"`` takes the last input record and ``"first"`` the
            first (SAS ``LAST.``/``FIRST.``); add a sequence variable
            to remove the dependence on input order.  For
            ``"first"``/``"last"`` a missing value sorts last in each
            key, as admiral (ADR-0020): ``"last"`` takes a record with a
            missing key, and ``"first"`` takes one only when every
            candidate misses it.  SAS sorts a missing value first, so a
            QC program with PROC SORT differs on such a group.
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` take one column
            only; build one ordered key (ADTM) for date and time.
        value_col: Value column required for ``"max"``/``"min"``.
        where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates;
            rows that fail it take no part, even on a tie.
        from_dataset: External dataset(s) for ``"exists"`` and
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` criteria.
        on: Join key columns for ``"exists"`` criteria.
        source_filter: Filter applied to *from_dataset* before key
            extraction or join; an expression string is parsed as
            *where* is.
        condition: Boolean expression (or expression string) identifying landmark rows for
            ``"before"``/``"after"`` or the current-row condition for
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"``.
        inclusive: Whether the landmark row itself is included in the
            flag (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_no_ref_groups: If ``False``, groups without a landmark
            condition match get ``None`` instead of being flagged
            (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_all: If ``True``, all tied extreme values receive the
            flag (for ``"first"``/``"last"``). Default ``False``.
        flag_value: Value to assign when condition is met (default
            ``"Y"``).
        false_value: Value to assign when condition is not met.
            Default ``None`` (null).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        VerbUsageError: When a parameter irrelevant to the selected
            criteria mode is passed.
        DerivationError: When a mode-required parameter is missing,
            or a bare-identifier *criteria* matches neither a
            keyword nor a column.

    References:
        admiral ``derive_var_extreme_flag`` (pharmaverse): the order of
        ``"first"``/``"last"``, a missing value last in each key (ADR-0020).

    Examples:
        First observation per group::

            advs = (
                vs_raw.adam
                .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
                      by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Existence flag from external dataset::

            adsl = (
                dm.adam.adsl
                .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
                      from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
                      source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Relative flag — before first PD::

            result = (
                response.adam
                .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
                      condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
                      order_by="AVISITN", by=["USUBJID"],
                      inclusive=True)
                .to_frame()
            )

        Population flag from the treatment start date (a population
        flag is never blank, so non-members get ``"N"``)::

            adsl = (
                adsl.adam.adsl
                .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null(),
                      false_value="N")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    grps = by or ["USUBJID"]
    order_cols: list[str] | None = None
    if order_by is not None:
        order_cols = [order_by] if isinstance(order_by, str) else list(order_by)

    criteria_lower = criteria.lower() if isinstance(criteria, str) else None
    mode = criteria_lower if criteria_lower in _FLAG_CRITERIA_KEYWORDS else "expression"
    if mode == "expression":
        # Keyword typos ("frist") must surface as a did-you-mean error
        # before any parameter validation blames the wrong thing.
        self._check_flag_criteria_typo(target, criteria)
    self._validate_flag_params(
        target,
        criteria,
        mode,
        {
            "by": by,
            "order_by": order_by,
            "value_col": value_col,
            "where": where,
            "from_dataset": from_dataset,
            "on": on,
            "source_filter": source_filter,
            "condition": condition,
            "inclusive": inclusive,
            "flag_no_ref_groups": flag_no_ref_groups,
            "flag_all": flag_all,
            "false_value": false_value,
        },
    )

    where_expr: pl.Expr | None = None
    if where is not None:
        where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))
    # A string condition or source filter is parsed as where= is.
    if isinstance(condition, str):
        condition = parse_expression(condition, self._lazy.collect_schema())
    if isinstance(source_filter, str):
        source_filter = parse_expression(source_filter)

    false_lit = pl.lit(false_value) if false_value is not None else pl.lit(None)

    if mode in ("first", "last"):
        return self._flag_ranked(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_all=flag_all,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode in ("max", "min"):
        return self._flag_extreme(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            value_col=value_col,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode == "exists":
        return self._flag_exists(
            target,
            grps=grps,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode in ("before", "after"):
        return self._flag_relative(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            inclusive=inclusive,
            flag_no_ref_groups=flag_no_ref_groups,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )
    elif mode in ("exists_after", "exists_before"):
        return self._flag_temporal_exists(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
        )
    else:
        return self._flag_expression(
            target,
            criteria=criteria,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )

criterion(number, *, condition, description)

Derive criterion flag triple: CRITy, CRITyFL, CRITyFN.

Produces three columns following CDISC ADaM conventions:

  • CRIT{number} — the criterion description (constant string).
  • CRIT{number}FL — "Y" if condition is met, "N" if not.
  • CRIT{number}FN — 1 if met, 0 if not.

When the condition is null (for example AVAL is missing), FL and FN are null, as admiral derive_vars_crit_flag(). For a SAP rule "missing is not met", pass condition=(...).fill_null(False).

References

admiral derive_vars_crit_flag(values_yn = TRUE, create_numeric_flag = TRUE), which asserts a positive crit_nr and a description; ADaMIG 1.3 CRITy (text, y a positive integer); ADR-0033.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default number int

Criterion number, 1 or more (e.g. 1 → CRIT1, CRIT1FL, CRIT1FN).

required condition str | Expr

Boolean Polars expression defining the criterion, or an expression string as for where=.

required description str

Human-readable description stored in CRITy.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with three new columns appended; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Raises:

Type Description VerbUsageError

When number is below 1 or description is blank.

Examples:

Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

adlb = (
    lb_df.adam
    .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,
               description="AVAL >= 10")
    .to_frame()
)
Source code in src/fleet/core/_flag_mixin.py 
def criterion(
    self,
    number: int,
    *,
    condition: str | pl.Expr,
    description: str,
) -> Self:
    """Derive criterion flag triple: CRITy, CRITyFL, CRITyFN.

    Produces three columns following CDISC ADaM conventions:

    - ``CRIT{number}`` — the criterion description (constant string).
    - ``CRIT{number}FL`` — ``"Y"`` if condition is met, ``"N"`` if not.
    - ``CRIT{number}FN`` — ``1`` if met, ``0`` if not.

    When the condition is null (for example AVAL is missing), FL and FN are
    null, as admiral ``derive_vars_crit_flag()``. For a SAP rule "missing is
    not met", pass ``condition=(...).fill_null(False)``.

    References:
        admiral ``derive_vars_crit_flag(values_yn = TRUE,
        create_numeric_flag = TRUE)``, which asserts a positive
        ``crit_nr`` and a description; ADaMIG 1.3 CRITy (text, y a
        positive integer); ADR-0033.

    Args:
        number: Criterion number, 1 or more (e.g. 1 → CRIT1, CRIT1FL,
            CRIT1FN).
        condition: Boolean Polars expression defining the criterion, or
            an expression string as for ``where=``.
        description: Human-readable description stored in CRITy.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with three new columns appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        VerbUsageError: When *number* is below 1 or *description* is
            blank.

    Examples:
        Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

            adlb = (
                lb_df.adam
                .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,
                           description="AVAL >= 10")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, int) or number < 1:
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"criterion({number!r}): the criterion number is a positive integer "
            "(ADaMIG CRITy), for example criterion(1, ...)."
        )
    if not isinstance(description, str) or not description.strip():
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"criterion({number}): description= is required; CRIT{number} holds it."
        )
    if isinstance(condition, str):
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        condition = parse_expression(condition, self._lazy.collect_schema())
    col_crit = f"CRIT{number}"
    col_fl = f"CRIT{number}FL"
    col_fn = f"CRIT{number}FN"

    desc_expr = pl.lit(description).alias(col_crit)
    fl_expr = (
        pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit("Y")).when(~condition).then(pl.lit("N")).alias(col_fl)
    )
    fn_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit(1)).when(~condition).then(pl.lit(0)).alias(col_fn)

    return self._chain(desc_expr, fl_expr, fn_expr, verb="criterion")

Examples:

Pin DM to an AE pipeline for study-day derivation::

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .pin("DM", dm_df)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")

Declare every upstream dataset of an ADaM pipeline at once::

adae = (
    ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
    .pin(ADSL=adsl_df, EX=ex_df)

def pin(
    self,
    domain: str | None = None,
    df: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
    **frames: pl.DataFrame,
) -> Self:
    """Attach one or more reference domains to this pipeline.

    Two equivalent forms, usable together — the keyword form declares
    every upstream dataset in one call (kwarg name = dataset name),
    mirroring the define.yaml ``inputs:`` block:

    * ``pin("DM", dm_df)`` — one pin, positional.
    * ``pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df)`` — several pins, one call.

    The name/frame pair is positional-only, so *every* keyword except
    ``join_on`` is a dataset pin — no dataset name is reserved.

    Args:
        domain: Logical name (e.g. ``"DM"``, ``"ADSL"``, ``"TV"``).
        df: The reference DataFrame for *domain*.  A LazyFrame is
            collected once, at pin time.
        join_on: Column(s) used to join these references into the
            pipeline.  Applies to every pin in this call; pin
            separately for per-domain join keys.
        **frames: ``NAME=frame`` pins (names are upper-cased).

    Returns:
        Self: A shallow copy with the pin(s) attached; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When called with no pins, a name without its
            frame (or vice versa), or a pinned value that is not a
            DataFrame/LazyFrame.

    Examples:
        Pin DM to an AE pipeline for study-day derivation::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
                .pin("DM", dm_df)
                .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Declare every upstream dataset of an ADaM pipeline at once::

            adae = (
                ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
                .pin(ADSL=adsl_df, EX=ex_df)
                .join_adsl("TRTSDT", "SAFFL")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    pins: dict[str, pl.DataFrame] = {}
    if domain is not None or df is not None:
        if domain is None or df is None:
            raise DerivationError(
                "pin() requires both a domain name and a DataFrame — "
                'pin("DM", dm_df) — or keyword pins: pin(DM=dm_df).'
            )
        pins[domain] = df
    pins.update(frames)
    if not pins:
        raise DerivationError(
            'pin() requires at least one pin: pin("DM", dm_df) or pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df).'
        )

    new = copy.copy(self)
    pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = dict(getattr(self, "_pinned", {}))
    for name, frame in pins.items():
        frame = _pin_frame(name, frame)
        key = name.upper()
        if key in pinned:
            warnings.warn(
                f"Pin '{key}' replaced. Use .repin() to suppress this warning.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        pinned[key] = (frame, _normalize_key(join_on))
    new._pinned = pinned
    return new

def fk_policy(self, severity: str) -> Self:
    """Set the FK-check severity for this pipeline.

    The check runs once, at the public ``to_frame()`` (and the
    terminal verbs that call it), on the final frame, with the
    severity in force at that point.  The order of ``pin``,
    ``fk_policy`` and the verbs does not matter.  It checks
    ``USUBJID`` against the pinned ``DM`` (SDTM) or ``ADSL`` (ADaM),
    and the SDTM trial-design keys of ``_FK_RULES`` against a pinned
    TA, TE or TV.

    Args:
        severity: One of ``"warn"`` (emit ``UserWarning``),
            ``"error"`` (raise ``DerivationError``), or ``"off"``
            (disable FK checks).

    Returns:
        Self: A shallow copy with the updated policy.

    Examples:
        Enforce strict FK checking::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .pin("DM", dm_df)
                .fk_policy("error")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if severity not in ("warn", "error", "off"):
        raise DerivationError(
            f"fk_policy severity must be 'warn', 'error', or 'off', got '{severity}'"
        )
    new = copy.copy(self)
    new._fk_severity = severity
    return new

def to_frame(self) -> DataFrame:
    """Materialise the accumulated pipeline into a Polars DataFrame.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: The fully materialised result of all chained
            verbs — a plain ``pl.DataFrame`` at runtime, typed as
            :class:`fleet.DataFrame` so re-entering ``.sdtm`` /
            ``.adam`` / ``.tlg`` type-checks.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When collection fails because a column is
            missing — enriched with the lineage entries that
            reference the column, so the error names the verb(s)
            involved.  Also when a ``merge(validate=...)`` fails, with
            the repeated keys named, or when a foreign-key check runs
            under ``fk_policy("error")``.

    Examples:
        Collect the pipeline result::

            result = (
                df.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    try:
        df = self._lazy.collect()
    except (
        pl.exceptions.ColumnNotFoundError,
        pl.exceptions.SchemaFieldNotFoundError,
        pl.exceptions.StructFieldNotFoundError,
    ) as err:
        raise self._enrich_collect_error(err) from err
    except pl.exceptions.ComputeError as err:
        named = next(
            (
                msg
                for check in getattr(self, "_pending_join_checks", [])
                if (msg := check.explain_validation()) is not None
            ),
            None,
        )
        if named is None:
            raise self._polars_error(err) from err
        raise DerivationError(named) from err
    except pl.exceptions.PolarsError as err:
        raise self._polars_error(err) from err
    run_checks = getattr(self, "_run_fk_checks", None)
    if run_checks is not None and not _is_internal_collect():
        run_checks(df)
    join_checks = getattr(self, "_pending_join_checks", [])
    # Rebind, never mutate: earlier chain copies keep their own queue.
    self._pending_join_checks = []
    for check in join_checks:
        check.warn_many_to_many()
    return cast("DataFrame", df)

    label: str | None = None,

    """Materialise the pipeline and write a CDISC Dataset-JSON v1.1 file.

    This is a terminal verb — it collects the lazy plan and writes the
    result.  No further chaining is possible after this call.  After
    :meth:`from_spec` on a define.yaml, the file gets the define labels,
    lengths, key sequence and OIDs of the dataset.

    Args:
        path: Destination file path (should end in ``.json``).
        domain: Dataset / domain name (e.g. ``"DM"``, ``"ADSL"``).
        label: Optional human-readable dataset label; it wins over
            the define label.

    Returns:
        Path: Path to the written file.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When a foreign-key check fails under
            ``fk_policy("error")``; no file is written.

    Examples:
        Export a dataset to Dataset-JSON::

            path = (
                df.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .to_dataset_json("outputs/dm.json", domain="DM")
            )
    """
    from fleet.io.dataset_json import metadata_from_define, save_dataset_json

    meta: dict[str, Any] = {}
    source = getattr(self, "_spec_source", None)
    if source is not None and source[1].upper() == domain.upper():
        meta = metadata_from_define(source[0], source[1])
    if label is not None:
        meta["label"] = label
    return save_dataset_json(self.to_frame(), path, domain=domain, **meta)

trail()

Log a table of each derived variable's origin in the pipeline.

Renders the accumulated variable lineage — the verb that produced each column and the source columns it consumed, including cross-domain pin sources — as a table through the "fleet" logger (INFO level, stdout by default — see :mod:fleet.core.log), then returns the namespace unchanged so the chain continues. Unlike inspect, nothing is materialised: the trail is pure metadata captured automatically on every verb call.

Only derived variables appear; columns that pass through untouched from the source frame are not listed. When a variable is derived more than once, each derivation is shown in pipeline order. Variables with no source column (e.g. hardcoded constants) are marked (literal).

Examples:

Print the origin of every derived variable before collecting::

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .trail()
    .to_frame()
)

def trail(self) -> Self:
    """Log a table of each derived variable's origin in the pipeline.

    Renders the accumulated variable lineage — the verb that produced
    each column and the source columns it consumed, including
    cross-domain pin sources — as a table through the ``"fleet"``
    logger (INFO level, stdout by default — see
    :mod:`fleet.core.log`), then returns the namespace unchanged so
    the chain continues. Unlike ``inspect``, nothing is
    materialised: the trail is pure metadata captured automatically on
    every verb call.

    Only *derived* variables appear; columns that pass through untouched
    from the source frame are not listed. When a variable is derived more
    than once, each derivation is shown in pipeline order. Variables with
    no source column (e.g. hardcoded constants) are marked ``(literal)``.

    Returns:
        Self: The same namespace instance (unchanged); call further
            verbs or ``.to_frame()`` to continue.

    Examples:
        Print the origin of every derived variable before collecting::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
                .pin("DM", dm)
                .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                .trail()
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core.lineage import lineage_of, pin_lineage_of

    fleet_log.ensure_default_handler()
    nodes = lineage_of(self)
    # A pin read that made no lineage node (join_adsl) still gets its own row.
    named = {node.name for node in nodes}
    nodeless = [dep for dep in pin_lineage_of(self) if dep.target_col not in named]
    if not nodes and not nodeless:
        logger.info("Variable trail: (empty — no derivations recorded yet)")
        return self

    def _label(dep: Any) -> str:
        cols = ", ".join(dep.source_cols) if dep.source_cols else "*"
        label = f"{dep.source_domain}.{cols}"
        if dep.relationship != "derivation":
            label += f" [{dep.relationship}]"
        return label

    entries: list[tuple[str, str, list[str], str | None]] = []
    for node in nodes:
        # Drop bare local sources already attributed to a pinned domain.
        covered = {col for dep in node.pin_sources for col in dep.source_cols}
        local = [src for src in node.sources if src not in covered]
        labels = [_label(dep) for dep in node.pin_sources]
        entries.append((node.name, node.verb, [*local, *labels], node.domain))
    for dep in nodeless:
        entries.append((dep.target_col, dep.verb, [_label(dep)], dep.target_domain))
    has_domain = any(entry[3] for entry in entries)
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for i, (name, verb, origins, domain) in enumerate(entries, start=1):
        shown = list(dict.fromkeys(origins))
        row: dict[str, object] = {
            "#": i,
            "Variable": name,
            "Verb": verb,
            "Origin": ", ".join(shown) if shown else "(literal)",
        }
        if has_domain:
            row["Domain"] = domain or "—"
        rows.append(row)

    table = pl.DataFrame(rows)
    logger.info("Variable trail (%d derivation(s)):", table.height)
    with pl.Config(
        tbl_hide_dataframe_shape=True,
        tbl_hide_column_data_types=True,
        fmt_str_lengths=100,
        tbl_rows=table.height,
    ):
        logger.info("%s", table)
    return self

def write_parquet(
    self,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    mkdir: bool = True,
) -> DataFrame:
    """Materialise the pipeline, write to Parquet, and return the DataFrame.

    This is a drop-in alternative to ``to_frame()`` when you want to
    persist the dataset as part of the chain.

    Args:
        path: Destination file path.
        mkdir: When ``True`` (default) any missing parent directories
            are created automatically.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: The materialised result (typed as
            :class:`fleet.DataFrame` — see ``to_frame()``).

    Examples:
        Write a domain to Parquet::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                .write_parquet("outputs/dm.parquet")
            )
    """
    df = self.to_frame()
    dest = Path(path)
    if mkdir:
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    df.write_parquet(dest)
    return df

    """
    if len(columns) == 1 and isinstance(columns[0], list):
        cols: list[str] = list(columns[0])
    else:
        cols = [c for c in columns]  # type: ignore[misc]
    if not cols:
        raise DerivationError("keep() requires at least one column name.")
    require_columns("keep()", cols, self._lazy.collect_schema().names(), where="the frame")
    return self._with_lazy(self._lazy.select(cols))

def derivation(
    self,
    target: str | Derivation | None = None,
    *,
    expression: str | pl.Expr | Callable[[], pl.Expr] | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Derive *target* using an expression, lambda, or ``Derivation`` object.

    Four call forms are supported:

    **Case 1 — string (checked against an allow-list, YAML-compatible)**::

        .derivation("COL", expression="pl.col('src').cast(pl.String)")

    **Case 2 — direct ``pl.Expr``**::

        .derivation("COL", expression=pl.col("src").cast(pl.String))

    **Case 3 — zero-arg lambda returning ``pl.Expr`` (full IDE support)**::

        .derivation("COL", expression=lambda: pl.col("src").cast(pl.Int32))

    **Case 4 — ``@derivation`` object (file-based, full lineage)**::

        from specs.study01.derivations import MY_DRULE
        .derivation(MY_DRULE)

    Args:
        target: For Cases 1–3, the name of the output variable
            (required).  For Case 4, the
            :class:`~fleet.core.derivation.Derivation` object to dispatch.
        expression: A Polars expression, expression string, or zero-arg
            callable returning ``pl.Expr``.  Required for Cases 1–3.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call ``.to_frame()``
            to materialise.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: If *target* is a string but *expression* is not
            provided, or vice-versa.
        VerbUsageError: If *target* is neither a string nor a
            ``Derivation``, if *expression* is a frame-kind
            ``Derivation``, or if a lambda-style *expression* does not
            return ``pl.Expr``.

    Examples:
        Case 1 — string expression::

            result = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .derivation("SITEID", expression="pl.col('site_id').cast(pl.String)")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Case 3 — lambda::

            result = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .derivation("VISITNUM", expression=lambda: pl.col("visit").cast(pl.Int32))
                .to_frame()
            )

        Case 4 — ``@derivation`` object::

            from specs.study01.derivations import MY_DRULE

            result = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .derivation(MY_DRULE)
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core.derivation import Derivation
    from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    # Case 4: Derivation object passed as first positional arg.
    if target is not None and not isinstance(target, str):
        if not isinstance(target, Derivation):
            raise VerbUsageError(
                f"derivation() takes a target name with expression= (a string, a "
                f"pl.Expr or a zero-argument lambda) or a @derivation object, got "
                f"{type(target).__name__}."
            )
        return self._apply_derivation(target)

    # Cases 1–3 require a string target.
    if target is None:
        raise DerivationError("target is required when expression= is provided.")
    if expression is None:
        raise DerivationError("expression is required when target is a string.")
    if isinstance(expression, Derivation) and expression.kind != "column":
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"derivation('{target}'): expression= takes a column derivation, but "
            f"'{expression.name}' is kind={expression.kind!r}. Pass it alone: "
            f".derivation({expression.name})."
        )

    params = {"target": target, "expression": expression}

    # Case 2: direct pl.Expr.
    if isinstance(expression, pl.Expr):
        return self._chain(expression.alias(target), verb="derivation", params=params)

    # Case 3: lambda / zero-arg callable.
    if callable(expression) and not isinstance(expression, str):
        expr = expression()
        if not isinstance(expr, pl.Expr):
            raise VerbUsageError(
                f"expression callable must return pl.Expr, got {type(expr).__name__}"
            )
        return self._chain(expr.alias(target), verb="derivation", params=params)

    # Case 1: string checked against an allow-list.
    return self._chain(
        parse_expression(str(expression), self._lazy.collect_schema()).alias(target),
        verb="derivation",
        params=params,
    )

duration(
    target,
    *,
    start,
    end,
    unit="days",
    add_one=None,
    out="numeric"
)

Compute the duration between two date/datetime columns.

Supports column references (str) and Polars expressions for start and end; an expression is read by its type, as a column is. --DTC text is read by its date part for day-based units and by its date-time for hours, minutes and seconds; a partial value gives null, and for hours, minutes and seconds a warning gives the count of text values with no time.

The add_one parameter controls inclusive counting:

  • None (default): auto-resolves from the target suffix and the unit. *DY targets in days use the CDISC study-day convention (no day 0). Days, weeks, months and years add one day before the division; hours, minutes and seconds give the raw difference (PK elapsed time).
  • True: add one day (day-based units) or one unit (sub-day).
  • False: raw difference.

One is added only when the end is on or after the start, as admiral compute_duration does: an end one day before the start gives -1, never 0. Weeks, months and years divide the day count by 7, 30.4375 and 365.25, so this verb does not give a completed age in years.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output column.

required start str | Expr

Start date column name or expression.

required end str | Expr

End date column name or expression.

required unit Literal['seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', 'days', 'weeks', 'months', 'years']

Duration unit — "seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days" (default), "weeks", "months", "years".

'days' add_one bool | None

Override for inclusive counting.

None out Literal['numeric', 'iso8601']

Output format — "numeric" (default) or "iso8601". "iso8601" keeps the sign (-PT15M), writes hours, minutes and seconds from the total (PT1H30M) and adds one only when add_one=True is given (an elapsed time, P9D for 1 to 10 January). Weeks give null with a warning for a span that is not whole weeks; months and years raise. "iso8601" is incompatible with the *DY study-day convention: pass add_one explicitly (or use a non-DY target) to combine them.

'numeric'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target appended; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

On an unknown unit/out value, when out="iso8601" is combined with a *DY target while add_one is unset (the study-day convention would silently override the requested format), with months or years, or when a column holds numbers (no date origin is guessed).

References

ISO 8601 durations and SDTMIG 3.4 --ELTM; admiral compute_duration; ADR-0011 and ADR-0022.

Examples:

ISO 8601 duration::

ex = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .date("EXSTDTC", source="dose_start")
    .date("EXENDTC", source="dose_end")
    .duration("EXDUR", start="EXSTDTC", end="EXENDTC",
              out="iso8601")
    .to_frame()
)

Treatment duration in days::

adsl = (
    dm_df.adam.adsl
    .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")
    .to_frame()
)
