Immutable pipeline builder for SDTM derivations.

Each verb adds one step to the plan of one LazyFrame; to_frame() collects the plan once. Accepts both pl.DataFrame and pl.LazyFrame inputs, so scanned sources stay lazy end-to-end.

Source code in src/fleet/sdtm/namespace.py 
@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("sdtm")
@pl.api.register_lazyframe_namespace("sdtm")
class SDTMNamespace(SharedVerbsMixin, PinMixin, FlagCriterionMixin, TrialDesignMixin):
    """
    Immutable pipeline builder for SDTM derivations.

    Each verb adds one step to the plan of one LazyFrame; `to_frame()`
    collects the plan once.  Accepts both ``pl.DataFrame``
    and ``pl.LazyFrame`` inputs, so scanned sources stay lazy end-to-end.
    """

    # -- SharedVerbsMixin configuration --
    _STUDY_DAY_REF_COL: str = "RFSTDTC"
    _STUDY_DAY_REF_PIN: str = "DM"
    _SEQ_DEFAULT_GROUPS: list[str] = ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"]

    _FK_RULES: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {
        "USUBJID": {"pin": "DM", "ref_col": "USUBJID"},
        # TV holds planned visits only, so an unscheduled visit is never an error.
        "VISITNUM": {
            "pin": "TV",
            "ref_col": "VISITNUM",
            "max_severity": "warn",
            "note": "TV holds planned visits only",
        },
        "VISIT": {
            "pin": "TV",
            "ref_col": "VISIT",
            "max_severity": "warn",
            "note": "TV holds planned visits only",
        },
        "EPOCH": {"pin": "TA", "ref_col": "EPOCH"},
        "ETCD": {"pin": "TE", "ref_col": "ETCD", "allow": "UNPLAN"},
    }

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame | pl.LazyFrame) -> None:
        self._lazy = df.lazy()
        self._root_lazy = self._lazy  # the start of the chain, for to_spec_yaml()
        self._nsv_meta: list[NSVMeta] = []
        self._domain: str | None = None
        self._pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = {}
        self._pin_lineage: list = []
        self._pending_fk_checks: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # assign / case_when are inherited from SharedVerbsMixin.             #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 3. date — unified date verb                                          #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def date(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        source: str | None = None,
        value: str | None = None,
        output: str | None = None,
        time: str | None = None,
        impute: str = "first",
        impute_time: str | None = None,
        highest: str | None = None,
        flag: bool | str = True,
        min_date: str | None = None,
        max_date: str | None = None,
        format: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Parse, convert, impute, and flag a date or datetime column.

        For a DT or DTM target, a partial date is imputed to the first day
        or month by default (ADR-0021).  Give ``highest="n"`` for no
        imputation, as the admiral ``derive_vars_dt`` default.

        Dispatches behavior based on the CDISC suffix of *target* (DTC, DT,
        DTM) or an explicit *output* override.

        For DTC targets: converts raw text to ISO 8601 and never guesses.
        A valid ISO 8601 value stays as it is, partial dates included
        (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4).  ``YYYYMMDD``, ``DD-MON-YYYY``,
        ``DD MON YYYY`` and ``DDMONYYYY`` convert with no *format*.  A slash
        date or a two-digit year raises until *format* names the layout.
        Any other value becomes null, with one warning at collect that
        gives the count and the first values.  With *time*, a blank time
        leaves the date alone, a partial date takes a hyphen for each
        missing component (``2021-03--T08:30``), and a time with no date
        gives ``-----T08:30`` (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4.2).  Imputation
        parameters are ignored.

        For DT/DTM targets: delegates to the imputation engine that
        ``.adam.date()`` uses, so both give the same result.  A
        ``pl.Date`` or ``pl.Datetime`` source is read as its ISO 8601 text;
        a number raises, because Fleet does not guess its origin.  With
        *time*, the date and the time first become one ``--DTC`` value
        (``2021-03--T08:30`` for a partial date), which then takes the
        imputation and *highest* (ADR-0045).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column.
            source: Column name to read values from.  Mutually exclusive
                with *value*.
            value: Literal date value to broadcast.  Mutually exclusive
                with *source*.
            output: Explicit output type: ``"dtc"``, ``"dt"``, or ``"dtm"``.
            time: Time column or literal to combine with date (DTM/DTC).
            impute: Imputation strategy (DT/DTM only).
            impute_time: Time-part imputation override (DTM only).
            highest: Imputation ceiling, as admiral ``highest_imputation``:
                ``"n"``, ``"D"`` or ``"M"``, and on a DTM target also
                ``"h"``, ``"m"`` and ``"s"``.  ``"Y"`` raises.
            flag: DTF/TMF flag control.
            min_date: Lower bound for an imputed date.  Applies only when
                the bound is inside the possible range of the partial value;
                a complete date never changes.  DT targets only.
            max_date: Upper bound for an imputed date, with the same rule.
            format: ``strptime`` layout of the raw text (DTC only), e.g.
                ``"%m/%d/%Y"``.  Use ``%y`` for a two-digit year: it reads
                00-69 as 20xx and 70-99 as 19xx.

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        References:
            SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4; admiral 1.4.1 ``derive_vars_dt`` and
            ``derive_vars_dtm``; ADR-0021; ADR-0045.

        Examples:
            Parse raw date to ISO 8601 DTC::

                ae = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .date("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Custom input format::

                ae = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .date("AEENDTC", source="ae_end_date",
                          format="%d/%m/%Y")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from fleet.adam.utils import (
            _resolve_output_type,
            dtm_source_text,
            impute_and_flag,
            source_text,
        )

        # Validate source / value mutual exclusivity
        if source is not None and value is not None:
            raise DerivationError("Cannot specify both source= and value=. Choose one.")
        if source is None and value is None:
            raise DerivationError("Must specify either source= or value=.")

        output_type = _resolve_output_type(target, output)

        # value= path
        if value is not None:
            if flag is True:
                flag = False
            exprs = impute_and_flag(None, target, value=value, output_type=output_type, flag=flag)
            return self._chain(*exprs, verb="date")

        # source= path
        assert source is not None

        if output_type == "dtc":
            return self._dtc(target, source, time=time, format=format)

        # DT/DTM: delegate to imputation engine
        if time is not None and output_type != "dtm":
            raise DerivationError(
                f"time= parameter is only valid for DTM targets, "
                f"but target '{target}' resolves to output='{output_type}'."
            )
        schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()
        if time is not None:
            src = dtm_source_text(
                schema, source=source, target=target, time=time, input_format=format
            )
        else:
            src = source_text(source, schema.get(source), verb=f"date('{target}')")
        exprs = impute_and_flag(
            src,
            target,
            output_type=output_type,
            impute=impute,
            impute_time=impute_time,
            highest=highest,
            min_date=min_date,
            max_date=max_date,
            flag=flag,
        )
        return self._chain(*exprs, verb="date")

    def _dtc(self, target: str, source: str, *, time: str | None, format: str | None) -> Self:
        """``--DTC`` text from raw text: ISO 8601 or null, never a guess, with warnings."""
        raw = pl.col(source)
        guessed = guessed_values(raw, input_format=format).fill_null(False)
        sample = (
            self._lazy.select(raw.cast(pl.String).filter(guessed).unique(maintain_order=True))
            .head(3)
            .collect()
            .to_series()
            .to_list()
        )
        if sample and format is None:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"date('{target}'): {source} needs a guess to become a date (the order of day "
                "and month, or the century of a two-digit year). Name the layout with "
                "format='%m/%d/%Y' (month first) or format='%d/%m/%Y' (day first); for a "
                "two-digit year use %y, which reads 00-69 as 20xx and 70-99 as 19xx. "
                f"Values: {sample}"
            )
        if sample:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"date('{target}', format='{format}'): {source} gives a year before 1000 with "
                f"this layout, so the year has two digits: use %y in place of %Y. Values: {sample}"
            )

        text = dtc_text(raw, input_format=format)
        given = raw.cast(pl.String).str.strip_chars().fill_null("") != ""
        value = warn_on_collect(
            text,
            given & text.is_null(),
            lambda n, values: (
                f"date('{target}'): {n} value(s) of {source} are not ISO 8601 and could not be "
                f"converted, so {target} is null for them (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4.1). Name the "
                f"layout with format=. Values: {values}"
            ),
            dtype=pl.String,
            shown=raw.cast(pl.String),
        )
        if time is not None:
            raw_time = pl.lit(time) if TIME_LITERAL.match(time) else pl.col(time)
            value = warn_on_collect(
                dtc_with_time(value, raw, raw_time),
                bad_time(raw_time),
                lambda n, values: (
                    f"date('{target}'): {n} time value(s) of {time} are not hh:mm[:ss], so "
                    f"{target} keeps the date only. Values: {values}"
                ),
                dtype=pl.String,
                shown=raw_time.cast(pl.String),
            )
        return self._chain(value.alias(target), verb="date")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 5b. nsv — Non-Standard Variable (qualifier) derivation               #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def nsv(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        source: str | None = None,
        value: Any | None = None,
        label: str,
        origin: str = "Derived",
        evaluator: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive a Non-Standard Variable with qualifier metadata.

        Behaves like ``assign(source=...)`` (when *source* is given) or
        ``assign(value=...)`` (when *value* is given) but additionally
        registers SUPPQUAL metadata (label, origin, evaluator) on the
        pipeline.  Use ``export_supp()`` to produce the vertical SUPPQUAL
        structure for SDTM IG ≤3.4.  For a future IG that keeps NSVs in
        the parent domain, ``to_frame()`` keeps them unchanged.

        Args:
            target: Name of the qualifier variable (becomes QNAM in SUPP).
            source: Name of the raw column to copy from.  Mutually
                exclusive with *value*.
            value: A literal value to broadcast.  Mutually exclusive with
                *source*.
            label: Human-readable label (becomes QLABEL in SUPP).
            origin: Variable origin (becomes QORIG in SUPP) — the
                Define-XML 2.1 vocabulary shared with ``origin:`` in a
                define.yaml (``Collected``, ``Derived``, ``Assigned``,
                ``Protocol``, ``Predecessor``).
            evaluator: Optional evaluator (becomes QEVAL in SUPP).

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Derive population flag NSVs for DM::

                dm = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                    .nsv("SAFETY", source="safety_flag",
                         label="Safety Population Flag")
                    .nsv("ITT", source="itt_flag",
                         label="Intent to Treat Population Flag")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        if source is None and value is None:
            raise DerivationError("nsv() requires either 'source' or 'value'.")
        if source is not None and value is not None:
            raise DerivationError("nsv() accepts 'source' or 'value', not both.")
        if not str(label or "").strip():
            raise DerivationError(
                f"nsv('{target}'): missing label. QLABEL is required in SUPP-- (SDTMIG 8.4); "
                "give label= (label: on the define.yaml variable)."
            )

        expr = pl.col(source).alias(target) if source else pl.lit(value).alias(target)
        new = self._chain(expr, verb="nsv")
        # Copy-on-write: avoid mutating shared list across copies
        new._nsv_meta = [
            *self._nsv_meta,
            NSVMeta(target=target, label=label, origin=origin, evaluator=evaluator),
        ]
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 5c. study_day is inherited from SharedVerbsMixin (one shared        #
    # implementation; `dm=` / `adsl=` are documented ref_df aliases).     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 5d. baseline_flag — last pre-reference-date observation flag        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def baseline_flag(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        date_col: str,
        testcd_col: str | None,
        ref_col: str,
        ref_pin: str = "DM",
        dm: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        by: list[str] | None = None,
        result_col: str | None = None,
        order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Flag the last observation with a result before the reference date as baseline.

        Sets *target* to ``"Y"`` for one record (per subject and optional
        grouping variables): the last record with a result strictly before
        the reference date/time, and ``null`` for all other records.  A
        record on the reference date is eligible only when it and the
        reference both have a time and the record time is earlier; a record
        on that date with no time is not eligible, because it may follow
        the dose (SDTMIG "prior to"; sdtm.oak ``derive_blfl``).  Among
        eligible records the latest date, then the latest time, wins.

        A record has a result when *result_col* is not null or blank and
        ``--STAT`` (when present) is not ``"NOT DONE"``.  When ``--ORRES`` is
        present and is not *result_col*, it must hold a value too, unless
        ``--DRVFL`` is ``"Y"`` (CG0553).  A tie on the last date and time
        goes to the last record by *order_by*, then input order, as SAS
        ``LAST.`` after PROC SORT; with no *order_by* the tie is broken by
        ``--SEQ`` (when present) and a warning names the groups.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag variable
                (e.g. ``"VSBLFL"``).
            date_col: Column containing the observation date
                (e.g. ``"VSDTC"``).
            testcd_col: Test code column to group by (e.g.
                ``"VSTESTCD"``), so each test gets its own flag.  Required:
                pass ``None`` only when the frame holds one test.
            ref_col: Reference date column, in the frame or in the pinned
                DM.  Required, so the call shows the reference: SDTMIG 3.4
                ``--LOBXFL`` uses ``"RFXSTDTC"``; a sponsor ``--BLFL``
                often uses ``"RFSTDTC"``.
            ref_pin: Pinned domain for the reference date
                (default ``"DM"``).
            dm: Optional explicit DataFrame override.
            by: Additional grouping columns beyond USUBJID and
                *testcd_col*, such as ``--CAT``, ``--SCAT``, ``--SPEC`` and
                ``--METHOD``.
            result_col: Result column (default ``--STRESC`` when present,
                else ``--ORRES``; the prefix comes from *target*).
            order_by: Column(s) that break a tie on the last date and time
                (default ``--SEQ`` when present).

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Raises:
            DerivationError: When no result column is found or named.

        References:
            SDTMIG 3.4, ``--LOBXFL``: the last non-missing value prior to
            RFXSTDTC; CDISC CORE FB2603/FB2604 (one flag per group);
            admiral ``ad_advs.R`` order (ADT, VISITNUM, VSSEQ); sdtm.oak
            ``derive_blfl`` (no default for ``ref_var``);
            ``docs/adr/0051-baseline-flag-names-its-reference-and-test-code.md``.

        Examples:
            Flag the last value before first exposure::

                vs = (
                    vs_raw.sdtm
                    .assign("DOMAIN", value="VS")
                    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                    .assign("VSTESTCD", source="vstestcd")
                    .assign("VSORRES", source="vsresult")
                    .date("VSDTC", source="vs_date")
                    .pin("DM", dm_df)
                    .baseline_flag("VSLOBXFL", date_col="VSDTC",
                                   testcd_col="VSTESTCD", ref_col="RFXSTDTC")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        import warnings

        from fleet.core.lineage import record_pin_lineage, sanitise_params

        # The call as given, for to_spec_yaml (result_col is resolved below).
        call_params = sanitise_params(
            {
                "target": target,
                "date_col": date_col,
                "testcd_col": testcd_col,
                "ref_col": ref_col,
                "ref_pin": ref_pin,
                "dm": dm,
                "by": by,
                "result_col": result_col,
                "order_by": order_by,
            }
        )
        df = self._lazy.collect()

        prefix = next(
            (target[: -len(s)] for s in ("LOBXFL", "BLFL") if target.endswith(s) and target != s),
            target[:2],
        )
        if result_col is None:
            candidates = (f"{prefix}STRESC", f"{prefix}ORRES")
            result_col = next((c for c in candidates if c in df.columns), None)
            if result_col is None:
                raise DerivationError(
                    f"baseline_flag('{target}'): neither {candidates[0]} nor {candidates[1]} "
                    "is in the frame. Name the result column with result_col=."
                )
        elif result_col not in df.columns:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"baseline_flag('{target}'): result_col={result_col!r} is not in the frame."
            )

        # Resolve reference date
        if dm is not None:
            ref_df = dm
            join_key = ["USUBJID"]
        elif ref_col in df.columns:
            ref_df = None
            join_key = []
        else:
            ref_df = self._require_pin(ref_pin.upper(), "baseline_flag", columns=[ref_col])
            join_key = self._pin_join_key(ref_pin.upper())

        # Join reference if needed
        _ref_tmp = f"__pin_{ref_col}__"
        if ref_df is not None:
            from fleet.core.joins import refuse_repeated_keys

            ref_slim = ref_df.select(
                [c for c in dict.fromkeys(join_key + [ref_col]) if c in ref_df.columns]
            )
            if join_key:
                ref_slim = refuse_repeated_keys(
                    "baseline_flag()",
                    ref_slim,
                    join_key,
                    source="DM" if dm is not None else ref_pin.upper(),
                )
            ref_slim = ref_slim.rename({ref_col: _ref_tmp})
            df = df.join(ref_slim, on=join_key, how="left", nulls_equal=True)
            ref_col_name = _ref_tmp
        else:
            ref_col_name = ref_col

        # Build grouping keys
        grp_keys = ["USUBJID"]
        if testcd_col is not None:
            grp_keys.append(testcd_col)
        if by:
            grp_keys.extend(by)
        grp_keys = list(dict.fromkeys(grp_keys))

        # Last record strictly before the reference (Q1 B, 2026-11-02): on the reference
        # date a record is eligible only when both times are known and it is earlier.
        def day_and_time(name: str) -> tuple[pl.Expr, pl.Expr]:
            dtype = df.schema[name]
            if dtype == pl.String:
                return date_part(pl.col(name)), datetime_part(pl.col(name))
            if isinstance(dtype, pl.Datetime):
                return pl.col(name).cast(pl.Date), pl.col(name).cast(pl.Datetime("us"))
            return pl.col(name), pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Datetime("us"))

        day, time = day_and_time(date_col)
        ref_day, ref_time = day_and_time(ref_col_name)
        before_ref = (day < ref_day) | ((day == ref_day) & (time < ref_time))

        has_result = pl.col(result_col).is_not_null()
        if df.schema[result_col] == pl.String:
            has_result = has_result & (pl.col(result_col).str.strip_chars() != "")
        stat_col, orres_col, drvfl_col = f"{prefix}STAT", f"{prefix}ORRES", f"{prefix}DRVFL"
        if stat_col in df.columns:
            has_result = has_result & (pl.col(stat_col).fill_null("") != "NOT DONE")
        if orres_col in df.columns and orres_col != result_col:
            orres_ok = pl.col(orres_col).cast(pl.String).str.strip_chars().fill_null("") != ""
            if drvfl_col in df.columns:
                orres_ok = orres_ok | (pl.col(drvfl_col).fill_null("") == "Y")
            has_result = has_result & orres_ok

        eligible = before_ref.fill_null(False) & has_result.fill_null(False)
        key = pl.coalesce(time, day.cast(pl.Datetime("us")))
        df = df.with_row_index("__bl_row__").with_columns(
            pl.when(eligible).then(key).alias("__bl_key__"),
        )

        if order_by is not None:
            tie_cols = [order_by] if isinstance(order_by, str) else list(order_by)
        else:
            tie_cols = [c for c in (f"{prefix}SEQ",) if c in df.columns]
        last_day = (
            df.filter(pl.col("__bl_key__").is_not_null())
            .filter(pl.col("__bl_key__") == pl.col("__bl_key__").max().over(grp_keys))
            .sort(["__bl_key__", *tie_cols, "__bl_row__"], descending=True, nulls_last=True)
            .group_by(grp_keys, maintain_order=True)
            .agg(pl.col("__bl_row__").first().alias("__bl_win__"), pl.len().alias("__bl_n__"))
        )
        n_ties = last_day.filter(pl.col("__bl_n__") > 1).height
        if n_ties and order_by is None:
            rule = f"the last {tie_cols[0]}" if tie_cols else "the last input record"
            warnings.warn(
                f"baseline_flag('{target}'): {n_ties} group(s) have more than one record with a "
                f"result on the last date and time before the reference. The flag goes to "
                f"{rule}; pass order_by= to state the SAP rule.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )

        df = df.with_columns(
            pl.when(pl.col("__bl_row__").is_in(last_day["__bl_win__"]))
            .then(pl.lit("Y"))
            .otherwise(pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.String))
            .alias(target)
        )

        # Clean up temp columns
        drop_cols = ["__bl_row__", "__bl_key__"]
        if ref_df is not None:
            drop_cols.append(_ref_tmp)
        df = df.drop([c for c in drop_cols if c in df.columns])

        new = self._materialise_then(df)

        # Record variable lineage
        from fleet.core.dag import VariableNode as _VN

        var_lineage: list = list(getattr(new, "_lineage", []))
        var_lineage.append(
            _VN(
                name=target,
                verb="baseline_flag",
                sources=[date_col, ref_col, result_col],
                method="fleet.sdtm.namespace.SDTMNamespace.baseline_flag",
                domain=getattr(new, "_domain", None),
                params=call_params,
            )
        )
        new._lineage = var_lineage

        if ref_df is not None:
            record_pin_lineage(
                new,
                target_col=target,
                verb="baseline_flag",
                source_domain=ref_pin.upper(),
                source_cols=[ref_col],
                join_key=join_key,
                relationship="derivation",
            )
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 6. condition_add — if condition then value else null                 #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def condition_add(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        condition: str | pl.Expr,
        then_value: Any,
    ) -> Self:
        """Set *target* to *then_value* where *condition* is true.

        Other rows keep the current value of *target*, or get null when
        *target* is a new column, as a SAS ``if ... then`` statement.  So
        a chain of calls on one target keeps the value of each call.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output SDTM variable.
            condition: A Polars expression (or string) that evaluates to a
                boolean mask.
            then_value: The value to assign when *condition* is true.

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Set ``AEOUT`` to ``"FATAL"`` where the death flag is set::

                ae = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .condition_add(
                        "AEOUT",
                        condition='pl.col("death_flag") == "Y"',
                        then_value="FATAL",
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        cond_expr = condition if isinstance(condition, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(condition)
        current = pl.col(target) if target in self._lazy.collect_schema() else pl.lit(None)
        expr = pl.when(cond_expr).then(pl.lit(then_value)).otherwise(current).alias(target)
        return self._chain(expr, verb="condition_add")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 8. ae_aerel — AE causality string mapping                           #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    _DEFAULT_AEREL_MAP: dict[str, str] = {
        "yes": "RELATED",
        "y": "RELATED",
        "related": "RELATED",
        "possibly related": "POSSIBLY RELATED",
        "probable": "PROBABLE",
        "no": "NOT RELATED",
        "n": "NOT RELATED",
        "not related": "NOT RELATED",
        "remote": "REMOTE",
        "unlikely related": "UNLIKELY RELATED",
    }

    def ae_aerel(
        self,
        target: str = "AEREL",
        *,
        source: str = "ae_relationship",
        aerel_map: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Map free-text AE causality strings to ``AEREL`` values.

        Mapping is case-insensitive against *aerel_map*, and leading and
        trailing blanks do not count.  A value with no mapping becomes its
        trimmed upper-case text, and one warning lists these values.  The
        default map is Fleet's own convention, not CDISC terminology:
        SDTM IG v3.4 gives AEREL no codelist, so the sponsor defines the
        terms and the map must be complete.  The
        AE relationship table (``AERelationshipSpec.relationship_order``)
        must list the same terms; a term it does not list stops the
        table.

        Args:
            target: Output column name (default ``"AEREL"``).
            source: Raw column containing causality strings.
            aerel_map: Optional ``{raw_text: decoded_value}`` override.

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        References:
            SDTM IG v3.4, AE domain, AEREL (no controlled terminology).

        Examples:
            Derive ``AEREL`` from raw causality using the default mapping::

                ae = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .ae_aerel("AEREL", source="ae_relationship")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        import warnings

        given = aerel_map if aerel_map is not None else self._DEFAULT_AEREL_MAP
        mapping = {k.strip().lower(): v for k, v in given.items()}

        raw = pl.col(source).cast(pl.String)
        normalised = raw.str.to_lowercase().str.strip_chars()
        unmapped = (
            self._lazy.select(raw.str.strip_chars().alias("v"))
            .filter((pl.col("v") != "") & ~pl.col("v").str.to_lowercase().is_in(list(mapping)))
            .unique()
            .sort("v")
            .collect()["v"]
            .to_list()
        )
        if unmapped:
            warnings.warn(
                f"ae_aerel('{target}'): {len(unmapped)} value(s) have no mapping: {unmapped}; "
                "pass aerel_map=. They are kept in upper case.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        expr = normalised.replace_strict(
            mapping,
            default=normalised.str.to_uppercase(),
            return_dtype=pl.String,
        ).alias(target)
        return self._chain(expr, verb="ae_aerel")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 9. seq — --SEQ sequence number (with SDTM naming convention check)  #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def seq(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        order_by: list[str] | None = None,
        by: list[str] | None = None,
        start_at: int = 1,
        check_uniqueness: bool = False,
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive the ``--SEQ`` sequence number variable.

        Generates a 1-based integer sequence that uniquely identifies each
        record within the domain, per subject.  The dataset is sorted by
        *order_by* columns within each *by* partition before numbering
        — this follows the sdtm.oak ``derive_seq()`` pattern and ensures
        deterministic, reproducible sequence values.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output ``--SEQ`` variable (e.g. ``"AESEQ"``,
                ``"VSSEQ"``).  A warning is emitted if the name does not end
                in ``SEQ``.
            order_by: Columns that define the sort order within each group.
                Records that tie keep their input order, as PROC SORT
                EQUALS.  When ``None``, the current row order is preserved.
            by: Subject-level grouping columns (default
                ``["STUDYID", "USUBJID"]``).  The sequence restarts at
                *start_at* for each unique combination.
            start_at: First sequence value (default ``1``).
            check_uniqueness: If ``True``, emit a warning when the
                combination of *by* + *order_by* does not uniquely
                identify each row.

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: A fresh namespace with *target* appended.  Call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Derive ``AESEQ`` ordered by start date within each subject::

                ae = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
                    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                    .assign("AETERM", source="ae_term")
                    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
                    .seq("AESEQ", order_by=["AESTDTC"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        import warnings

        if not target.endswith("SEQ"):
            warnings.warn(
                f"Target variable '{target}' does not end in 'SEQ'. "
                "SDTM --SEQ variables should follow the naming convention.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )

        return super().seq(
            target,
            order_by=order_by,
            by=by,
            start_at=start_at,
            check_uniqueness=check_uniqueness,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 10. merge is inherited from SharedVerbsMixin (canonical join verb). #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 10. group_by — aggregate records                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def group_by(
        self,
        *,
        by: list[str],
        agg: list[pl.Expr],
    ) -> Self:
        """Group by *by* and apply *agg* aggregations (lazily).

        The groups come out in the order of their first record, so the
        same input gives the same row order at each run.

        Args:
            by: Column(s) to group by.
            agg: List of Polars aggregation expressions.

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: A fresh namespace continuing from the grouped
                plan.

        Raises:
            DerivationError: When a column of *by* is not in the frame.

        Examples:
            Compute max vital-sign result per subject and test::

                vs_agg = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .group_by(
                        by=["USUBJID", "VSTESTCD"],
                        agg=[pl.col("VSSTRESN").max().alias("AVAL")],
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        self._require_columns("group_by(by=...)", by)
        return self._with_lazy(self._lazy.group_by(by, maintain_order=True).agg(agg))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 13. notsubmitted — mark variable as null / not-submitted            #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def notsubmitted(self, *targets: str) -> Self:
        """Mark one or more variables as not submitted (set to null).

        Useful to explicitly null out eCRF fields that are not included in
        the SDTM submission.

        Args:
            *targets: One or more variable names to null out.

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: The namespace with each *target* set to null;
                call ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Null out internal scratch fields before submission::

                dm = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                    .notsubmitted("_raw_id", "_site_code")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        exprs = [pl.lit(None).alias(t) for t in targets]
        return self._chain(*exprs, verb="notsubmitted")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 14. multiple_responses — expand multi-value eCRF fields             #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def multiple_responses(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        source: str,
        delimiter: str = "|",
    ) -> Self:
        """Explode a delimited multi-response field into separate rows.

        Splits *source* on *delimiter* and explodes, lazily, as part of
        the accumulated plan.  One row per response.  Blanks around a
        response are removed, and an empty response gives no row, as SAS
        ``scan()``.  A value with no response keeps one row with a null.

        Not for non-result qualifiers such as DM RACE: DM has one record
        per subject.  For two races, set RACE to ``"MULTIPLE"`` with
        ``assign`` or ``case_when``, put RACE1, RACE2, ... in columns, and
        write them to SUPPDM with ``nsv`` and ``export_supp`` (SDTMIG 3.4
        section 4.2.8.3).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column for the split values.
            source: Name of the raw column containing delimited responses.
            delimiter: Separator between responses (default ``"|"``).

        Returns:
            SDTMNamespace: A fresh namespace with one row per response.

        Examples:
            Explode pipe-delimited AE terms into separate rows::

                ae = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .multiple_responses(
                        "AETERM", source="ae_terms", delimiter="|",
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        tokens = (
            pl.col(source)
            .str.split(delimiter)
            .list.eval(pl.element().str.strip_chars())
            .list.eval(pl.element().filter(pl.element() != ""))
        )
        return self._with_lazy(
            self._lazy.with_columns(tokens.alias("__split__"))
            .explode("__split__", empty_as_null=True)
            .with_columns(pl.col("__split__").alias(target))
            .drop("__split__")
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Spec-driven pipeline: from_spec() is inherited from                  #
    # SharedVerbsMixin and executes through fleet.core.spec_registry.      #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Terminal operations                                                  #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def export_supp(
        self,
        *,
        qualifiers: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None,
        spec: str | Path | None = None,
        dataset: str | None = None,
        idvar: str | None = None,
        domain: str | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Export Non-Standard Variables as a vertical SUPPQUAL DataFrame.

        Produces the CDISC SUPPQUAL structure (STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID,
        IDVAR, IDVARVAL, QNAM, QLABEL, QVAL, QORIG, QEVAL) for SDTM
        IG ≤3.4 submissions.

        Resolution order (first match wins):

        1. **qualifiers** dict — explicit metadata per qualifier column.
        2. **spec** + **dataset** — reads ``role: qualifier`` variables
           from a ``define.yaml``.
        3. **Pipeline metadata** — uses ``_nsv_meta`` populated by prior
           ``nsv()`` calls in the chain.

        Args:
            qualifiers: Explicit qualifier metadata mapping.  Keys are
                column names (QNAM), values are dicts with ``"label"``
                and optionally ``"origin"`` and ``"evaluator"`` keys.
            spec: Path to a ``define.yaml`` file.  Used with *dataset*
                to discover ``role: qualifier`` variables.
            dataset: Dataset name within the spec (e.g. ``"DM"``).
            idvar: Name of the identifying variable column (e.g.
                ``"AESEQ"``).  Required for every RDOMAIN except DM;
                for DM, IDVAR and IDVARVAL are null.
            domain: Explicit RDOMAIN value.  When ``None``, inferred
                from the ``DOMAIN`` column in the frame.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: Vertical SUPPQUAL frame with columns STUDYID,
                RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, QNAM, QLABEL, QVAL,
                QORIG, QEVAL.  A null or blank value gives no record.  A
                float is written with no ``.0`` end and a date as ISO 8601.

        Raises:
            DerivationError: When no source gives qualifier metadata, a
                qualifier or *idvar* is not a column, *idvar* is missing
                for a domain other than DM, RDOMAIN is unknown, DOMAIN
                holds more than one value and *domain* is not given,
                STUDYID or USUBJID is not a column, a QNAM is not 1 to 8
                upper-case letters, digits or underscores with no digit
                first, a QLABEL is not 1 to 40 characters, or the *spec*
                dataset is not found.  A QVAL over 200 characters gives a
                warning.

        References:
            SDTMIG 3.4 section 8.4 (SUPPQUAL: STUDYID, RDOMAIN and
            USUBJID are Req; QNAM and QLABEL limits) and section 4.5.3.2
            (text over 200 characters).

        Examples:
            Export from pipeline metadata (Pattern A)::

                ns = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                    .nsv("SAFETY", source="safety_flag",
                         label="Safety Population Flag")
                )
                suppdm = ns.export_supp()

            Export from define.yaml spec (Pattern D)::

                dm = raw_df.sdtm.from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="DM").to_frame()
                suppdm = dm.sdtm.export_supp(spec="define.yaml", dataset="DM")

            Export an AE qualifier linked by AESEQ::

                suppae = ae.sdtm.export_supp(
                    qualifiers={"AETOXGR": {"label": "AE Toxicity Grade"}},
                    idvar="AESEQ",
                )

            Export with explicit qualifier dict (Pattern C)::

                suppdm = dm.sdtm.export_supp(
                    qualifiers={
                        "COMPLT16": {"label": "Completers of Week 16",
                                     "origin": "Derived"},
                        "SAFETY": {"label": "Safety Population Flag",
                                   "origin": "Derived"},
                    },
                )
        """
        # Resolve qualifier metadata from one of three sources
        meta: list[NSVMeta] = self._resolve_supp_meta(qualifiers, spec, dataset)

        if not meta:
            if qualifiers is None and spec is None:
                raise DerivationError(
                    "export_supp(): no NSV metadata. Pass qualifiers= or spec=, or call "
                    "export_supp() before to_frame(), which drops the nsv() metadata."
                )
            # qualifiers={} or a spec dataset with no qualifier: a legal empty SUPP
            return pl.DataFrame(schema=dict.fromkeys(_SUPP_COLUMNS, pl.String))

        df = self._lazy.collect()

        domains = (
            df["DOMAIN"].drop_nulls().unique().sort().to_list() if "DOMAIN" in df.columns else []
        )
        if domain:
            rdomain = domain
        elif len(domains) == 1:
            rdomain = domains[0]
        elif domains:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"export_supp(): DOMAIN holds {' and '.join(domains)}; export one domain or "
                "pass domain=."
            )
        else:
            raise DerivationError(
                "export_supp(): RDOMAIN is unknown, because the frame has no DOMAIN value. "
                "Pass domain=."
            )
        keys_absent = [c for c in ("STUDYID", "USUBJID") if c not in df.columns]
        if keys_absent:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"export_supp(): the frame has no {' and no '.join(keys_absent)}. SUPP{rdomain} "
                "needs STUDYID and USUBJID (Req in SUPPQUAL): add them before export_supp()."
            )
        absent = [m.target for m in meta if m.target not in df.columns]
        if absent:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"export_supp(): qualifier(s) {absent} are not columns of the frame. "
                f"Available: {df.columns}"
            )
        _check_supp_meta(meta)
        if idvar is not None and idvar not in df.columns:
            raise DerivationError(f"export_supp(): idvar '{idvar}' is not a column of the frame.")
        if idvar is None and rdomain != "DM":
            raise DerivationError(
                f"export_supp(): give idvar= (for example {rdomain}SEQ) for RDOMAIN "
                f"{rdomain}. Only DM may have no IDVAR (SDTMIG 3.4 section 8.4)."
            )

        qual_cols = [m.target for m in meta]
        label_map = {m.target: m.label for m in meta}
        origin_map = {m.target: m.origin for m in meta}
        eval_map = {m.target: m.evaluator for m in meta}

        base_cols = ["STUDYID", "USUBJID"]
        id_cols = [idvar] if idvar is not None and idvar not in base_cols else []

        # Each qualifier becomes text before the unpivot, so mixed types keep their value.
        supp = df.select(
            *base_cols,
            *id_cols,
            *(to_char(pl.col(c), df.schema[c]).alias(c) for c in qual_cols),
        ).unpivot(
            on=qual_cols,
            index=base_cols + id_cols,
            variable_name="QNAM",
            value_name="QVAL",
        )

        # SDTMIG 3.4: no SUPP record with a null QVAL; a blank is missing too.
        supp = supp.filter(pl.col("QVAL").is_not_null() & (pl.col("QVAL").str.strip_chars() != ""))
        long = supp.filter(pl.col("QVAL").str.len_chars() > 200)
        if long.height:
            import warnings

            warnings.warn(
                f"export_supp(): {long.height} QVAL value(s) are over 200 characters "
                f"(QNAM {sorted(set(long['QNAM'].to_list()))}). Split the text into QNAM, "
                "QNAM1, ... (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.5.3.2).",
                stacklevel=2,
            )

        # Add SUPPQUAL metadata columns
        supp = supp.with_columns(
            pl.lit(rdomain).cast(pl.String).alias("RDOMAIN"),
            pl.col("QNAM").replace_strict(label_map, default=None).cast(pl.String).alias("QLABEL"),
            pl.col("QNAM")
            .replace_strict(origin_map, default="Derived")
            .cast(pl.String)
            .alias("QORIG"),
            pl.col("QNAM").replace_strict(eval_map, default=None).cast(pl.String).alias("QEVAL"),
        )

        if idvar is not None:
            supp = supp.with_columns(
                pl.lit(idvar).alias("IDVAR"),
                to_char(pl.col(idvar), df.schema[idvar]).alias("IDVARVAL"),
            )
            if id_cols:
                supp = supp.drop(idvar)
        else:
            supp = supp.with_columns(
                pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.String).alias("IDVAR"),
                pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.String).alias("IDVARVAL"),
            )

        return supp.select(_SUPP_COLUMNS)

    def _resolve_supp_meta(
        self,
        qualifiers: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None,
        spec: str | Path | None,
        dataset: str | None,
    ) -> list[NSVMeta]:
        """Resolve NSV metadata from qualifiers dict, spec file, or pipeline."""
        # Priority 1: explicit qualifiers dict
        if qualifiers is not None:
            return [
                NSVMeta(
                    target=name,
                    label=info.get("label", ""),
                    origin=info.get("origin", "Derived"),
                    evaluator=info.get("evaluator"),
                )
                for name, info in qualifiers.items()
            ]

        # Priority 2: spec file
        if spec is not None:
            spec_data = load_define_spec(spec)
            if not spec_data.datasets:
                raise DerivationError(f"export_supp(spec='{spec}'): the spec has no datasets.")
            ds = spec_data.select(dataset)
            meta = []
            for var in ds.variables:
                is_qual = (
                    var.role == "qualifier" or (var.derivation or {}).get("algorithm") == "nsv"
                )
                if is_qual:
                    meta.append(
                        NSVMeta(
                            target=var.name,
                            label=var.label or "",
                            origin=var.origin or "Derived",
                            evaluator=var.evaluator,
                        )
                    )
            return meta

        # Priority 3: pipeline metadata
        return list(self._nsv_meta)

    save_to=None,

Query the CDISC Library for domain's IG structure.

When define_path is given the domain variables (including core) are read from the define.yaml first; if the domain is not found the method falls back to the online CDISC Library.

When save_to is given the fetched metadata is cached as YAML; on subsequent calls the cache is read instead of hitting the API.

SDTMIG 3.4 structures for the nine TDD domains (TE, TA, TV, TS, TI, TD, TM, SV, SE) ship with Fleet, so the default flow needs no network access and no API key; the CDISC Library is only queried for other domains or IG versions.

Keeps the IG metadata on the namespace and compares it with the static Pydantic model; each difference gives a warning. The requested domain is kept too: study_header and the add_* verb must name the same domain.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default domain str

SDTM domain code (e.g. "TE", "TA").

required ig_version str

SDTM IG version slug (default "3-4").

'3-4' save_to str | Path | None

Optional path to cache the fetched YAML. A cache that holds another domain or IG version raises.

None define_path str | Path | None

Optional path to a define.yaml. When provided, domain metadata is extracted from the spec (offline) before falling back to the CDISC Library API.

None

Raises:

Type Description FileNotFoundError

When define_path is not a file.

ValueError

When the save_to cache holds another domain or IG version.

When the CDISC Library cannot give the domain; the message gives the cause (for example a missing API key).

Examples:

Fetch the TE structure from the CDISC Library::

te = (
    pl.DataFrame().sdtm
    .fetch_structure("TE", ig_version="3-4",
                     save_to="metadata/te_structure.yaml")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TE")
    .add_elements(te_rows)
    .to_frame()
)

def fetch_structure(
    self,
    domain: str,
    *,
    ig_version: str = "3-4",
    save_to: str | Path | None = None,
    define_path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> Self:  # type: ignore[type-var]
    """Query the CDISC Library for *domain*'s IG structure.

    When *define_path* is given the domain variables (including ``core``)
    are read from the define.yaml first; if the domain is not found the
    method falls back to the online CDISC Library.

    When *save_to* is given the fetched metadata is cached as YAML; on
    subsequent calls the cache is read instead of hitting the API.

    SDTMIG 3.4 structures for the nine TDD domains (TE, TA, TV, TS, TI,
    TD, TM, SV, SE) ship with Fleet, so the default flow needs no
    network access and no API key; the CDISC Library is only queried
    for other domains or IG versions.

    Keeps the IG metadata on the namespace and compares it with the
    static Pydantic model; each difference gives a warning.  The
    requested domain is kept too: ``study_header`` and the ``add_*``
    verb must name the same domain.

    Args:
        domain: SDTM domain code (e.g. ``"TE"``, ``"TA"``).
        ig_version: SDTM IG version slug (default ``"3-4"``).
        save_to: Optional path to cache the fetched YAML.  A cache
            that holds another domain or IG version raises.
        define_path: Optional path to a ``define.yaml``. When provided,
            domain metadata is extracted from the spec (offline) before
            falling back to the CDISC Library API.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace at stage 1; call ``study_header()`` next.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When *define_path* is not a file.
        ValueError: When the *save_to* cache holds another domain or
            IG version.
        CTError: When the CDISC Library cannot give the domain; the
            message gives the cause (for example a missing API key).

    Examples:
        Fetch the TE structure from the CDISC Library::

            te = (
                pl.DataFrame().sdtm
                .fetch_structure("TE", ig_version="3-4",
                                 save_to="metadata/te_structure.yaml")
                .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TE")
                .add_elements(te_rows)
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    self._check_stage("fetch_structure", required=0)
    domain = domain.upper()

    # Priority: define_path → save_to cache → packaged IG 3.4 → online
    meta: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    if define_path is not None:
        if not Path(define_path).is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"fetch_structure('{domain}'): no file {define_path}")
        meta = _extract_domain_from_define(domain, Path(define_path))

    cache_path = Path(save_to) if save_to else None
    if meta is None and cache_path and cache_path.exists():
        meta = yaml.safe_load(cache_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        cached = {k: (meta or {}).get(k) for k in ("domain", "ig_version")}
        if cached["domain"] and str(cached["domain"]).upper() != domain:
            raise ValueError(
                f"fetch_structure('{domain}'): the cache {cache_path} holds domain "
                f"{cached['domain']}, not {domain}."
            )
        if cached["ig_version"] and cached["ig_version"] != ig_version:
            raise ValueError(
                f"fetch_structure('{domain}', ig_version='{ig_version}'): the cache "
                f"{cache_path} holds SDTM IG {cached['ig_version']}."
            )

    if meta is None:
        meta = _load_packaged_structure(domain, ig_version)
        if meta is None:
            try:
                meta = self._fetch_ig_domain(domain, ig_version)
            except Exception as exc:
                raise CTError(
                    f"Could not get domain '{domain}' from SDTM IG {ig_version}: {exc}. "
                    f"If this is a company-specific domain, provide its structure "
                    f"via define_path= or a cached YAML via save_to=."
                ) from exc
        if cache_path:
            cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            cache_path.write_text(
                yaml.dump(meta, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False), encoding="utf-8"
            )

    # Propagate to the new namespace instance
    new = self._chain()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    new._domain_meta = meta
    new._tdd_domain = domain
    new._tdd_stage = 1
    new._reconciliation_report = _reconcile_schema(domain, meta)
    for msg in new._reconciliation_report:
        warnings.warn(msg, UserWarning, stacklevel=2)
    return new  # type: ignore[return-value]

def study_header(
    self,
    study_id: str,
    domain: str,
) -> Self:  # type: ignore[type-var]
    """Hardcode ``STUDYID`` and ``DOMAIN`` columns.

    Args:
        study_id: The study identifier value (a non-empty string).
        domain: The SDTM domain code; it must match ``fetch_structure``.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace at stage 2; call an ``add_*()`` verb next.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When *study_id* is empty or not a string, or when
            *domain* is not the domain of ``fetch_structure``.

    Examples:
        Set the study header for a TE domain::

            te = (
                pl.DataFrame().sdtm
                .fetch_structure("TE")
                .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TE")
                .add_elements(te_rows)
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    self._check_stage("study_header", required=1)
    if not isinstance(study_id, str) or not study_id.strip():
        raise ValueError(
            f"study_header(): study_id must be a non-empty string, got {study_id!r}"
        )
    fetched = getattr(self, "_tdd_domain", None)
    if fetched is not None and domain.upper() != fetched:
        raise ValueError(
            f"study_header('{domain.upper()}') does not match fetch_structure('{fetched}')."
        )
    new = self._chain(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        pl.lit(study_id).alias("STUDYID"),
        pl.lit(domain.upper()).alias("DOMAIN"),
    )
    new._tdd_stage = 2
    return new  # type: ignore[return-value]

def add_arms(
    self,
    arms: TrialArms,
    *,
    te: TrialElements | None = None,
) -> Self:  # type: ignore[type-var]
    """Materialise a validated ``TrialArms`` collection into the pipeline.

    Args:
        arms: A ``TrialArms`` collection.
        te: Optional ``TrialElements`` for FK validation (ETCD ∈ TE.ETCD).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace at stage 3 with TA rows loaded.

    Examples:
        Add trial arms with FK validation::

            ta = (
                pl.DataFrame().sdtm
                .fetch_structure("TA")
                .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TA")
                .add_arms(ta_rows, te=te_rows)
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    self._check_stage("add_arms", required=2)
    if te is not None:
        valid_etcds = {e.etcd for e in te.elements}
        for a in arms.arms:
            if a.etcd not in valid_etcds:
                raise ValueError(

visit_map(
    target_num,
    target_name,
    *,
    date_col,
    planned_visits,
    ref_date=None,
    tolerance=None
)

Map raw visit dates to planned visits from TV, by nearest study day.

Use it only when the CRF does not collect the visit: it never replaces a collected VISITNUM. For each row, the verb takes the planned visit whose VISITDY is nearest to the actual study day (from date_col and ref_date), within the optional tolerance window. The distance is the difference of the study-day numbers, as abs(SVSTDY - VISITDY) in a SAS program: across the missing Day 0, Day -1 is 2 days from VISITDY 1. Ties resolve to the earlier VISITNUM. When TV has ARMCD values, a row only takes a visit of its own arm or a visit with a blank ARMCD.

A dated row outside every window is an unscheduled visit. It gets the VISITNUM of the last planned visit on or before its study day plus .1, .2, ... in date order within the subject, and the VISIT UNSCHEDULED <VISITNUM>. A row with no study day gets a null. One warning gives both counts. With DOMAIN SV, one warning gives the USUBJID + VISITNUM keys that repeat.

With no tolerance, every dated record takes the nearest planned visit, however far it is, so no record is unscheduled (ADR-0035). One warning then gives the count and the largest distance.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target_num str

Name of the output VISITNUM column. An existing column of that name is replaced.

required target_name str

Name of the output VISIT column. An existing column of that name is replaced.

required date_col str

Column containing the actual visit date (ISO 8601 string).

required planned_visits TrialVisits | DataFrame

A TrialVisits collection or a DataFrame with VISITNUM, VISIT, and VISITDY columns (and optionally ARMCD).

required ref_date str | None

Column with the reference date for the study day. When it is not a column of the frame, it is read from the pinned DM, as study_day() does. When None, the frame must hold the study day in a VISITDY column.

None tolerance dict[str, int] | None

Optional {"before": n, "after": n} window in study days, boundaries inclusive: the actual study day may precede the planned VISITDY by up to before and follow it by up to after.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target_num and target_name appended.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

When date_col or ref_date cannot be found, when TV has arm-specific visits and the frame has no ARMCD, or when an unscheduled number would repeat a planned VISITNUM or reach the next whole number.

References

SDTMIG 3.4 SV and TV: USUBJID + VISITNUM is the SV key, VISITNUM is Req, a null TV ARMCD means all arms. The decimal number of an unscheduled visit is a sponsor convention (the CDISC pilot uses UNSCHEDULED 5.1); see docs/adr/0035-visit-map-numbers-an-unscheduled-visit.md.

Examples:

Map subject visits to planned visits::

sv = (
    raw_visits.sdtm
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="SV")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("SVSTDTC", source="visit_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .visit_map("VISITNUM", "VISIT",
               date_col="SVSTDTC",
               planned_visits=tv_rows,
               ref_date="RFSTDTC",
               tolerance={"before": 3, "after": 3})
    .to_frame()
)

def visit_map(
    self,
    target_num: str,
    target_name: str,
    *,
    date_col: str,
    planned_visits: TrialVisits | pl.DataFrame,
    ref_date: str | None = None,
    tolerance: dict[str, int] | None = None,
) -> Self:  # type: ignore[type-var]
    """Map raw visit dates to planned visits from TV, by nearest study day.

    Use it only when the CRF does not collect the visit: it never
    replaces a collected VISITNUM.  For each row, the verb takes the
    planned visit whose ``VISITDY`` is nearest to the actual study day
    (from *date_col* and *ref_date*), within the optional *tolerance*
    window.  The distance is the difference of the study-day numbers,
    as ``abs(SVSTDY - VISITDY)`` in a SAS program: across the missing
    Day 0, Day -1 is 2 days from ``VISITDY`` 1.  Ties resolve to the
    earlier ``VISITNUM``.  When TV has ``ARMCD`` values, a row only
    takes a visit of its own arm or a visit with a blank ``ARMCD``.

    A dated row outside every window is an unscheduled visit.  It gets
    the ``VISITNUM`` of the last planned visit on or before its study
    day plus .1, .2, ... in date order within the subject, and the
    ``VISIT`` ``UNSCHEDULED <VISITNUM>``.  A row with no study day gets
    a null.  One warning gives both counts.  With ``DOMAIN`` SV, one
    warning gives the ``USUBJID`` + ``VISITNUM`` keys that repeat.

    With no *tolerance*, every dated record takes the nearest planned
    visit, however far it is, so no record is unscheduled (ADR-0035).
    One warning then gives the count and the largest distance.

    Args:
        target_num: Name of the output ``VISITNUM`` column.  An
            existing column of that name is replaced.
        target_name: Name of the output ``VISIT`` column.  An existing
            column of that name is replaced.
        date_col: Column containing the actual visit date (ISO 8601 string).
        planned_visits: A ``TrialVisits`` collection or a DataFrame with
            ``VISITNUM``, ``VISIT``, and ``VISITDY`` columns (and
            optionally ``ARMCD``).
        ref_date: Column with the reference date for the study day.
            When it is not a column of the frame, it is read from the
            pinned DM, as ``study_day()`` does.  When ``None``, the
            frame must hold the study day in a ``VISITDY`` column.
        tolerance: Optional ``{"before": n, "after": n}`` window in
            study days, boundaries inclusive: the actual study day may
            precede the planned ``VISITDY`` by up to *before* and
            follow it by up to *after*.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target_num* and *target_name* appended.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When *date_col* or *ref_date* cannot be found,
            when TV has arm-specific visits and the frame has no
            ``ARMCD``, or when an unscheduled number would repeat a
            planned ``VISITNUM`` or reach the next whole number.

    References:
        SDTMIG 3.4 SV and TV: ``USUBJID`` + ``VISITNUM`` is the SV key,
        ``VISITNUM`` is Req, a null TV ``ARMCD`` means all arms.  The
        decimal number of an unscheduled visit is a sponsor convention
        (the CDISC pilot uses ``UNSCHEDULED 5.1``); see
        ``docs/adr/0035-visit-map-numbers-an-unscheduled-visit.md``.

    Examples:
        Map subject visits to planned visits::

            sv = (
                raw_visits.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="SV")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .date("SVSTDTC", source="visit_date")
                .pin("DM", dm)
                .visit_map("VISITNUM", "VISIT",
                           date_col="SVSTDTC",
                           planned_visits=tv_rows,
                           ref_date="RFSTDTC",
                           tolerance={"before": 3, "after": 3})
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    tv_df = (
        planned_visits.to_polars()
        if isinstance(planned_visits, TrialVisits)
        else planned_visits
    )
    verb = f"visit_map({target_num})"
    df = self._lazy.collect().with_row_index("__row_idx__")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    df = df.drop([c for c in (target_num, target_name) if c in df.columns])
    actual = self._visit_map_study_day(df, verb, date_col, ref_date)
    df = df.with_columns(actual.alias("__actual_dy__"))

    tv_arm = (
        pl.col("ARMCD").cast(pl.String).replace("", None)
        if "ARMCD" in tv_df.columns
        else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.String)
    )
    tv_slim = tv_df.select(
        pl.col("VISITNUM").alias("__tv_num__"),
        pl.col("VISIT").alias("__tv_name__"),
        pl.col("VISITDY").alias("__tv_dy__"),
        tv_arm.alias("__tv_arm__"),
    )
    arm_specific = tv_slim["__tv_arm__"].is_not_null().any()
    if arm_specific and "ARMCD" not in df.columns:
        raise DerivationError(
            f"{verb}: the planned visits hold arm-specific ARMCD values, and the frame "
            "has no ARMCD column. Add ARMCD so each subject takes only the visits of its arm."
        )

    crossed = df.select("__row_idx__", "__actual_dy__", *(["ARMCD"] if arm_specific else []))
    crossed = crossed.join(tv_slim, how="cross").filter(pl.col("__actual_dy__").is_not_null())
    if arm_specific:
        crossed = crossed.filter(
            pl.col("__tv_arm__").is_null() | (pl.col("__tv_arm__") == pl.col("ARMCD"))
        )
    offset = pl.col("__actual_dy__") - pl.col("__tv_dy__")
    candidates = crossed.filter(offset.is_not_null()).with_columns(
        offset.abs().alias("__diff__")
    )
    if tolerance:
        before = tolerance.get("before", 999999)
        after = tolerance.get("after", 999999)
        candidates = candidates.filter((offset >= -before) & (offset <= after))

    best = (
        candidates.sort("__row_idx__", "__diff__", "__tv_num__")
        .group_by("__row_idx__", maintain_order=True)
        .first()
        .select("__row_idx__", "__tv_num__", "__tv_name__", "__diff__")
    )
    if not tolerance and best.height:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{verb}: no tolerance=: {best.height} row(s) mapped to the nearest visit, the "
            f"largest distance is {best['__diff__'].max()} study days. Give tolerance= to "
            "make a record outside every window an unscheduled visit.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    best = best.drop("__diff__")
    unscheduled = _unscheduled_visits(df, crossed, best, verb, tv_slim)
    best = pl.concat([best, unscheduled], how="vertical_relaxed").rename(
        {"__tv_num__": target_num, "__tv_name__": target_name}
    )

    df = (
        df.join(best, on="__row_idx__", how="left")
        .sort("__row_idx__")
        .drop("__row_idx__", "__actual_dy__")
    )
    _warn_visit_map(df, verb, target_num, unscheduled.height)
    return self._materialise_then(df)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

The end date is the start of the next element by start date within the subject: the verb sorts on the ISO 8601 start text (a null start last, then the row order), so the input row order does not matter. The output keeps the input row order. The last element gets a null end.

def element_boundaries(
    self,
    target_start: str,
    target_end: str,
    *,
    milestones: dict[str, str],
    element_col: str = "ETCD",
    subject_col: str = "USUBJID",
) -> Self:  # type: ignore[type-var]
    """Derive element start/end dates from milestone columns.

    For each *element_col* value, maps the corresponding column from
    *milestones* to produce *target_start*.  The end date is the start
    of the next element by start date within the subject: the verb
    sorts on the ISO 8601 start text (a null start last, then the row
    order), so the input row order does not matter.  The output keeps
    the input row order.  The last element gets a null end.

    Args:
        target_start: Name of the output start-date column (e.g. ``"SESTDTC"``).
        target_end: Name of the output end-date column (e.g. ``"SEENDTC"``).
        milestones: ``{element_code: source_date_column}`` mapping.
        element_col: Column identifying the element (default ``"ETCD"``).
        subject_col: Column identifying the subject (default ``"USUBJID"``).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target_start* and *target_end* appended.

    Examples:
        Derive SE element boundaries::

            se = (
                disposition_df.sdtm
                .element_boundaries("SESTDTC", "SEENDTC",
                                    milestones={"SCRN": "screening_date",
                                                 "TRT": "first_dose_date"})
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    # Build a when/then chain mapping element codes to date columns
    cases: list[tuple[str, str]] = list(milestones.items())
    if not cases:
        return self._chain(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
            pl.lit(None).alias(target_start),
            pl.lit(None).alias(target_end),
        )

    first_code, first_col = cases[0]
    expr = pl.when(pl.col(element_col) == first_code).then(pl.col(first_col))
    for code, col in cases[1:]:
        expr = expr.when(pl.col(element_col) == code).then(pl.col(col))
    start_expr = expr.otherwise(pl.lit(None)).alias(target_start)

    # End = next element's start within the subject, in start-date order
    df = self._lazy.collect().with_row_index("__row_idx__")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    df = df.with_columns(start_expr)
    df = (
        df.sort(subject_col, target_start, "__row_idx__", nulls_last=True)
        .with_columns(pl.col(target_start).shift(-1).over(subject_col).alias(target_end))
        .sort("__row_idx__")
        .drop("__row_idx__")
    )

    return self._materialise_then(df)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

epoch_assign(
    target,
    *,
    date_col,
    epoch_ranges=None,
    se=None,
    subject_col="USUBJID",
    same_day="by_class"
)

Assign EPOCH based on date ranges or per-subject SE intervals.

With epoch_ranges, each entry maps a study-level date interval to an Epoch value; the first matching range wins. With se, the subject's own element intervals drive the assignment: for each row, the epoch of the SE record whose [SESTDTC, SEENDTC] interval contains the date (SDTMIG 3.4: EPOCH of the start or collection date/time). A blank or null SEENDTC is open-ended; an element whose dates are partial is skipped, with a warning.

On a transition date, where one element ends and the next starts, the time decides when the record and the boundary both have one. When one of them has no time, same_day decides, and one warning gives the count and the rule:

  • "by_class" (default): a Findings date (--DTC) takes the earlier element, an Events or Interventions date (--STDTC) the later one. Any other date_col name raises.
  • "earlier": the element that ends on that date.
  • "later": the element that starts on that date.

No guidance fixes this case, so state the rule in the SDRG.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output EPOCH column.

required date_col str

Column containing the date to classify.

required epoch_ranges list[dict[str, str]] | DataFrame | None

A list of {"start": date, "end": date, "epoch": str} dicts, or a DataFrame with those columns.

None se DataFrame | LazyFrame | None

An SE domain frame with USUBJID, SESTDTC, SEENDTC, and EPOCH columns. Mutually exclusive with epoch_ranges. EPOCH is Permissible in SE: an SE with no EPOCH raises.

None subject_col str

Subject key used to join se (default "USUBJID").

'USUBJID' same_day Literal['by_class', 'earlier', 'later']

The rule for a record with no time on a transition date (with se only).

'by_class'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target appended.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

When neither or both of epoch_ranges and se are provided.

DerivationError

When same_day="by_class" and date_col is neither a --DTC nor a --STDTC name, or when se has no EPOCH.

Examples:

Stamp EPOCH onto any domain from the subject's SE intervals::

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .epoch_assign("EPOCH", date_col="AESTDTC", se=se)
    .to_frame()
)

def epoch_assign(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    date_col: str,
    epoch_ranges: list[dict[str, str]] | pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    se: pl.DataFrame | pl.LazyFrame | None = None,
    subject_col: str = "USUBJID",
    same_day: Literal["by_class", "earlier", "later"] = "by_class",
) -> Self:  # type: ignore[type-var]
    """Assign ``EPOCH`` based on date ranges or per-subject SE intervals.

    With *epoch_ranges*, each entry maps a study-level date interval to
    an ``Epoch`` value; the first matching range wins.  With *se*, the
    subject's own element intervals drive the assignment: for each row,
    the epoch of the SE record whose ``[SESTDTC, SEENDTC]`` interval
    contains the date (SDTMIG 3.4: EPOCH of the start or collection
    date/time).  A blank or null ``SEENDTC`` is open-ended; an element
    whose dates are partial is skipped, with a warning.

    On a transition date, where one element ends and the next starts,
    the time decides when the record and the boundary both have one.
    When one of them has no time, *same_day* decides, and one warning
    gives the count and the rule:

    - ``"by_class"`` (default): a Findings date (``--DTC``) takes the
      earlier element, an Events or Interventions date (``--STDTC``)
      the later one.  Any other *date_col* name raises.
    - ``"earlier"``: the element that ends on that date.
    - ``"later"``: the element that starts on that date.

    No guidance fixes this case, so state the rule in the SDRG.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output ``EPOCH`` column.
        date_col: Column containing the date to classify.
        epoch_ranges: A list of ``{"start": date, "end": date,
            "epoch": str}`` dicts, or a DataFrame with those columns.
        se: An SE domain frame with ``USUBJID``, ``SESTDTC``,
            ``SEENDTC``, and ``EPOCH`` columns.  Mutually exclusive
            with *epoch_ranges*.  EPOCH is Permissible in SE: an SE
            with no EPOCH raises.
        subject_col: Subject key used to join *se* (default
            ``"USUBJID"``).
        same_day: The rule for a record with no time on a transition
            date (with *se* only).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When neither or both of *epoch_ranges* and *se*
            are provided.
        DerivationError: When ``same_day="by_class"`` and *date_col*
            is neither a ``--DTC`` nor a ``--STDTC`` name, or when *se*
            has no ``EPOCH``.

    Examples:
        Stamp EPOCH onto any domain from the subject's SE intervals::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .date("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
                .epoch_assign("EPOCH", date_col="AESTDTC", se=se)
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if (epoch_ranges is None) == (se is None):
        raise ValueError("epoch_assign() takes exactly one of epoch_ranges= or se=")

    if se is not None:
        rule = _same_day_rule(date_col, same_day)
        df = self._lazy.collect().with_row_index("__row_idx__")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        best = _epoch_from_se(df, se, target, date_col, subject_col, rule, same_day)
        out = (
            df.drop(target, strict=False)
            .join(best, on="__row_idx__", how="left")
            .drop("__row_idx__")
        )
        return self._materialise_then(out)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    if isinstance(epoch_ranges, pl.DataFrame):
        ranges = epoch_ranges.to_dicts()
    else:
        ranges = epoch_ranges

    if not ranges:
        return self._chain(pl.lit(None).alias(target))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    day = to_day(pl.col(date_col), self._lazy.collect_schema().get(date_col))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    expr = pl.when(pl.lit(False)).then(pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.String))
    for r in ranges:
        start = date_part(pl.lit(str(r["start"])))
        end = date_part(pl.lit(str(r["end"])))
        expr = expr.when((day >= start) & (day <= end)).then(pl.lit(r["epoch"]))

    final_expr = expr.otherwise(pl.lit(None)).alias(target)
    return self._chain(final_expr)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
