flag(
    target,
    *,
    criteria,
    by=None,
    order_by=None,
    value_col=None,
    where=None,
    from_dataset=None,
    on=None,
    source_filter=None,
    condition=None,
    inclusive=True,
    flag_no_ref_groups=True,
    flag_all=False,
    flag_value="Y",
    false_value=None
)

Set target to flag_value for records matching criteria.

Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

  • "first" / "last" — rank-based edge detection within groups.
  • "max" / "min" — value-based extreme within groups.
  • "exists" — set-membership from external dataset(s).
  • "before" / "after" — relative to a landmark condition.
  • "exists_after" / "exists_before" — temporal/self-join flag.

Parameters that are irrelevant to the selected criteria mode raise :class:~fleet.core.exceptions.VerbUsageError instead of being silently ignored. The flag_first / flag_last / flag_extreme / flag_exists / flag_relative wrappers expose each mode with only its own parameters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output flag column.

required criteria str | Expr

A Polars expression, or one of "first", "last", "max", "min", "exists", "before", "after", "exists_after", "exists_before".

required by list[str] | None

Partition columns (default ["USUBJID"]) for "first"/"last", "max"/"min" and "before"/"after". An expression flags each row on its own, so by raises there and in the exists modes.

None order_by str | list[str] | None

Sort column(s) required for "first"/"last" and "before"/"after". On a tie among candidates, "last" takes the last input record and "first" the first (SAS LAST./FIRST.); add a sequence variable to remove the dependence on input order. For "first"/"last" a missing value sorts last in each key, as admiral (ADR-0020): "last" takes a record with a missing key, and "first" takes one only when every candidate misses it. SAS sorts a missing value first, so a QC program with PROC SORT differs on such a group. "exists_after"/"exists_before" take one column only; build one ordered key (ADTM) for date and time.

None value_col str | None

Value column required for "max"/"min".

None where str | Expr | None

Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates; rows that fail it take no part, even on a tie.

None from_dataset DataFrame | list[DataFrame] | None

External dataset(s) for "exists" and "exists_after"/"exists_before" criteria.

None on list[str] | None

Join key columns for "exists" criteria.

None source_filter str | Expr | None

Filter applied to from_dataset before key extraction or join; an expression string is parsed as where is.

None condition str | Expr | None

Boolean expression (or expression string) identifying landmark rows for "before"/"after" or the current-row condition for "exists_after"/"exists_before".

None inclusive bool

Whether the landmark row itself is included in the flag (for "before"/"after"). Default True.

True flag_no_ref_groups bool

If False, groups without a landmark condition match get None instead of being flagged (for "before"/"after"). Default True.

True flag_all bool

If True, all tied extreme values receive the flag (for "first"/"last"). Default False.

False flag_value str

Value to assign when condition is met (default "Y").

'Y' false_value str | None

Value to assign when condition is not met. Default None (null).

None

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target appended; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Raises:

Type Description VerbUsageError

When a parameter irrelevant to the selected criteria mode is passed.

DerivationError

When a mode-required parameter is missing, or a bare-identifier criteria matches neither a keyword nor a column.

References

admiral derive_var_extreme_flag (pharmaverse): the order of "first"/"last", a missing value last in each key (ADR-0020).

Examples:

First observation per group::

advs = (
    vs_raw.adam
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
          by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .to_frame()
)

Existence flag from external dataset::

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl
    .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
          from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
          source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
    .to_frame()
)

Relative flag — before first PD::

result = (
    response.adam
    .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
          condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
          order_by="AVISITN", by=["USUBJID"],
          inclusive=True)
    .to_frame()
)

Population flag from the treatment start date (a population flag is never blank, so non-members get "N")::

adsl = (
    adsl.adam.adsl
    .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null(),
          false_value="N")
    .to_frame()
)

def flag(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    criteria: str | pl.Expr,
    by: list[str] | None = None,
    order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
    value_col: str | None = None,
    where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    from_dataset: pl.DataFrame | list[pl.DataFrame] | None = None,
    on: list[str] | None = None,
    source_filter: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    condition: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    inclusive: bool = True,
    flag_no_ref_groups: bool = True,
    flag_all: bool = False,
    flag_value: str = "Y",
    false_value: str | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Set *target* to *flag_value* for records matching *criteria*.

    Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

    - ``"first"`` / ``"last"`` — rank-based edge detection within groups.
    - ``"max"`` / ``"min"`` — value-based extreme within groups.
    - ``"exists"`` — set-membership from external dataset(s).
    - ``"before"`` / ``"after"`` — relative to a landmark condition.
    - ``"exists_after"`` / ``"exists_before"`` — temporal/self-join flag.

    Parameters that are irrelevant to the selected criteria mode
    raise :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.VerbUsageError` instead of
    being silently ignored.  The ``flag_first`` / ``flag_last`` /
    ``flag_extreme`` / ``flag_exists`` / ``flag_relative`` wrappers
    expose each mode with only its own parameters.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output flag column.
        criteria: A Polars expression, or one of ``"first"``,
            ``"last"``, ``"max"``, ``"min"``, ``"exists"``,
            ``"before"``, ``"after"``, ``"exists_after"``,
            ``"exists_before"``.
        by: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``) for
            ``"first"``/``"last"``, ``"max"``/``"min"`` and
            ``"before"``/``"after"``.  An expression flags each row
            on its own, so *by* raises there and in the exists modes.
        order_by: Sort column(s) required for ``"first"``/``"last"``
            and ``"before"``/``"after"``.  On a tie among candidates,
            ``"last"`` takes the last input record and ``"first"`` the
            first (SAS ``LAST.``/``FIRST.``); add a sequence variable
            to remove the dependence on input order.  For
            ``"first"``/``"last"`` a missing value sorts last in each
            key, as admiral (ADR-0020): ``"last"`` takes a record with a
            missing key, and ``"first"`` takes one only when every
            candidate misses it.  SAS sorts a missing value first, so a
            QC program with PROC SORT differs on such a group.
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` take one column
            only; build one ordered key (ADTM) for date and time.
        value_col: Value column required for ``"max"``/``"min"``.
        where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates;
            rows that fail it take no part, even on a tie.
        from_dataset: External dataset(s) for ``"exists"`` and
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` criteria.
        on: Join key columns for ``"exists"`` criteria.
        source_filter: Filter applied to *from_dataset* before key
            extraction or join; an expression string is parsed as
            *where* is.
        condition: Boolean expression (or expression string) identifying landmark rows for
            ``"before"``/``"after"`` or the current-row condition for
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"``.
        inclusive: Whether the landmark row itself is included in the
            flag (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_no_ref_groups: If ``False``, groups without a landmark
            condition match get ``None`` instead of being flagged
            (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_all: If ``True``, all tied extreme values receive the
            flag (for ``"first"``/``"last"``). Default ``False``.
        flag_value: Value to assign when condition is met (default
            ``"Y"``).
        false_value: Value to assign when condition is not met.
            Default ``None`` (null).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        VerbUsageError: When a parameter irrelevant to the selected
            criteria mode is passed.
        DerivationError: When a mode-required parameter is missing,
            or a bare-identifier *criteria* matches neither a
            keyword nor a column.

    References:
        admiral ``derive_var_extreme_flag`` (pharmaverse): the order of
        ``"first"``/``"last"``, a missing value last in each key (ADR-0020).

    Examples:
        First observation per group::

            advs = (
                vs_raw.adam
                .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
                      by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Existence flag from external dataset::

            adsl = (
                dm.adam.adsl
                .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
                      from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
                      source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Relative flag — before first PD::

            result = (
                response.adam
                .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
                      condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
                      order_by="AVISITN", by=["USUBJID"],
                      inclusive=True)
                .to_frame()
            )

        Population flag from the treatment start date (a population
        flag is never blank, so non-members get ``"N"``)::

            adsl = (
                adsl.adam.adsl
                .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null(),
                      false_value="N")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    grps = by or ["USUBJID"]
    order_cols: list[str] | None = None
    if order_by is not None:
        order_cols = [order_by] if isinstance(order_by, str) else list(order_by)

    criteria_lower = criteria.lower() if isinstance(criteria, str) else None
    mode = criteria_lower if criteria_lower in _FLAG_CRITERIA_KEYWORDS else "expression"
    if mode == "expression":
        # Keyword typos ("frist") must surface as a did-you-mean error
        # before any parameter validation blames the wrong thing.
        self._check_flag_criteria_typo(target, criteria)
    self._validate_flag_params(
        target,
        criteria,
        mode,
        {
            "by": by,
            "order_by": order_by,
            "value_col": value_col,
            "where": where,
            "from_dataset": from_dataset,
            "on": on,
            "source_filter": source_filter,
            "condition": condition,
            "inclusive": inclusive,
            "flag_no_ref_groups": flag_no_ref_groups,
            "flag_all": flag_all,
            "false_value": false_value,
        },
    )

    where_expr: pl.Expr | None = None
    if where is not None:
        where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))
    # A string condition or source filter is parsed as where= is.
    if isinstance(condition, str):
        condition = parse_expression(condition, self._lazy.collect_schema())
    if isinstance(source_filter, str):
        source_filter = parse_expression(source_filter)

    false_lit = pl.lit(false_value) if false_value is not None else pl.lit(None)

    if mode in ("first", "last"):
        return self._flag_ranked(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_all=flag_all,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode in ("max", "min"):
        return self._flag_extreme(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            value_col=value_col,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode == "exists":
        return self._flag_exists(
            target,
            grps=grps,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif mode in ("before", "after"):
        return self._flag_relative(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            inclusive=inclusive,
            flag_no_ref_groups=flag_no_ref_groups,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )
    elif mode in ("exists_after", "exists_before"):
        return self._flag_temporal_exists(
            target,
            criteria_lower=mode,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
        )
    else:
        return self._flag_expression(
            target,
            criteria=criteria,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )

Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

    .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,

def criterion(
    self,
    number: int,
    *,
    condition: str | pl.Expr,
    description: str,
) -> Self:
    """Derive criterion flag triple: CRITy, CRITyFL, CRITyFN.

    Produces three columns following CDISC ADaM conventions:

    - ``CRIT{number}`` — the criterion description (constant string).
    - ``CRIT{number}FL`` — ``"Y"`` if condition is met, ``"N"`` if not.
    - ``CRIT{number}FN`` — ``1`` if met, ``0`` if not.

    When the condition is null (for example AVAL is missing), FL and FN are
    null, as admiral ``derive_vars_crit_flag()``. For a SAP rule "missing is
    not met", pass ``condition=(...).fill_null(False)``.

    References:
        admiral ``derive_vars_crit_flag(values_yn = TRUE,
        create_numeric_flag = TRUE)``, which asserts a positive
        ``crit_nr`` and a description; ADaMIG 1.3 CRITy (text, y a
        positive integer); ADR-0033.

    Args:
        number: Criterion number, 1 or more (e.g. 1 → CRIT1, CRIT1FL,
            CRIT1FN).
        condition: Boolean Polars expression defining the criterion, or
            an expression string as for ``where=``.
        description: Human-readable description stored in CRITy.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with three new columns appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        VerbUsageError: When *number* is below 1 or *description* is
            blank.

    Examples:
        Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

            adlb = (
                lb_df.adam
                .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,
                           description="AVAL >= 10")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, int) or number < 1:
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"criterion({number!r}): the criterion number is a positive integer "
            "(ADaMIG CRITy), for example criterion(1, ...)."
        )
    if not isinstance(description, str) or not description.strip():
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"criterion({number}): description= is required; CRIT{number} holds it."
        )
    if isinstance(condition, str):
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        condition = parse_expression(condition, self._lazy.collect_schema())
    col_crit = f"CRIT{number}"
    col_fl = f"CRIT{number}FL"
    col_fn = f"CRIT{number}FN"

    desc_expr = pl.lit(description).alias(col_crit)
    fl_expr = (
        pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit("Y")).when(~condition).then(pl.lit("N")).alias(col_fl)
    )
    fn_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit(1)).when(~condition).then(pl.lit(0)).alias(col_fn)

    return self._chain(desc_expr, fl_expr, fn_expr, verb="criterion")

    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")

def pin(
    self,
    domain: str | None = None,
    df: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
    **frames: pl.DataFrame,
) -> Self:
    """Attach one or more reference domains to this pipeline.

    Two equivalent forms, usable together — the keyword form declares
    every upstream dataset in one call (kwarg name = dataset name),
    mirroring the define.yaml ``inputs:`` block:

    * ``pin("DM", dm_df)`` — one pin, positional.
    * ``pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df)`` — several pins, one call.

    The name/frame pair is positional-only, so *every* keyword except
    ``join_on`` is a dataset pin — no dataset name is reserved.

    Args:
        domain: Logical name (e.g. ``"DM"``, ``"ADSL"``, ``"TV"``).
        df: The reference DataFrame for *domain*.  A LazyFrame is
            collected once, at pin time.
        join_on: Column(s) used to join these references into the
            pipeline.  Applies to every pin in this call; pin
            separately for per-domain join keys.
        **frames: ``NAME=frame`` pins (names are upper-cased).

    Returns:
        Self: A shallow copy with the pin(s) attached; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When called with no pins, a name without its
            frame (or vice versa), or a pinned value that is not a
            DataFrame/LazyFrame.

    Examples:
        Pin DM to an AE pipeline for study-day derivation::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
                .pin("DM", dm_df)
                .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Declare every upstream dataset of an ADaM pipeline at once::

            adae = (
                ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
                .pin(ADSL=adsl_df, EX=ex_df)
                .join_adsl("TRTSDT", "SAFFL")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    pins: dict[str, pl.DataFrame] = {}
    if domain is not None or df is not None:
        if domain is None or df is None:
            raise DerivationError(
                "pin() requires both a domain name and a DataFrame — "
                'pin("DM", dm_df) — or keyword pins: pin(DM=dm_df).'
            )
        pins[domain] = df
    pins.update(frames)
    if not pins:
        raise DerivationError(
            'pin() requires at least one pin: pin("DM", dm_df) or pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df).'
        )

    new = copy.copy(self)
    pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = dict(getattr(self, "_pinned", {}))
    for name, frame in pins.items():
        frame = _pin_frame(name, frame)
        key = name.upper()
        if key in pinned:
            warnings.warn(
                f"Pin '{key}' replaced. Use .repin() to suppress this warning.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        pinned[key] = (frame, _normalize_key(join_on))
    new._pinned = pinned
    return new

def fk_policy(self, severity: str) -> Self:
    """Set the FK-check severity for this pipeline.

    The check runs once, at the public ``to_frame()`` (and the
    terminal verbs that call it), on the final frame, with the
    severity in force at that point.  The order of ``pin``,
    ``fk_policy`` and the verbs does not matter.  It checks
    ``USUBJID`` against the pinned ``DM`` (SDTM) or ``ADSL`` (ADaM),
    and the SDTM trial-design keys of ``_FK_RULES`` against a pinned
    TA, TE or TV.

    Args:
        severity: One of ``"warn"`` (emit ``UserWarning``),
            ``"error"`` (raise ``DerivationError``), or ``"off"``
            (disable FK checks).

    Returns:
        Self: A shallow copy with the updated policy.

    Examples:
        Enforce strict FK checking::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .pin("DM", dm_df)
                .fk_policy("error")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if severity not in ("warn", "error", "off"):
        raise DerivationError(
            f"fk_policy severity must be 'warn', 'error', or 'off', got '{severity}'"
        )
    new = copy.copy(self)
    new._fk_severity = severity
    return new

def to_frame(self) -> DataFrame:
    """Materialise the accumulated pipeline into a Polars DataFrame.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: The fully materialised result of all chained
            verbs — a plain ``pl.DataFrame`` at runtime, typed as
            :class:`fleet.DataFrame` so re-entering ``.sdtm`` /
            ``.adam`` / ``.tlg`` type-checks.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When collection fails because a column is
            missing — enriched with the lineage entries that
            reference the column, so the error names the verb(s)
            involved.  Also when a ``merge(validate=...)`` fails, with
            the repeated keys named, or when a foreign-key check runs
            under ``fk_policy("error")``.

    Examples:
        Collect the pipeline result::

            result = (
                df.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    try:
        df = self._lazy.collect()
    except (
        pl.exceptions.ColumnNotFoundError,
        pl.exceptions.SchemaFieldNotFoundError,
        pl.exceptions.StructFieldNotFoundError,
    ) as err:
        raise self._enrich_collect_error(err) from err
    except pl.exceptions.ComputeError as err:
        named = next(
            (
                msg
                for check in getattr(self, "_pending_join_checks", [])
                if (msg := check.explain_validation()) is not None
            ),
            None,
        )
        if named is None:
            raise self._polars_error(err) from err
        raise DerivationError(named) from err
    except pl.exceptions.PolarsError as err:
        raise self._polars_error(err) from err
    run_checks = getattr(self, "_run_fk_checks", None)
    if run_checks is not None and not _is_internal_collect():
        run_checks(df)
    join_checks = getattr(self, "_pending_join_checks", [])
    # Rebind, never mutate: earlier chain copies keep their own queue.
    self._pending_join_checks = []
    for check in join_checks:
        check.warn_many_to_many()
    return cast("DataFrame", df)

                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .to_dataset_json("outputs/dm.json", domain="DM")
            )
    """
    from fleet.io.dataset_json import metadata_from_define, save_dataset_json

    meta: dict[str, Any] = {}
    source = getattr(self, "_spec_source", None)
    if source is not None and source[1].upper() == domain.upper():
        meta = metadata_from_define(source[0], source[1])
    if label is not None:
        meta["label"] = label
    return save_dataset_json(self.to_frame(), path, domain=domain, **meta)

trail()

Log a table of each derived variable's origin in the pipeline.

Renders the accumulated variable lineage — the verb that produced each column and the source columns it consumed, including cross-domain pin sources — as a table through the "fleet" logger (INFO level, stdout by default — see :mod:fleet.core.log), then returns the namespace unchanged so the chain continues. Unlike inspect, nothing is materialised: the trail is pure metadata captured automatically on every verb call.

Only derived variables appear; columns that pass through untouched from the source frame are not listed. When a variable is derived more than once, each derivation is shown in pipeline order. Variables with no source column (e.g. hardcoded constants) are marked (literal).

Name Type Description Self Self

The same namespace instance (unchanged); call further verbs or .to_frame() to continue.

Examples:

Print the origin of every derived variable before collecting::

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .trail()
    .to_frame()
)
Source code in src/fleet/core/_verb_mixin.py 
def trail(self) -> Self:
    """Log a table of each derived variable's origin in the pipeline.

    Renders the accumulated variable lineage — the verb that produced
    each column and the source columns it consumed, including
    cross-domain pin sources — as a table through the ``"fleet"``
    logger (INFO level, stdout by default — see
    :mod:`fleet.core.log`), then returns the namespace unchanged so
    the chain continues. Unlike ``inspect``, nothing is
    materialised: the trail is pure metadata captured automatically on
    every verb call.

    Only *derived* variables appear; columns that pass through untouched
    from the source frame are not listed. When a variable is derived more
    than once, each derivation is shown in pipeline order. Variables with
    no source column (e.g. hardcoded constants) are marked ``(literal)``.

    Returns:
        Self: The same namespace instance (unchanged); call further
            verbs or ``.to_frame()`` to continue.

    Examples:
        Print the origin of every derived variable before collecting::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
                .pin("DM", dm)
                .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                .trail()
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core.lineage import lineage_of, pin_lineage_of

    fleet_log.ensure_default_handler()
    nodes = lineage_of(self)
    # A pin read that made no lineage node (join_adsl) still gets its own row.
    named = {node.name for node in nodes}
    nodeless = [dep for dep in pin_lineage_of(self) if dep.target_col not in named]
    if not nodes and not nodeless:
        logger.info("Variable trail: (empty — no derivations recorded yet)")
        return self

    def _label(dep: Any) -> str:
        cols = ", ".join(dep.source_cols) if dep.source_cols else "*"
        label = f"{dep.source_domain}.{cols}"
        if dep.relationship != "derivation":
            label += f" [{dep.relationship}]"
        return label

    entries: list[tuple[str, str, list[str], str | None]] = []
    for node in nodes:
        # Drop bare local sources already attributed to a pinned domain.
        covered = {col for dep in node.pin_sources for col in dep.source_cols}
        local = [src for src in node.sources if src not in covered]
        labels = [_label(dep) for dep in node.pin_sources]
        entries.append((node.name, node.verb, [*local, *labels], node.domain))
    for dep in nodeless:
        entries.append((dep.target_col, dep.verb, [_label(dep)], dep.target_domain))
    has_domain = any(entry[3] for entry in entries)
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for i, (name, verb, origins, domain) in enumerate(entries, start=1):
        shown = list(dict.fromkeys(origins))
        row: dict[str, object] = {
            "#": i,
            "Variable": name,
            "Verb": verb,
            "Origin": ", ".join(shown) if shown else "(literal)",
        }
        if has_domain:
            row["Domain"] = domain or "—"
        rows.append(row)

    table = pl.DataFrame(rows)
    logger.info("Variable trail (%d derivation(s)):", table.height)
    with pl.Config(
        tbl_hide_dataframe_shape=True,
        tbl_hide_column_data_types=True,
        fmt_str_lengths=100,
        tbl_rows=table.height,
    ):
        logger.info("%s", table)
    return self

def write_parquet(
    self,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    mkdir: bool = True,
) -> DataFrame:
    """Materialise the pipeline, write to Parquet, and return the DataFrame.

    This is a drop-in alternative to ``to_frame()`` when you want to
    persist the dataset as part of the chain.

    Args:
        path: Destination file path.
        mkdir: When ``True`` (default) any missing parent directories
            are created automatically.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: The materialised result (typed as
            :class:`fleet.DataFrame` — see ``to_frame()``).

    Examples:
        Write a domain to Parquet::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                .write_parquet("outputs/dm.parquet")
            )
    """
    df = self.to_frame()
    dest = Path(path)
    if mkdir:
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    df.write_parquet(dest)
    return df

def keep(self, *columns: str | list[str]) -> Self:
    """Restrict the frame to *columns*, in the given order.

    Accepts either variadic names — ``keep("STUDYID", "USUBJID")`` —
    or a single list — ``keep(["STUDYID", "USUBJID"])``.  Stays lazy.

    Args:
        *columns: Column names (or one list of names) to keep.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace continuing from the restricted plan.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When a requested column is absent (with a
            did-you-mean suggestion), or no columns are given.

    Examples:
        Keep only the submission variables::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .keep("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "SEX")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if len(columns) == 1 and isinstance(columns[0], list):
        cols: list[str] = list(columns[0])
    else:
        cols = [c for c in columns]  # type: ignore[misc]
    if not cols:
        raise DerivationError("keep() requires at least one column name.")
    require_columns("keep()", cols, self._lazy.collect_schema().names(), where="the frame")
    return self._with_lazy(self._lazy.select(cols))

def derivation(
    self,
    target: str | Derivation | None = None,
    *,
    expression: str | pl.Expr | Callable[[], pl.Expr] | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Derive *target* using an expression, lambda, or ``Derivation`` object.

    Four call forms are supported:

    **Case 1 — string (checked against an allow-list, YAML-compatible)**::

        .derivation("COL", expression="pl.col('src').cast(pl.String)")

    **Case 2 — direct ``pl.Expr``**::

        .derivation("COL", expression=pl.col("src").cast(pl.String))

    **Case 3 — zero-arg lambda returning ``pl.Expr`` (full IDE support)**::

        .derivation("COL", expression=lambda: pl.col("src").cast(pl.Int32))

    **Case 4 — ``@derivation`` object (file-based, full lineage)**::

        from specs.study01.derivations import MY_DRULE
        .derivation(MY_DRULE)

    Args:
        target: For Cases 1–3, the name of the output variable
            (required).  For Case 4, the
            :class:`~fleet.core.derivation.Derivation` object to dispatch.
        expression: A Polars expression, expression string, or zero-arg
            callable returning ``pl.Expr``.  Required for Cases 1–3.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call ``.to_frame()``
            to materialise.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: If *target* is a string but *expression* is not
            provided, or vice-versa.
        VerbUsageError: If *target* is neither a string nor a
            ``Derivation``, if *expression* is a frame-kind
            ``Derivation``, or if a lambda-style *expression* does not
            return ``pl.Expr``.

    Examples:
        Case 1 — string expression::

            result = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .derivation("SITEID", expression="pl.col('site_id').cast(pl.String)")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Case 3 — lambda::

            result = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .derivation("VISITNUM", expression=lambda: pl.col("visit").cast(pl.Int32))
                .to_frame()
            )

        Case 4 — ``@derivation`` object::

            from specs.study01.derivations import MY_DRULE

            result = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .derivation(MY_DRULE)
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core.derivation import Derivation
    from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    # Case 4: Derivation object passed as first positional arg.
    if target is not None and not isinstance(target, str):
        if not isinstance(target, Derivation):
            raise VerbUsageError(
                f"derivation() takes a target name with expression= (a string, a "
                f"pl.Expr or a zero-argument lambda) or a @derivation object, got "
                f"{type(target).__name__}."
            )
        return self._apply_derivation(target)

    # Cases 1–3 require a string target.
    if target is None:
        raise DerivationError("target is required when expression= is provided.")
    if expression is None:
        raise DerivationError("expression is required when target is a string.")
    if isinstance(expression, Derivation) and expression.kind != "column":
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"derivation('{target}'): expression= takes a column derivation, but "
            f"'{expression.name}' is kind={expression.kind!r}. Pass it alone: "
            f".derivation({expression.name})."
        )

    params = {"target": target, "expression": expression}

    # Case 2: direct pl.Expr.
    if isinstance(expression, pl.Expr):
        return self._chain(expression.alias(target), verb="derivation", params=params)

    # Case 3: lambda / zero-arg callable.
    if callable(expression) and not isinstance(expression, str):
        expr = expression()
        if not isinstance(expr, pl.Expr):
            raise VerbUsageError(
                f"expression callable must return pl.Expr, got {type(expr).__name__}"
            )
        return self._chain(expr.alias(target), verb="derivation", params=params)

    # Case 1: string checked against an allow-list.
    return self._chain(
        parse_expression(str(expression), self._lazy.collect_schema()).alias(target),
        verb="derivation",
        params=params,
    )

duration(

    *,
    start,
    end,
    unit="days",
    add_one=None,
    out="numeric"

Compute the duration between two date/datetime columns.

Supports column references (str) and Polars expressions for start and end; an expression is read by its type, as a column is. --DTC text is read by its date part for day-based units and by its date-time for hours, minutes and seconds; a partial value gives null, and for hours, minutes and seconds a warning gives the count of text values with no time.

The add_one parameter controls inclusive counting:

  • None (default): auto-resolves from the target suffix and the unit. *DY targets in days use the CDISC study-day convention (no day 0). Days, weeks, months and years add one day before the division; hours, minutes and seconds give the raw difference (PK elapsed time).
  • True: add one day (day-based units) or one unit (sub-day).
  • False: raw difference.

One is added only when the end is on or after the start, as admiral compute_duration does: an end one day before the start gives -1, never 0. Weeks, months and years divide the day count by 7, 30.4375 and 365.25, so this verb does not give a completed age in years.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output column.

required start str | Expr

Start date column name or expression.

required end str | Expr

End date column name or expression.

required unit Literal['seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', 'days', 'weeks', 'months', 'years']

Duration unit — "seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days" (default), "weeks", "months", "years".

'days' add_one bool | None

Override for inclusive counting.

None out Literal['numeric', 'iso8601']

Output format — "numeric" (default) or "iso8601". "iso8601" keeps the sign (-PT15M), writes hours, minutes and seconds from the total (PT1H30M) and adds one only when add_one=True is given (an elapsed time, P9D for 1 to 10 January). Weeks give null with a warning for a span that is not whole weeks; months and years raise. "iso8601" is incompatible with the *DY study-day convention: pass add_one explicitly (or use a non-DY target) to combine them.

'numeric'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target appended; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

On an unknown unit/out value, when out="iso8601" is combined with a *DY target while add_one is unset (the study-day convention would silently override the requested format), with months or years, or when a column holds numbers (no date origin is guessed).

References

ISO 8601 durations and SDTMIG 3.4 --ELTM; admiral compute_duration; ADR-0011 and ADR-0022.

Examples:

ISO 8601 duration::

ex = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .date("EXSTDTC", source="dose_start")
    .date("EXENDTC", source="dose_end")
    .duration("EXDUR", start="EXSTDTC", end="EXENDTC",
              out="iso8601")
    .to_frame()
)

Treatment duration in days::

adsl = (
    dm_df.adam.adsl
    .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")

def duration(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    start: str | pl.Expr,
    end: str | pl.Expr,
    unit: Literal["seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days", "weeks", "months", "years"] = "days",
    add_one: bool | None = None,
    out: Literal["numeric", "iso8601"] = "numeric",
) -> Self:
    """Compute the duration between two date/datetime columns.

    Supports column references (``str``) and Polars expressions
    for *start* and *end*; an expression is read by its type, as a
    column is.  ``--DTC`` text is read by its date part for
    day-based units and by its date-time for hours, minutes and
    seconds; a partial value gives null, and for hours, minutes and
    seconds a warning gives the count of text values with no time.

    The ``add_one`` parameter controls inclusive counting:

    - ``None`` (default): auto-resolves from the target suffix and the
      unit.  ``*DY`` targets in days use the CDISC study-day
      convention (no day 0).  Days, weeks, months and years add one
      **day** before the division; hours, minutes and seconds give
      the raw difference (PK elapsed time).
    - ``True``: add one day (day-based units) or one unit (sub-day).
    - ``False``: raw difference.

    One is added only when the end is on or after the start, as
    admiral ``compute_duration`` does: an end one day before the start
    gives -1, never 0.  Weeks, months and years divide the day count
    by 7, 30.4375 and 365.25, so this verb does not give a completed
    age in years.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output column.
        start: Start date column name or expression.
        end: End date column name or expression.
        unit: Duration unit — ``"seconds"``, ``"minutes"``, ``"hours"``,
            ``"days"`` (default), ``"weeks"``, ``"months"``, ``"years"``.
        add_one: Override for inclusive counting.
        out: Output format — ``"numeric"`` (default) or ``"iso8601"``.
            ``"iso8601"`` keeps the sign (``-PT15M``), writes hours,
            minutes and seconds from the total (``PT1H30M``) and adds
            one only when ``add_one=True`` is given (an elapsed time,
            ``P9D`` for 1 to 10 January).  Weeks give null with a
            warning for a span that is not whole weeks; months and
            years raise.  ``"iso8601"`` is incompatible with the
            ``*DY`` study-day convention: pass ``add_one`` explicitly
            (or use a non-DY target) to combine them.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call ``.to_frame()``
            to materialise.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: On an unknown *unit*/*out* value, when
            ``out="iso8601"`` is combined with a ``*DY`` target while
            ``add_one`` is unset (the study-day convention would
            silently override the requested format), with months or
            years, or when a column holds numbers (no date origin is
            guessed).

    References:
        ISO 8601 durations and SDTMIG 3.4 ``--ELTM``; admiral
        ``compute_duration``; ADR-0011 and ADR-0022.

    Examples:
        ISO 8601 duration::

            ex = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .date("EXSTDTC", source="dose_start")
                .date("EXENDTC", source="dose_end")
                .duration("EXDUR", start="EXSTDTC", end="EXENDTC",
                          out="iso8601")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Treatment duration in days::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam.adsl
                .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if not isinstance(start, (str, pl.Expr)):
        raise VerbUsageError(f"start must be a column name (str) or pl.Expr, got {type(start)}")
    if not isinstance(end, (str, pl.Expr)):
        raise VerbUsageError(f"end must be a column name (str) or pl.Expr, got {type(end)}")
    if out not in ("numeric", "iso8601"):
        raise DerivationError(
            f"duration out={out!r} is not supported. Choose 'numeric' or 'iso8601'."
        )
    if out == "iso8601" and add_one is None and target.endswith("DY"):
        raise DerivationError(
            f"duration('{target}', out='iso8601'): targets ending in 'DY' follow the "
            "CDISC study-day convention (integer day count, no day 0) and always "
            "produce numeric output, so out='iso8601' would be ignored. Either use a "
            "target that does not end in 'DY', or pass add_one=True/False explicitly "
            "to opt out of the study-day convention and get ISO 8601 output."
        )

    duration_params = {
        "target": target,
        "start": start,
        "end": end,
        "unit": unit,
        "add_one": add_one,
        "out": out,
    }

    schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()
    sub_day = unit in ("seconds", "minutes", "hours")
    call = f"duration('{target}')"

    def _to_date_expr(col_or_expr: str | pl.Expr) -> pl.Expr:
        """Resolve a column or an expression to a date (day units) or a date-time (sub-day)."""
        if isinstance(col_or_expr, str):
            col, dtype = pl.col(col_or_expr), schema.get(col_or_expr)
        else:
            col = col_or_expr
            dtype = self._lazy.select(col).collect_schema().dtypes()[0]
        if not sub_day:
            return to_day(col, dtype, verb=call)
        refuse_number(
            col.meta.output_name(raise_if_undetermined=False) or "the column", dtype, verb=call
        )
        if dtype != pl.String:
            return col
        name = col.meta.output_name(raise_if_undetermined=False) or "the text"
        given = col.str.strip_chars().fill_null("") != ""
        return warn_on_collect(
            datetime_part(col),
            given & datetime_part(col).is_null(),
            lambda n, values: (
                f"{call}: {n} value(s) of {name} have no hour and minute, or are not "
                f"ISO 8601, so {target} is null for them. To impute a time with a flag, "
                f"derive a *DTM variable with .date() first. Values: {values}"
            ),
            dtype=pl.Datetime("us"),
            shown=col,
        )

    s_expr = _to_date_expr(start)
    e_expr = _to_date_expr(end)

    valid_units = {
        "seconds",
        "minutes",
        "hours",
        "days",
        "weeks",
        "months",
        "years",
    }
    if unit not in valid_units:
        raise DerivationError(
            f"duration unit={unit!r} is not supported. Choose one of: {sorted(valid_units)}"
        )

    if sub_day:
        s_dtm = s_expr.cast(pl.Datetime("us"))
        e_dtm = e_expr.cast(pl.Datetime("us"))
        seconds = (e_dtm - s_dtm).dt.total_seconds()
        diff_s = seconds.cast(pl.Float64)
        if unit == "seconds":
            diff = diff_s.cast(pl.Int64)
        elif unit == "minutes":
            diff = diff_s / 60.0
        else:  # hours
            diff = diff_s / 3600.0
    else:
        diff_days = (e_expr - s_expr).dt.total_days()
        divisor = {"days": 1, "weeks": 7.0, "months": 30.4375, "years": 365.25}[unit]
        diff = diff_days if unit == "days" else diff_days.cast(pl.Float64) / divisor

    if out == "iso8601":
        if unit in ("months", "years"):
            raise DerivationError(
                f"{call}: out='iso8601' with unit='{unit}' would cut the day count to whole "
                f"{unit}, because a month or a year has no fixed length. Use unit='days'."
            )
        if sub_day:
            iso_expr = _iso_clock(seconds, unit, add_one=add_one is True)
        else:
            iso_expr = _iso_days(
                diff_days, unit, add_one=add_one is True, call=call, target=target
            )
        return self._chain(iso_expr.alias(target), verb="duration", params=duration_params)

    # Resolve add_one
    if add_one is None:
        if target.endswith("DY") and unit == "days":
            # CDISC study day: +1 if >= 0, no day 0
            result_expr = cdisc_day(diff).cast(pl.Int64).alias(target)
            return self._chain(result_expr, verb="duration", params=duration_params)
        add_one = not sub_day

    if add_one and sub_day:
        result_expr = cdisc_day(diff).alias(target)
    elif add_one:
        inclusive = pl.when(diff_days >= 0).then(diff_days + 1).otherwise(diff_days)
        result_expr = (
            inclusive if unit == "days" else inclusive.cast(pl.Float64) / divisor
        ).alias(target)
    else:
        result_expr = diff.alias(target)

    return self._chain(result_expr, verb="duration", params=duration_params)

def study_day(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    date_col: str,
    ref_col: str | None = None,
    ref_pin: str | None = None,
    ref_df: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    dm: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Derive a CDISC study day variable from a date column and reference date.

    Uses the CDISC algorithm: ``date - ref_date + 1`` when
    ``date >= ref_date``, else ``date - ref_date`` (no day 0), on the
    date portion of each value (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4.4): a time
    part is ignored, and a partial date gives null.

    The reference date is resolved in this order:

    1. Explicit ``ref_df=`` parameter (highest priority).  ``dm=``
       and ``adsl=`` are accepted aliases of ``ref_df=`` matching
       the SDTM/ADaM vocabulary.
    2. Pinned domain (via ``.pin(...)``).
    3. ``ref_col`` already present in the current frame.
    4. Actionable ``LookupError``.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output study day variable
            (e.g. ``"AESTDY"``, ``"ASTDY"``).
        date_col: Column containing the date to measure from.
        ref_col: Reference date column name.  Defaults to
            ``_STUDY_DAY_REF_COL`` class constant (``RFSTDTC`` on
            SDTM, ``TRTSDT`` on ADaM).
        ref_pin: Pinned domain name.  Defaults to
            ``_STUDY_DAY_REF_PIN`` class constant (``DM`` on SDTM,
            ``ADSL`` on ADaM).
        ref_df: Optional explicit DataFrame override — bypasses pinning.
            Lineage records no pinned domain for it, unless *ref_pin*
            names one.
        dm: Alias of *ref_df* (SDTM vocabulary); lineage records DM.
        adsl: Alias of *ref_df* (ADaM vocabulary); lineage records ADSL.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        LookupError: If the reference date cannot be resolved from
            any source.
        VerbUsageError: If more than one of *ref_df* / *dm* / *adsl*
            is given.
        DerivationError: If the reference frame has two different
            reference dates for one subject (ADR-0032).

    Examples:
        Derive study day from pinned reference::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .pin("DM", dm_df)
                .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                .to_frame()
            )

        ADaM study day::

            adae = (
                ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
                .pin("ADSL", adsl_df)
                .study_day("ASTDY", date_col="ASTDT")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core.lineage import record_pin_lineage

    provided = [f for f in (ref_df, dm, adsl) if f is not None]
    if len(provided) > 1:
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"study_day() accepts only one of ref_df= / dm= / adsl= — got {len(provided)}."
        )
    ref_df = provided[0] if provided else None
    # The domain a reference frame stands for: dm= is DM, adsl= is ADSL on both
    # namespaces; an anonymous ref_df= is no pinned domain unless ref_pin= names one.
    ref_domain: str | None = None
    if dm is not None:
        ref_domain = "DM"
    elif adsl is not None:
        ref_domain = "ADSL"
    elif ref_df is not None and ref_pin is not None:
        ref_domain = ref_pin.upper()

    # Resolve defaults from class constants
    _ref_col = ref_col if ref_col is not None else self._STUDY_DAY_REF_COL
    _ref_pin = ref_pin if ref_pin is not None else self._STUDY_DAY_REF_PIN

    schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()

    # Resolve reference date source: explicit frame, then pin, then frame column.
    if ref_df is not None:
        source_df = ref_df
        join_key = ["USUBJID"]
    elif _ref_pin.upper() in getattr(self, "_pinned", {}):
        source_df = self._require_pin(_ref_pin.upper(), "study_day", columns=[_ref_col])
        join_key = self._pin_join_key(_ref_pin.upper())
        ref_domain = _ref_pin.upper()
    elif _ref_col in schema.names():
        # ref_col already in frame — no join needed; stays lazy.
        date_expr = to_day(pl.col(date_col), schema.get(date_col), verb="study_day")
        ref_expr = to_day(pl.col(_ref_col), schema.get(_ref_col), verb="study_day")
        diff = (date_expr - ref_expr).dt.total_days()
        study_day_expr = cdisc_day(diff).alias(target)
        return self._chain(
            study_day_expr,
            verb="study_day",
            params={"target": target, "date_col": date_col, "ref_col": _ref_col},
        )
    else:
        source_df = self._require_pin(_ref_pin.upper(), "study_day", columns=[_ref_col])
        join_key = self._pin_join_key(_ref_pin.upper())

    df = self._lazy.collect()

    # Join, compute, drop temp column
    ref_slim = refuse_repeated_keys(
        "study_day()",
        source_df.select(
            [c for c in dict.fromkeys(join_key + [_ref_col]) if c in source_df.columns]
        ),
        join_key,
        source=ref_domain or "the reference frame",
    )

    _ref_tmp = f"__pin_{_ref_col}__"
    ref_slim = ref_slim.rename({_ref_col: _ref_tmp})

    df = df.join(ref_slim, on=join_key, how="left", nulls_equal=True, maintain_order="left")

    date_expr = to_day(pl.col(date_col), df.schema.get(date_col), verb="study_day")
    ref_expr = to_day(pl.col(_ref_tmp), df.schema.get(_ref_tmp), verb="study_day")

    diff = (date_expr - ref_expr).dt.total_days()
    study_day_expr = cdisc_day(diff).alias(target)
    df = df.with_columns(study_day_expr).drop(_ref_tmp)

    new = self._materialise_then(df)

    # Record variable lineage
    from fleet.core.dag import VariableNode
    from fleet.core.lineage import sanitise_params

    node_params: dict[str, Any] = {"target": target, "date_col": date_col, "ref_col": _ref_col}
    if ref_domain is not None:
        node_params["ref_pin"] = ref_domain
    if ref_df is not None and ref_domain is None:
        node_params["ref_df"] = ref_df  # an anonymous frame: to_spec_yaml writes a stub
    var_lineage: list = list(getattr(new, "_lineage", []))
    var_lineage.append(
        VariableNode(
            name=target,
            verb="study_day",
            sources=[date_col, _ref_col],
            method=f"{self.__class__.__module__}.{self.__class__.__qualname__}.study_day",
            domain=getattr(new, "_domain", None),
            params=sanitise_params(node_params),
        )
    )
    new._lineage = var_lineage

    if ref_domain is not None:
        record_pin_lineage(
            new,
            target_col=target,
            verb="study_day",
            source_domain=ref_domain,
            source_cols=[_ref_col],
            join_key=join_key,
            relationship="derivation",
        )
    return new

validate(
    dataset_or_domain,
    *,
    version=None,
    rules_engine_path=None,
    custom_rules=None,
    report="smart",
    on_fail="warn"
)

Run CDISC conformance validation and report the findings.

Returns a namespace copy so the chain can continue after validation; the full :class:~fleet.validation.models.ValidationResult is retrievable via the :attr:last_validation property. The report is emitted through the "fleet.validation" logger (stdout by default — see :mod:fleet.core.log).

Every input comes from a run setup (:func:fleet.validation.run_setup.build_run_setup): an explicit argument, then the study config found from the working directory, then FLEET_RULES_ENGINE (engine only), then the built-in default (SDTMIG 3.4, ADaMIG 1.3). The namespace gives the standard. The report header prints each input with its source.

Issues are cross-linked to the chain's own variable lineage, so a finding on a column this pipeline derived also reports the verb that produced it (see :func:fleet.validation.lineage_join.enrich_with_lineage).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dataset_or_domain str

Domain code (SDTM: e.g. "DM") or dataset name (ADaM: e.g. "ADSL").

required version str | None

IG version, "3-4" or "3.4". Defaults to sdtm.ig_version / adam.ig_version in the study config, else the built-in default.

None rules_engine_path Path | None

Engine executable. Defaults to validation.engine_path, then FLEET_RULES_ENGINE, then the managed install.

None custom_rules str | Path | None

Directory of custom rule YAML files, passed to the engine via -lr. Defaults to validation.custom_rules.

None report Literal['smart', 'summary', 'full']

Report detail level — "smart" (default) for a deduplicated view grouping identical findings with row ranges, "summary" for one line per issue, "full" for every individual finding expanded.

'smart' on_fail Literal['warn', 'raise', 'ignore']

What to do when a finding blocks (every CORE finding that validation.accepted in the study config does not list, ADR-0017) — "warn" (default) emits a UserWarning and continues, "raise" raises :class:~fleet.core.exceptions.ValidationError, "ignore" continues silently.

'warn'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

A namespace copy carrying the result in last_validation (for continued chaining).

Raises:

Type Description ValidationSetupError

The validation could not run, in every on_fail mode: no rules engine is installed or the given engine path does not exist, the dataset name belongs to the other standard (adae.adam.validate("AE")), the IG version is not supported, the custom rules directory is missing, or the engine crashed, timed out (validation.timeout) or wrote no report.

ValidationError

When a finding blocks and on_fail="raise".

DerivationError

On an invalid on_fail value.

Examples:

Validate an SDTM domain::

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .validate("DM")
    .to_frame()
)

Gate a CI pipeline on the ADaM validation outcome::

adsl = (
    dm_df.adam.adsl
    .validate("ADSL", on_fail="raise")
    .to_frame()
)

def validate(
    self,
    dataset_or_domain: str,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    rules_engine_path: Path | None = None,
    custom_rules: str | Path | None = None,
    report: Literal["smart", "summary", "full"] = "smart",
    on_fail: Literal["warn", "raise", "ignore"] = "warn",
) -> Self:
    """Run CDISC conformance validation and report the findings.

    Returns a namespace copy so the chain can continue after
    validation; the full :class:`~fleet.validation.models.ValidationResult`
    is retrievable via the :attr:`last_validation` property.  The
    report is emitted through the ``"fleet.validation"`` logger
    (stdout by default — see :mod:`fleet.core.log`).

    Every input comes from a run setup
    (:func:`fleet.validation.run_setup.build_run_setup`): an explicit
    argument, then the study config found from the working directory,
    then ``FLEET_RULES_ENGINE`` (engine only), then the built-in
    default (SDTMIG 3.4, ADaMIG 1.3).  The namespace gives the
    standard.  The report header prints each input with its source.

    Issues are cross-linked to the chain's own variable lineage, so a
    finding on a column this pipeline derived also reports the verb
    that produced it (see
    :func:`fleet.validation.lineage_join.enrich_with_lineage`).

    Args:
        dataset_or_domain: Domain code (SDTM: e.g. ``"DM"``) or
            dataset name (ADaM: e.g. ``"ADSL"``).
        version: IG version, ``"3-4"`` or ``"3.4"``.  Defaults to
            ``sdtm.ig_version`` / ``adam.ig_version`` in the study
            config, else the built-in default.
        rules_engine_path: Engine executable.  Defaults to
            ``validation.engine_path``, then ``FLEET_RULES_ENGINE``,
            then the managed install.
        custom_rules: Directory of custom rule YAML files, passed to
            the engine via ``-lr``.  Defaults to
            ``validation.custom_rules``.
        report: Report detail level — ``"smart"`` (default) for a
            deduplicated view grouping identical findings with row
            ranges, ``"summary"`` for one line per issue, ``"full"``
            for every individual finding expanded.
        on_fail: What to do when a finding blocks (every CORE finding
            that ``validation.accepted`` in the study config does not
            list, ADR-0017) — ``"warn"`` (default) emits a
            ``UserWarning`` and continues, ``"raise"`` raises
            :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.ValidationError`,
            ``"ignore"`` continues silently.

    Returns:
        Self: A namespace copy carrying the result in
            ``last_validation`` (for continued chaining).

    Raises:
        ValidationSetupError: The validation could not run, in every
            *on_fail* mode: no rules engine is installed or the given
            engine path does not exist, the dataset name belongs to the other
            standard (``adae.adam.validate("AE")``), the IG version is
            not supported, the custom rules directory is missing, or
            the engine crashed, timed out (``validation.timeout``) or
            wrote no report.
        ValidationError: When a finding blocks and
            ``on_fail="raise"``.
        DerivationError: On an invalid *on_fail* value.

    Examples:
        Validate an SDTM domain::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                .validate("DM")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Gate a CI pipeline on the ADaM validation outcome::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam.adsl
                .validate("ADSL", on_fail="raise")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core.lineage import latest_lineage_of
    from fleet.validation.lineage_join import enrich_with_lineage
    from fleet.validation.run_setup import build_run_setup, missing_engine_reason
    from fleet.validation.service import ValidationService

    _check_on_fail("validate", on_fail)
    try:
        setup = build_run_setup(
            name=dataset_or_domain,
            namespace=self._VALIDATE_STANDARD,
            version=version,
            custom_rules=custom_rules,
            engine=rules_engine_path,
        )
        if setup.engine.value is None:
            raise ValidationSetupError(missing_engine_reason(setup))
        svc = ValidationService(rules_engine_path=setup.engine.value)
    except FileNotFoundError as err:
        raise ValidationSetupError(str(err)) from err

    frame = self.to_frame()
    if setup.standard.value == "adam":
        result = svc.validate_adam(
            frame,
            dataset=dataset_or_domain,
            version=setup.ig_version.value,
            custom_rules=setup.custom_rules.value,
            timeout=setup.timeout.value,
        )
    else:
        result = svc.validate_sdtm(
            frame,
            domain=dataset_or_domain,
            version=setup.ig_version.value,
            custom_rules=setup.custom_rules.value,
            timeout=setup.timeout.value,
        )

    result.apply_setup(setup)
    enrich_with_lineage(result, latest_lineage_of(self))
    result.print_report(report_type=report)
    if result.could_not_run is not None:
        raise ValidationSetupError(
            f"CDISC validation of '{dataset_or_domain}' could not run: {result.could_not_run}"
        )

    new = self._materialise_then(frame)
    new._last_validation = result
    if not result.is_valid:
        summary = (
            f"CDISC validation failed for '{dataset_or_domain}': "
            f"{len(result.errors)} error(s): findings that validation.accepted "
            "does not list. Access details via .last_validation."
        )
        _settle_on_fail(on_fail, summary, ValidationError)
    return new

compare(
    base,
    *,
    keys,
    by=None,
    pairs=None,
    variables=None,
    abs_tol=0.0,
    rel_tol=0.0,
    ignore_trailing_whitespace=False,
    blank_is_missing=False,
    allow_duplicates=False,
    max_print=50,
    base_name=None,
    candidate_name=None,
    on_fail="warn"
)

Compare the chain against a base dataset, PROC COMPARE style.

The chain is the candidate and base is the reference it is measured against. The chain is materialised, paired with the base on keys through :func:fleet.compare, and the report is printed through the "fleet.comparison" logger (stdout by default — see :mod:fleet.core.log). Differences never stop the chain by default: the verb returns a namespace copy carrying the :class:~fleet.comparison.ComparisonReport as :attr:last_comparison, so the pipeline continues.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default base DataFrame | LazyFrame

The reference dataset, as a DataFrame or LazyFrame.

required keys str | Sequence[str]

Variable(s) that identify one observation on each side. Required; the compare refuses to run when a key is missing or not unique on either side.

required by str | Sequence[str] | None

Variable(s) the report is sectioned by. They are prepended to keys automatically, label the listing's group column, and give the observation and values summaries a per-group breakdown. A group present on one side only raises a flag; the verdict stays global.

None pairs Mapping[str, str] | None

Base variable names mapped to the names the chain gives them, on top of the automatic name matching, so a renamed column is compared rather than reported missing. The report names a paired variable by its base name.

None variables str | Sequence[str] | None

Restrict the comparison to these variables, in base names, so a work-in-progress chain is checked on the columns that are finished. What is outside the restriction is neither compared nor reported as missing.

None abs_tol float

Absolute tolerance on the numeric variables; 0.0 (the default) is exact.

0.0 rel_tol float

Relative tolerance on the numeric variables, as a fraction of the base value; 0.0 (the default) is exact. A numeric pair differs when the absolute difference exceeds max(abs_tol, rel_tol * abs(base)).

0.0 ignore_trailing_whitespace bool

Strip trailing whitespace from both sides of a string before comparing, so a legacy SAS dataset's padded values equal the chain's stripped ones. Leading whitespace still differs.

False blank_is_missing bool

Read an empty string as null on both sides, keys included, as SAS does. Off by default.

False allow_duplicates bool

Pair duplicate keys by their position within each key group instead of refusing to run; the report then counts them, raises duplicate_keys and warns.

False max_print MaxPrint

Print limits for the text report (differences per variable, a (per_variable, total) pair, or None for everything). The report's listing is never truncated.

50 base_name str | None

Label for the base in the report, when known.

None candidate_name str | None

Label for the chain in the report, when known.

None on_fail Literal['warn', 'raise', 'ignore']

What to do when the datasets differ — "warn" (default) emits a UserWarning and continues, "raise" raises :class:~fleet.core.exceptions.ComparisonFailed, "ignore" continues silently.

'warn'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

A namespace copy carrying the report in last_comparison (for continued chaining).

Raises:

Type Description ComparisonFailed

When the datasets differ and on_fail="raise". A subclass of ComparisonError.

ComparisonError

When the comparison cannot run (a key missing, duplicated or of an incompatible type).

DerivationError

On an invalid on_fail value.

Examples:

Prove an independently programmed ADAE matches its base, and keep chaining::

adae_qc = (
    ae_df.adam.occds
    .source("USUBJID")
    .source("AESEQ")
    .compare(adae_prod, keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"])
    .to_frame()
)

Gate a CI script on the comparison outcome::

adsl = (
    dm_df.adam.adsl
    .source("USUBJID")
    .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", on_fail="raise")
    .to_frame()
)

Absorb the engine noise of a legacy SAS dataset without hiding a real difference::

advs = (
    vs_df.adam
    .source("USUBJID")
    .compare(
        advs_legacy,
        keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISITN"],
        rel_tol=1e-9,
        ignore_trailing_whitespace=True,
    )
    .to_frame()
)

Section the comparison by treatment arm, so a difference in one arm stands out::

adsl = (
    dm_df.adam.adsl
    .source("USUBJID")
    .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", by="TRT01P")
    .to_frame()
)

Check a work-in-progress chain on the variables that are finished, one of which the base names differently::

advs = (
    vs_df.adam
    .source("USUBJID")
    .compare(
        advs_prod,
        keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
        pairs={"AVAL": "RESULT"},
        variables=["AVAL", "AVISIT"],
    )
    .to_frame()
)

def compare(
    self,
    base: pl.DataFrame | pl.LazyFrame,
    *,
    keys: str | Sequence[str],
    by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    pairs: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    variables: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    abs_tol: float = 0.0,
    rel_tol: float = 0.0,
    ignore_trailing_whitespace: bool = False,
    blank_is_missing: bool = False,
    allow_duplicates: bool = False,
    max_print: MaxPrint = 50,
    base_name: str | None = None,
    candidate_name: str | None = None,
    on_fail: Literal["warn", "raise", "ignore"] = "warn",
) -> Self:
    """Compare the chain against a base dataset, PROC COMPARE style.

    The chain is the **candidate** and *base* is the reference it is
    measured against.  The chain is materialised, paired with the base
    on *keys* through :func:`fleet.compare`, and the report is printed
    through the ``"fleet.comparison"`` logger (stdout by default — see
    :mod:`fleet.core.log`).  Differences never stop the chain by
    default: the verb returns a namespace copy carrying the
    :class:`~fleet.comparison.ComparisonReport` as
    :attr:`last_comparison`, so the pipeline continues.

    Args:
        base: The reference dataset, as a DataFrame or LazyFrame.
        keys: Variable(s) that identify one observation on each side.
            Required; the compare refuses to run when a key is missing
            or not unique on either side.
        by: Variable(s) the report is sectioned by.  They are prepended
            to *keys* automatically, label the listing's ``group``
            column, and give the observation and values summaries a
            per-group breakdown.  A group present on one side only
            raises a flag; the verdict stays global.
        pairs: Base variable names mapped to the names the chain gives
            them, on top of the automatic name matching, so a renamed
            column is compared rather than reported missing.  The report
            names a paired variable by its **base** name.
        variables: Restrict the comparison to these variables, in
            **base** names, so a work-in-progress chain is checked on
            the columns that are finished.  What is outside the
            restriction is neither compared nor reported as missing.
        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance on the numeric variables; ``0.0``
            (the default) is exact.
        rel_tol: Relative tolerance on the numeric variables, as a
            fraction of the **base** value; ``0.0`` (the default) is
            exact.  A numeric pair differs when the absolute difference
            exceeds ``max(abs_tol, rel_tol * abs(base))``.
        ignore_trailing_whitespace: Strip trailing whitespace from both
            sides of a string before comparing, so a legacy SAS dataset's
            padded values equal the chain's stripped ones.  Leading
            whitespace still differs.
        blank_is_missing: Read an empty string as null on both sides,
            keys included, as SAS does.  Off by default.
        allow_duplicates: Pair duplicate keys by their position within
            each key group instead of refusing to run; the report then
            counts them, raises ``duplicate_keys`` and warns.
        max_print: Print limits for the text report (differences per
            variable, a ``(per_variable, total)`` pair, or ``None`` for
            everything).  The report's listing is never truncated.
        base_name: Label for the base in the report, when known.
        candidate_name: Label for the chain in the report, when known.
        on_fail: What to do when the datasets differ — ``"warn"``
            (default) emits a ``UserWarning`` and continues,
            ``"raise"`` raises
            :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.ComparisonFailed`,
            ``"ignore"`` continues silently.

    Returns:
        Self: A namespace copy carrying the report in
            ``last_comparison`` (for continued chaining).

    Raises:
        ComparisonFailed: When the datasets differ and
            ``on_fail="raise"``.  A subclass of ``ComparisonError``.
        ComparisonError: When the comparison cannot run (a key
            missing, duplicated or of an incompatible type).
        DerivationError: On an invalid *on_fail* value.

    Examples:
        Prove an independently programmed ADAE matches its base, and
        keep chaining::

            adae_qc = (
                ae_df.adam.occds
                .source("USUBJID")
                .source("AESEQ")
                .compare(adae_prod, keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Gate a CI script on the comparison outcome::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam.adsl
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", on_fail="raise")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Absorb the engine noise of a legacy SAS dataset without hiding
        a real difference::

            advs = (
                vs_df.adam
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(
                    advs_legacy,
                    keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISITN"],
                    rel_tol=1e-9,
                    ignore_trailing_whitespace=True,
                )
                .to_frame()
            )

        Section the comparison by treatment arm, so a difference in one
        arm stands out::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam.adsl
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", by="TRT01P")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Check a work-in-progress chain on the variables that are
        finished, one of which the base names differently::

            advs = (
                vs_df.adam
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(
                    advs_prod,
                    keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
                    pairs={"AVAL": "RESULT"},
                    variables=["AVAL", "AVISIT"],
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.comparison import compare as compare_frames

    _check_on_fail("compare", on_fail)
    frame = self.to_frame()
    report = compare_frames(
        base,
        frame,
        keys=keys,
        by=by,
        pairs=pairs,
        variables=variables,
        abs_tol=abs_tol,
        rel_tol=rel_tol,
        ignore_trailing_whitespace=ignore_trailing_whitespace,
        blank_is_missing=blank_is_missing,
        allow_duplicates=allow_duplicates,
        max_print=max_print,
        base_name=base_name,
        candidate_name=candidate_name,
    )
    report.print_report()

    new = self._materialise_then(frame)
    new._last_comparison = report
    if not report.is_equal:
        summary = f"{report.summary}. Access details via .last_comparison."
        _settle_on_fail(on_fail, summary, ComparisonFailed)
    return new

select(
    columns=None,
    *,
    spec=None,
    dataset=None,
    drop_pattern="^_"
)

Select and reorder columns (lazily — nothing is materialised).

Resolution order:

  1. spec + dataset: derive the ordered column list from a define.yaml. Only columns present in the frame are kept.
  2. columns: explicit list to keep (in that order).
  3. Neither: keep all current columns (subject to drop_pattern).

With a spec on an ADaM namespace, a text column the define types date becomes the date part of a complete date, and one typed datetime the date-time of a value with hours and minutes. Anything else becomes null, with one warning at collect: select never imputes. SDTM columns and every *DTC stay text, because --DTC is character (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4).

drop_pattern (default r"^_"): regex applied before the explicit selection — columns whose names match are removed. This enforces the convention that _-prefixed columns are scratch variables. Set to None to disable (e.g. during debugging). A scratch name listed in columns is removed too, unless drop_pattern=None.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default columns str | list[str] | None

Explicit list of columns to keep (in order). A single string is one column name.

None spec str | Path | None

Path to a define.yaml file.

None dataset str | None

Dataset name within the spec.

None drop_pattern str | None

Regex for columns to auto-drop.

'^_'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

A fresh namespace continuing from the selected plan.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

When a name in columns is not in the frame (with a did-you-mean suggestion).

Examples:

Keep only spec columns::

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .select(spec="specs/sdtm/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
    .to_frame()
)
