docs.text:
aval(*, unit='days', add_one=True, avalu=True)

Derive AVAL (and AVALU) from STARTDT/ADT.

AVAL = (ADT − STARTDT [+ 1 day]) / unit using the CDISC conventions (7, 30.4375, 365.25 days per week/month/year). The + 1 inclusive convention matches admiral's derive_vars_duration(add_one=TRUE). Each row takes its end as the date of ADTM, else ADT, and its start as the date of STARTDTM, else STARTDT, so one chain can mix date and date-time parameters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default unit Literal['days', 'weeks', 'months', 'years']

Output unit (default "days").

'days' add_one bool

Include both endpoints (CDISC day convention).

True avalu bool

Also stamp the AVALU unit variable (default True — a required BDS variable admiral leaves to the user). AVALU is null where AVAL is null (admiral derive_vars_duration).

True

Returns:

Name Type Description TTENamespace Self

The namespace with AVAL (and AVALU) appended; call .to_frame() to materialise.

Examples:

Analysis value in months::

adtte = (
    adsl.adam.tte
    .param("OS", "Overall Survival", start="TRTSDT",
           events={"DEATH": adsl.filter(pl.col("DTHFL") == "Y")
                                .select("USUBJID", ADT="DTHDT")},
           censors={1: adsl.select("USUBJID", ADT="LSTALVDT",
                                   EVNTDESC=pl.lit("ALIVE"))})
    .aval(unit="months")
    .to_frame()
)
Source code in src/fleet/adam/tte_namespace.py 
def aval(
    self,
    *,
    unit: Literal["days", "weeks", "months", "years"] = "days",
    add_one: bool = True,
    avalu: bool = True,
) -> Self:
    """Derive ``AVAL`` (and ``AVALU``) from ``STARTDT``/``ADT``.

    ``AVAL = (ADT − STARTDT [+ 1 day]) / unit`` using the CDISC
    conventions (7, 30.4375, 365.25 days per week/month/year).  The
    ``+ 1`` inclusive convention matches admiral's
    ``derive_vars_duration(add_one=TRUE)``.  Each row takes its end as
    the date of ``ADTM``, else ``ADT``, and its start as the date of
    ``STARTDTM``, else ``STARTDT``, so one chain can mix date and
    date-time parameters.

    Args:
        unit: Output unit (default ``"days"``).
        add_one: Include both endpoints (CDISC day convention).
        avalu: Also stamp the ``AVALU`` unit variable (default True —
            a required BDS variable admiral leaves to the user). AVALU
            is null where AVAL is null (admiral ``derive_vars_duration``).

    Returns:
        TTENamespace: The namespace with ``AVAL`` (and ``AVALU``)
            appended; call ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Examples:
        Analysis value in months::

            adtte = (
                adsl.adam.tte
                .param("OS", "Overall Survival", start="TRTSDT",
                       events={"DEATH": adsl.filter(pl.col("DTHFL") == "Y")
                                            .select("USUBJID", ADT="DTHDT")},
                       censors={1: adsl.select("USUBJID", ADT="LSTALVDT",
                                               EVNTDESC=pl.lit("ALIVE"))})
                .aval(unit="months")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if unit not in _UNIT_DAYS:
        raise DerivationError(
            f"aval() unit={unit!r} is not supported. Choose one of {sorted(_UNIT_DAYS)}."
        )
    schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()

    def day(*names: str) -> pl.Expr:
        present = [
            to_day(pl.col(n), schema.get(n), verb="aval").cast(pl.Date)
            for n in names
            if n in schema.names()
        ]
        return pl.coalesce(present) if present else pl.lit(None, dtype=pl.Date)

    days = (day("ADTM", "ADT") - day("STARTDTM", "STARTDT")).dt.total_days()
    if add_one:
        days = pl.when(days >= 0).then(days + 1).otherwise(days)
    exprs = [(days / _UNIT_DAYS[unit]).alias("AVAL")]
    if avalu:
        exprs.append(pl.when(days.is_not_null()).then(pl.lit(unit.upper())).alias("AVALU"))
    return self._chain(*exprs, verb="aval")

km_data(paramcd=None, *, by=None)

Return the (duration, event) frame survival libraries consume.

duration = AVAL and event = CNSR == 0 — exactly the inputs of lifelines.KaplanMeierFitter.fit / scikit-survival, with optional grouping columns carried through. No new dependency: just the shape.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default paramcd str | None

Restrict to one parameter (required when the frame holds several).

None by list[str] | None

Grouping columns to carry (e.g. ["TRT01P"]). Columns not present on the ADTTE rows are pulled from the pinned ADSL automatically.

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

pl.DataFrame: <subject keys> | duration | event [| by...]; the subject keys are the ADSL pin's join key, else USUBJID.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

When AVAL/CNSR are missing (call aval() first), several parameters are present and paramcd is not given, or paramcd is not in the PARAMCD values.

Warns:

Type Description UserWarning

When rows of the parameter have a null AVAL.

Examples:

Fit a KM curve per treatment arm::

km = adtte_ns.km_data("OS", by=["TRT01P"])
# lifelines: kmf.fit(km["duration"], km["event"])
Source code in src/fleet/adam/tte_namespace.py 
def km_data(
    self,
    paramcd: str | None = None,
    *,
    by: list[str] | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Return the ``(duration, event)`` frame survival libraries consume.

    ``duration = AVAL`` and ``event = CNSR == 0`` — exactly the inputs of
    ``lifelines.KaplanMeierFitter.fit`` / scikit-survival, with optional
    grouping columns carried through.  No new dependency: just the shape.

    Args:
        paramcd: Restrict to one parameter (required when the frame
            holds several).
        by: Grouping columns to carry (e.g. ``["TRT01P"]``).  Columns
            not present on the ADTTE rows are pulled from the pinned
            ADSL automatically.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: ``<subject keys> | duration | event [| by...]``;
            the subject keys are the ADSL pin's join key, else
            ``USUBJID``.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When AVAL/CNSR are missing (call ``aval()``
            first), several parameters are present and *paramcd* is
            not given, or *paramcd* is not in the PARAMCD values.

    Warns:
        UserWarning: When rows of the parameter have a null AVAL.

    Examples:
        Fit a KM curve per treatment arm::

            km = adtte_ns.km_data("OS", by=["TRT01P"])
            # lifelines: kmf.fit(km["duration"], km["event"])
    """
    df = self.to_frame()
    missing = [c for c in ("AVAL", "CNSR") if c not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise DerivationError(
            f"km_data(): missing column(s) {missing} — derive them with "
            "param() and aval() first."
        )
    if paramcd is not None:
        if "PARAMCD" not in df.columns:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"km_data(): paramcd='{paramcd}' given, but the frame has no PARAMCD column."
            )
        present = df.get_column("PARAMCD").unique(maintain_order=True).to_list()
        if paramcd not in present:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"km_data(): PARAMCD '{paramcd}' not found; present: {present}"
            )
        df = df.filter(pl.col("PARAMCD") == paramcd)
    elif "PARAMCD" in df.columns and df.get_column("PARAMCD").n_unique() > 1:
        raise DerivationError(
            "km_data(): several parameters present — pass paramcd= to pick one."
        )

    pinned = getattr(self, "_pinned", {})
    id_cols = self._pin_join_key("ADSL") if "ADSL" in pinned else ["USUBJID"]

    # Group columns absent from the ADTTE rows resolve from the pinned
    # ADSL (the admiral template's post-hoc derive_vars_merged, built in).
    needed = [c for c in (by or []) if c not in df.columns]
    if needed:
        if "ADSL" not in pinned:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"km_data(): column(s) {needed} not on the ADTTE rows and no "
                "ADSL is pinned to resolve them — pin ADSL or join_adsl() first."
            )
        adsl_df, join_on = pinned["ADSL"]
        missing = [c for c in needed if c not in adsl_df.columns]
        if missing:
            raise DerivationError(
                f"km_data(): column(s) {missing} not found on the ADTTE rows "
                "nor in the pinned ADSL."
            )
        ref = refuse_repeated_keys(
            "km_data()", adsl_df.select(list(join_on) + needed), list(join_on), source="ADSL"
        )
        df = df.join(
            ref,
            on=list(join_on),
            how="left",
            nulls_equal=True,
        )

    null_aval = df.filter(pl.col("AVAL").is_null())
    if null_aval.height:
        ids = null_aval.get_column(id_cols[-1]).head(5).to_list()
        warnings.warn(
            f"km_data(): {null_aval.height} row(s) have a null AVAL (duration), for "
            f"example {ids}. Survival fits drop them. Check STARTDT and ADT, and call "
            "aval() after the last param().",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    cols = [
        *[pl.col(c) for c in id_cols],
        pl.col("AVAL").alias("duration"),
        (pl.col("CNSR") == 0).alias("event"),
    ]
    return df.select(cols + [pl.col(c) for c in (by or [])])

docs.title: fleet.adam.tte
docs.text:
Time-to-event (ADTTE) selection engine behind df.adam.tte.param().

Each event or censor source is a plain Polars frame with the subject keys and an ADT column. :func:select_tte selects one record per subject: the first event on or before the first stop date (CNSR = 0), else the last censor record on or before it. The censor record gives the date; the stop gives CNSR and EVNTDESC (ADR-0043). It also returns a decision trace that tells why each record was selected and which rule gave the CNSR.

param_label(paramcd, domain='ADTTE')

Return the PARAM of paramcd from the study's controlled terminology.

The study is the first study_config.yaml in the working directory or above it. The label is the decode of the paramcd item in a codelist that a PARAMCD variable of the ADaM define.yaml references (the domain dataset first, then the others). fleet init ct writes the CDISC CT preferred terms as these decodes, so a PARAMCD in a pinned CDISC CT codelist resolves here too.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default paramcd str

The parameter code, for example "OS".

required domain str

The dataset whose PARAMCD codelist is read first.

'ADTTE'

Returns:

Name Type Description str str

The decode, for example "Overall Survival".

Raises:

When no source gives a label. The message names paramcd, the places searched and the fix (param=).

ADaMIG v1.3, BDS analysis parameter variables: PARAM and PARAMCD map one to one. CDISC ADaM CT (NCI EVS) has no time-to-event PARAMCD codelist; its parameter codelists are questionnaire and scale codes. ADR-0043.

docs.title: select_tte
docs.text:
select_tte(
    *,
    universe,
    start,
    events,
    censors,
    subject_keys,
    stop_at=None,
    keep_reason=None,
    by=None,
    create_datetime=False,
    retain="drop"
)

Select one time-to-event record per subject (per stratum).

The stop date of a subject is the earliest non-null stop_at date in universe. Event and censor records after it are dropped. The first event left wins (CNSR = 0, EVNTDESC = its key). A subject without an event takes the date of the last censor record left; on a date tie the censor frame given last wins. CNSR and EVNTDESC of a censored subject come from, in this order: the censor frame when its key is in keep_reason; else the stop of the subject (on a stop date tie, the first column in stop_at order); else the censor frame (CNSR = its key). CNSDTDSC always comes from the censor frame. An event or censor date before the start date is set to the start date; the CNSR does not change.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default universe DataFrame

Subject-level frame (ADSL) with start, stop_at and the subject keys.

required start str

Date column in universe that starts the clock (STARTDT).

required events dict[str, DataFrame | LazyFrame]

EVNTDESC -> frame. Each frame holds the subject keys and ADT.

required censors dict[int, DataFrame | LazyFrame]

CNSR -> frame (CNSR >= 1). Each frame holds the subject keys and ADT; EVNTDESC comes from a frame column, else it is null and a warning names the frame.

required subject_keys list[str]

Subject identifier columns (usually ["USUBJID"]).

required stop_at dict[str, tuple[int, str]] | None

ADSL date column -> (CNSR, EVNTDESC). The earliest non-null date ends the observation of the subject; its CNSR and EVNTDESC go onto a censored row.

None keep_reason list[int] | None

Censor keys whose frame keeps its own CNSR and EVNTDESC, also before a stop (for example no baseline assessment).

None by list[str] | None

Stratum columns, present in every event frame. A censor frame with none of them (for example from ADSL) is crossed with the strata of the event frames; a frame with only some raises.

None create_datetime bool

Give ADTM/STARTDTM instead of dates.

False retain Literal['drop', 'censor_at_start']

"drop" (a subject with no record left is dropped with a warning) or "censor_at_start" (censored at STARTDT with EVNTDESC = "NO EVENT OBSERVED").

'drop'

ADSL flags of start go onto the rows: <start>DTF as STARTDTF and, with create_datetime, <start>TMF as STARTTMF (admiral rules (DT|DTM)$ to DTF and DTM$ to TMF).

Returns:

Type Description tuple[DataFrame, DataFrame]

tuple[pl.DataFrame, pl.DataFrame]: The selected rows, and the decision trace (one row per candidate: kind, source, date, selected, reason, cnsr_from; also a row per record after the stop date and per subject with no record). cnsr_from names the rule that gave the CNSR of the selected row: event, keep_reason, stop_at <column>, censors key or retain.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

On a missing column (with a did-you-mean hint), a date column that is not Date/Datetime, a bad dict key, a stop_at that is not a dict of (CNSR, EVNTDESC), a CNSR used twice in stop_at or in both stop_at and censors, a keep_reason key that is not in censors, a retain value other than "drop" or "censor_at_start", or a subject with two different rows in ADSL.

References

admiral 1.5 derive_param_tte (end_dates, event_type = "negative"; a censor record takes the CNSR and set_values_to of the first end date unless consider_end_dates = FALSE); FDA Guidance for Industry, Clinical Trial Endpoints for the Approval of Cancer Drugs and Biologics (2018), PFS censoring table; EMA Guideline on the evaluation of anticancer medicinal products, Appendix 1 on methodological considerations for PFS; CDISC ADaM BDS-TTE v1.0 (CNSR, EVNTDESC, CNSDTDSC); ADR-0043 (docs/adr/0043-tte-censors-at-the-last-record-before-the-stop-date.md).

Examples:

PFS, censored at the last assessment before new therapy::

rows, trace = select_tte(
    universe=adsl,
    start="TRTSDT",
    events={"PD": adrs.filter(pl.col("AVALC") == "PD")},
    censors={1: adrs.select("USUBJID", "ADT")},
    subject_keys=["USUBJID"],
    stop_at={
        "EOSDT": (4, "END OF STUDY"),
        "NACTDT": (2, "NEW ANTICANCER THERAPY"),
    },
)

docs.title: fleet.sdtm.design
docs.text:
Study design aggregate — define the trial design once, derive every domain.

StudyDesign is the single typed source of truth for a study's structure: elements, arms (as ordered element paths), visits, criteria, and summary parameters. Every Trial Design domain (TE, TA, TV, TS, TI, TD, TM) is derived from it, so TAETORD ordering, element/epoch duplication across arms, and cross-domain FK consistency fall out mechanically instead of being hand-maintained per row.

Usage::

import fleet

design = fleet.StudyDesign(
    study_id="CDISCPILOT01",
    elements=[
        {"etcd": "SCRN", "element": "Screening", "tedur": "P14D",
         "epoch": "SCREENING"},
        {"etcd": "TRT", "element": "Treatment", "tedur": "P84D",
         "epoch": "TREATMENT"},
        {"etcd": "FU", "element": "Follow-up", "tedur": "P28D",
         "epoch": "FOLLOW-UP"},
    ],
    arms={"PBO": ["SCRN", "TRT", "FU"], "XAN_LO": ["SCRN", "TRT", "FU"]},
    arm_names={"PBO": "Placebo", "XAN_LO": "Xanomeline Low Dose"},
)
ta = design.to_ta()
frames = design.domains()       # {"TE": df, "TA": df, ...}
findings = design.audit()       # P21-style conformance pre-check

docs.title: ArmStep
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

One position of an arm path, with the TA values of that position.

A plain ETCD string in a path is the short form of a step with no override. epoch replaces the element's epoch at this position (a crossover, an element that repeats). tabranch replaces the default Randomized to <arm> text, and tatrans gives the TATRANS rule.

docs.title: StudyDesign
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Typed aggregate of a study's trial design.

arms maps each ARMCD to its ordered path of element codes — the per-arm element name/epoch/TAETORD repetition of raw TA rows is derived, never written by hand. A path entry is an ETCD string or an :class:ArmStep ({"etcd": ..., "epoch": ..., "tabranch": ..., "tatrans": ...}) for the TA values of one position. All fields accept plain dicts (Pydantic coerces), so a trial_design.yaml deserialises directly via :meth:from_yaml. An unknown key raises.

TABRANCH defaults to Randomized to <arm> on the last element that every arm shares, or on the randomized_at element when it is given. A step's tabranch replaces that text: state the real rule when the branch is not a randomization.

Each arm needs its protocol name in arm_names (TA.ARM); an arm with no name raises.

References

SDTMIG 3.4 TA (ARM is the protocol name of the arm); docs/adr/0052-a-trial-design-arm-needs-its-protocol-name.md.

audit(*, dm=None)

Run the P21-style conformance pre-check over the derived domains.

Two design checks come first: arms with the same path (FLEETTD04), and an element that repeats in one arm with no per-position epoch (FLEETTD05). An empty elements or arms section is an error, and an empty visits or criteria section a warning (FLEETTD09).

None

findings = design.audit()

docs.title: from_usdm classmethod
docs.text:
from_usdm(data, *, study_id=None)

Build a design from a CDISC USDM (DDF) study definition.

Maps the structural subset of USDM v3/v4 JSON: arms + epochs + elements + studyCells become the arm paths (with the epoch of each cell), encounters become visits, and eligibility criteria become TI rows. TI text comes from the v4 criterion item (or the v3 population criteria), with usdm:tag resolved through the syntax dictionary and XHTML removed. An identifier that starts with a digit takes an IN or EX prefix (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.5.3).

Epochs and encounters follow their previousId/nextId chain when it is complete, else the array order. An encounter's transition rules give TVSTRL and TVENRL; one warning counts the visits with no start rule. Only the first study design is mapped, with a warning when there are more. A study cell with an unknown armId, epochId or elementId raises.

ponytail: schedule timelines, objectives/endpoints, and biomedical concepts are intentionally not mapped — extend when a consumer needs them.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default data dict

Parsed USDM JSON (the {"study": ...} wrapper or the study object itself).

required study_id str | None

Override for STUDYID; defaults to the study identifier whose scope organization type is "Clinical Study Sponsor", else the first study identifier.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description StudyDesign StudyDesign

Design with the mapped structural subset.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

When the version has no study design, a study cell holds an unknown reference, a criterion has no text or no inclusion or exclusion category, a tag cannot be resolved, or two criteria give the same IETESTCD.

Examples:

Import an OpenStudyBuilder / DDF export::

import json
design = fleet.StudyDesign.from_usdm(
    json.loads(Path("usdm.json").read_text()),
    study_id="CDISCPILOT01",
)

docs.title: fleet.sdtm.tdd_audit
docs.text:
Trial Design conformance pre-check — a P21-style dry run, offline.

Encodes the published, machine-checkable conformance rules that hit Trial Design domains hardest: the SD-series cross-domain structural checks and the FDA Technical Conformance Guide TS parameter profile (TS is the only rejection-level dataset — eCTD Technical Rejection Criterion 1734).

Rule IDs reference the public Pinnacle 21 Community / FDA business rule identifiers so findings can be cross-checked against a real P21 report. Sources: FDA TCG TS parameter list (fda.gov/media/153632), PHUSE US Connect 2026 paper DS22, PharmaSUG 2023 DS-149.

ponytail: a curated high-signal subset, not the full 100+ TDM rule catalog — fleet validate runs the CDISC Rules Engine for exhaustive coverage.

Every argument is optional — checks run only when the domains they need are present. Inputs may be DataFrames, LazyFrames, or the TDD collection models (TrialElements, TrialArms, ...). docs.title: fleet.sdtm.tdd
docs.text:
Trial Design Domain (TDD) Pydantic models.

Provides row models, collection models, constrained types, and an Epoch enum for the CDISC Trial Design domains: TE, TA, TV, TS, TI, TD, TM (protocol-reference) and SV, SE (subject-level).

Each row model maps one record in the target SDTM domain and carries a _SDTM_MAP that translates Python-friendly field names to official CDISC variable names.

Each collection model wraps a list of row models and enforces integrity constraints (uniqueness, ordering, FK references) at construction time via Pydantic @model_validator. The to_polars() method converts the validated collection into a pl.DataFrame with CDISC column names.

Usage::

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialElement, TrialElements, Epoch

te = TrialElements(elements=[
    TrialElement(etcd="SCRN", element="Screening",
                 tedur="P14D", epoch=Epoch.SCREENING),
    TrialElement(etcd="TRT", element="Treatment",
                 tedur="P84D", epoch=Epoch.TREATMENT),
])
df = te.to_polars()

from_schedule(
    schedule, *, anchor="RANDOMIZATION", window=None
)

Build a visit schedule from day offsets relative to an anchor event.

Visits are sorted by offset; VISITNUM is assigned 1..N in that order and VISITDY follows the CDISC no-day-zero convention (offset 0 → day 1, negative offsets stay negative). TVSTRL is rendered deterministically from the offset, anchor, and window, so rule text stays consistent across visits and study amendments.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default schedule list[tuple[str, int]]

(visit_name, day_offset) pairs; offsets are days relative to the anchor event (day 0).

Name of the anchoring milestone (e.g. "RANDOMIZATION").

None

Returns:

Name Type Description TrialVisits TrialVisits

A validated collection ready for add_visits().

tv_rows = TrialVisits.from_schedule(
    [("Screening", -14), ("Baseline", 0), ("Week 4", 28),
     ("Week 8", 56), ("Week 12", 84)],
    anchor="RANDOMIZATION",
    window=3,

    fleet.frame(pl.DataFrame()).sdtm

docs.title: parse_trial_design
docs.text:
parse_trial_design(mermaid_text)

Parse a Mermaid flowchart into TE and TA collections.

Each subgraph ID[TITLE] is an epoch; each node inside it is an element (ETCD["Element name<br/>P14D"]); each path from the start node to an end node is an arm, named by the last |ARMCD| label on its edges. A title that is not a C99079 term is kept, upper case, as a sponsor epoch, with a warning. %% comment lines are skipped.

The diagram carries ETCD, ELEMENT, TEDUR, EPOCH and the arm paths. It does not carry ARM, TESTRL, TEENRL, TABRANCH or TATRANS, and it cannot carry a crossover or an element that repeats in one arm: YAML is the lossless round trip.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mermaid_text str

A Mermaid flowchart TD string.

required

Returns:

Type Description tuple[TrialElements, TrialArms]

tuple[TrialElements, TrialArms]: Validated collections ready for add_elements() and add_arms().

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

On an empty diagram, a line of an unknown form, a node outside a subgraph, an unlabelled fork, a cycle, a node with no edge, more than one start node, or two nodes or two arms that give the same code.

Examples:

Parse a simple 3-element design::

te, ta = parse_trial_design('''
    flowchart TD
    subgraph SCR[SCREENING]
        SCRN["Screening<br/>P14D"]
    end
    subgraph TRT[TREATMENT]
        TREAT["Treatment<br/>P84D"]
    end
    subgraph FU[FOLLOW-UP]
        FOLL["Follow-up<br/>P28D"]
    end
    SCRN --> TREAT
    TREAT --> FOLL
''')

Provides two families of verbs:

Protocol-reference verbs fetch_structure(), study_header(), add_elements(), add_arms(), add_visits(), add_parameters(), add_criteria(), add_disease_assessments(), add_milestones() — follow a fixed stage sequence.

Subject-level verbs visit_map(), element_boundaries(), epoch_assign(), study_day() — freely mixable with any existing SDTM verb.

docs.title: fetch_structure
docs.text:
fetch_structure(
    domain,
    *,
    ig_version="3-4",
    save_to=None,
    define_path=None
)

Query the CDISC Library for domain's IG structure.

When define_path is given the domain variables (including core) are read from the define.yaml first; if the domain is not found the method falls back to the online CDISC Library.

When save_to is given the fetched metadata is cached as YAML; on subsequent calls the cache is read instead of hitting the API.

SDTMIG 3.4 structures for the nine TDD domains (TE, TA, TV, TS, TI, TD, TM, SV, SE) ship with Fleet, so the default flow needs no network access and no API key; the CDISC Library is only queried for other domains or IG versions.

Keeps the IG metadata on the namespace and compares it with the static Pydantic model; each difference gives a warning. The requested domain is kept too: study_header and the add_* verb must name the same domain.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default domain str

SDTM domain code (e.g. "TE", "TA").

required ig_version str

SDTM IG version slug (default "3-4").

'3-4' save_to str | Path | None

Optional path to cache the fetched YAML. A cache that holds another domain or IG version raises.

None define_path str | Path | None

Optional path to a define.yaml. When provided, domain metadata is extracted from the spec (offline) before falling back to the CDISC Library API.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace at stage 1; call study_header() next.

Raises:

Type Description FileNotFoundError

When define_path is not a file.

ValueError

When the save_to cache holds another domain or IG version.

CTError

When the CDISC Library cannot give the domain; the message gives the cause (for example a missing API key).

Examples:

Fetch the TE structure from the CDISC Library::

te = (
    pl.DataFrame().sdtm
    .fetch_structure("TE", ig_version="3-4",
                     save_to="metadata/te_structure.yaml")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TE")
    .add_elements(te_rows)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: visit_map
docs.text:
visit_map(
    target_num,
    target_name,
    *,
    date_col,
    planned_visits,
    ref_date=None,
    tolerance=None
)

Map raw visit dates to planned visits from TV, by nearest study day.

Use it only when the CRF does not collect the visit: it never replaces a collected VISITNUM. For each row, the verb takes the planned visit whose VISITDY is nearest to the actual study day (from date_col and ref_date), within the optional tolerance window. The distance is the difference of the study-day numbers, as abs(SVSTDY - VISITDY) in a SAS program: across the missing Day 0, Day -1 is 2 days from VISITDY 1. Ties resolve to the earlier VISITNUM. When TV has ARMCD values, a row only takes a visit of its own arm or a visit with a blank ARMCD.

A dated row outside every window is an unscheduled visit. It gets the VISITNUM of the last planned visit on or before its study day plus .1, .2, ... in date order within the subject, and the VISIT UNSCHEDULED <VISITNUM>. A row with no study day gets a null. One warning gives both counts. With DOMAIN SV, one warning gives the USUBJID + VISITNUM keys that repeat.

With no tolerance, every dated record takes the nearest planned visit, however far it is, so no record is unscheduled (ADR-0035). One warning then gives the count and the largest distance.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target_num str

Name of the output VISITNUM column. An existing column of that name is replaced.

required target_name str

Name of the output VISIT column. An existing column of that name is replaced.

required date_col str

Column containing the actual visit date (ISO 8601 string).

required planned_visits TrialVisits | DataFrame

A TrialVisits collection or a DataFrame with VISITNUM, VISIT, and VISITDY columns (and optionally ARMCD).

required ref_date str | None

Column with the reference date for the study day. When it is not a column of the frame, it is read from the pinned DM, as study_day() does. When None, the frame must hold the study day in a VISITDY column.

None tolerance dict[str, int] | None

Optional {"before": n, "after": n} window in study days, boundaries inclusive: the actual study day may precede the planned VISITDY by up to before and follow it by up to after.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target_num and target_name appended.

Raises:

Type Description DerivationError

When date_col or ref_date cannot be found, when TV has arm-specific visits and the frame has no ARMCD, or when an unscheduled number would repeat a planned VISITNUM or reach the next whole number.

References

SDTMIG 3.4 SV and TV: USUBJID + VISITNUM is the SV key, VISITNUM is Req, a null TV ARMCD means all arms. The decimal number of an unscheduled visit is a sponsor convention (the CDISC pilot uses UNSCHEDULED 5.1); see docs/adr/0035-visit-map-numbers-an-unscheduled-visit.md.

Examples:

Map subject visits to planned visits::

sv = (
    raw_visits.sdtm
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="SV")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("SVSTDTC", source="visit_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .visit_map("VISITNUM", "VISIT",
               date_col="SVSTDTC",
               planned_visits=tv_rows,
               ref_date="RFSTDTC",
               tolerance={"before": 3, "after": 3})
    .to_frame()
)

docs.text:
element_boundaries(
    target_start,
    target_end,
    *,
    milestones,
    element_col="ETCD",
    subject_col="USUBJID"
)

Derive element start/end dates from milestone columns.

For each element_col value, maps the corresponding column from milestones to produce target_start. The end date is the start of the next element by start date within the subject: the verb sorts on the ISO 8601 start text (a null start last, then the row order), so the input row order does not matter. The output keeps the input row order. The last element gets a null end.

Name of the output start-date column (e.g. "SESTDTC").

required target_end str

Name of the output end-date column (e.g. "SEENDTC").

required milestones dict[str, str]

{element_code: source_date_column} mapping.

required element_col str

Column identifying the element (default "ETCD").

'ETCD' subject_col str

Column identifying the subject (default "USUBJID").

'USUBJID'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target_start and target_end appended.

Examples:

Derive SE element boundaries::

se = (
    disposition_df.sdtm
    .element_boundaries("SESTDTC", "SEENDTC",
                        milestones={"SCRN": "screening_date",
                                     "TRT": "first_dose_date"})
    .to_frame()

docs.title: epoch_assign
docs.text:
epoch_assign(
    target,
    *,
    date_col,
    epoch_ranges=None,
    se=None,
    subject_col="USUBJID",
    same_day="by_class"
)

Assign EPOCH based on date ranges or per-subject SE intervals.

With epoch_ranges, each entry maps a study-level date interval to an Epoch value; the first matching range wins. With se, the subject's own element intervals drive the assignment: for each row, the epoch of the SE record whose [SESTDTC, SEENDTC] interval contains the date (SDTMIG 3.4: EPOCH of the start or collection date/time). A blank or null SEENDTC is open-ended; an element whose dates are partial is skipped, with a warning.

On a transition date, where one element ends and the next starts, the time decides when the record and the boundary both have one. When one of them has no time, same_day decides, and one warning gives the count and the rule:

  • "by_class" (default): a Findings date (--DTC) takes the earlier element, an Events or Interventions date (--STDTC) the later one. Any other date_col name raises.
  • "earlier": the element that ends on that date.
  • "later": the element that starts on that date.

No guidance fixes this case, so state the rule in the SDRG.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output EPOCH column.

required date_col str

Column containing the date to classify.

required epoch_ranges list[dict[str, str]] | DataFrame | None

A list of {"start": date, "end": date, "epoch": str} dicts, or a DataFrame with those columns.

None se DataFrame | LazyFrame | None

An SE domain frame with USUBJID, SESTDTC, SEENDTC, and EPOCH columns. Mutually exclusive with epoch_ranges. EPOCH is Permissible in SE: an SE with no EPOCH raises.

None subject_col str

Subject key used to join se (default "USUBJID").

'USUBJID' same_day Literal['by_class', 'earlier', 'later']

The rule for a record with no time on a transition date (with se only).

'by_class'

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target appended.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

When neither or both of epoch_ranges and se are provided.

DerivationError

When same_day="by_class" and date_col is neither a --DTC nor a --STDTC name, or when se has no EPOCH.

Examples:

Stamp EPOCH onto any domain from the subject's SE intervals::

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .epoch_assign("EPOCH", date_col="AESTDTC", se=se)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: TLG Namespace
docs.text:
The df.tlg namespace produces Tables, Listings, and Graphs from ADaM datasets. Nine domain sub-namespaces expose domain-specific summary and listing methods, and each mirrors an inline fluent builder ↔ YAML-spec workflow through an open template registry.

The fleet.tlg.render sub-module converts ARD DataFrames into pharma-style HTML tables, RTF and PDF documents (RTF is built-in; PDF via WeasyPrint), editable PPTX slides, and supports pagination (paginate / paginate_listing) and HTML injection into wrapper templates for embedding in sponsor portals or Quarto documents.

import fleet  # registers df.tlg alongside df.sdtm and df.adam
import polars as pl

df.tlg.ae  # AE overview, SOC/PT, severity, grade, relationship, listing
df.tlg.vs  # Vital-signs summary
df.tlg.catalog()  # every registered template as a DataFrame

Every table/listing is a registered template: an id, its CDISC class, the namespace method that builds it, and its output type. df.tlg.catalog() (or fleet.tlg.catalog()) returns the live catalog. The fleet tlg list CLI command prints the same table.

lbt04 reads the ANRIND codes of the directions from low_values and high_values (default LOW/LOW LOW, HIGH/HIGH HIGH). When ANRIND holds codes such as H and L, set them in the spec (LBAbnormalSpec(low_values=["L"], high_values=["H"])): the table stops when no code of the data is in either list. A cell prints n/N (%), with N the subjects at risk in that direction.

docs.title: Dual-mode API
docs.text:
Fleet TLG supports two equivalent paths to the same ARD output — plus a YAML-spec front door that reproduces a table from a file alone.

Inline builderSpec objectYAML spec file 
ard = (
    adae.tlg.ae.population(adsl, adsl_filter=pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y", group_col="TRT01A")
    .by("TRTA")
    .header_rows(
        [
            OverallStat(label="Subjects with any AE"),
            OverallStat(label="Serious AEs", filter=pl.col("AESER") == "Y"),
        ]
    )
    .rows(["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"])
    .stats([Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT])
    .pools([GroupPool(label="Total", arms="*")])
    .to_ard()
)

spec = AESummarySpec(
    adsl_filter=pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y",
    header_rows=[
        OverallStat(label="Subjects with any AE"),
        OverallStat(label="Serious AEs", filter=pl.col("AESER") == "Y"),
    ],
    pools=[GroupPool(label="Total", arms="*")],
    adsl_group_col="TRT01A",
)
ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(adsl=adsl, spec=spec)

import fleet.tlg as tlg

spec = tlg.load_spec("examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml")
ard = tlg.run_spec(spec, adae, adsl=adsl)

Listings work through the same dual API: l_listing(spec=...) or the builder's .columns([...]).sort_by([...]).to_listing().

docs.title: Spec runner — YAML as a workflow
docs.text: load_spec reads a YAML file, resolves its template: id through the registry, and returns the right spec model; run_spec dispatches the spec to the template's namespace method (or a user-registered function). spec_schema returns a template's JSON schema for editor auto-complete, and register_template adds a study-specific template to the open registry.

load_spec(path)

Load a TLG spec from a YAML file, dispatching on its template id.

The file must carry template: <id>; the id resolves the concrete spec class through the template registry (built-ins and user registrations alike), so callers never need to know which spec class a YAML file belongs to. All errors name the offending file.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str | Path

Path to a YAML spec file.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description TLGSpec TLGSpec

The validated spec instance (a concrete subclass such as AEOverviewSpec), ready for run_spec().

Raises:

Type Description SchemaError

If the file is unreadable, is not valid YAML, lacks a template: id, references an unknown template, or fails spec-model validation.

Examples:

Reproduce a table from its YAML spec alone::

import fleet.tlg as tlg

spec = tlg.load_spec("specs/aet01.yaml")
ard = tlg.run_spec(spec, adae, adsl=adsl)
Source code in src/fleet/tlg/_runner.py 
def load_spec(path: str | Path) -> TLGSpec:
    """Load a TLG spec from a YAML file, dispatching on its template id.

    The file must carry ``template: <id>``; the id resolves the concrete
    spec class through the template registry (built-ins and user
    registrations alike), so callers never need to know which spec class
    a YAML file belongs to.  All errors name the offending file.

    Args:
        path: Path to a YAML spec file.

    Returns:
        TLGSpec: The validated spec instance (a concrete subclass such
            as ``AEOverviewSpec``), ready for
            [`run_spec()`][fleet.tlg.run_spec].

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If the file is unreadable, is not valid YAML, lacks
            a ``template:`` id, references an unknown template, or fails
            spec-model validation.

    Examples:
        Reproduce a table from its YAML spec alone::

            import fleet.tlg as tlg

            spec = tlg.load_spec("specs/aet01.yaml")
            ard = tlg.run_spec(spec, adae, adsl=adsl)
    """
    p = Path(path)
    try:
        text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise SchemaError(f"{p}: cannot read spec file: {exc}") from exc
    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(text)
    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
        raise SchemaError(f"{p}: invalid YAML: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise SchemaError(f"{p}: a TLG spec must be a YAML mapping, got {type(data).__name__}.")
    template_id = data.get("template")
    if not template_id:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"{p}: missing 'template:' key — load_spec() needs it to resolve "
            f"the spec class through the registry. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
        )
    meta = TEMPLATES.get(template_id)
    if meta is None:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"{p}: unknown template id {template_id!r}. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
        )
    spec_cls = resolve_spec_cls(meta)
    try:
        return spec_cls.model_validate(data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        raise SchemaError(f"{p}: invalid {spec_cls.__name__} spec:\n{exc}") from exc

run_spec(spec, df, *, adsl=None, groupby=None)

Execute a template-carrying spec against an analysis dataset.

Dispatches spec.template through the registry to the template's namespace method (built-ins) or registered function (user templates). Listings ignore adsl and groupby by design — they have no population denominator or column grouping.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spec TLGSpec

A spec carrying template=<id> (e.g. from load_spec()).

required df DataFrame

The primary analysis dataset (e.g. ADAE for aet01).

required adsl DataFrame | None

ADSL population for big-N denominators.

None groupby str | None

Treatment-arm column override.

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

pl.DataFrame: The ARD in the {cards} long layout (tables) or plain listing DataFrame (listings).

Raises:

Type Description SchemaError

If the spec carries no template id, the id is unknown, or the spec's class does not match the template's registered spec class.

Examples:

YAML file → published numbers, no code in between::

import fleet.tlg as tlg

spec = tlg.load_spec("specs/vst01.yaml")
ard = tlg.run_spec(spec, advs, adsl=adsl, groupby="TRT01A")
Source code in src/fleet/tlg/_runner.py 
def run_spec(
    spec: TLGSpec,
    df: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    groupby: str | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Execute a template-carrying spec against an analysis dataset.

    Dispatches ``spec.template`` through the registry to the template's
    namespace method (built-ins) or registered function (user
    templates).  Listings ignore *adsl* and *groupby* by design — they
    have no population denominator or column grouping.

    Args:
        spec: A spec carrying ``template=<id>`` (e.g. from
            [`load_spec()`][fleet.tlg.load_spec]).
        df: The primary analysis dataset (e.g. ADAE for ``aet01``).
        adsl: ADSL population for big-N denominators.
        groupby: Treatment-arm column override.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: The ARD in the {cards} long layout (tables) or plain
            listing DataFrame (listings).

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If the spec carries no template id, the id is
            unknown, or the spec's class does not match the template's
            registered spec class.

    Examples:
        YAML file → published numbers, no code in between::

            import fleet.tlg as tlg

            spec = tlg.load_spec("specs/vst01.yaml")
            ard = tlg.run_spec(spec, advs, adsl=adsl, groupby="TRT01A")
    """
    if spec.template is None:
        raise SchemaError(
            "run_spec() needs spec.template to dispatch through the registry "
            "— set template=<id> on the spec (or in the YAML file). Known "
            f"ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}"
        )
    meta = TEMPLATES.get(spec.template)
    if meta is None:
        raise SchemaError(f"Unknown template id {spec.template!r}. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}")
    expected_cls = resolve_spec_cls(meta)
    if not isinstance(spec, expected_cls):
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Template {meta.id!r} expects a {expected_cls.__name__} spec, "
            f"got {type(spec).__name__}. Load the spec via "
            "fleet.tlg.load_spec() to resolve the right class."
        )
    if meta.func is not None:
        return meta.func(df, adsl=adsl, spec=spec, groupby=groupby)
    ns = NAMESPACE_CLASSES[meta.namespace](df)
    method = getattr(ns, meta.method)
    if meta.output_type is OutputType.LISTING:
        return method(spec=spec)
    return method(spec=spec, adsl=adsl, groupby=groupby)

def spec_schema(template_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the JSON Schema for a template's spec model.

    Generated via Pydantic's ``model_json_schema()`` — point an editor's
    YAML language server at the exported schema for auto-complete and
    inline validation of spec files.

    Args:
        template_id: Registry id (e.g. ``"aet01"``).

    Returns:
        dict[str, Any]: The JSON Schema of the template's spec class.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If *template_id* is not registered.

    Examples:
        Export the AET01 spec schema for editor validation::

            import json

            import fleet.tlg as tlg

            schema = tlg.spec_schema("aet01")
            Path("aet01.schema.json").write_text(json.dumps(schema, indent=2))
    """
    meta = TEMPLATES.get(template_id)
    if meta is None:
        raise SchemaError(f"Unknown template id {template_id!r}. Known ids: {sorted(TEMPLATES)}")
    return resolve_spec_cls(meta).model_json_schema()

register_template(meta, fn)

Register a user-defined TLG template without touching Fleet source.

The template becomes a first-class citizen: it appears in :func:catalog, resolves through :func:get, is reachable from the inline builder via .template(meta.id), and executes from a YAML spec through run_spec().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default meta TemplateMeta

Catalog metadata for the template. Set meta.spec_cls to a custom spec model to control which YAML fields the template accepts (defaults to SummarySpecBase).

required fn TemplateFunc

Template function with signature fn(df, *, adsl, spec, groupby) -> ARD returning a DataFrame in the {cards} long layout.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description TemplateMeta TemplateMeta

The stored registry entry (meta with func attached).

Raises:

Type Description SchemaError

If meta.id is already registered or fn is not callable.

Examples:

Register and run a sponsor shell::

import fleet.tlg as tlg

def my_shell(df, *, adsl, spec, groupby):
    return df.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl, spec=spec)

tlg.register_template(
    tlg.TemplateMeta(
        id="spon01", title="Sponsor AE Shell",
        cdisc_class=tlg.CDISCClass.EVENTS, namespace="ae",
        method="my_shell", output_type=tlg.OutputType.TABLE,
        domains=("ADSL", "ADAE"), source_ref="sponsor",
        status=tlg.Status.DONE, spec_cls=tlg.AESummarySpec,
    ),
    my_shell,
)
ard = adae.tlg.ae.population(adsl).by("TRTA").template("spon01").to_ard()
Source code in src/fleet/tlg/_registry.py 
def register_template(meta: TemplateMeta, fn: TemplateFunc) -> TemplateMeta:
    """Register a user-defined TLG template without touching Fleet source.

    The template becomes a first-class citizen: it appears in
    :func:`catalog`, resolves through :func:`get`, is reachable from the
    inline builder via ``.template(meta.id)``, and executes from a YAML
    spec through [`run_spec()`][fleet.tlg.run_spec].

    Args:
        meta: Catalog metadata for the template.  Set ``meta.spec_cls``
            to a custom spec model to control which YAML fields the
            template accepts (defaults to ``SummarySpecBase``).
        fn: Template function with signature
            ``fn(df, *, adsl, spec, groupby) -> ARD`` returning a
            DataFrame in the {cards} long layout.

    Returns:
        TemplateMeta: The stored registry entry (*meta* with ``func``
            attached).

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If ``meta.id`` is already registered or *fn* is not
            callable.

    Examples:
        Register and run a sponsor shell::

            import fleet.tlg as tlg

            def my_shell(df, *, adsl, spec, groupby):
                return df.tlg.ae.t_summary(groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl, spec=spec)

            tlg.register_template(
                tlg.TemplateMeta(
                    id="spon01", title="Sponsor AE Shell",
                    cdisc_class=tlg.CDISCClass.EVENTS, namespace="ae",
                    method="my_shell", output_type=tlg.OutputType.TABLE,
                    domains=("ADSL", "ADAE"), source_ref="sponsor",
                    status=tlg.Status.DONE, spec_cls=tlg.AESummarySpec,
                ),
                my_shell,
            )
            ard = adae.tlg.ae.population(adsl).by("TRTA").template("spon01").to_ard()
    """
    if meta.id in TEMPLATES:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Template id {meta.id!r} is already registered "
            f"({TEMPLATES[meta.id].title!r}). Template ids are stable "
            "identifiers — pick a new id or unregister_template() first."
        )
    if not callable(fn):
        raise SchemaError(f"Template function for {meta.id!r} must be callable, got {fn!r}.")
    entry = dataclasses.replace(meta, func=fn)
    TEMPLATES[meta.id] = entry
    return entry

def catalog() -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Return the template catalog as a DataFrame (one row per template).

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: Columns ``id``, ``title``, ``cdisc_class``,
            ``namespace``, ``method``, ``output_type``, ``domains``,

    """
    return pl.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "id": m.id,
                "title": m.title,
                "cdisc_class": m.cdisc_class.value,
                "namespace": m.namespace,
                "method": m.method,
                "output_type": m.output_type.value,
                "domains": list(m.domains),
                "source_ref": m.source_ref,
                "status": m.status.value,
            }
            for m in TEMPLATES.values()

    )

Root TLG namespace, accessed as df.tlg.

This namespace acts as a router to domain-specific sub-namespaces. It holds a reference to the underlying DataFrame and passes it to sub-namespaces on property access.

@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("tlg")
class TLGNamespace:
    """Root TLG namespace, accessed as ``df.tlg``.

    This namespace acts as a router to domain-specific sub-namespaces.
    It holds a reference to the underlying DataFrame and passes it to
    sub-namespaces on property access.
    """

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        self._df = df

    @property
    def ae(self) -> AETLGNamespace:
        """AE (adverse event) tables and listings."""
        from .ae_namespace import AETLGNamespace

        return AETLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def vs(self) -> VSTLGNamespace:
        """Vital-signs summary tables."""
        from .vs_namespace import VSTLGNamespace

        return VSTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def cm(self) -> CMTLGNamespace:
        """Concomitant-medication tables."""
        from .cm_namespace import CMTLGNamespace

        return CMTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def ex(self) -> EXTLGNamespace:
        """Exposure tables."""
        from .ex_namespace import EXTLGNamespace

        return EXTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def dm(self) -> DMTLGNamespace:
        """Demographic tables."""
        from .dm_namespace import DMTLGNamespace

        return DMTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def ds(self) -> DSTLGNamespace:
        """Disposition, deaths, enrollment, and deviation tables."""
        from .ds_namespace import DSTLGNamespace

        return DSTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def eg(self) -> EGTLGNamespace:
        """ECG summary tables."""
        from .eg_namespace import EGTLGNamespace

        return EGTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def lb(self) -> LBTLGNamespace:
        """Laboratory tables and listings."""
        from .lb_namespace import LBTLGNamespace

        return LBTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def mh(self) -> MHTLGNamespace:
        """Medical-history tables."""
        from .mh_namespace import MHTLGNamespace

        return MHTLGNamespace(self._df)

    def verbs(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """List the public verbs of ``df.tlg`` (call it on a sub-namespace for its own).

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: Columns ``verb``, ``summary`` and ``origin``,
                sorted by verb name.

        Examples:
            ``adae.tlg.verbs()``; ``adae.tlg.ae.verbs()``
        """
        from fleet.core._verb_mixin import list_verbs

        return list_verbs(type(self))

    def catalog(self) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Return the TLG template catalog (built-ins + user templates).

        Passthrough to [`fleet.tlg.catalog()`][fleet.tlg.catalog] so the
        catalog is discoverable from any DataFrame.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: One row per registered template — ``id``,
                ``title``, ``cdisc_class``, ``namespace``, ``method``,
                ``output_type``, ``domains``, ``source_ref``, ``status``.

        Examples:
            ``adae.tlg.catalog().filter(pl.col("namespace") == "ae")``
        """
        from ._registry import catalog as _catalog

        return _catalog()

    def check(self) -> list[str]:
        """Run pre-validation diagnostics on every applicable sub-namespace.

        A sub-namespace is *applicable* when its default summary spec's
        required columns are all present in the DataFrame — e.g. a frame
        with ``AEBODSYS``/``AEDECOD`` triggers the AE checks, one with
        ``PARAMCD``/``AVAL`` the findings checks.  Namespaces whose
        required columns are absent are skipped (they would only report
        that this isn't their dataset).

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages prefixed with the namespace
                name, or a single message when no sub-namespace applies.

        Examples:
            ``report = adae.tlg.check()``
        """
        from ._runner import NAMESPACE_CLASSES

        available = set(self._df.columns)
        diagnostics: list[str] = []
        applicable = 0
        for name, ns_cls in NAMESPACE_CLASSES.items():
            spec_cls = getattr(ns_cls, "_builder_specs", {}).get("t_summary")
            if spec_cls is None:
                continue
            spec = spec_cls()
            if not set(spec.required_columns) <= available:
                continue
            applicable += 1
            diagnostics.extend(f"[{name}] {msg}" for msg in ns_cls(self._df).check())
        if applicable == 0:
            diagnostics.append(
                "NO APPLICABLE NAMESPACE: no sub-namespace's required columns "
                f"are all present (available: {sorted(available)}). Run "
                "df.tlg.<ns>.check() directly for a specific diagnosis."
            )
        return diagnostics

class AETLGNamespace(BuilderVerbsMixin):
    """AE tables, listings, and diagnostics.

    Accessed as ``df.tlg.ae``.  Supports both spec-driven
    (``t_summary(spec=...)``) and inline builder (``df.tlg.ae.by(...)``)
    workflows.

    Args:
        df: A Polars DataFrame containing ADaM AE-level data.
    """

    _builder_specs = {
        "t_summary": AESummarySpec,
        "t_overview": AEOverviewSpec,
        "t_soc_pt": AESocPtSpec,
        "t_severity": AESeveritySpec,
        "t_grade": AEGradeSpec,
        "t_relationship": AERelationshipSpec,
        "l_listing": AEListingSpec,
    }

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        self._df = df

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Summary table                                                        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def t_summary(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: AESummarySpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Produce an AE summary ARD (Analysis Results Dataset).

        Computes big-N from *adsl*, then n / % subjects and optionally
        event counts for each SOC→PT (or custom row hierarchy).

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment arm column name.  Overrides
                ``spec.columns[0]`` when given.
            adsl: ADSL DataFrame for big-N denominators.  Required for
                percentage calculations.
            spec: Optional ``AESummarySpec`` override.  If ``None``, the
                default spec is used.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: ARD in the {cards} long layout, with columns
                ``group1``, ``group1_level``, ``group2``, ``group2_level``,
                ``variable``, ``variable_level``, ``stat_name``,
                ``stat_label``, ``stat``, ``fmt_fn``, ``stat_fmt``,
                ``warning``, ``error``, ``context``.

        Examples:
            AE summary, ADSL arm in TRT01A::

                spec = AESummarySpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
                ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)

            Custom spec with pooled arms::

                from fleet.tlg import AESummarySpec, GroupPool

                spec = AESummarySpec(
                    pools=[GroupPool(label="Total", arms="*")],
                    adsl_group_col="TRT01A",
                )
                ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
        """
        return summarize_spec(self._df, spec or AESummarySpec(), groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Overview (AET01)                                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def t_overview(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: AEOverviewSpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Overview of adverse events (AET01): whole-population header rows.

        Counts subjects with any AE, any serious AE, any AE leading to
        treatment discontinuation, and fatal AEs — one n / % row each,
        no SOC→PT hierarchy (that is :meth:`t_soc_pt` / AET02).  The
        default filters read ``AESER`` / ``AEACN`` / ``AESDTH``;
        override ``spec.header_rows`` for sponsor-specific definitions.

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment-arm column; overrides ``spec.columns[0]``.
            adsl: ADSL for big-N denominators (percentages).
            spec: Optional ``AEOverviewSpec`` override.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: ARD in the {cards} long layout.

        Examples:
            ADSL arm in TRT01A::

                spec = AEOverviewSpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
                ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_overview(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
        """
        return summarize_spec(self._df, spec or AEOverviewSpec(), groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Hierarchical variants (AET02 / AET03 / AET04)                        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def t_soc_pt(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: AESocPtSpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """AE by SOC → PT (AET02): n / % subjects per arm × SOC → PT.

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment-arm column; overrides ``spec.columns[0]``.
            adsl: ADSL for big-N denominators (percentages).
            spec: Optional ``AESocPtSpec`` override.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: ARD in the {cards} long layout.

        Examples:
            ADSL arm in TRT01A::

                spec = AESocPtSpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
                ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_soc_pt(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
        """
        return summarize_spec(self._df, spec or AESocPtSpec(), groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl)

    def t_severity(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: AESeveritySpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """AE by greatest severity (AET03): n / % by SOC → worst intensity.

        Each subject is counted once per SOC at their greatest intensity
        (``spec.severity_order`` rank), so intensity rows partition the
        SOC's subject count instead of double-counting a subject at
        every intensity they reported.  The reduction runs after the
        pools, so a subject on two arms counts once in Total; the SOC
        rows and header rows count every record.

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment-arm column; overrides ``spec.columns[0]``.
            adsl: ADSL for big-N denominators (percentages).
            spec: Optional ``AESeveritySpec`` override.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: ARD in the {cards} long layout.

        References:
            tern ``count_occurrences_by_grade``; GDSR AET03.

        Examples:
            ADSL arm in TRT01A::

                spec = AESeveritySpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
                ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_severity(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
        """
        return summarize_spec(self._df, spec or AESeveritySpec(), groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl)

    def t_grade(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: AEGradeSpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """AE by highest NCI CTCAE grade (AET04): n / % by SOC → worst grade.

        Each subject is counted once per SOC at their highest toxicity
        grade (``spec.grade_order`` rank).

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment-arm column; overrides ``spec.columns[0]``.
            adsl: ADSL for big-N denominators (percentages).
            spec: Optional ``AEGradeSpec`` override.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: ARD in the {cards} long layout.

        Examples:
            ADSL arm in TRT01A::

                spec = AEGradeSpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
                ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_grade(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
        """
        spec = spec or AEGradeSpec()
        df = self._df
        grade_col = spec.rows[-1].field
        if grade_col in df.columns:
            df = df.with_columns(pl.col(grade_col).cast(pl.Utf8).str.replace(r"\.0$", ""))
        return summarize_spec(df, spec, groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl)

    def t_relationship(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: AERelationshipSpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """AE by relationship: n / % by SOC → relationship.

        Each subject is counted once per SOC — related if any of their
        events in the SOC is related (``spec.relationship_order`` rank).

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment-arm column; overrides ``spec.columns[0]``.
            adsl: ADSL for big-N denominators (percentages).
            spec: Optional ``AERelationshipSpec`` override.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: ARD in the {cards} long layout.

        Examples:
            ADSL arm in TRT01A::

                spec = AERelationshipSpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
                ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_relationship(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
        """
        return summarize_spec(self._df, spec or AERelationshipSpec(), groupby=groupby, adsl=adsl)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Listing                                                              #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def l_listing(
        self,
        *,
        spec: AEListingSpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Produce an AE listing DataFrame.

        Applies ``dataset_filter``, sorts by ``sort_by`` (a key need not
        be a displayed column; ties keep the input order), formats each
        column with its ``Column.format`` and keeps the requested
        columns, as PROC SORT BY then PROC PRINT VAR.

        Args:
            spec: Optional ``AEListingSpec`` override.  If ``None``, the
                default spec is used.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: A plain DataFrame with the requested columns,
                sorted per spec.

        Raises:
            SchemaError: If a listing column or a sort key that the user
                set is not in the dataset, or a format cannot print a
                value.

        Examples:
            Default AE listing::

                listing = adae.tlg.ae.l_listing()

            Custom listing with additional columns::

                from fleet.tlg import AEListingSpec, Column

                spec = AEListingSpec(
                    columns=[
                        Column(field="USUBJID", label="Subject"),
                        Column(field="AEDECOD", label="Preferred Term"),
                    ],
                    sort_by=["USUBJID"],
                )
                listing = adae.tlg.ae.l_listing(spec=spec)
        """
        spec = spec or AEListingSpec()
        spec.validate_dataframe(self._df)

        df = self._df
        dataset_filter = resolve_filter(spec.dataset_filter)
        if dataset_filter is not None:
            df = df.filter(dataset_filter)
        return listing_frame(df, spec)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Pre-validation diagnostic                                            #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def check(
        self,
        *,
        spec: AESummarySpec | None = None,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Run pre-validation diagnostics without computing.

        Args:
            spec: Optional spec to check against.  If ``None``, the
                default ``AESummarySpec`` is used.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).

        Examples:
            Check data readiness::

                report = adae.tlg.ae.check()
        """
        spec = spec or AESummarySpec()
        return spec.check(self._df)

def t_grade(

    groupby: str | None = None,
    adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    spec: AEGradeSpec | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """AE by highest NCI CTCAE grade (AET04): n / % by SOC → worst grade.

    Each subject is counted once per SOC at their highest toxicity
    grade (``spec.grade_order`` rank).

    Args:

def l_listing(
    self,
    *,
    spec: AEListingSpec | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Produce an AE listing DataFrame.

    Applies ``dataset_filter``, sorts by ``sort_by`` (a key need not
    be a displayed column; ties keep the input order), formats each
    column with its ``Column.format`` and keeps the requested
    columns, as PROC SORT BY then PROC PRINT VAR.

    Args:
        spec: Optional ``AEListingSpec`` override.  If ``None``, the
            default spec is used.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: A plain DataFrame with the requested columns,
            sorted per spec.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If a listing column or a sort key that the user
            set is not in the dataset, or a format cannot print a
            value.

    Examples:
        Default AE listing::

            listing = adae.tlg.ae.l_listing()

        Custom listing with additional columns::

            from fleet.tlg import AEListingSpec, Column

            spec = AEListingSpec(
                columns=[
                    Column(field="USUBJID", label="Subject"),
                    Column(field="AEDECOD", label="Preferred Term"),
                ],
                sort_by=["USUBJID"],
            )
            listing = adae.tlg.ae.l_listing(spec=spec)
    """
    spec = spec or AEListingSpec()
    spec.validate_dataframe(self._df)

    df = self._df
    dataset_filter = resolve_filter(spec.dataset_filter)
    if dataset_filter is not None:
        df = df.filter(dataset_filter)
    return listing_frame(df, spec)
