class SummarySpecBase(TLGSpec):
    """Shared fields for every summary-table spec.

    Domain specs subclass this and override only their defaults (rows,
    statistics, required columns, the uncoded rule, the prefilter) —
    one declaration of the shared shape instead of nine divergent
    copies.  Every field is also settable inline through
    [`TLGBuilder`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder].  The spec is the whole engine
    contract: [`summarize_spec()`][fleet.tlg.summarize_spec] reads every
    engine argument from it (ADR-0005).
    """

    #: The cards ``context`` tag written to every ARD row.  One spec
    #: class serves one template method, so the tag is a class fact,
    #: not a YAML field.
    context: ClassVar[str] = ""
    #: ``True`` when ``rows`` is a hierarchy (SOC → PT, PARAM → visit);
    #: ``False`` when each row field is an independent flat breakdown.
    nested: ClassVar[bool] = False
    #: Extra text for the missing-prefilter-column error (e.g. how to
    #: state a post-baseline rule without ONTRTFL).
    prefilter_hint: ClassVar[str] = ""
    #: Arm columns tried in order when ``columns`` is not set: the first
    #: one in the data is the arm.  Empty: ``columns[0]`` is the arm.
    arm_fallback: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ()

    output_type: str = "summary"
    rows: list[Row] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Row groupings (hierarchy for nested templates).  Set inline "
            "via [`TLGBuilder.rows()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.rows]."
        ),
    )
    uncoded: Uncoded | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The uncoded rule: coding columns whose nulls become a "
            "visible level before counting.  Each template sets its own "
            "default; ``null`` switches the rule off.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.uncoded()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.uncoded]."
        ),
    )
    prefilter: Any | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The template's own record filter, applied after "
            "``dataset_filter`` — a ``pl.Expr`` or a string expression "
            '(e.g. ``\'pl.col("ABLFL").ne_missing("Y")\'`` on a '
            "change-from-baseline table).  Each template sets its own "
            "default; ``null`` switches it off.  Every column it names "
            "is a required column.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.prefilter()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.prefilter]."
        ),
    )

    _validate_prefilter = field_validator("prefilter")(_check_filter_field)
    missing: MissingLevel | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The missing-level rule: category columns whose null or blank "
            'values are counted in a "Missing" row, last in the block, '
            "with big N as the percent base.  Each template sets its own "
            "default; ``null`` switches the rule off.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.missing()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.missing]."
        ),
    )
    adsl_group_col: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Arm column of ADSL for the big N when it differs from the "
            "analysis arm column (e.g. ``TRT01A`` for an ADAE grouped by "
            "``TRTA``).  The arm values must match.  In a crossover the "
            "N is then the period 1 count.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.population()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.population]; "
            "CLI ``--adsl-groupby``."
        ),
    )
    columns: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: ["TRTA"],
        description=(
            "Column-grouping variables (typically a treatment column).  "
            "Exactly one entry — multi-column grouping is not implemented "
            "yet, and the engine would silently read only the first.  "
            "Set inline via [`TLGBuilder.by()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.by]."
        ),
    )
    statistics: list[Statistic] = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: [Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT],
        description=(
            "Statistics computed for each row.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.stats()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.stats]."
        ),
    )
    pools: list[GroupPool] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Composite (pooled) treatment groups.  Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.pools()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.pools]."
        ),
    )
    column_order: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description=(
            "Explicit ordering of column labels in the rendered output.  "
            "Set inline via "
            "[`TLGBuilder.column_order()`][fleet.tlg.TLGBuilder.column_order]."
        ),
    )
    value_col: str = Field(
        default="AVAL",
        description=(
            "Analysis-value column used for continuous statistics "
            "(mean/SD/median/…).  Summarize ``CHG``, ``PCHG`` or ``BASE`` "
            "by pointing this at the column — no pre-renaming needed.  "
            "When the column is missing but continuous statistics are "
            "requested, the engine raises instead of emitting null stats."
        ),
    )
    label_col: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Column holding display labels for the first row field's "
            'values (e.g. ``"PARAM"`` when the row field is '
            '``"PARAMCD"``) so stubs show display names instead of '
            "codes.  ``None`` shows the raw values."
        ),
    )
    decimals: dict[str, str] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Per-statistic format overrides — ARD ``stat_name`` (e.g. "
            '``"mean"``, ``"sd"``, ``"pct"``) to format string (e.g. '
            '``"xx.xx"``).  Overrides the built-in defaults for this '
            "table; individual rows may override again via "
            ":attr:`Row.decimals`.  A key that is not an ARD stat name "
            "or a pattern that is not ``xx.x`` raises."
        ),
    )

    @field_validator("decimals")
    @classmethod
    def _check_decimals(cls, value: dict[str, str] | None) -> dict[str, str] | None:
        return check_decimals(value)

    def prefilter_columns(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the columns the spec's prefilter names.

        Every one of them is a required column of the template, so a
        change table's ``ABLFL`` guard makes ``ABLFL`` required and
        ``prefilter=None`` lifts that requirement with it.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Column names in first-seen order; empty when the
                prefilter is ``None``.

        Examples:
            ``LBChgSpec().prefilter_columns() == ["ABLFL", "CHG"]``
        """
        expr = resolve_filter(self.prefilter)
        if expr is None:
            return []
        return list(dict.fromkeys(expr.meta.root_names()))

    def default_group_col(self, columns: Iterable[str]) -> str:
        """Return the arm column of a run that gives no ``groupby``.

        A subject-level template (DM, DS on ADSL) sets
        ``arm_fallback = ("TRT01A", "TRT01P")``: when ``columns`` is not
        set, the first of them in the data is the arm.  In all other
        cases the arm is ``columns[0]``.

        Args:
            columns: Column names of the analysis dataset.

        Returns:
            str: The arm column.  When no fallback column is in the
                data, ``columns[0]``, so the required-columns error
                names it.

        Examples:
            ``DMSummarySpec().default_group_col(["USUBJID", "TRT01P"]) == "TRT01P"``
        """
        if self.arm_fallback and "columns" not in self.model_fields_set:
            present = set(columns)
            found = next((c for c in self.arm_fallback if c in present), None)
            if found is not None:
                return found
        return self.columns[0] if self.columns else "TRTA"

    def check(self, df: pl.DataFrame, *, group_col: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Run the pre-validation diagnostic without computing.

        The base checks (required columns, prefilter columns, required
        flag values) plus one line per row field absent from *df*, for
        which the engine stops.

        Args:
            df: The DataFrame to check.
            group_col: Treatment-arm column.  ``None`` takes the arm a
                run without ``groupby`` takes
                ([`default_group_col()`][fleet.tlg.SummarySpecBase.default_group_col]).

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).

        Examples:
            ``MHSummarySpec().check(admh)``
        """
        group_col = group_col or self.default_group_col(df.columns)
        diagnostics = super().check(df, group_col=group_col)
        available = set(df.columns)
        for row_def in self.rows:
            if row_def.field not in available:
                diagnostics.append(
                    f"MISSING ROW FIELD: Column '{row_def.field}' not present — "
                    f"the '{row_def.label or row_def.field}' rows cannot be built "
                    "and the table stops."
                )
        return diagnostics

    def leaf_rank(self) -> tuple[list[str], str] | None:
        """Return the rank that reduces the last row level, or ``None``.

        A worst-case table (greatest intensity, highest grade) counts a
        subject once at the worst value of its last row field.  The
        engine applies the rank after the pools, at the last depth only.

        Returns:
            tuple[list[str], str] | None: The values from least to most
                severe and the spec field name that holds them; ``None``
                for a table without a reduction.

        Examples:
            ``AESeveritySpec().leaf_rank() == (["MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE"], "severity_order")``
        """
        return None

    @field_validator("columns")
    @classmethod
    def _single_group_column(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        """Reject multi-column (or empty) grouping loudly.

        The engine reads only ``columns[0]``; accepting more would
        silently discard the rest of the grouping.
        """
        if len(value) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'columns' must contain exactly one treatment-arm column "
                f"(got {value!r}). Multi-column grouping is not implemented "
                "— the engine would silently read only the first entry. "
                "Move additional grouping into the row hierarchy ('rows') "
                "or file a feature request."
            )
        return value

docs.title: Engine seam
docs.text:
Every summary table is one call on the shared engine. The forwarding tables call summarize_spec(df, spec, groupby=, adsl=), which resolves the group column, validates the frame, runs prepare_frame (uncoded rule, dataset filter, prefilter, in that order) and reads every other engine argument from the spec. Composite tables, such as deaths and the lab shift table, call prepare_frame and then summarize_ard with keyword arguments. User-registered templates may call either.

TLG (Tables, Listings, Graphs) Polars namespace extension.

Registers df.tlg on every Polars DataFrame. Sub-structures are accessed via properties: - df.tlg.ae — AE summary tables and listings - df.tlg.vs — Vital-signs summary tables

def summarize_spec(
    df: pl.DataFrame,
    spec: SummarySpecBase,
    *,
    groupby: str | None = None,
    adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Build a summary ARD from a spec — the seam every forwarding table uses.

    The spec is the whole engine contract: every :func:`summarize_ard`
    argument is read from its fields, and the cards ``context`` tag and
    the ``nested`` flag from its class.  The group column is *groupby*,
    else :meth:`SummarySpecBase.default_group_col` (the spec's first
    column, or the first ``arm_fallback`` column in the data); the frame is
    validated against the spec, then prepared by :func:`prepare_frame`.

    Args:
        df: The analysis dataset.
        spec: A summary spec (any :class:`SummarySpecBase` subclass).
        groupby: Treatment-arm column; overrides ``spec.columns[0]``.
        adsl: ADSL for big-N denominators and the arm universe.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: Validated ARD in the {cards} long layout.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: If the frame fails the spec's validation, or on any
            engine refusal (see :func:`summarize_ard`).

    Examples:
        ``ard = summarize_spec(admh, MHSummarySpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A"), adsl=adsl)``
    """
    group_col = groupby or spec.default_group_col(df.columns)
    spec.validate_dataframe(df, group_col=group_col)
    return summarize_ard(
        prepare_frame(df, spec),
        rows=spec.rows,
        stats=spec.statistics,
        context=spec.context,
        group_col=group_col,
        pools=spec.pools,
        column_order=spec.column_order,
        adsl=adsl,
        adsl_filter=spec.adsl_filter,
        header_rows=spec.header_rows,
        nested=spec.nested,
        value_col=spec.value_col,
        label_col=spec.label_col,
        decimals=spec.decimals,
        missing=spec.missing,
        leaf_rank=spec.leaf_rank(),
        adsl_group_col=spec.adsl_group_col,
    )

prepare_frame(df, spec)

Apply a summary spec's record rules to the analysis dataset, in order.

The order is fixed and shared by every summary table: the uncoded rule first (so a dataset filter may name the uncoded label), then the dataset filter, then the template's prefilter. The seam (:func:summarize_spec) calls it; a composite table that does its own work between the filter and the engine calls it first and then passes no dataset_filter to :func:summarize_ard. A prefilter that keeps no record of a non-empty frame gives a UserWarning with the values of its columns, as a SAS log NOTE for a WHERE with no match.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default df DataFrame

The analysis dataset.

required spec SummarySpecBase

A summary spec carrying uncoded, dataset_filter and prefilter.

required

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

pl.DataFrame: df with the three rules applied.

Examples:

A composite table prepares its frame, then does its own work::

df = prepare_frame(adae, spec)
df = worst_case(df, by=["USUBJID", "TRTA", "AEBODSYS"], order_col="AESEV")

def prepare_frame(df: pl.DataFrame, spec: SummarySpecBase) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Apply a summary spec's record rules to the analysis dataset, in order.

    The order is fixed and shared by every summary table: the uncoded
    rule first (so a dataset filter may name the uncoded label), then
    the dataset filter, then the template's prefilter.  The seam
    (:func:`summarize_spec`) calls it; a composite table that does its
    own work between the filter and the engine calls it first and then
    passes no ``dataset_filter`` to :func:`summarize_ard`.  A prefilter
    that keeps no record of a non-empty frame gives a ``UserWarning``
    with the values of its columns, as a SAS log NOTE for a WHERE with
    no match.

    Args:
        df: The analysis dataset.
        spec: A summary spec carrying ``uncoded``, ``dataset_filter``
            and ``prefilter``.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: *df* with the three rules applied.

    Examples:
        A composite table prepares its frame, then does its own work::

            df = prepare_frame(adae, spec)
            df = worst_case(df, by=["USUBJID", "TRTA", "AEBODSYS"], order_col="AESEV")
    """
    if spec.uncoded is not None:
        df = fill_uncoded(df, spec.uncoded.columns, spec.uncoded.label)
    dataset_filter = resolve_filter(spec.dataset_filter)
    if dataset_filter is not None:
        df = df.filter(dataset_filter)
    prefilter = resolve_filter(spec.prefilter)
    if prefilter is not None:
        before = df
        df = df.filter(prefilter)
        if before.height and not df.height:
            seen = "; ".join(
                f"{c} values: "
                + ", ".join(level_text(v) for v in before[c].unique(maintain_order=True).head(10))
                for c in dict.fromkeys(prefilter.meta.root_names())
                if c in before.columns
            )
            warnings.warn(
                f"prefilter {spec.prefilter} kept 0 of {before.height} records; {seen}. "
                "Set the prefilter to the study's values, or prefilter=None.",
                UserWarning,
                stacklevel=3,
            )
    return df

Build an ARD in the {cards} long layout: the single shared TLG engine.

The layout follows {cards}, but the names differ: fmt_fn (not fmt_fun), pct on 0 to 100 (not p on 0 to 1), and big-N rows with variable="". Convert the ARD before you give it to R tools such as gtsummary.

Every summary table (categorical counts and continuous statistics) goes through this function: big-N rows, header rows (OverallStat), then stats per arm × row level, with explicit zero cells.

Denominator rules (loud, never silently wrong): - Percentages (n_pct) require adsl; omitting it raises. - The arm universe comes from adsl when given — an arm with zero analysis records keeps its column (N row + zero cells) instead of vanishing, and an arm in the data but absent from ADSL raises. - Without adsl no big-N rows are emitted (there is no population).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default df DataFrame

Analysis dataset.

required rows Sequence[str | Row]

Row fields — names or Row objects (honouring Row.filter_value), e.g. ["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"]. Levels sort by Row.order_by, else by <field>N when the dataset has it (AVISIT by AVISITN), else as text.

required stats list[Statistic]

Statistics computed per arm × level.

required context str

ARD context tag written to every row.

required group_col str

Treatment-arm column.

'TRTA' pools list[GroupPool] | None

Composite arms; None for none.

None column_order list[str] | None

Explicit arm ordering; remaining arms keep their order: arms first (Enum category order, else text order), then pools. A name that is not an arm or pool raises.

None adsl DataFrame | None

Population source for big-N denominators and the arm universe. Analysis records of subjects outside the filtered ADSL are left out of every count (ADR-0016).

None adsl_filter Any | None

Population filter (pl.Expr or expression string). It selects the ADSL subjects for N and, through them, the analysis records for n. Requires adsl.

None dataset_filter Any | None

Filter applied to df before counting (pl.Expr or expression string).

None prefilter Any | None

Extra df filter (e.g. DTHFL == "Y"), a pl.Expr or an expression string.

None header_rows list[OverallStat] | None

OverallStat aggregate rows emitted above the hierarchy (variable="", variable_level=label).

None nested bool

When True, rows is a hierarchy: count statistics are emitted at every depth and continuous statistics only at the deepest level, computed per level combination (e.g. PT-within-SOC, visit-within-parameter) with the parent level in group2 / group2_level. When False each field is summarized as an independent flat breakdown.

False value_col str

Analysis-value column for continuous statistics (default "AVAL"). Point at CHG/PCHG/BASE to summarize those without pre-renaming. Missing while continuous statistics are requested raises.

'AVAL' label_col str | None

Column holding display labels for the first row field's values (e.g. "PARAM" for "PARAMCD" stubs). The mapped label replaces the raw value in variable_level / group2_level.

None decimals dict[str, str] | None

Per-statistic format overrides — ARD stat_name (e.g. "mean") to format string (e.g. "xx.xx"). Row.decimals overrides again for that row's leaf level.

None missing MissingLevel | None

The missing-level rule. A null or blank value of its columns is counted under missing.label, last in the block; with label=None the count goes to the ARD warning column (ADR-0038).

None leaf_rank tuple[Sequence[str], str] | None

(order, order_field) of a worst-case table. At the last depth of a nested hierarchy each subject is counted once, at the worst value of the last row field, within its arm (pools included) and its parent levels. Parent levels and header rows count every record; no n_events is emitted at the reduced level.

None adsl_group_col str | None

Arm column of adsl when it differs from group_col (an ADAE with TRTA, an ADSL with TRT01A). The arm values must match.

None

Raises:

Type Description SchemaError

On missing group column, missing percentage denominator, missing or non-numeric value_col with continuous statistics requested, an infinite value_col value, missing label_col, a row field absent from df, a numeric arm column, an unknown column_order entry, unknown arms/pools, or ARD schema violations.

            ``pl.Expr`` or an expression string.
        header_rows: ``OverallStat`` aggregate rows emitted above the
            hierarchy (``variable=""``, ``variable_level=label``).
        nested: When ``True``, *rows* is a hierarchy: count statistics
            are emitted at every depth and continuous statistics only at
            the deepest level, computed per level *combination* (e.g.
            PT-within-SOC, visit-within-parameter) with the parent level
            in ``group2`` / ``group2_level``.  When ``False`` each field
            is summarized as an independent flat breakdown.
        value_col: Analysis-value column for continuous statistics
            (default ``"AVAL"``).  Point at ``CHG``/``PCHG``/``BASE`` to
            summarize those without pre-renaming.  Missing while
            continuous statistics are requested raises.
        label_col: Column holding display labels for the first row
            field's values (e.g. ``"PARAM"`` for ``"PARAMCD"`` stubs).
            The mapped label replaces the raw value in
            ``variable_level`` / ``group2_level``.
        decimals: Per-statistic format overrides — ARD ``stat_name``
            (e.g. ``"mean"``) to format string (e.g. ``"xx.xx"``).
            ``Row.decimals`` overrides again for that row's leaf level.
        missing: The missing-level rule.  A null or blank value of its
            columns is counted under ``missing.label``, last in the
            block; with ``label=None`` the count goes to the ARD
            ``warning`` column (ADR-0038).
        leaf_rank: ``(order, order_field)`` of a worst-case table.  At
            the last depth of a nested hierarchy each subject is counted
            once, at the worst value of the last row field, within its
            arm (pools included) and its parent levels.  Parent levels
            and header rows count every record; no ``n_events`` is
            emitted at the reduced level.
        adsl_group_col: Arm column of *adsl* when it differs from
            *group_col* (an ADAE with ``TRTA``, an ADSL with
            ``TRT01A``).  The arm values must match.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: Validated ARD in the {cards} long layout.

    Raises:
        SchemaError: On missing group column, missing percentage
            denominator, missing or non-numeric *value_col* with
            continuous statistics requested, an infinite *value_col*
            value, missing *label_col*, a row field absent from *df*,
            a numeric arm column, an unknown *column_order* entry,
            unknown arms/pools, or ARD schema violations.

    References:
        ADaMIG v1.3 (TRTxxA on ADSL, TRTA on OCCDS/BDS; AVISITN is the
        sort key of AVISIT); FDA CDER
        Standard Safety Tables and Figures IG v2.0, 2.1.2 (missing row);
        ADR-0038; ADR-0049 (row and column order); ADR-0050 (NaN, inf).

    Examples:
        ``summarize_ard(adae, rows=["AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD"], stats=[Statistic.N_PCT],
        context="t_ae", adsl=adsl, adsl_group_col="TRT01A")``
    """
    pools = pools or []
    header_rows = header_rows or []
    row_defs = [r if isinstance(r, Row) else Row(field=r) for r in rows]

    if group_col not in df.columns:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Group column '{group_col}' not found in the analysis dataset. "
            f"Available: {sorted(df.columns)}"
        )
    absent_rows = [r.field for r in row_defs if r.field not in df.columns]
    if absent_rows:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Row field(s) {absent_rows} are not in the analysis dataset. "
            f"Available: {sorted(df.columns)}"
        )
    absent_order = [r.order_by for r in row_defs if r.order_by and r.order_by not in df.columns]
    if absent_order:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Row order_by column(s) {absent_order} are not in the analysis dataset. "
            f"Available: {sorted(df.columns)}"
        )
    order_cols = {}
    for r in row_defs:
        order_col = r.order_by or f"{r.field}N"
        if order_col in df.columns:
            order_cols[r.field] = order_col
    check_text_arm(df, group_col, "the analysis dataset")
    adsl_col = adsl_group_col or group_col
    if adsl is not None and adsl_col in adsl.columns:
        check_text_arm(adsl, adsl_col, "adsl")
    categories = enum_arms(adsl, adsl_col) or enum_arms(df, group_col)
    df = df.with_columns(pl.col(group_col).cast(pl.Utf8))
    known_arms = set(df[group_col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())

    dataset_filter_expr = resolve_filter(dataset_filter)
    if dataset_filter_expr is not None:
        df = df.filter(dataset_filter_expr)
    prefilter_expr = resolve_filter(prefilter)
    if prefilter_expr is not None:
        df = df.filter(prefilter_expr)
    if leaf_rank is not None and row_defs:
        check_rank_values(
            df,
            row_defs[-1].field,
            leaf_rank[0],
            leaf_rank[1],
            [missing.label] if missing is not None and missing.label else (),
        )
    if adsl is not None:
        if "USUBJID" not in adsl.columns:
            raise SchemaError(f"adsl has no USUBJID column. Available: {sorted(adsl.columns)}")
        df = restrict_to_population(df, adsl, adsl_filter)
    elif adsl_filter is not None:
        raise SchemaError(
            "adsl_filter is set but no adsl was given. The population filter "
            "selects ADSL subjects, so it cannot apply without ADSL: pass "
            "adsl=..., or filter the analysis dataset with dataset_filter."
        )

    pct_requested = Statistic.N_PCT in stats or any(
        Statistic.N_PCT in (hdr.statistics or stats) for hdr in header_rows
    )
    if pct_requested and adsl is None:
        raise SchemaError(
            "Percentage statistics (n_pct) require an ADSL population for "
            "the denominator — pass adsl=... . A percentage computed "
            "without a population denominator would be silently wrong."
        )

    cont_requested = sorted(
        {
            s.value
            for s in [*stats, *(s for hdr in header_rows for s in (hdr.statistics or stats))]
            if s in _CONT_STAT_META
        }
    )
    if cont_requested and value_col not in df.columns:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Continuous statistics {cont_requested} require the value "
            f"column '{value_col}', which is not in the analysis dataset. "
            f"Available: {sorted(df.columns)}. Pass value_col=... to point "
            "at the analysis value (e.g. CHG), or drop the continuous "
            "statistics."
        )
    if cont_requested and not df[value_col].dtype.is_numeric():
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Continuous statistics {cont_requested} need a numeric {value_col}; "
            f"{value_col} is {df[value_col].dtype}. Cast it: "
            f"pl.col('{value_col}').cast(pl.Float64)"
        )
    if cont_requested:
        df = nan_to_null(df, value_col)
    if label_col is not None and label_col not in df.columns:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"label_col '{label_col}' not found in the analysis dataset. "
            f"Available: {sorted(df.columns)}"
        )

    data_arms = set(df[group_col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())
    arms, big_n = resolve_arms(
        data_arms,
        group_col,
        adsl=adsl,
        adsl_group_col=adsl_group_col,
        adsl_filter=adsl_filter,
        pools=pools,
        column_order=column_order,
        known_arms=known_arms,
        categories=categories,
    )

    df, missing_notes = _apply_missing(df, missing)
    missing_label = missing.label if missing is not None else None
    df = expand_pools(df, pools, group_col, strict=False)

    ard_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    table_fmt = decimals or {}

    # Big-N rows exist only when a population is given.
    if adsl is not None:
        ard_rows += [
            ard_row(
                group_col,
                arm,
                "",
                "",
                "N",
                "N",
                big_n.get(arm),
                context,
                fmt_fn=table_fmt.get("N"),
            )
            for arm in arms
        ]

    # Header rows (OverallStat) — whole-dataset aggregates above the hierarchy.
    for hdr in header_rows:
        hdr_df = df
        hdr_filter = resolve_filter(hdr.filter)
        hdr_warning = None
        if hdr_filter is not None:
            blank = blank_filter_columns(hdr_filter, hdr_df)
            if blank:
                hdr_warning = (
                    f"filter column {', '.join(blank)} is null or blank on every "
                    f"record (row '{hdr.label}')"
                )
                warnings.warn(hdr_warning, UserWarning, stacklevel=2)
            hdr_df = hdr_df.filter(hdr_filter)
        effective_stats = hdr.statistics or stats
        hdr_values = value_col in hdr_df.columns and any(
            s in _CONT_STAT_META for s in effective_stats
        )
        for arm in arms:
            arm_hdr = hdr_df.filter(pl.col(group_col) == arm)
            arm_n = big_n.get(arm, 0)
            for stat_type in effective_stats:
                sn, sl, sv = compute_stat(
                    stat_type, arm_hdr, arm_n, value_col=value_col, count_values=hdr_values
                )
                ard_rows.append(
                    ard_row(
                        group_col,
                        arm,
                        "",
                        hdr.label,
                        sn,
                        sl,
                        sv,
                        context,
                        fmt_fn=table_fmt.get(sn),
                        warning=hdr_warning,
                    )
                )

    present = row_defs
    field_labels = {r.field: (r.label or "") for r in row_defs}
    if nested:
        fields = [r.field for r in present]
        if len(fields) > 2:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Nested row hierarchies support at most 2 levels — the ARD "
                f"schema carries one parent (group2/group2_level) per row, so "
                f"deeper lineages would emit indistinguishable duplicate rows. "
                f"Got {fields}. Reduce the hierarchy or pass nested=False."
            )
        for depth in range(len(fields)):
            is_leaf = depth == len(fields) - 1
            depth_stats = stats if is_leaf else [s for s in stats if s in COUNT_STATS]
            if is_leaf and leaf_rank is not None:
                # One reduced record per subject: an event count means nothing here.
                depth_stats = [s for s in depth_stats if s != Statistic.N_EVENTS]
            if not depth_stats:
                continue
            # A row's filter_value scopes that row's own depth and its
            # descendants — never its ancestors' counts.
            frame = df
            for row_def in present[:depth]:
                if row_def.filter_value is not None:
                    frame = frame.filter(pl.col(row_def.field) == row_def.filter_value)
            if is_leaf and leaf_rank is not None:
                order, order_field = leaf_rank
                frame = worst_case(
                    frame,
                    by=["USUBJID", group_col, *fields[:-1]],
                    order_col=fields[-1],
                    order=order,
                    order_field=order_field,
                    unranked=[missing_label] if missing_label else (),
                )
            if present[depth].filter_value is not None:
                frame = frame.filter(pl.col(fields[depth]) == present[depth].filter_value)
            ard_rows += _level_rows(
                frame,
                fields[: depth + 1],
                depth_stats,
                arms,
                big_n,
                group_col,
                context,
                value_col=value_col,
                field_labels=field_labels,
                fmt_overrides={**table_fmt, **(present[depth].decimals or {})},
                count_values=bool(cont_requested),
                missing_label=missing_label,
                order_cols=order_cols,
            )
    else:
        for row_def in present:
            frame = df
            if row_def.filter_value is not None:
                frame = frame.filter(pl.col(row_def.field) == row_def.filter_value)
            ard_rows += _level_rows(
                frame,
                [row_def.field],
                stats,
                arms,
                big_n,
                group_col,
                context,
                value_col=value_col,
                field_labels=field_labels,
                fmt_overrides={**table_fmt, **(row_def.decimals or {})},
                count_values=bool(cont_requested),
                missing_label=missing_label,
                order_cols=order_cols,
            )

    ard = rows_to_ard(ard_rows)
    for column, note in missing_notes.items():
        ard = ard.with_columns(
            pl.when(pl.col("variable") == column)
            .then(pl.lit(note))
            .otherwise(pl.col("warning"))
            .alias("warning")
        )
    if label_col is not None and present:
        ard = _apply_label_col(ard, df, present[0].field, label_col)
    issues = validate_ard(ard)
    if issues:
        raise SchemaError("ARD output failed schema validation:\n  " + "\n  ".join(issues))
    return ard

The ARD keeps every statistic unrounded. format_ard and apply_fmt_fn round only for display. A tie rounds half away from zero, as SAS ROUND and the {cards} default: 5/16 = 31.25 % prints 31.3 at xx.x. A value that rounds to zero prints 0.0, never -0.0 (ADR-0037).

TLG (Tables, Listings, Graphs) Polars namespace extension.

Registers df.tlg on every Polars DataFrame. Sub-structures are accessed via properties: - df.tlg.ae — AE summary tables and listings - df.tlg.vs — Vital-signs summary tables

def build_ard_row(
    *,
    group1: str = "",
    group1_level: str = "",
    group2: str = "",
    group2_level: str = "",
    variable: str,
    variable_level: str = "",
    variable_label: str = "",
    stat_name: str,
    stat_label: str,
    stat: float | int | str | None,
    fmt_fn: str | None = None,
    warning: str | None = None,
    error: str | None = None,
    context: str = "",
) -> dict[str, str | float | int | None]:
    """Build a single ARD row as a dict (public API).

    Args:
        group1: Primary grouping variable name (e.g. ``"TRTA"``).
        group1_level: Level within group1 (e.g. ``"Placebo"``).
        group2: Secondary grouping variable name (e.g. ``"SEX"``).
        group2_level: Level within group2 (e.g. ``"F"``).
        variable: Analysis variable name (e.g. ``"AEDECOD"``).
        variable_level: Level of the analysis variable (e.g. ``"HEADACHE"``).
        variable_label: Display label for *variable* (e.g. ``"Preferred
            Term"``); ``""`` when no label applies.
        stat_name: Short stat identifier (e.g. ``"n"``, ``"pct"``).
        stat_label: Human-readable label (e.g. ``"n (%)"``, ``"N"``).
        stat: The computed statistic value.
        fmt_fn: Format specifier (e.g. ``"xx.x"``).  If ``None``,
            ``default_fmt_fn(stat_name)`` is used.
        warning: Warning message from computation (``None`` if clean).
        error: Error message from computation (``None`` if clean).
        context: TLG context identifier (e.g. ``"t_ae_summary"``).

    Returns:
        dict: A single ARD row.
    """
    return {
        "group1": group1,
        "group1_level": group1_level,
        "group2": group2,
        "group2_level": group2_level,
        "variable": variable,
        "variable_level": variable_level,
        "variable_label": variable_label,
        "stat_name": stat_name,
        "stat_label": stat_label,
        "stat": stat,
        "fmt_fn": fmt_fn if fmt_fn is not None else default_fmt_fn(stat_name),
        "stat_fmt": None,
        "warning": warning,
        "error": error,
        "context": context,
    }

def validate_ard(df: pl.DataFrame, *, strict: bool = True) -> list[str]:
    """Validate that *df* conforms to the Fleet ARD schema.

    Checks required column presence, data types, and structural integrity.
    Group columns (``group1``, ``group2``, etc.) are optional — matching
    {cards} where not all ARDs have grouping.

    Args:
        df: A DataFrame to validate as ARD.
        strict: When ``True`` (default), columns outside the ARD schema
            are flagged.  Pass ``strict=False`` for post-processing
            workflows (the standard {cards} pattern of annotating an ARD
            with extra columns) — unknown columns are then accepted and
            ignored, while the known columns are still fully checked.

    Returns:
        list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if valid).

    Examples:
        Validate an ARD after computation::

            from fleet.tlg._ard import validate_ard

            issues = validate_ard(ard)
            assert issues == [], issues

        Accept a post-processed ARD carrying annotation columns::

            issues = validate_ard(annotated_ard, strict=False)
    """
    issues: list[str] = []

    # Required columns must be present
    missing_required = [c for c in ARD_REQUIRED_COLUMNS if c not in df.columns]
    if missing_required:
        issues.append(f"Missing required ARD columns: {missing_required}")

    # Check for completely unknown columns (strict mode only)
    if strict:
        known = set(ARD_SCHEMA.keys())
        extra = [c for c in df.columns if c not in known]
        if extra:
            issues.append(
                f"Unexpected columns (not in ARD schema): {extra}. "
                "Pass strict=False to accept post-processing columns."
            )

    # Data types (only check columns that exist)
    for col, expected_dtype in ARD_SCHEMA.items():
        if col in df.columns:
            actual = df[col].dtype
            if actual != expected_dtype:
                issues.append(f"Column '{col}': expected {expected_dtype}, got {actual}")

    # Non-empty check
    if len(df) == 0:
        issues.append("ARD is empty (0 rows)")

    return issues

def format_ard(ard: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Apply ``fmt_fn`` to every row and produce a ``stat_fmt`` column.

    This mirrors ``{cards}::apply_fmt_fn()`` — takes the ARD and produces
    human-readable formatted strings from the numeric ``stat`` column.
    A tie rounds half away from zero (SAS ``ROUND``), see
    :func:`apply_fmt_fn`.

    Args:
        ard: An ARD DataFrame with ``stat`` and ``fmt_fn`` columns.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: The ARD with ``stat_fmt`` column populated.
    """
    if "fmt_fn" not in ard.columns or "stat" not in ard.columns:
        return ard

    formatted = []
    stat_vals = ard["stat"].to_list()
    fmt_vals = ard["fmt_fn"].to_list()

    for val, fmt in zip(stat_vals, fmt_vals):
        if fmt is None:
            formatted.append("" if val is None else str(val))
        else:
            formatted.append(apply_fmt_fn(val, fmt))

    return ard.with_columns(pl.Series("stat_fmt", formatted, dtype=pl.Utf8))

Apply a format specifier to a numeric value.

A tie rounds half away from zero, as SAS ROUND and the {cards} default: 31.25 at "xx.x" prints 31.3, -2.25 prints -2.3. A value that rounds to zero prints 0.0, never -0.0.

Supported format patterns
  • "xx" → integer (e.g. "86")
  • "xx.x" → 1 decimal (e.g. "75.2")
  • "xx.xx" → 2 decimals (e.g. "8.59")
  • "xx.xxx" → 3 decimals
  • "xx.x%" → 1 decimal with % suffix

The numeric value to format (None → "").

required fmt str

The format specifier string.

apply_fmt_fn(31.25, "xx.x") == "31.3"

def apply_fmt_fn(value: float | None, fmt: str) -> str:
    """Apply a format specifier to a numeric value.

    A tie rounds half away from zero, as SAS ``ROUND`` and the {cards}
    default: 31.25 at ``"xx.x"`` prints ``31.3``, -2.25 prints ``-2.3``.
    A value that rounds to zero prints ``0.0``, never ``-0.0``.

    Supported format patterns:
      - ``"xx"``       → integer (e.g. ``"86"``)
      - ``"xx.x"``     → 1 decimal (e.g. ``"75.2"``)
      - ``"xx.xx"``    → 2 decimals (e.g. ``"8.59"``)
      - ``"xx.xxx"``   → 3 decimals
      - ``"xx.x%"``    → 1 decimal with % suffix

    Args:
        value: The numeric value to format (None → ``""``).
        fmt: The format specifier string.

    Returns:
        str: The formatted string.

    References:
        SAS ROUND function (half away from zero); {cards}
        ``round_type`` default; ADR-0037.

    Examples:
        ``apply_fmt_fn(31.25, "xx.x") == "31.3"``
    """
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value)):
        return ""

    # Count decimal places from the "xx.xxx" pattern
    pct_suffix = fmt.endswith("%")
    clean = fmt.rstrip("%")

    if "." in clean:
        decimals = len(clean.split(".")[1])
    else:
        decimals = 0

    formatted = _round_half_away(float(value), decimals)
    if pct_suffix:
        formatted += "%"
    return formatted

def ard_to_table_model(
    ard: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> TableModel:
    """Shape a long-format ARD into a display-ready ``TableModel``.

    This is the core Phase 2 shaping function.  It:
    1. Extracts big-N from ``stat_name == "N"`` rows → column headers.
    2. Identifies header rows (``variable == ""``) → ``TableRow(row_type="header")``.
    3. Emits parent stubs (``"group"``), flat-block headings
       (``"section"`` from ``variable_label``), and level rows.
    4. Merges ``n`` + ``pct`` count stats into single display cells;
       expands continuous statistics into one display row per statistic
       under the level stub (the universal pharma layout).

    Args:
        ard: An ARD DataFrame in the {cards} long layout.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.  If ``None``, a blank
            ``RenderMetadata`` is used.

    Returns:
        TableModel: A display-ready table model suitable for any renderer.

    References:
        ADR-0039 (SOC row count, ``n (%) E`` and ``n/N (%)`` cells).

    Examples:
        Shape an ARD for rendering::

            spec = AESummarySpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()
    # The group columns are optional in the ARD schema.
    ard = ard.with_columns(
        pl.lit("", dtype=pl.Utf8).alias(c)
        for c in ("group2", "group2_level")
        if c not in ard.columns
    )

    # ── 1. Extract column order (arms) ──
    # Respect the order already present in the ARD (set by column_order in spec)
    arm_order: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for val in ard["group1_level"].to_list():
        if val and val not in seen:
            arm_order.append(val)
            seen.add(val)

    # ── 2. Extract big-N for column headers ──
    big_n_rows = ard.filter((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == ""))
    big_n_map: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in big_n_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        arm = row["group1_level"]
        val = row["stat"]
        if arm and val is not None and math.isfinite(val):
            big_n_map[arm] = int(val)

    columns = [ColumnHeader(label=arm, big_n=big_n_map.get(arm)) for arm in arm_order]

    # ── 3. Get non-big-N rows ──
    data_rows = ard.filter(~((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == "")))

    # ── 4. Display-row identity in appearance order ──
    # Nested ARDs emit the same child level once per parent, so the
    # parent lineage must be part of the display-row identity or cells
    # from different parents collapse into one row (last-write-wins).
    row_keys: list[_RowKey] = []
    row_keys_seen: set[_RowKey] = set()
    var_labels: dict[str, str] = {}
    has_var_label = "variable_label" in ard.columns
    for row in data_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        key = (
            row.get("group2") or "",
            row.get("group2_level") or "",
            row["variable"],
            row["variable_level"],
        )
        if key not in row_keys_seen:
            row_keys.append(key)
            row_keys_seen.add(key)
        if has_var_label and row["variable"] not in var_labels:
            var_labels[row["variable"]] = row.get("variable_label") or ""

    variable_set = {k[2] for k in row_keys}
    parent_vars = {k[0] for k in row_keys if k[0]}
    explicit_parents = parent_vars & variable_set
    # A parent of continuous rows (PARAMCD) keeps a blank stub; a count
    # parent (SOC) prints its own subject count.
    continuous_parents = set(
        data_rows.filter(~pl.col("stat_name").is_in(list(_COUNT_STAT_NAMES)))
        .select(pl.col("group2").fill_null(""), pl.col("group2_level").fill_null(""))
        .iter_rows()
    )
    stat_names = set(data_rows["stat_name"].unique().to_list())
    if {"n", "n_events"} <= stat_names and EVENTS_FOOTNOTE not in meta.footnotes:
        meta = replace(meta, footnotes=[*meta.footnotes, EVENTS_FOOTNOTE])

    # Stub column heading: one line per hierarchy level, top level first
    # and each child indented ("System Organ Class" / "  Preferred Term").
    # Non-breaking spaces survive the renderers' whitespace collapsing.
    stub_label = ""
    for k in row_keys:
        if not k[0] and k[2] in explicit_parents:
            parent = k[2]
            lines = [var_labels.get(parent, "")]
            for child in dict.fromkeys(kk[2] for kk in row_keys if kk[0] == parent):
                if child != parent and var_labels.get(child):
                    lines.append("  " + var_labels[child])
            stub_label = "\n".join(line for line in lines if line.strip())
            break

    # ── 5. Build display rows ──
    table_rows: list[TableRow] = []
    current_section: str | None = None
    current_synth_parent: tuple[str, str] | None = None

    for g2, g2l, variable, variable_level in _ordered_display_keys(row_keys):
        vl_rows = data_rows.filter(
            (pl.col("group2").fill_null("") == g2)
            & (pl.col("group2_level").fill_null("") == g2l)
            & (pl.col("variable") == variable)
            & (pl.col("variable_level") == variable_level)
        )
        stat_order, stat_labels, per_arm = _collect_cell_stats(vl_rows, arm_order)
        continuous = any(s not in _COUNT_STAT_NAMES for s in stat_order)
        empty_cells = {arm: "" for arm in arm_order}

        # ── Structure: header / group stub / synthetic parent / section ──
        if variable == "":
            # Header row (OverallStat)
            current_section = None
            current_synth_parent = None
            row_type, indent, bold = "header", 0, False
        elif variable in explicit_parents and not g2:
            # Parent stub row: SOC prints its count, PARAMCD stays blank.
            current_section = None
            current_synth_parent = None
            table_rows.append(
                TableRow(
                    label=variable_level,
                    row_type="group",
                    indent=0,
                    cells=dict(empty_cells)
                    if (variable, variable_level) in continuous_parents
                    else _merged_cells(arm_order, per_arm),
                    bold=True,
                    variable=variable,
                )
            )
            continue
        elif g2:
            # Child level inside a hierarchy.
            current_section = None
            if g2 not in explicit_parents:
                # No explicit parent rows — synthesise the stub from the
                # parent level so children don't float unanchored.
                if current_synth_parent != (g2, g2l):
                    table_rows.append(
                        TableRow(
                            label=g2l,
                            row_type="group",
                            indent=0,
                            cells=dict(empty_cells),
                            bold=True,
                            variable=g2,
                        )
                    )
                    current_synth_parent = (g2, g2l)
            else:
                current_synth_parent = None
            row_type, indent, bold = "data", 1, False
        else:
            # Flat block — emit the variable label as a section heading.
            current_synth_parent = None
            section_label = var_labels.get(variable, "")
            if section_label:
                if current_section != variable:
                    table_rows.append(
                        TableRow(
                            label=section_label,
                            row_type="section",
                            indent=0,
                            cells=dict(empty_cells),
                            bold=True,
                            variable=variable,
                        )
                    )
                    current_section = variable
                row_type, indent, bold = "data", 1, False
            else:
                current_section = None
                row_type, indent, bold = "flat", 0, False

        # ── Cells: merged count cell, or one row per statistic ──
        if continuous:
            table_rows.append(
                TableRow(
                    label=variable_level,
                    row_type=row_type,
                    indent=indent,
                    cells=dict(empty_cells),
                    bold=bold,
                    variable=variable,
                )
            )
            table_rows += _stat_rows(
                stat_order,
                stat_labels,
                arm_order,
                per_arm,
                indent=indent + 1,
                variable=variable,
            )
        else:
            table_rows.append(
                TableRow(
                    label=variable_level,
                    row_type=row_type,
                    indent=indent,
                    cells=_merged_cells(arm_order, per_arm),
                    bold=bold,
                    variable=variable,
                )
            )

    return TableModel(metadata=meta, columns=columns, rows=table_rows, stub_label=stub_label)

def listing_to_model(
    listing: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> ListingModel:
    """Shape a listing DataFrame into a display-ready ``ListingModel``.

    Args:
        listing: A Polars DataFrame from ``l_listing()``.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.

    Returns:
        ListingModel: A display-ready listing model.

    Examples:
        Shape a listing for rendering::

            listing = adae.tlg.ae.template("ael01").to_listing()
            model = listing_to_model(listing, RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7"))
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()
    col_labels = list(listing.columns)

    data: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for row in listing.iter_rows(named=True):
        data.append({col: _cell_text(v) for col, v in row.items()})

    return ListingModel(metadata=meta, column_labels=col_labels, data=data)

def render_html(
    model: TableModel,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
    page_by: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Pagination happens in the model layer (:func:`~fleet.tlg.render.paginate`):
    each page repeats title, column headers, and footnotes, carries a
    ``Page X of Y`` footer, and breaks on a real page in print/PDF media.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string.  If given, the
            generated ``<table>`` block replaces the ``{table}`` placeholder,
            enabling embedding in sponsor portals, Quarto documents, or
            interactive dashboards.  A wrapper with no ``{table}`` raises
            ``ValueError``.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page; ``None`` disables
            row-count splitting.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.

    Returns:
        str: An HTML fragment (a ``<div>`` with its ``<style>`` block,
            pure ASCII) or the fragment injected into *html_wrapper*.
            :func:`html_document` makes a complete document of it.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If *html_wrapper* has no ``{table}`` placeholder.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary to HTML::

            spec = AESummarySpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            html = render_html(model)
    """
    _check_wrapper(html_wrapper)
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page, page_by=page_by)

    parts: list[str] = ['<div class="fleet-table-container">', _SUMMARY_CSS]
    if len(pages) == 1:
        parts += _table_page_parts(pages[0])
    else:
        for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
            parts.append('<div class="fleet-page">')
            parts += _table_page_parts(page, page_footer=f"Page {idx} of {len(pages)}")
            parts.append("</div>")
    parts.append("</div>")

    return _wrap("\n".join(parts), html_wrapper)

def render_rtf(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
    page_by: str | None = None,
    body_title: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style RTF table.

    Every physical page carries the title, the column-header row (also
    flagged ``\\trhdr``), the footnotes, and ``Page X of Y`` from Word
    PAGE and NUMPAGES fields.  By default the title is in the Word page
    header and the footnotes in the page footer.  With *body_title*,
    they are body paragraphs, written again at each page break.  A page
    holds the rows that fit its height in points (title, header lines,
    footnotes and wrapped rows count), at most *rows_per_page*.  A page
    that starts inside a block repeats its parent rows with
    ``(continued)``.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum body rows per page (default 40).  ``None``
            keeps only the height budget.
        page_by: ARD variable to page-break on (e.g. ``"PARAMCD"``).
            Defaults to ``model.metadata.page_by``.
        body_title: Write the title and footnotes in the document body
            (SAS ODS RTF BODYTITLE) instead of the page header and footer.
            A text check of the body then sees them, but the page header
            is empty.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    References:
        ADR-0040 (title placement, page fields, page budget).  SAS ODS
        RTF: titles and footnotes in the page header and footer unless
        BODYTITLE.  r2rtf ``rtf_page(nrow=)`` counts title, header and
        footnote lines in the page budget.

    Examples:
        Inline AE summary to a submission RTF::

            spec = AESummarySpec(adsl_group_col="TRT01A")
            ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1"))
            render_rtf(model, "outputs/t_ae_summary.rtf")

        Title and footnotes in the body, as ODS RTF BODYTITLE::

            render_rtf(model, "outputs/t_ae_summary.rtf", body_title=True)
    """
    meta = model.metadata
    stub_w = int(_USABLE_W * 0.34)
    arm_w = (_USABLE_W - stub_w) // max(len(model.columns), 1)
    widths = [stub_w] + [arm_w] * len(model.columns)
    positions = _cell_positions(widths)
    aligns = [r"\ql"] + [r"\qc"] * len(model.columns)
    header_cells = [model.stub_label] + [col.display for col in model.columns]

    def row_cells(row: TableRow) -> list[str]:
        return [row.label] + [row.cells.get(col.label, "") for col in model.columns]

    groups, budget = _page_budget(meta, header_cells, widths, body_title=body_title)
    pages = _paginate(
        model,
        rows_per_page=rows_per_page,
        page_by=page_by,
        row_cost=lambda row: _row_height(row_cells(row), widths, row.indent),
        budget=budget,
    )

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER, *groups]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(_PAGE_BREAK)
        if body_title:
            parts += _title_block(meta.title, meta.subtitle)

        # Column headers: heavy rule above, light rule below.
        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                header_cells,
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row in enumerate(page.rows):
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    row_cells(row),
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    bold=row.bold,
                    indent=row.indent,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.rows) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        if body_title:
            parts += _footnote_block(meta.footnotes, spacer=True)

    parts += [_DOC_END, "}"]
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

def render_listing_rtf(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    rows_per_page: int | None = _DEFAULT_ROWS_PER_PAGE,
    body_title: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` as a pharma-style RTF listing.

    The page layout follows :func:`render_rtf`: title and footnotes in
    the page header and footer (or in the body with *body_title*),
    ``Page X of Y`` from Word fields, and a page budget in points that
    counts wrapped rows.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Optional output file path; the RTF is written when given.
        rows_per_page: Maximum data rows per page (default 40).  ``None``
            keeps only the height budget.
        body_title: Write the title and footnotes in the document body
            instead of the page header and footer.

    Returns:
        str: The complete RTF document.

    References:
        ADR-0040 (title placement, page fields, page budget).

    Examples:
        Lab abnormalities listing to RTF::

            listing = adlb.tlg.lb.l_listing()
            model = listing_to_model(listing, RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.8.1"))
            render_listing_rtf(model, "outputs/l_lb_abnormal.rtf")
    """
    meta = model.metadata
    n_cols = max(len(model.column_labels), 1)
    widths = [_USABLE_W // n_cols] * n_cols
    positions = _cell_positions(widths)
    aligns = [r"\ql"] * n_cols
    header_cells = list(model.column_labels)

    def row_cells(row_data: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
        return [row_data.get(label, "") for label in model.column_labels]

    groups, budget = _page_budget(meta, header_cells, widths, body_title=body_title)
    pages = _paginate_listing(
        model,
        rows_per_page=rows_per_page,
        row_cost=lambda row_data: _row_height(row_cells(row_data), widths),
        budget=budget,
    )

    parts: list[str] = [_DOC_HEADER, *groups]
    for idx, page in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        if idx > 1:
            parts.append(_PAGE_BREAK)
        if body_title:
            parts += _title_block(meta.title, meta.subtitle)

        parts.append(
            _row_rtf(
                header_cells,
                positions,
                aligns,
                header=True,
                border_top=_BDR_HEAVY,
                border_bottom=_BDR_LIGHT,
            )
        )

        for r_idx, row_data in enumerate(page.data):
            parts.append(
                _row_rtf(
                    row_cells(row_data),
                    positions,
                    aligns,
                    border_bottom=_BDR_HEAVY if r_idx == len(page.data) - 1 else None,
                )
            )

        if body_title:
            parts += _footnote_block(meta.footnotes, spacer=True)

    parts += [_DOC_END, "}"]
    return _write("\n".join(parts), path)

Each slide contains a fully editable PowerPoint table with: - Title and subtitle from RenderMetadata - Column headers with optional (N=xx) display - Row hierarchy with indentation and bold formatting - Footnotes rendered below the table

If python-pptx is not installed.

Render an AE summary ARD to editable slides::

def render_pptx(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    rows_per_page: int | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a fully editable PowerPoint table with:
    - Title and subtitle from ``RenderMetadata``
    - Column headers with optional (N=xx) display
    - Row hierarchy with indentation and bold formatting
    - Footnotes rendered below the table

    Long tables are chunked across slides via the model-layer paginator
    (title, headers, and footnotes repeat per slide), so a 300-row table
    never lands on one unreadable slide.

    The output is editable: users can modify fonts, colours, text, and
    layout in PowerPoint or LibreOffice Impress after export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.  Keys include
            ``font_name``, ``font_size_body``, ``header_bg``, etc.
            See ``_DEFAULT_THEME`` for all available keys.
        rows_per_page: Body rows per slide (default 15 — what fits a
            16:9 slide at the default body font).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary ARD to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import ard_to_table_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1", subtitle="AE Summary")
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
            render_pptx(model, "ae_summary.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    # Landscape 16:9
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank layout
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
        top = _add_title_block(slide, page.metadata, th)

        # ── Table dimensions ──
        n_cols = 1 + len(page.columns)  # stub + arms
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.rows)  # header + data rows

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        # Distribute column widths: stub gets 30%, rest evenly split
        stub_width = int(table_width * 0.30)
        arm_width = int((table_width - stub_width) / max(len(page.columns), 1))
        table.columns[0].width = Emu(stub_width)
        for ci in range(1, n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(arm_width)

        # ── Helper: set cell text + style ──
        def _set_cell(
            row_idx: int,
            col_idx: int,
            text: str,
            *,
            bold: bool = False,
            font_size: int | None = None,
            bg: str | None = None,
            fg: str | None = None,
            align: Any = PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
            table: Any = table,
        ) -> None:
            cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = text
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(font_size or th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = bold
            p.alignment = align
            if fg:
                p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(fg)
            if bg:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

        # ── Column headers ──
        _set_cell(0, 0, page.stub_label, bold=True, bg=th["header_bg"], fg=th["header_fg"])
        for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
            _set_cell(
                0,
                ci,
                col.display,
                bold=True,
                bg=th["header_bg"],
                fg=th["header_fg"],
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
            )

        # ── Data rows ──
        for ri, row in enumerate(page.rows, start=1):
            # Row background
            if row.row_type in ("group", "section"):
                bg = th["group_bg"]
            elif ri % 2 == 0:
                bg = th["alt_row_bg"]
            else:
                bg = None

            # Stub cell; the row model alone decides bold, as in HTML and RTF.
            indent_spaces = "  " * row.indent
            _set_cell(ri, 0, f"{indent_spaces}{row.label}", bold=row.bold, bg=bg)

            # Value cells
            for ci, col in enumerate(page.columns, start=1):
                val = row.cells.get(col.label, "")
                _set_cell(ri, ci, val, bold=row.bold, bg=bg, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        _add_footnotes(slide, page.metadata.footnotes, top + table_height, th)

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.
        rows_per_page: Data rows per slide (default 15).

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE listing to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import listing_to_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_listing_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7.1", subtitle="AE Listing")
            model = listing_to_model(listing_df, meta)
            render_listing_pptx(model, "ae_listing.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)
    pages = paginate_listing(model, rows_per_page=rows_per_page or _MAX_ROWS_PER_SLIDE)

    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    for page in pages:
        slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
        top = _add_title_block(slide, page.metadata, th)

        # ── Table ──
        n_cols = len(page.column_labels)
        n_rows = 1 + len(page.data)  # header + data

        table_width = Inches(12.3)
        table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
        table_left = Inches(0.5)

        tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(
            n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height
        )
        table = tbl_shape.table

        col_width = int(table_width / max(n_cols, 1))
        for ci in range(n_cols):
            table.columns[ci].width = Emu(col_width)

        # Headers
        for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
            cell = table.cell(0, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = lbl
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
            p.font.bold = True
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_bg"])
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_fg"])

        # Data rows
        for ri, row_data in enumerate(page.data, start=1):
            bg = th["alt_row_bg"] if ri % 2 == 0 else None
            for ci, lbl in enumerate(page.column_labels):
                cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
                cell.text = ""
                p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
                p.text = row_data.get(lbl, "")
                p.font.name = th["font_name"]
                p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
                p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
                if bg:
                    cell.fill.solid()
                    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

        _add_footnotes(slide, page.metadata.footnotes, top + table_height, th)

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

docs.title: Advanced Patterns
docs.text: Fleet provides significant flexibility to handle complex clinical trial scenarios that don't fit perfectly into standard CDISC verbs.

docs.title: Custom Derivations with Polars Expressions
docs.text: While Fleet provides verbs like .study_day() or .baseline(), you will often need custom logic to derive variables specific to a study.

docs.title: Simple Inline Derivations
docs.text:
For row-by-row logic or straightforward column math, use the .derivation() verb. It accepts four forms:

String expression (YAML-compatible, checked before it runs):

A string may use Polars expression constructors (pl.col, pl.lit, pl.when, ...), data types and expression methods. Fleet refuses anything else before evaluation: file and module access such as pl.read_csv, and methods that take a function or (de)serialise, such as pipe and map_elements. A callable: or derivations_module: in a define.yaml imports Python code, so review a received spec that holds them as a program.

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "AGEGR1",
    expression="pl.when(pl.col('AGE') < 65).then(pl.lit('<65 yrs')).otherwise(pl.lit('>=65 yrs'))",
).to_frame()

Direct pl.Expr (full Polars power):

import polars as pl

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "AGEGR1",
    expression=(
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 18)
        .then(pl.lit("<18"))
        .when(pl.col("AGE") <= 65)
        .then(pl.lit("18-65"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit(">65"))
    ),
).to_frame()

Date differences are durations, not days. In Polars, TRTEDT - TRTSDT gives a Duration, not a number of days as in SAS. In a string expression, flag, case_when and derivation refuse TRTEDT - TRTSDT > 10 and name the correct form, (TRTEDT - TRTSDT).dt.total_days() > 10. A direct pl.Expr is not checked: write (pl.col("TRTEDT") - pl.col("TRTSDT")).dt.total_days() yourself, or > 10 compares with 10 microseconds.

Lambda returning pl.Expr (inline, IDE auto-complete, no string sandbox):

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "AGEGR1",
    expression=lambda: (
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65)
        .then(pl.lit("<65 yrs"))
        .when(pl.col("AGE") >= 65)
        .then(pl.lit(">=65 yrs"))  # a missing AGE stays missing
    ),
).to_frame()

docs.title: @derivation — File-Based, Lineage-Tracked Derivations
docs.text: For study-specific logic that should be versioned, reused, and automatically documented in Define-XML, use the @derivation decorator. This is the primary escape-hatch pattern for anything too complex for a one-liner.

docs.title: Two kind values
docs.text:
Kind When to use Signature column Row-by-row expression (no DataFrame needed) () -> pl.Expr frame Multi-column or aggregation logic (df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame

What the function receives and returns:

  • column — the function takes no arguments and returns a pl.Expr. Fleet splices the expression into the lazy pipeline, so nothing is materialised: it behaves exactly like an inline .derivation(expression=...), just versioned in its own file. The result goes to the column named as the function (AGEGR1 below). An explicit .alias() on the expression wins.
  • frame — the df parameter is the pipeline's current state, materialised as a plain pl.DataFrame at the point the derivation runs (every column derived by earlier verbs is present). The function returns a pl.DataFrame — usually df.with_columns(...) — and Fleet wraps the result back into the namespace so the chain continues.

You rarely need to pass kind= yourself — it is inferred from the signature: a return annotation of pl.Expr (or a zero-argument function) means column; everything else is frame.

A new parameter row, such as BMI from WEIGHT and HEIGHT, is not a @derivation: use .adam.derive_param(). @derivation(by=..., set_values_to=...) raises VerbUsageError.

docs.title: kind="column" example
docs.text:
# programs/derivations/AGEGR1.py
from fleet.core.derivation import derivation
import polars as pl


@derivation
def AGEGR1() -> pl.Expr:
    """Classify AGE into pooled age groups for ADSL."""
    return (
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65)
        .then(pl.lit("<65 yrs"))
        .when(pl.col("AGE") >= 65)
        .then(pl.lit(">=65 yrs"))  # a missing AGE stays missing
    ).alias("AGEGR1")

Use it directly in a pipeline:

from programs.derivations import AGEGR1

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.derivation(AGEGR1).to_frame()

docs.title: kind="frame" example
docs.text:
@derivation(targets=["SAFFL", "ITTFL"])
def add_pop_flags(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add SAFFL and ITTFL population flags."""
    return df.with_columns(
        pl.lit("Y").alias("SAFFL"),
        pl.lit("Y").alias("ITTFL"),
    )

docs.title: A new parameter row: derive_param
docs.text:
advs = vs.adam.derive_param(
    by=["USUBJID", "ADT"],
    set_values_to={"PARAMCD": "BMI", "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"},
    parameter_filter={"WEIGHT": "WEIGHT", "HEIGHT": "HEIGHT"},
    analysis_value=pl.col("WEIGHT") / (pl.col("HEIGHT") / 100) ** 2,
).to_frame()

docs.title: Derivations folder convention
docs.text:
Study derivations live under the study's configured programs tree:

programs/derivations/       # <programs dir from study_config.yaml>
    __init__.py
    AGEGR1.py
    BMI.py

Scaffold a new derivation with the CLI (config-context — run it anywhere inside the study workspace):

fleet derivation add AGEGR1 --dataset ADSL --kind column

The convention is standard-agnostic: the same @derivation objects and callable: escape hatch work in SDTM pipelines and specs exactly as in ADaM — both dispatch through the shared core registry.

docs.title: Complex Multi-Dataset Derivations (Escaping the Pipeline)
docs.text:
For highly complex, advanced logic—such as derivations requiring customized multi-dataset joins, complex rolling window aggregations, or logic that simply cannot be expressed linearly in standard verbs—the recommended pattern is to "escape" the automated pipeline.

Because Fleet is built securely on Polars DataFrames, you can drop out to native Polars, compute your advanced logic, merge it back, and then seamlessly resume your Fleet pipeline.

import polars as pl

# 1. Start by compiling your base ADSL dataset to a Polars DataFrame
# (Assuming you already have adsl base and adverse events dataframes)
base_adsl = (
    adsl_pipeline.to_frame()
)  # or dm.adam.from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL").to_frame()

# 2. Compute complex custom logic using pure Polars (e.g. tracking a multi-step clinical event pattern)
# Here we find patients who had a Severe AE specifically after taking a certain concomitant medication.
complex_events = (
    base_adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT"])
    .join(ae_df.filter(pl.col("AESEV") == "SEVERE"), on="USUBJID", how="inner")
    .join(cm_df.filter(pl.col("CMINDC") == "NAUSEA"), on="USUBJID", how="left")
    .group_by("USUBJID")
    .agg(
        [
            pl.when(pl.col("AESTDTC").min() > pl.col("CMSTDTC").min())
            .then(pl.lit("Y"))
            .otherwise(pl.lit("N"))
            .alias("CUSTFL")
        ]
    )
)

# 3. Merge the result natively using Polars
merged_adsl = base_adsl.join(complex_events, on="USUBJID", how="left")

# 4. Jump back into Fleet if you need to finalize any remaining standard derivations or metadata
final_adsl = merged_adsl.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "CUSTFL", expression=pl.col("CUSTFL").fill_null("N")
).to_frame()

This pattern ensures you are never bottlenecked by the package API: if you can write it in Polars, you can execute it in Fleet.

docs.title: Subclassing Namespaces
docs.text:
If your organisation uses standard proprietary derivations across multiple datasets, you can extend Fleet namespaces by subclassing them. Every Fleet verb returns Self, so a chain of Fleet verbs keeps the subclass type.

from typing import Self

from fleet.adam.namespace import AdamNamespace
import polars as pl


class CompanyAdamNamespace(AdamNamespace):
    def proprietary_flag(self, target_col: str, condition: str) -> Self:
        """Re-usable custom flag for your company."""
        expr = pl.when(pl.col(condition) == "Y").then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit(None))
        return self._chain(expr.alias(target_col))


# You can register this as a custom accessor using Polars
@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("company_adam")
class _CompanyAdamPolarsAccessor(CompanyAdamNamespace):
    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame):
        super().__init__(df)

docs.title: Handling Non-CDISC Raw Sources
docs.text:
