The define refuses a qualifier that cannot move: the parent has no STUDYID or USUBJID, a parent other than DM has no <domain>SEQ, the spec also declares SUPP<domain>, the name has more than 8 characters (QNAM), the label has more than 40 characters (QLABEL), or the qualifier is a key of the parent. Give CRF pages of a qualifier with crf_pages: on the variable: a key AE.AETRTEM in an external page map does not reach SUPPAE.

docs.title: CRF Page References
docs.text:
Variables with origin: Collected can include page references to the annotated Case Report Form PDF. Fleet emits these as <def:DocumentRef> / <def:PDFPageRef> elements inside <def:Origin> in the Define-XML, and the standard define2-1.xsl stylesheet renders them as clickable links.

One origin vocabulary

origin: uses the Define-XML 2.1 Origin Types — Collected, Derived, Assigned, Protocol, Predecessor — and the same values flow into QORIG in generated SUPPQUAL datasets. Collected values also carry def:Source, which defaults to Investigator (CRF data); override it with origin_source: Vendor | Sponsor | Subject. The Define-XML 2.0 spellings CRF and eDT are not valid.

How the Origin description renders, per origin type:

  • Predecessor requires predecessor: DATASET.VARIABLE (schema-enforced); the define renders Predecessor: DM.COUNTRY. A condition may follow: predecessor: "DS.DSDECOD where DS.DSCAT='DISPOSITION EVENT'". In an ADaM spec, a variable carried with algorithm: assign and source: but still marked Collected triggers a generation-time warning suggesting the Predecessor form. When freezing an inline pipeline, to_spec_yaml(dataset="ADSL", predecessor="DM") pre-fills these entries for carry-through columns and pure copies of a column present at the start of the chain. A column a verb added with no lineage (merge) gets a TODO stub, never a Predecessor. The emitted YAML stays the explicit, reviewable source of truth.
  • Derived describes the derivation in its MethodDef.
  • Assigned / Protocol show the comment: — e.g. comment: DM.ARM renders Assigned: DM.ARM.
  • Collected with CRF pages renders the page links; Investigator-collected variables without pages fall back to a Case Report Form description.
  • A variable with value-level metadata and no comment: renders See Value Level Metadata.
- name: COUNTRY
  label: Country
  type: text
  origin: Predecessor
  predecessor: DM.COUNTRY

docs.title: Setup: declare the aCRF document
docs.text:
Scaffold the block with one command (config-context: it edits the study's own define.yaml; --standard adam|both covers the ADaM spec too):

uv run fleet add-acrf --href blankcrf.pdf
uv run fleet add-acrf --href blankcrf.pdf --page-map acrf_pages.yaml --standard both

Which adds a documents block to the study: section:

study:
  id: CDISCPILOT01
  standard: SDTMIG
  standard_version: "3.4"
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf # path in the submission package
      title: Annotated Case Report Form # displayed in Define-XML

This emits the top-level <def:AnnotatedCRF> container and the <def:leaf> element that the XSLT needs to render document links.

docs.title: Layer 1 — Simple page strings (most common)
docs.text:
Add crf_pages to any collected variable:

variables:
  - name: SEX
    label: Sex
    type: text
    origin: Collected
    crf_pages: "8" # single page
    derivation:
      algorithm: assign
      source: sex
      ct: C66731

  - name: RACE
    label: Race
    type: text
    origin: Collected
    crf_pages: "8 9" # space-separated multiple pages

The string value maps directly to the PageRefs attribute with Type="PhysicalRef". A number (crf_pages: 8 in YAML) is read as the page string "8". Without study.documents.annotated_crf, the pages cannot be written: Fleet gives a warning that names each variable.

A value-level variable takes its own pages: the key of its page map entry is DATASET.VARIABLE.<where values> (for example LB.LBORRES.ALB), and the parent DATASET.VARIABLE is the fallback.

docs.title: Layer 2 — Rich references (named destinations, page ranges)
docs.text:
For PDF bookmarks or page ranges, use the dict form:

- name: SEX
  origin: Collected
  crf_pages:
    pages: "DM_SEX" # PDF bookmark name
    type: NamedDestination # or PhysicalRef (default)

- name: RACE
  origin: Collected
  crf_pages:
    pages: "8 9"
    type: PhysicalRef
    first_page: "8" # optional range attributes
    last_page: "9"

doc: names the href of the annotated CRF or of a supplemental document. A doc: that matches no declared document stops generation with a SpecError that names the variable.

docs.title: Layer 3 — External page map (EDC-driven workflows)
docs.text:
For studies where CRF annotations are extracted from an EDC system, point to an external YAML file:

study:
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf
      page_map: acrf_pages.yaml # relative to the define.yaml directory

The page map file uses DOMAIN.VARIABLE keys:

# acrf_pages.yaml — auto-generated from EDC export
DM.SEX: "7"
DM.BRTHDTC: "8"
AE.AETERM: "12 13"
VS.VSTESTCD: "20"

Inline crf_pages on individual variables always take precedence over the external page map. A page_map file that does not exist stops generation with a SpecError. Page map keys that match no variable of the spec give one warning that lists them.

docs.title: Supplemental documents
docs.text:
Additional supporting documents (reviewer's guide, protocol, etc.) can be declared alongside the annotated CRF:

study:
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf
    supplemental_docs:
      - id: LF.ReviewerGuide
        href: reviewers-guide.pdf
        title: Reviewer's Guide

These emit <def:SupplementalDoc> and corresponding <def:leaf> elements.

docs.title: Trust: a study folder is code
docs.text:
Treat a define.yaml or a study_config.yaml from another party as code, not as data. Read it before you run it.

  • callable: and derivations_module: import a Python module and run it.
  • validation.engine_path in study_config.yaml starts a program.
  • An expression: string is checked against an allow-list of Polars names and methods. The allow-list stops mistakes. It is not a security boundary.

To report a security problem, see SECURITY.md at the root of the repository.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The inputs block declares which upstream datasets the pipeline should join/merge.
  • Variables with no derivation block are expected to flow in via the source dataset — they appear in Define-XML as origin: Collected.
  • Run uv run fleet check (or fleet define-xml --strict) to catch schema errors and Define-XML gaps before submission.

docs.title: Exporting Datasets
docs.text:
Fleet writes datasets in three formats, selected the same way everywhere — one --format flag on the CLI, one output_format: key in the spec, one writer function per format in Python.

Format File When to use Requires Parquet (default) .parquet Working format: fast, typed, compressed; ideal between pipeline steps and for QC — SAS XPT (v5 Transport) .xpt Regulatory submission datasets; SAS interop io extra (pyreadstat) CDISC Dataset-JSON v1.1 .json The emerging submission exchange format; typed, metadata-rich —

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
Every dataset-writing command takes the same flag and resolves its output directory from study_config.yaml:

uv run fleet run --format xpt                 # define.yaml pipelines → <sdtm_data>/<adam_data>
uv run fleet run --format dataset-json --dataset ADSL
uv run fleet tdd build --format xpt           # trial design domains → <sdtm_data>

docs.title: From the spec (output_format:)
docs.text:
Declare the format once in define.yaml — per dataset or spec-wide. The choice is recorded in the pipeline DAG and drives the Define-XML leaf hrefs. fleet run writes each dataset in the same format: --format, else the dataset's output_format:, else the spec's, else parquet. A --format that differs from the define warns, and fleet define-xml warns when a leaf names a file that the data folder does not hold. output: names the leaf href only; fleet run warns when it writes another file name:

output_format: parquet          # spec-level default
datasets:
  - name: ADSL
    output_format: xpt          # per-dataset override

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
from fleet import save_parquet, save_dataset_json
from fleet.io import save_xpt

save_parquet(adsl, Path("data/adam/adsl.parquet"))
save_xpt(adsl, Path("data/adam/adsl.xpt"))
save_dataset_json(
    adsl, "data/adam/adsl.json", domain="ADSL", label="Subject-Level Analysis Dataset"
)

Format-specific behaviour worth knowing:

  • XPT is SAS transport version 5, the submission format of FDA TCG 3.1.1, and the member is named as the file (adsl.xpt holds ADSL). Names are upper-cased. A pl.Date is stored as a SAS date with DATE9, a pl.Datetime with DATETIME20 and a pl.Time with TIME8. NaN and infinity become SAS missing. Nothing is cut: a name over 8 characters, a label over 40 or a value over 200 bytes stops the write. A value that is not ASCII is written as UTF-8 bytes, with a warning. Pass label= and column_labels= for the dataset and variable labels; fleet run takes them from define.yaml. Install the writer with uv add "fleet-cdisc[io]".
  • Dataset-JSON embeds dataset metadata (domain, label, originator, file OID) alongside typed column data. Pass columns= for the variable labels, lengths and key sequence, and study_oid= and metadata_version_oid= for the define. fleet run and to_dataset_json after from_spec take them from define.yaml. Each itemOID is the ItemDef OID of the Define-XML. A pl.Date, pl.Datetime or pl.Time is written with targetDataType: integer and DATE9., DATETIME20. or TIME8., so read_dataset_json gives the date back. NaN and infinity are written as null, with a warning, because JSON has no such number. A duration column stops the write: convert it to a number first. read_dataset_json reads float and decimal as pl.Float64, as SAS holds them, and an integer written as 63.0 as 63.
  • Parquet forwards any keyword arguments to Polars' write_parquet (compression, statistics, ...).

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
The mirror-image loaders auto-detect format from the extension — CSV, Parquet, XPT, and SAS7BDAT all land as LazyFrames:

from fleet import load_raw_data, load_datasets

dm_raw = load_raw_data("data/raw/dm_raw.csv")  # one file → LazyFrame
frames = load_datasets(
    {"DM": "data/sdtm/dm.parquet", "AE": "data/sdtm/ae.xpt"}  # many files → dict
)

What the readers decide for you:

  • A SAS blank is a missing value. SAS has one character missing value, the blank, so a blank in an XPT or SAS7BDAT file reads as null and is_null() finds it. A variable with no value keeps its SAS type.
  • A CSV file holds no types. Polars infers them from every row. A column with a leading zero (SITEID 001) stays text, with a warning, because a number would lose the zero. schema_overrides={"LBORRES": pl.String} is the $ informat; your types always win. fleet run reads the variables of define type text, and their raw source columns, as text.
  • The encoding is yours to name. A file from a WLATIN1 SAS session needs load_raw_data(path, encoding="iso-8859-1"), or --encoding iso-8859-1 on fleet compare and fleet validate. A keyword the reader does not take raises; it is never dropped.

In a join on keys a missing key matches a missing key, as SAS MERGE BY does, in every verb that joins (merge, pick, first_date, derive_param, ...).

docs.title: Not to be confused with TLG render formats
docs.text: Tables and listings render to display formats — HTML, RTF, PDF, PPTX — via fleet tlg run --format .... Those are outputs for humans; this page covers dataset files for machines and submissions. See TLG from a Spec.

docs.title: Interactive Explorer — One Definition, Two Run Modes
docs.text: Interactive exploration apps and batch TLG programs usually drift apart because the table definition lives twice — once in the app's modules, once in the production scripts. Fleet avoids that structurally: the TLG spec YAML is the definition, and both run modes consume the same file through the same engine.

docs.title: Declare degrees of freedom on the spec
docs.text:
Add an interactive: block to a TLG spec. Every choice is just a value for an existing spec field — a widget is a spec-field selector, nothing more:

template: aet01
schema_version: 1
adsl_filter: 'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"'
statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct]

interactive:
  population:                            # -> adsl_filter
    - {label: Safety, filter: 'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"', default: true}
    - {label: All subjects, filter: null}
  dataset_filter:                        # -> dataset_filter
    - {label: All AEs, filter: null, default: true}
    - {label: Serious only, filter: 'pl.col("AESER") == "Y"'}
  stats:                                 # -> statistics
    - {label: "n (%)", statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct], default: true}
    - {label: "+ events", statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct, n_events]}

Axes: groupby (arm column), population (ADSL filter presets), dataset_filter, and stats. Each axis needs exactly one default: true; an absent axis stays fixed at the spec value. Each default must equal the spec field it maps onto (groupby to columns[0], population to adsl_filter, dataset_filter to dataset_filter, stats to statistics). If not, the spec does not load, and the error names the axis.

docs.title: Two run modes, same artifact
docs.text:
# Batch — renders the default variant (submission output):
fleet tlg run examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml --data adae.parquet --adsl adsl.parquet -o out/

# Interactive — one self-contained HTML file, no server, no new dependencies:
fleet tlg explore examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml --data adae.parquet --adsl adsl.parquet -o explorer.html

The explorer pre-renders every declared variant through the identical spec → ARD → render path and embeds, per variant: the HTML fragment, the ARD as downloadable JSON (for QC), and the exact spec YAML in a "show definition" panel. The embedded JavaScript only shows/hides pre-rendered fragments — no statistics or layout logic exists client-side, so there is no second implementation that could drift. Works from a shared drive; makes no network requests.

docs.title: Why drift is impossible
docs.text:
• The batch output is the explorer's default variant — same functions, same build. A golden test pins them byte-identical, and the spec refuses to load when an axis default differs from the spec field that batch reads.
  • Promotion needs no transcription: the "show definition" panel displays the current view's spec YAML, with that view's choices marked default: true; adopting it means saving that YAML into your specs directory, which the batch run then consumes.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Variant space is the cartesian product of declared choices: hard error above 500 variants, warning above 100. This is not an engine bottleneck — the Polars pipeline renders hundreds of variants in seconds. The cap protects the artifact: the explorer is one self-contained HTML file with every variant pre-rendered and embedded (fragment + ARD JSON + spec YAML), so the file grows linearly with the variant count and a 500-variant page is unusable to open, review, and share — which defeats its purpose. Beyond that scale, a live server that renders on demand is the right tool (a future fleet tlg serve); the static explorer deliberately trades variant count for zero-infrastructure portability.
  • Views are sanctioned-only (declared choices, not free-form filtering) — every number a reviewer sees was produced by the validated engine at build time.

docs.title: Multi-Source Event Derivation with pick()
docs.text: Many ADaM variables scan several data sources and keep one value per subject: the latest date over all sources, or the first source that has a value. Admiral calls this pattern derive_vars_extreme_event / event(). Fleet provides pick(), one verb that replaces multi-step joins, coalesces, and manual priority logic.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Consider LSTALVDT (Last Date Known Alive). The derivation spec typically reads:

Set LSTALVDT to the latest date from:

  1. Death date (DTHDT) — if the subject died
  2. Last AE end date (AENDT)
  3. Last AE start date (ASTDT)
  4. Treatment end date (TRTEDT) — fallback

Each "event" has its own source dataset, filter condition, and column to extract. The latest date over all events wins for each subject, whatever the list position.

Without pick(), you'd need:

# Manual approach — 3 last_date lookups + a row-wise maximum
adsl = (
    adsl.adam.adsl.last_date("_dth", from_dataset=adsl_df, date_col="DTHDT")
    .last_date("_ae_end", from_dataset=adae, date_col="AENDT")
    .last_date("_ae_start", from_dataset=adae, date_col="ASTDT")
    .derivation(
        "LSTALVDT", expression='pl.max_horizontal("_dth", "_ae_end", "_ae_start", "TRTEDT")'
    )
    .to_frame()
    .drop(["_dth", "_ae_end", "_ae_start"])
)

This is verbose, error-prone, and loses traceability: the record behind each date is gone.

docs.title: The Solution: pick()
docs.text:
adsl = adsl.adam.adsl.pick(
    "LSTALVDT",
    events=[
        {
            "when": pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT"},
            "source": adsl_df,
            "label": "Death date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AENDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AENDT"},
            "source": adae,
            "label": "AE end date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("ASTDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "ASTDT"},
            "source": adae,
            "label": "AE start date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("TRTEDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "TRTEDT"},
            "label": "Treatment end (self)",
        },
    ],
    by=["USUBJID"],
    order_by=["LSTALVDT"],
    mode="last",
).to_frame()

order_by=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last" at top level makes every event compete on the date: the latest one wins. Each event's "label" documents intent. No temporary columns needed.

All events set LSTALVDT from date columns (AENDT and ASTDT come from .date() on the AE text). An event that sets a target from DTC text while another sets it from a date raises a DerivationError.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Events list] --> PE

    subgraph PE["For each event"]
        direction TB
        C[Filter source by 'when' condition]
        D[Apply 'set' mappings to targets]
        E[Group by 'by' vars]
        F[Select record per mode / order]
        G[Tag with event list position]
        C --> D --> E --> F --> G
    end

    PE --> H[Stack all candidate records]
    H --> I[Sort by top-level order, then list position]
    I --> J[Keep first per group = winner]
    J --> K[Left-join targets back to base frame]

Key properties:

  1. Within-event selection uses the event's mode and order_by, or the top-level ones.
  2. With a top-level order_by, every event's record competes on that order and mode, as admiral derive_vars_extreme_event does. order_by=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last" gives the latest date over all sources. A tie goes to the first listed event.
  3. With no top-level order_by, the first listed event that has a record wins: a priority cascade, as the admiral DTHCAUS template.
  4. Subjects with no matching events get null for all targets. A target keeps the type of its source columns, also when no event has a record.
  5. A target that is already a pipeline column is replaced.

docs.title: Event Dict Reference
docs.text:
Each event is a Python dict with these keys:

Key Required Type Description "when" Yes str \| pl.Expr Boolean filter — which records qualify "set" Yes dict[str, str \| pl.Expr \| Any] Maps each target to a source column name, expression, or literal (pl.lit("Y")). A key that is not a target raises "source" No pl.DataFrame External dataset to scan. Omit to use the current pipeline frame "mode" No str Override top-level mode for this event ("first" / "last") "order_by" No str \| list[str] Override top-level sort for this event "label" No str Documentation-only description (ignored at runtime)

docs.title: Multiple Targets
docs.text:
pick() can derive several columns simultaneously from the same events:

adsl = adsl.adam.adsl.pick(
    ["LSTALVDT", "DTHFL"],
    events=[
        {
            "when": pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT", "DTHFL": pl.lit("Y")},
            "source": adsl_df,
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AENDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AENDT", "DTHFL": pl.lit("N")},
            "source": adae,
        },
    ],
    by=["USUBJID"],
    order_by=["LSTALVDT"],
    mode="last",
).to_frame()

When an event only sets some targets, the others remain null for that event's candidates.

docs.title: String Conditions (YAML-Compatible)
docs.text:
For spec-driven pipelines, conditions can be strings that get evaluated safely:

events = [
    {"when": 'pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null()', "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT"}},
]

This gives the same result as a pl.Expr, and a define.yaml can hold it. When an event holds a pl.DataFrame or a pl.Expr, to_spec_yaml() cannot write it and writes a TODO stub for the variable.

docs.title: Admiral Comparison
docs.text:
Admiral Fleet event(dataset, condition, set_values_to, order, mode) Event dict in events list derive_vars_extreme_event(events, source_datasets, by_vars, order, mode, check_type) .pick(targets, events=..., by=..., order_by=..., mode=...) order = exprs(LSTALVDT), mode = "last": latest value over all events order_by=["LSTALVDT"], mode="last" Ties on order go to the first event in the list Ties on order_by go to the first event in events DTHCAUS template: first listed event with a record No top-level order_by: first listed event with a record Requires pre-built event objects + explicit dataset references Inline dicts with optional "source" — current frame used by default

Compared with admiral, Fleet's pick():

  • Eliminates the need for a separate event() constructor
  • Supports per-event mode/order overrides
  • Accepts literals (pl.lit("Y")) directly in "set" alongside column references
  • Chains into the ADaM pipeline with no .to_frame() call (it reads the data once, at the verb)

docs.title: When to Use pick() vs @derivation
docs.text:
Scenario Use Multi-source extreme value or first-source cascade (LSTALVDT, DTHCAUS, LDDTHELD) pick() Simple conditional (AGEGR1, EOSSTT) case_when() Complex cross-record logic within one source (CBOR confirmation rules) @derivation(kind="frame") Aggregation that needs custom grouping (derived parameters) derive_param()

Rule of thumb: If your logic is "the latest (or first) value over sources A, B and C", or "try source A, then B, then C", use pick(). If it requires comparing multiple records within the same subject to determine a single result (e.g., sustained response confirmation), use a @derivation.

docs.title: Spec-Driven Usage
docs.text:
In a define.yaml, the pick block goes under the variable's derivation:. Use date columns (AEENDT, not the text AEENDTC), so that the dates compare as dates:

variables:
  - name: LSTALVDT
    label: Last Date Known Alive
    type: date
    derivation:
      algorithm: pick
      events:
        - when: 'pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null()'
          set: {LSTALVDT: DTHDT}
          source: ADSL
        - when: 'pl.col("AEENDT").is_not_null()'
          set: {LSTALVDT: AEENDT}
          source: AE
        - when: 'pl.col("TRTEDT").is_not_null()'
          set: {LSTALVDT: TRTEDT}
          source: ADSL
      by: [USUBJID]
      order_by: [LSTALVDT]
      mode: last

Each source: name is a pinned dataset. Pin them before from_spec(); a name with no pin raises PinError:

adsl = (
    adsl_df.adam.adsl.pin(ADSL=adsl_df, AE=adae).from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL").to_frame()
)

algorithm:, events: or targets: beside name: (not under derivation:) raise SpecError.

docs.title: Namespace Pipeline Architecture
docs.text: Fleet lets you write the same pipeline in two notations: Code-driven (chaining verbs in Python) or Spec-driven (declaring the same verbs in a define.yaml that Fleet executes for you). Verb names and argument names are identical in both, so a step can move between them.

docs.title: The Recommended Approach: Spec-First with Custom Extensions
docs.text:
For the majority of modern statistical programming tasks, we highly recommend a hybrid "Spec-First" workflow.

In this approach, you let AI or your documentation team generate the define.yaml. Fleet consumes this YAML to automatically manage 90% of the derivations, dependencies, traceability, and Define-XML generation. Then, for the 10% of highly complex, proprietary derivations that do not fit neatly into a YAML file, you apply a thin layer of manual Polars python code on top of the built data step.

This hybrid approach ensures high reproducibility and documentation sync, while leaving an "escape hatch" open for when code must take over.

docs.title: 1. Code-Driven (Inline Python)
docs.text:
Best for: Quick exploration, ad-hoc analysis, smaller studies, or initial data discovery.

You construct your pipelines entirely in Python by chaining namespace verbs on Polars DataFrames. All logic is embedded directly in your scripts.

Example:

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID").duration("ADY", start="TRTSDT", end="ADT").to_frame()

docs.title: 2. Spec-Driven (define.yaml)
docs.text:
Best for: Production clinical trials, regulatory submissions, repeatability across projects.

You define metadata, controlled terminology, and derivations in a central define.yaml file. Fleet reads the specification and automatically builds the datasets. In this model, your Python scripts simply load the study context and call .from_spec().

Example of the Hybrid Escape Hatch:

# The standard derivations live in define.yaml.
import polars as pl
import fleet  # noqa: F401

dm = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/dm.parquet")
base_adsl = dm.adam.from_spec("specs/study01/adam/define.yaml", dataset="ADSL").to_frame()

# Add custom logic for the 10% of edge-case scenarios not covered by the spec:
final_adsl = base_adsl.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "CUSTOM_FLAG", expression=pl.when(pl.col("AGE") > 80).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit("N"))
).to_frame()

docs.title: How the pipeline works underneath
docs.text:
Every Fleet namespace (sdtm, adam, adsl, occds) follows the same pattern:

  1. Access the namespace on a Polars DataFrame: df.sdtm
  2. Chain verb calls — each returns a new namespace object accumulating pl.Expr objects
  3. Materialise with .to_frame() — Polars runs the lazy plan
result = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")  # 1. access  # 2. chain
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"Male": "M", "Female": "F"})
    .to_frame()  # 3. materialise
)

assign is the one canonical assignment verb (source= copies, value= hardcodes, ct=/ct_map= add CT). Most verbs append to one lazy plan. Some verbs read data before the chain continues: checks (baseline, date to a DTC variable) and verbs that build or filter records (whereclauses, pick, derive_*, nodup). The chain does not break at these verbs.

To inspect intermediate state or the query plan during development, use the chainable debug verbs .inspect() (hard checkpoint with diagnostic output) and .explain() (print the Polars query plan). See Advanced Patterns for details.

docs.title: Lazy evaluation
docs.text:
df.sdtm                              one LazyFrame (df.lazy())
  │
  ├─ .assign("USUBJID", source=...)  →  plan + with_columns(USUBJID)
  ├─ .assign("SEX", ct=...)          →  plan + with_columns(SEX)
  ├─ .explain()                      →  prints the plan, the chain continues
  └─ .to_frame()                     →  plan.collect(): one Polars query

Each verb adds one step to the plan of one LazyFrame. Nothing runs until to_frame(). Polars then optimises the full plan and runs it once. The steps run in the order of the chain. The verbs that read data before the chain continues are listed in the GUIDE laziness table ("What is lazy, and what checkpoints").

docs.title: SDTM verbs at a glance
docs.text: Verb Purpose assign(target, source=) Copy raw column assign(target, value=) Constant literal for all rows assign(target, source=, ct=, ct_map=) Copy + validate/recode through a codelist case_when(target, when=, else_=) Multi-branch conditional date(target, source=) Normalise to ISO 8601 date or datetime derivation(target, expression=) Arbitrary pl.Expr merge(dataset, on=, keep=) Join a reference dataset to_frame() Materialise

docs.title: ADaM verbs at a glance
docs.text: Verb Purpose source(*targets) Variadic pass-through column(s) derivation(target, expression=) Arbitrary pl.Expr assign(target, value=) Constant literal date(target, source=) Parse DTC → Date/Datetime with imputation duration(target, start=, end=) CDISC study day / elapsed time flag(target, criteria=, by=) Per-group boolean flag baseline(target, aval=, baseline_flag=, by=) Carry baseline AVAL within groups chg(target, aval, base) Change from baseline pchg(target, aval, base) Percent change from baseline bmi(target, weight, height) Body Mass Index nrind(target, value, low, high) Normal range indicator (LOW/NORMAL/HIGH) on_treatment(target, adt, trtsdt, trtedt) On-treatment flag shift(target, baseline_cat, post_cat) Categorical shift string bsa(target, weight, height, method) Body Surface Area (4 methods) map(target, systolic, diastolic) Mean Arterial Pressure qtc(target, qt, rr, method, rr_unit) Corrected QT (QT in ms, RR in ms by default) derive_summary_records(by, ...) Aggregate by group, append summary rows derive_locf_records(dataset_ref, by, order_by, ...) Add LOCF records for the expected visits derive_param(by=, set_values_to=, ...) Derive a new parameter and append as rows to_frame() Materialise

docs.text: Verb Purpose source(target) Pass-through column first_date(target, from_dataset, date_col, where) Earliest event date per subject last_date(target, from_dataset, date_col, where) Latest event date per subject duration(target, start, end) Elapsed days / duration flag(target, criteria) "Y" flag (expression, first/last/max/min/exists) count_events(target, from_dataset, where) Event count per subject age_years(target, age_col, age_unit_col) Unit-aware age conversion to years derive_period(periods=) Subperiod/Phase variables (APxxSDT, etc.) to_frame() Materialise

docs.title: StudyContext — workspace initialisation
docs.text:
The recommended way to start a new study is the bootstrapping pipeline via the Fleet CLI:

fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./studies/STUDY01
fleet init define --config ./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml  # queries CDISC Library IG → define.yaml
fleet init ct     --config ./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml  # reads define.yaml → codelists.py

Note

When --root points to a non-current directory, pass --config <root>/study_config.yaml to init define and init ct, or cd into the root directory before running them.

See the CLI Reference for full details.

StudyContext.init() can also be used programmatically — it creates the folder tree and writes study_config.yaml. Define specs and codelists are produced by the subsequent pipeline steps (fleet init define, fleet init ct).

from fleet import StudyContext, load_study_context
from fleet.core.study_context import ADAMConfig, SDTMConfig
from pathlib import Path

# ── Once, when starting a new study ──────────────────────────────────────
ctx = StudyContext.init(
    "./studies/STUDY01",
    study_id="STUDY01",
    company="Acme Pharma",
    sdtm=SDTMConfig(ig_version="3-4", domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]),
    adam=ADAMConfig(ig_version="1-1", datasets=["ADSL", "ADVS"]),
)

# ── Every subsequent session ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ctx = load_study_context(Path("./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml"))
Outcome Behaviour Directories already exist Silently skipped (mkdir -p semantics) study_config.yaml exists Raises StudyConfigError — use load_study_context() instead

docs.title: Trial Design Domains
docs.text:
Fleet provides first-class support for the seven CDISC Trial Design Model (TDD) domains, plus the subject-level SV and SE, through two complementary paths:

  1. fleet.StudyDesign — a typed aggregate: define the design once, derive every domain, audit it, round-trip it through YAML, import it from USDM, and draw it as a Mermaid review diagram.
  2. Row-level pipeline — a fixed-sequence verb chain with rich Pydantic models and collection-level validators, for full row control.

SDTMIG 3.4 structures for the TDD domains ship with Fleet, so everything on this page runs offline — no CDISC Library API key required.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Domain Full Name Structure Type TE Trial Elements 1 rec/element Protocol-reference TA Trial Arms 1 rec/element/arm Protocol-reference TV Trial Visits 1 rec/visit/arm Protocol-reference TS Trial Summary 1 rec/parameter/seq Protocol-reference TI Trial Inclusion/Exclusion 1 rec/criterion Protocol-reference TD Trial Disease Assessments 1 rec/assessment plan Protocol-reference TM Trial Disease Milestones 1 rec/milestone type Protocol-reference SV Subject Visits 1 rec/subject/visit Subject-level SE Subject Elements 1 rec/subject/element Subject-level

docs.title: StudyDesign — define once, derive everything
docs.text:
fleet.StudyDesign is the single source of truth for a study's structure. Arms are declared as element paths; TAETORD, ELEMENT, EPOCH, and TABRANCH (at the randomization branch point) are derived mechanically:

import fleet

design = fleet.StudyDesign(
    study_id="CDISCPILOT01",
    elements=[
        {
            "etcd": "SCRN",
            "element": "Screening",
            "tedur": "P14D",
            "epoch": "SCREENING",
            "testrl": "INFORMED CONSENT",
            "teenrl": "RANDOMIZATION - 1",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "PBO",
            "element": "Placebo Treatment",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "XANLO",
            "element": "Xanomeline Low Dose",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "FU",
            "element": "Follow-up",
            "tedur": "P28D",
            "epoch": "FOLLOW-UP",
            "testrl": "END OF TREATMENT + 1",
        },
    ],
    arms={"PBO": ["SCRN", "PBO", "FU"], "XAN_LO": ["SCRN", "XANLO", "FU"]},
    arm_names={"PBO": "Placebo", "XAN_LO": "Xanomeline Low Dose"},
)

te = design.to_te()  # one domain at a time
frames = design.domains()  # or every populated domain: {"TE": df, "TA": df, ...}

Referential integrity is validated at construction: arm paths must reference defined elements, visit armcd values must reference defined arms, and element codes must be unique. Each arm needs its protocol name in arm_names (TA.ARM). A key that the model does not read raises, in Python and in trial_design.yaml, and so does a repeated YAML key.

docs.title: Arm paths: steps, branches and epochs
docs.text:
A path entry is an ETCD, or a step that gives the TA values of one position (ADR 0036):

design = fleet.StudyDesign(
    study_id="S1",
    elements=[...],
    arms={
        "AB": ["SCRN", "A", "WO", "B"],
        "BA": [
            "SCRN",
            {"etcd": "B", "epoch": "TREATMENT 1"},  # crossover: epoch by position
            "WO",
            {"etcd": "A", "epoch": "TREATMENT 2"},
        ],
    },
    arm_names={"AB": "Drug A then Drug B", "BA": "Drug B then Drug A"},
    randomized_at="SCRN",  # TABRANCH "Randomized to <arm>" on SCRN
)

TABRANCH defaults to Randomized to <arm> on the last element that every arm shares, or on the randomized_at element. When the branch is not a randomization (a responder extension, a cohort assignment), give the real rule on the step: {"etcd": "CORE", "tabranch": "Responder at end of Core"}. tatrans gives TATRANS the same way. design.audit() warns when two arms have the same path (FLEETTD04) and when an element repeats in an arm with no per-position epoch (FLEETTD05).

docs.title: Interchange formats
docs.text: Method Direction Use case StudyDesign.from_yaml(path) / design.to_yaml(path) YAML ⇄ trial_design.yaml spec, versioned next to define.yaml StudyDesign.from_mermaid(text, study_id=...) / design.to_mermaid() Mermaid ⇄ Review diagram: arm paths, ETCD, ELEMENT, TEDUR, epochs. Not ARM, rules, TABRANCH or a crossover; YAML is the lossless path StudyDesign.from_usdm(json_dict) USDM → Import a CDISC USDM / DDF export (e.g. from OpenStudyBuilder): arms, epochs, elements, study cells, encounters, eligibility criteria TrialParameters.from_ctgov("NCT...") ctgov → Seed TS from the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API

docs.title: Conformance audit — a P21 dry-run, offline
docs.text:
One CLI command (config-context — the design spec resolves from study_config.yaml; exit code 1 on errors, so it drops straight into CI):

uv run fleet tdd audit

The same audit from Python — design.audit(), or the standalone fleet.sdtm.trial_design_audit(te=..., ta=..., tv=..., ts=..., ti=..., dm=..., td=..., tm=...) — checks the domains against published P21/FDA rule IDs and returns a findings DataFrame (rule_id, severity, domain, message):

findings = design.audit(dm=dm)
errors = findings.filter(pl.col("severity") == "error")

Encoded checks include:

Area Rules All A Req variable of the SDTMIG 3.4 structure that is absent, null or blank (FLEETTD08), for TE, TA, TV, TI, TD and TM TE ETCD length (SD1009), TEENRL/TEDUR presence (SD0089), duplicates (SD1271) TA TAETORD unique per arm (SD1052), ARM↔ARMCD one-to-one (SD1033/SD1034), reserved ARMCDs (SD1053), ARMCD length (SD1004) TA↔TE ETCD not in TE, and ELEMENT consistency when both have ELEMENT, UNPLAN-aware (SD0067); unused elements (SD1378) TV VISITNUM unique per ARMCD, no VISITNUM with both a blank-ARMCD row and an arm row (FLEETTD06), ARMCD FK vs TA TI IETESTCD format (SD0018), uniqueness within TIVERS (SD1286) DM↔TA Undefined arms, arms without subjects (SD1354), a DM (ARMCD, ARM) pair that TA does not hold (FLEETTD07, warning) TS The FDA Technical Conformance Guide required-parameter profile (SD22xx — a missing SSTDTC is flagged as rejection-level TRC 1734) and conditional rules (e.g. INTMODEL/INTTYPE/PCLAS when STYPE=INTERVENTIONAL — SD1310/11/12) Design design.audit() only: an empty elements or arms section (error) or visits or criteria section (warning) (FLEETTD09)

TS coded values are not checked: a TSVAL outside its codelist (for example SEXPOP ALL, which C66732 does not hold) and a TSPARM that does not match its TSPARMCD give no finding. Check them against the CT package by hand.

The audit is a curated high-signal subset; run fleet validate (CDISC Rules Engine) for exhaustive coverage.

docs.title: Visit schedules
docs.text:
Build TV from day offsets relative to an anchor event. VISITNUM, VISITDY (CDISC no-day-zero convention), and deterministic TVSTRL rule text are derived:

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialVisits

tv_rows = TrialVisits.from_schedule(
    [("Screening", -14), ("Baseline", 0), ("Week 4", 28), ("Week 8", 56)],
    anchor="RANDOMIZATION",
    window=3,  # or (before, after)
)

docs.title: CLI: fleet tdd
docs.text:
Like every Fleet command, fleet tdd runs in the context of the discovered study_config.yaml (git-style parent walk, --config to override): the design spec defaults to <metadata_sdtm>/trial_design.yaml and the output directory to the config's sdtm_data path — so the command works from any subdirectory of any company's folder structure. The YAML mirrors the StudyDesign schema; a top-level trial_design: wrapper key is accepted.

uv run fleet tdd audit                       # conformance pre-check
uv run fleet tdd build --format xpt          # audit + write to <sdtm_data>/
uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705           # print TS parameters from ClinicalTrials.gov
uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705 --write   # ...or merge them into trial_design.yaml
uv run fleet tdd build --design specs/td.yaml --out /tmp/out   # explicit overrides

build writes every populated domain (parquet, xpt, or dataset-json) and refuses to write when the audit reports errors (--force overrides).

docs.title: Protocol-Reference Domains
docs.text:
Protocol-reference domains (TE, TA, TV, TS, TI, TD, TM) follow a fixed sequence:

fetch_structure() → study_header() → add_*() → to_frame()

Each step validates that the previous step was completed. Calling verbs out of order raises a ValueError with a descriptive message.

import polars as pl
from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialElement, TrialElements, Epoch

te_rows = TrialElements(
    elements=[
        TrialElement(
            etcd="SCRN",
            element="Screening",
            testrl="INFORMED CONSENT",
            teenrl="RANDOMIZATION - 1",
            tedur="P14D",
            epoch=Epoch.SCREENING,
        ),
        TrialElement(
            etcd="TRT",
            element="Treatment",
            testrl="RANDOMIZATION",
            teenrl="END OF TREATMENT",
            tedur="P84D",
            epoch=Epoch.TREATMENT,
        ),
    ]
)

te = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TE", ig_version="3-4")
    .study_header(study_id="CDISCPILOT01", domain="TE")
    .add_elements(te_rows)
    .to_frame()
)

fetch_structure() resolves the domain structure in priority order: define_path= → save_to= cache → packaged SDTMIG 3.4 metadata → online CDISC Library. Discrepancies between the IG and Fleet's models are reported as UserWarning (schema reconciliation).

docs.title: Subject-Level Domains
docs.text:
Subject-level domains (SV, SE) use derivation verbs that freely mix with existing SDTM verbs:

sv = (
    raw_visits.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="SV")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("SVSTDTC", source="visit_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)  # RFSTDTC comes from DM
    .visit_map(
        "VISITNUM",
        "VISIT",
        date_col="SVSTDTC",
        planned_visits=tv_rows,
        ref_date="RFSTDTC",
        tolerance={"before": 3, "after": 3},
    )
    .study_day("SVSTDY", date_col="SVSTDTC")
    .to_frame()
)

visit_map() is a nearest-day window. Use it only when the CRF does not collect the visit, and never to replace a collected VISITNUM. Its rules:

  • The distance is the difference of study-day numbers, as abs(SVSTDY - VISITDY): across the missing Day 0, Day -1 is 2 days from VISITDY 1. TrialVisits.from_schedule() writes its TVSTRL window in the same study days.
  • When TV has ARMCD values, a subject takes only the visits of its arm and the visits with a blank ARMCD.
  • A dated record outside every window is an unscheduled visit: it gets the VISITNUM of the last planned visit before it plus .1, .2, ... and the VISIT UNSCHEDULED 5.1. This numbering is a sponsor convention: check it against the SDRG (ADR 0035).
  • A record with no study day keeps a null VISITNUM. One warning gives the counts, and a second warning gives the USUBJID + VISITNUM keys that repeat in SV.

For SE, derive boundaries with element_boundaries() and the sequence number with the standard seq() verb. The input has one row per subject and element: STUDYID (for seq), ETCD, EPOCH and the milestone dates:

import polars as pl

import fleet

disposition_df = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬────────────┬──────┬───────────┬────────────────┬─────────────────┐
│ STUDYID ┆ subject_id ┆ ETCD ┆ EPOCH     ┆ screening_date ┆ first_dose_date │
│ ---     ┆ ---        ┆ ---  ┆ ---       ┆ ---            ┆ ---             │
│ str     ┆ str        ┆ str  ┆ str       ┆ str            ┆ str             │
╞═════════╪════════════╪══════╪═══════════╪════════════════╪═════════════════╡
│ STUDY01 ┆ 01-001     ┆ SCRN ┆ SCREENING ┆ 2024-01-01     ┆ 2024-01-15      │
│ STUDY01 ┆ 01-001     ┆ TRT  ┆ TREATMENT ┆ 2024-01-01     ┆ 2024-01-15      │
└─────────┴────────────┴──────┴───────────┴────────────────┴─────────────────┘
""")

se = (
    disposition_df.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="SE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .element_boundaries(
        "SESTDTC", "SEENDTC", milestones={"SCRN": "screening_date", "TRT": "first_dose_date"}
    )
    .seq("SESEQ", order_by=["SESTDTC"])
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: EPOCH stamped from SE
docs.text:
epoch_assign(se=...) derives EPOCH for any domain from the subject's own element intervals — the cross-domain consistency that P21 checks against SE. (The study-level epoch_ranges= form remains available.) The SE frame must hold EPOCH:

ae_raw = pl.from_repr("""
┌────────────┬───────────────┐
│ subject_id ┆ ae_start_date │
│ ---        ┆ ---           │
│ str        ┆ str           │
╞════════════╪═══════════════╡
│ 01-001     ┆ 2024-01-05    │
│ 01-001     ┆ 2024-02-01    │
└────────────┴───────────────┘
""")

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .epoch_assign("EPOCH", date_col="AESTDTC", se=se)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Collection Models
docs.text:
Every add_*() verb requires a collection model (not a bare list). Collections enforce integrity at construction time:

Collection Checks TrialElements Unique ETCD TrialArms Unique TAETORD per arm, FK to TE (opt.) TrialVisits Unique VISITNUM per arm, FK to TA (opt.) TrialParameters Unique (TSPARMCD, TSSEQ) TrialCriteria Unique IETESTCD per TIVERS TrialDiseaseAssessments Unique TDORDER TrialMilestones Unique MIDSTYPE

docs.title: Cross-domain FK validation
docs.text:
ta = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TA")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TA")
    .add_arms(ta_rows, te=te_rows)  # TA.ETCD ∈ TE.ETCD
    .to_frame()
)

tv = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TV")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TV")
    .add_visits(tv_rows, ta=ta_rows)  # TV.ARMCD ∈ TA.ARMCD
    .to_frame()
)

Omit te= / ta= to skip the FK check during iterative development.

docs.title: TS: TSSEQ and dictionary-bound values
docs.text:
TrialParameter covers the full SDTMIG 3.4 variable set: TSSEQ for repeating parameters (one row per country for FCNTRY, per primary outcome for OUTMSPRI, ...) plus TSGRPID, TSVCDREF, TSVCDVER for dictionary-bound values (SNOMED, UNII, MED-RT):

TrialParameter(
    tsparmcd="INDIC",
    tsparm="Trial Disease/Condition Indication",
    tsval="Alzheimer's disease",
    tsvalcd="26929004",
    tsvcdref="SNOMED CT",
    tsvcdver="2014-03-01",
)

A TSVAL over 200 characters is split at a word boundary into TSVAL, TSVAL1, ..., TSVALn (SDTMIG 3.4 TS assumption 8). TSPARM holds 40 characters at most.

TrialParameters.from_ctgov("NCT00048217") seeds the registry-derivable parameters (REGID, TITLE, TPHASE, STYPE, INTMODEL, RANDOM, TBLIND, NARMS, PLANSUB (estimated enrollment) or ACTSUB (actual enrollment), AGEMIN/AGEMAX, SEXPOP, HLTSUBJI, SSTDTC/SENDTC, SPONSOR, OUTMSPRI, FCNTRY) from the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API. It is a starting point — dictionary-bound parameters are deliberately not guessed.

The same flow from the CLI — print the parameters: YAML block, or merge it directly into the study's trial_design.yaml (new TSPARMCD/TSSEQ rows only, existing entries untouched), then rebuild:

uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705           # print the parameters: YAML
uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705 --write   # merge into trial_design.yaml
uv run fleet tdd build                       # → ts.parquet in <sdtm_data>/

docs.title: Epoch values
docs.text:
The Epoch enum is bound to NCI C99079 with the 13 terms of the default CT package. C99079 is extensible: sponsor-defined terms are accepted as plain upper-case strings anywhere an epoch is expected:

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import Epoch, TrialElement

TrialElement(etcd="TRT", element="Treatment", epoch=Epoch.TREATMENT)
TrialElement(etcd="ESC", element="Escalation", epoch="DOSE ESCALATION")  # sponsor term

Note: TrialElement.epoch is a design-time attribute — it drives the element→epoch mapping when deriving TA, but is not written to the TE dataset (SDTMIG 3.4 has no EPOCH variable in TE). SE is not derived from it: epoch_assign(se=) needs an EPOCH column in SE.

docs.title: Mermaid parser
docs.text:
Parse a Mermaid flowchart directly into a design (or use the lower-level parse_trial_design() for raw TE/TA collections):

design = fleet.StudyDesign.from_mermaid(
    """
    flowchart TD
    subgraph SCR[SCREENING]
        SCRN["Screening<br/>P14D"]
    end
    subgraph TRT[TREATMENT]
        DRUG["Drug Treatment<br/>P84D"]
        PBO["Placebo<br/>P84D"]
    end
    SCRN -->|DRUG_ARM| DRUG
    SCRN -->|PBO_ARM| PBO
""",
    study_id="CDISCPILOT01",
)

print(design.to_mermaid())  # a review view; YAML is the lossless round trip

The parser reads the drawn structure or raises. Every line must be a header, a subgraph, an end, a node, an edge or a %% comment. A fork must label each edge with its ARMCD. A cycle (a crossover or an element that repeats in an arm), a node with no edge, a node outside a subgraph, more than one start node and an empty diagram raise a ValueError. A subgraph title that is not a C99079 term is kept as a sponsor epoch, with a warning.

docs.title: Validation with CORE (CDISC Rules Engine)
docs.text: Fleet's conformance validation is built on CORE — the open-source CDISC Rules Engine, the official executable implementation of CDISC's conformance rules. Fleet manages the engine lifecycle (download, discovery, health check) and wraps execution behind one CLI command and one namespace verb, so validation runs with the same rules that CDISC publishes for the engine.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
uv run fleet install-engine     # downloads the CORE binary to ~/.fleet
uv run fleet doctor             # confirms engine + extras are healthy

fleet install-engine installs CORE 0.15.0 (GitHub tag v0.15), the version that Fleet is tested with. --version latest installs the newest CORE release, but Fleet prints a warning, because that version is not tested with Fleet. Newer releases can fail on data that 0.15.0 validates.

fleet doctor prints the engine that validation will use, where it came from, and its version. It takes them from the same run setup as the verb and fleet validate.

Teams can pin a shared engine instead via validation.engine_path in study_config.yaml. Inside a study, validation.engine_path beats the FLEET_RULES_ENGINE environment variable, so that every programmer runs the same engine build. Outside a study, FLEET_RULES_ENGINE still applies.

When validation.engine_path names a file that does not exist, validation could not run, and the message names the pinned path. Fleet does not fall back to FLEET_RULES_ENGINE or the managed install, because that engine can run another rule build. fleet check and fleet doctor show a warning with the pinned path.

validation.engine_path names a program, so treat a received study config like code. fleet validate, the .validate() verb and fleet doctor start the pinned engine. fleet check only prints its path. The MCP tool fleet_validate refuses an engine that a study config names unless the server was started with fleet mcp --trust-study-engine: an assistant can pass any dataset path.

docs.title: Engine version
docs.text:
Every report header prints the engine version, so a QC programmer can check that two runs used the same rule build. Fleet takes the version from the first source that gives it:

  1. the engine's own core version command (0.15.0),
  2. the fleet-release-tag.txt file that fleet install-engine writes next to the managed binary (tag v0.15, printed as 0.15),
  3. else unknown.

docs.title: Running validation
docs.text:
Everything resolves from the discovered study_config.yaml:

uv run fleet validate                          # all datasets in <sdtm_data> and <adam_data>
uv run fleet validate data/sdtm/ae.parquet     # one dataset
uv run fleet validate --report findings.html   # HTML findings report
  • Sweep: the engine runs once for all SDTM datasets and once for all ADaM datasets, so rules that span several datasets of one standard can execute. The report shows one result per dataset.
  • Standard detection: a dataset in the configured sdtm_data or adam_data directory takes the standard of that directory. For any other path, AD* datasets validate as ADaM and everything else as SDTM. --standard overrides both.
  • IG versions come from the config's sdtm.ig_version / adam.ig_version (--version overrides).
  • Custom rules load automatically from validation.custom_rules (--custom-rules overrides). They run in a second engine run next to the official rules, so a sweep of both standards with custom rules makes four engine runs. See Custom Validation Rules.
  • Define-XML: --define outputs/define_sdtm.xml gives the define to CORE (-dxp), so the define rules (for example CG0010 on the ItemRef Role) run. It is opt-in: Fleet never passes a define by default (ADR 0042).
  • The report header of each dataset shows every input with its source, as on the verb.
  • HTML report: --report findings.html writes one page: a status row per dataset, then one row per finding and per dataset that could not run. ValidationResult.save_html_report() writes the same page for one dataset. Every cell is HTML-escaped.
  • Could not run: a dataset whose directory and file name disagree (data/sdtm/adsl.parquet), an unsupported IG version, or no rules engine (none installed, or a pinned engine path that does not exist), is not validated. The reason is printed, and the other datasets still run. An engine that crashes, writes no report, or does not finish within the timeout also gives "could not run", not a data failure.
  • Timeout: --timeout SECONDS, else validation.timeout in the study config, else 300 s. On timeout Fleet stops the engine and its workers.
  • Every finding blocks (ADR-0017). CORE gives no severity, so Fleet does not invent one. A finding stops blocking only when validation.accepted lists its rule and dataset with a reason, as an SDRG explanation does:
validation:
  accepted:
    - rule: CORE-000767
      dataset: AE
      reason: No FA domain in this study; see SDRG section 4.2.
  • Status words: PASS (at least one rule executed, no finding), FINDINGS (n) (every finding accepted), NOT ASSESSED (no rule executed), FAIL (a finding blocks), COULD NOT RUN. Study-level findings (dataset STUDY) get their own block in a sweep. In a single-dataset run (the verb, the MCP tool) they are information only, because one dataset cannot show what the study lacks.
  • Exit codes: 0 nothing blocks, 1 a finding blocks, 2 a dataset could not run. So fleet validate drops straight into CI. The last line counts each status and the findings.
  • Rule counts: each report states, per engine run (official, custom), how many rules executed, were skipped and could not run, for example Rules (engine run, official): 90 executed, 313 skipped, 27 could not run. The counts belong to the engine run, not to one dataset. A rule that could not run (status EXECUTION_ERROR, often because a dataset it needs is absent) is a rule problem, not a data finding: its rows are left out of the findings, and it does not change the status or the exit code. The rows are chosen by the rule status in Rules_Report, never by the message text. fleet validate and the HTML report also list the IDs of these rules; the verb prints the count line only.
  • Engine version: fleet install-engine installs the newest tested CORE release. The report header and fleet doctor name a version Fleet is not tested with. A weekly CI job runs Fleet on the newest CORE release.

docs.title: The CI gate: fleet check
docs.text:
fleet check builds the same run setup for SDTM and ADaM, with no datasets. It catches a setup error before delivery, without an engine: it starts no program and runs no study code (codelists.py is read as data):

  • sdtm.ig_version: 3-5, or any IG version not in the supported list, fails the gate.
  • A validation.custom_rules directory that does not exist fails the gate.
  • A codelists.py that disagrees with ct.package, ct.adam_package or the define.yaml files fails the gate; each row names the fix command. See controlled terminology in the spec path.
  • No engine found is a warning only, because CI installs no engine.

docs.title: The MCP tool
docs.text:
fleet_validate(dataset_path, standard=None, version=None, custom_rules=None) builds the same run setup. It looks for study_config.yaml from the directory of the dataset, not from the working directory of the server. A refused setup returns {"outcome": "could not run", "reason": ...} and does not raise. See IDE tooling.

The same run from Python, chainable at the end of a pipeline:

result = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    # ... derivations ...
    .validate("AE")  # runs CORE on the materialised frame
)

docs.title: Where the verb takes its inputs
docs.text:
The verb builds a run setup before the engine starts. Each input comes from the first source that gives it:

Input Argument Study config Environment Default Standard (none) (none) (none) the namespace: .sdtm or .adam IG version version= sdtm.ig_version / adam.ig_version (none) SDTMIG 3.4, ADaMIG 1.3 Custom rules custom_rules= validation.custom_rules (none) none Engine rules_engine_path= validation.engine_path FLEET_RULES_ENGINE managed install

The verb looks for study_config.yaml from the working directory, then each parent. version= accepts "3-4" and "3.4". The supported versions are SDTMIG 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 and ADaMIG 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3.

The report header prints each input with its source and the study config used:

Standard:     SDTMIG (namespace)
IG version:   3.3 (study config)
Custom rules: /study/metadata/custom_rules (study config)
Engine:       /study/tools/core/core (study config)
CORE version: 0.15.0
Study config: /study/study_config.yaml

docs.title: Could not run
docs.text:
Some setups are refused before the engine starts. The verb then raises ValidationSetupError in every on_fail mode, because no rule ran:

  • the dataset name belongs to the other standard: adae.adam.validate("AE") or ae.sdtm.validate("ADAE"),
  • the IG version is not supported, for example SDTMIG 3.1.3,
  • the custom rules directory does not exist.

docs.title: What a PASS does not cover: labels
docs.text: Fleet gives CORE each dataset as a Dataset-JSON file that it writes from the data frame alone. So the variable labels and the dataset label that CORE checks come from Fleet, not from the file: each variable label is the variable name. A label rule (for example CORE-000594, a label that is not in title case) does not fire through fleet validate, even when the XPT file holds a wrong label. fleet validate prints this note in each engine run. Check the labels of a submission file against the define with DatasetChecker, or in the Define-XML.

docs.title: What a PASS does not cover: controlled terminology
docs.text:
CORE checks only a few controlled terminology values. A PASS or a FAIL for other rules does not mean that the codelist values are correct. Fleet checks a value against its codelist at the line that assigns it (assign(..., ct=SEX)), and warns.

Example: a DM with SEX = "X", AGEU = "DECADES", RACE = "MARTIAN" and ETHNIC = "UNKNOWN ETHNIC", and an AE with AESER = "YES", AESEV = "HORRIBLE", AEOUT = "BETTER" and AESTDTC = "2020-13-45". fleet validate (CORE 0.15.0) reports only CORE-000087 and CORE-000266 (AESER) and CORE-000726 (ETHNIC) for these values. It names no finding for SEX, AGEU, RACE, AESEV, AEOUT or the bad ISO 8601 date.

docs.title: Which rules actually exist upstream
docs.text:
CORE executes the rule sets CDISC has published to its Library. As of mid-2026 that means:

Standard Published executable rules SDTMIG 3.2 / 3.3 / 3.4 ✅ full SD-series rule sets SENDIG 3.0 / 3.1 / 3.1.1 (+DART, GENETOX, AR) ✅ FDA Business Rules ✅ (SDTM/SEND-oriented) TIG 1.0 (incl. its ADaM substandard) ✅ USDM ✅ ADaMIG 1.0–1.3 ⚠️ selection plumbing exists (engine ≥ v0.13.0), but no executable ADaMIG rule set is published yet — ADaM Conformance Rules v5.0 remains a document, not machine rules

Practical consequence: an ADaM fleet validate run today executes your custom rules (plus any TIG-ADaM rules you opt into), while SDTM runs get the full official battery. Fleet tracks the upstream catalog — when CDISC publishes executable ADaMIG rules, the same command picks them up through the engine's standard/version selection with no Fleet change.

docs.title: Where CORE sits in Fleet's validation stack
docs.text:
Validation is layered — each layer fires at a different moment and catches a different error class:

Layer When What it catches Spec registry models from_spec() load time unknown algorithms, misspelled/missing derivation fields fleet check on demand / CI gate Define-XML generation in strict mode (schema, codelists, method text, Length, SignificantDigits), run setup (IG versions, custom rules directory) Trial-design audit (fleet tdd audit) on demand, offline P21-style SD-series + FDA TS profile for TDD domains CORE (fleet validate) after datasets materialise official CDISC conformance rules against the data itself

See Custom Validation Rules for extending CORE with sponsor-, study-, or TCG-specific checks — they run next to the official rules, report in the same format with their source, and live in version control next to the study.
