docs.title: Code-Driven Pipeline (Inline)¶
docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch this notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This notebook demonstrates building clinical datasets entirely in Python code. It is best suited for quick ad-hoc analysis, smaller studies, or initial data discovery.

docs.title: 1. Derive SDTM¶
docs.text: We use the .sdtm namespace to standardize the raw inputs.

docs.title: 2. Derive ADaM¶
docs.text: We use the .adam namespace. Notice how easily we define a custom derivation to flag subjects who are older than 40.

docs.title: ADTTE: Time-to-Event in One Chain
docs.text: A time-to-event parameter answers one question per subject: how long until X happened, and if it never did, how long did we watch? This walkthrough builds a two-parameter ADTTE (overall survival + time to first adverse event) in a single chain, shows why every subject got their row, and hands the result straight to a Kaplan-Meier fit. It then adds a PFS parameter that stops the observation at new anticancer therapy. Every output below is real.

docs.title: The model in 30 seconds
docs.text:
• An event or censor source is a plain Polars frame with USUBJID and ADT. Build it with filter and select.
  • .param() plays referee per parameter: the earliest event wins (CNSR = 0, EVNTDESC = its key in events=); no event gives the last censor record (CNSR = its key in censors=). STARTDT comes from ADSL; a date before it is set to it.
  • stop_at= maps ADSL date columns to (CNSR, EVNTDESC). The earliest one ends the observation: event and censor records after it are dropped (admiral 1.5 end_dates, ADR-0043). A censored subject takes the date from the censor frame and the reason from the stop.
  • .aval() turns ADT − STARTDT + 1 into AVAL (+AVALU) afterwards.

Choosing the time origin (start=)

TRTSDT (ADaMIG: Date of First Exposure to Treatment) is the conventional origin for safety endpoints like time to first AE. For ITT efficacy endpoints in randomized trials, overall survival in particular, use the randomization date (RANDDT): ITT time starts at randomization, not at first dose. start= accepts any ADSL date column, so pick per parameter.

docs.title: 1. Input data
docs.text:
from datetime import date

import polars as pl
import fleet

adsl = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "STUDYID": ["S1", "S1", "S1"],
        "USUBJID": ["01", "02", "03"],
        "TRT01P": ["Drug A", "Placebo", "Drug A"],
        "TRTSDT": [date(2023, 1, 1), date(2023, 1, 2), date(2023, 1, 3)],
        "DTHFL": ["Y", None, None],
        "DTHDT": [date(2023, 3, 1), None, None],
        "LSTALVDT": [date(2023, 3, 1), date(2023, 6, 30), None],
        "EOSDT": [date(2023, 3, 1), date(2023, 6, 30), date(2023, 2, 1)],
    }
)
adae = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "USUBJID": ["01", "01", "02"],
        "TRTEMFL": ["Y", "Y", "Y"],
        "ASTDT": [date(2023, 1, 20), date(2023, 1, 10), date(2023, 2, 5)],
        "AESEQ": [2, 1, 1],
    }
)

Note the traps this tiny study contains: subject 01 has an earlier and a later AE (tie-break needed), subject 03 has no death, no last-alive date, and no AE (the classic silently-dropped subject), and dates must be typed Date: a DTC string column is rejected with instructions to .date() it first.

docs.title: 2. Sources: plain frames
docs.text:
Each source is one select. The date goes to ADT. A source may also carry SRCDOM, SRCVAR, SRCSEQ, CNSDTDSC and (censors only) EVNTDESC; they go onto the selected row. SRCSEQ also breaks a tie on one date. A censor frame without EVNTDESC gives a null EVNTDESC and a warning: the reason of the censoring is study text.

Without a PARAM label, .param() reads it from the study CT: the decode of PARAMCD in the codelist of ADTTE.PARAMCD in the ADaM define.yaml. If there is no such decode, it raises and asks for param=.

death = adsl.filter(pl.col("DTHFL") == "Y").select(
    "USUBJID", ADT="DTHDT", SRCDOM=pl.lit("ADSL"), SRCVAR=pl.lit("DTHDT")
)
alive = adsl.select(
    "USUBJID",
    ADT="LSTALVDT",
    EVNTDESC=pl.lit("ALIVE"),
    SRCDOM=pl.lit("ADSL"),
    SRCVAR=pl.lit("LSTALVDT"),
)
first_ae = adae.filter(pl.col("TRTEMFL") == "Y").select(
    "USUBJID", ADT="ASTDT", SRCDOM=pl.lit("ADAE"), SRCVAR=pl.lit("ASTDT"), SRCSEQ="AESEQ"
)
eos = adsl.select(
    "USUBJID",
    ADT="EOSDT",
    EVNTDESC=pl.lit("END OF STUDY"),
    SRCDOM=pl.lit("ADSL"),
    SRCVAR=pl.lit("EOSDT"),
)

docs.title: 3. Derive both parameters in one chain
docs.text:
adtte_ns = (
    adsl.adam.tte.param(
        "OS",
        "Overall Survival",
        start="TRTSDT",
        events={"DEATH": death},
        censors={1: alive},
        retain="censor_at_start",
    )  # keep subject 03, censored at STARTDT
    .param(
        "TTAE",
        "Time to First Adverse Event",
        start="TRTSDT",
        events={"ADVERSE EVENT": first_ae},
        censors={1: eos},
        explain=True,
    )  # ← prints the decision trace below
    .join_adsl("TRT01P")  # after the last param(): earlier rows would get null
    .aval(unit="days")  # AVAL = ADT − STARTDT + 1, AVALU stamped
    .seq("ASEQ", order_by=["PARAMCD"])
)
adtte = adtte_ns.to_frame()

┌─────────┬─────────┬────────────┬────────────┬──────┬────────┬──────────┬───────────────────┬─────────┬─────────────────────────────┬────────┬─────────┬───────┬───────┬──────┐
│ STUDYID ┆ USUBJID ┆ STARTDT    ┆ ADT        ┆ CNSR ┆ SRCDOM ┆ SRCVAR   ┆ EVNTDESC          ┆ PARAMCD ┆ PARAM                       ┆ SRCSEQ ┆ TRT01P  ┆ AVAL  ┆ AVALU ┆ ASEQ │
╞═════════╪═════════╪════════════╪════════════╪══════╪════════╪══════════╪═══════════════════╪═════════╪═════════════════════════════╪════════╪═════════╪═══════╪═══════╪══════╡
│ S1      ┆ 01      ┆ 2023-01-01 ┆ 2023-03-01 ┆ 0    ┆ ADSL   ┆ DTHDT    ┆ DEATH             ┆ OS      ┆ Overall Survival            ┆ null   ┆ Drug A  ┆ 60.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 1    │
│ S1      ┆ 02      ┆ 2023-01-02 ┆ 2023-06-30 ┆ 1    ┆ ADSL   ┆ LSTALVDT ┆ ALIVE             ┆ OS      ┆ Overall Survival            ┆ null   ┆ Placebo ┆ 180.0 ┆ DAYS  ┆ 1    │
│ S1      ┆ 03      ┆ 2023-01-03 ┆ 2023-01-03 ┆ 1    ┆ ADSL   ┆ TRTSDT   ┆ NO EVENT OBSERVED ┆ OS      ┆ Overall Survival            ┆ null   ┆ Drug A  ┆ 1.0   ┆ DAYS  ┆ 1    │
│ S1      ┆ 01      ┆ 2023-01-01 ┆ 2023-01-10 ┆ 0    ┆ ADAE   ┆ ASTDT    ┆ ADVERSE EVENT     ┆ TTAE    ┆ Time to First Adverse Event ┆ 1      ┆ Drug A  ┆ 10.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 2    │
│ S1      ┆ 02      ┆ 2023-01-02 ┆ 2023-02-05 ┆ 0    ┆ ADAE   ┆ ASTDT    ┆ ADVERSE EVENT     ┆ TTAE    ┆ Time to First Adverse Event ┆ 1      ┆ Placebo ┆ 35.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 2    │
│ S1      ┆ 03      ┆ 2023-01-03 ┆ 2023-02-01 ┆ 1    ┆ ADSL   ┆ EOSDT    ┆ END OF STUDY      ┆ TTAE    ┆ Time to First Adverse Event ┆ null   ┆ Drug A  ┆ 30.0  ┆ DAYS  ┆ 2    │
└─────────┴─────────┴────────────┴────────────┴──────┴────────┴──────────┴───────────────────┴─────────┴─────────────────────────────┴────────┴─────────┴───────┴───────┴──────┘

Worth noticing:

  • The first .param() uses the base frame as ADSL and pins it, so the next .param(), .join_adsl() and .km_data() read it too.
  • STUDYID comes from ADSL on every row. Other ADSL variables, such as TRT01P, come from .join_adsl() after the last .param().
  • Subject 01's TTAE picked the earlier AE; SRCSEQ breaks same-date ties deterministically.
  • Subject 03 survived the OS derivation thanks to retain="censor_at_start". Without it Fleet warns with the count and the USUBJIDs instead of silently dropping, admiral-style.
  • AVALU is stamped by .aval(); unit="months"/"years" use the CDISC conversions (30.4375 / 365.25).

docs.title: 4. Why did subject 03 get censored? The decision trace
docs.text:
explain=True logs every candidate per subject with the selected one, the reason and cnsr_from, the rule that gave the CNSR:

TTE decision trace — TTAE (Time to First Adverse Event):
┌─────────┬────────┬───────────────┬────────────┬──────────┬────────────────────────┬─────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ kind   ┆ source        ┆ date       ┆ selected ┆ reason                 ┆ cnsr_from   │
╞═════════╪════════╪═══════════════╪════════════╪══════════╪════════════════════════╪═════════════╡
│ 01      ┆ event  ┆ ADVERSE EVENT ┆ 2023-01-10 ┆ true     ┆ earliest event         ┆ event       │
│ 02      ┆ event  ┆ ADVERSE EVENT ┆ 2023-02-05 ┆ true     ┆ earliest event         ┆ event       │
│ 01      ┆ censor ┆ CNSR 1        ┆ 2023-03-01 ┆ false    ┆ not selected           ┆ null        │
│ 02      ┆ censor ┆ CNSR 1        ┆ 2023-06-30 ┆ false    ┆ not selected           ┆ null        │
│ 03      ┆ censor ┆ CNSR 1        ┆ 2023-02-01 ┆ true     ┆ last censor (no event) ┆ censors key │
└─────────┴────────┴───────────────┴────────────┴──────────┴────────────────────────┴─────────────┘

A frame without ADT fails before a single row is computed, and the error shows the fix: adae.select("USUBJID", ADT="ASTDT").

docs.title: 5. Straight into a survival fit
docs.text:
km_data() returns exactly what lifelines / scikit-survival consume, and group columns you ask for resolve from ADSL automatically:

km = adtte_ns.km_data("OS", by=["TRT01P"])

┌─────────┬──────────┬───────┬─────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ duration ┆ event ┆ TRT01P  │
╞═════════╪══════════╪═══════╪═════════╡
│ 01      ┆ 60.0     ┆ true  ┆ Drug A  │
│ 02      ┆ 180.0    ┆ false ┆ Placebo │
│ 03      ┆ 1.0      ┆ false ┆ Drug A  │
└─────────┴──────────┴───────┴─────────┘

from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter  # optional — not a Fleet dependency

kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
for (arm,), grp in km.group_by("TRT01P"):
    kmf.fit(grp["duration"], grp["event"], label=arm)

docs.title: 6. PFS: stop the observation at new therapy or data cut-off
docs.text:
stop_at= follows admiral 1.5 derive_param_tte with end_dates and event_type = "negative" (ADR-0043). It maps an ADSL date column to a (CNSR, EVNTDESC) pair. The earliest non-null stop_at date of a subject ends the observation. Events and censor records after it are dropped, so a subject without progression is censored at the last assessment before the stop, not at the stop date.

A censored row holds two facts (FDA 2018 oncology endpoints guidance, EMA PFS appendix, ADaM BDS-TTE):

  • The date: the last adequate assessment. It comes from the censor frame, with CNSDTDSC.
  • The reason: why the observation stopped. It comes from the stop: CNSR and EVNTDESC.
adsl_pfs = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬────────────┬────────────┬────────────┬────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ TRTSDT     ┆ EOSDT      ┆ NACTDT     ┆ DCUTDT     │
│ ---     ┆ ---        ┆ ---        ┆ ---        ┆ ---        │
│ str     ┆ date       ┆ date       ┆ date       ┆ date       │
╞═════════╪════════════╪════════════╪════════════╪════════════╡
│ A       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 2024-06-30 ┆ 2024-04-01 ┆ 2024-05-31 │
│ B       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 2024-06-30 ┆ 2024-02-15 ┆ 2024-05-31 │
│ C       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ null       ┆ null       ┆ 2024-05-31 │
│ D       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ null       ┆ null       ┆ 2024-05-31 │
└─────────┴────────────┴────────────┴────────────┴────────────┘
""")
adrs = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬────────────┬───────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ ADT        ┆ AVALC │
│ ---     ┆ ---        ┆ ---   │
│ str     ┆ date       ┆ str   │
╞═════════╪════════════╪═══════╡
│ A       ┆ 2024-02-01 ┆ SD    │
│ A       ┆ 2024-03-01 ┆ SD    │
│ B       ┆ 2024-02-01 ┆ SD    │
│ B       ┆ 2024-03-10 ┆ PD    │
│ C       ┆ 2024-02-01 ┆ SD    │
│ C       ┆ 2024-04-15 ┆ SD    │
│ C       ┆ 2024-06-10 ┆ PD    │
└─────────┴────────────┴───────┘
""")
last_assessment = adrs.select(
    "USUBJID",
    "ADT",
    EVNTDESC=pl.lit("NO PROGRESSION"),
    CNSDTDSC=pl.lit("LAST ADEQUATE TUMOR ASSESSMENT"),
)
no_baseline = adsl_pfs.join(adrs, on="USUBJID", how="anti").select(
    "USUBJID", ADT="TRTSDT", EVNTDESC=pl.lit("NO BASELINE ASSESSMENT")
)

pfs = (
    adsl_pfs.adam.tte.param(
        "PFS",
        "Progression-Free Survival",
        start="TRTSDT",
        events={"PROGRESSIVE DISEASE": adrs.filter(pl.col("AVALC") == "PD")},
        censors={1: last_assessment, 3: no_baseline},  # key = CNSR
        stop_at={  # column: (CNSR, EVNTDESC)
            "EOSDT": (4, "END OF STUDY"),
            "NACTDT": (2, "NEW ANTICANCER THERAPY"),
            "DCUTDT": (5, "DATA CUT-OFF"),
        },
        keep_reason=[3],
    )
    .aval()
    .to_frame()
)

┌─────────┬────────────┬────────────┬──────┬────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┬───────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ STARTDT    ┆ ADT        ┆ CNSR ┆ EVNTDESC               ┆ CNSDTDSC                       ┆ AVAL  │
╞═════════╪════════════╪════════════╪══════╪════════════════════════╪════════════════════════════════╪═══════╡
│ A       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 2024-03-01 ┆ 2    ┆ NEW ANTICANCER THERAPY ┆ LAST ADEQUATE TUMOR ASSESSMENT ┆ 61.0  │
│ B       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 2024-02-01 ┆ 2    ┆ NEW ANTICANCER THERAPY ┆ LAST ADEQUATE TUMOR ASSESSMENT ┆ 32.0  │
│ C       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 2024-04-15 ┆ 5    ┆ DATA CUT-OFF           ┆ LAST ADEQUATE TUMOR ASSESSMENT ┆ 106.0 │
│ D       ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 3    ┆ NO BASELINE ASSESSMENT ┆ null                           ┆ 1.0   │
└─────────┴────────────┴────────────┴──────┴────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┴───────┘
  • Subject A has no progression: ADT is the last assessment (2024-03-01), not the new-therapy date (2024-04-01). The reason is the new therapy: CNSR 2.
  • Subject B progressed on 2024-03-10, after new therapy on 2024-02-15: the PD does not count. B is censored at the last assessment before it.
  • Subject C progressed on 2024-06-10, after the data cut-off: the PD does not count. C is censored at 2024-04-15 with CNSR 5, DATA CUT-OFF.
  • Subject D has no assessment. keep_reason=[3] keeps CNSR 3 and the text of its frame, although the data cut-off applies to D too (admiral consider_end_dates = FALSE). Without such a frame, D is dropped with a warning.

CNSR and EVNTDESC of a censored subject come from, in this order:

  1. A censor frame whose key is in keep_reason=.
  2. The stop of the subject. On a tie of two stop dates, the first column in stop_at= wins.
  3. The censor frame (CNSR = its key), when the subject has no stop date.

The stop codes must differ from each other and from the censors= keys, so that one CNSR value names one reason. explain=True adds a cnsr_from column to the trace, with the rule per subject.

For a favorable event (time to response, admiral event_type = "positive"), censor at the stop date: add {1: adsl.select("USUBJID", ADT=pl.min_horizontal("EOSDT", "NACTDT"))} to censors=.

docs.title: Going further
docs.text:
• Strata: by=["AEDECOD"] derives one parameter per term, with per-stratum PARAMCD built via an expression in set_values_to (a static PARAMCD across strata is rejected: the 1:1 mapping guard). Every source frame carries the by columns.
  • The full verb reference lives in the cheat sheet and the TA API page.

docs.title: End-to-End Walkthrough: Multi-Domain Pipeline
docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch a notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This guide walks the whole journey, in the order a study actually runs: scaffold the workspace, generate metadata and codelists, derive SDTM and ADaM, prove traceability with .trail(), validate against the CDISC Rules Engine, and generate the Define-XML with an annotated CRF. The code-only core of this flow lives in examples/full_pipeline_example.py.

docs.title: 1. Scaffold the study workspace
docs.text:
One command creates the folder tree, study_config.yaml, the IG-derived define.yaml skeletons, and the typed codelists.py (requires a CDISC Library API key in .env):

uv run fleet new STUDY01 --domains DM,VS,AE --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS
cd STUDY01

or step by step:

uv run fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,VS,AE --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./STUDY01
cd STUDY01
uv run fleet init define   # CDISC Library IG → metadata/*/define.yaml
uv run fleet init ct       # define.yaml codelists → metadata/sdtm/codelists.py
uv run fleet init rules    # conformance rules cache (optional)

Every Fleet command from here on discovers study_config.yaml by walking up from wherever you run it — paths below (data/sdtm, metadata/...) come from that config, not from hard-coding.

docs.title: DM (Demographics)
docs.text:
dm = (
    raw_dm.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign("ARM", source="arm")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex", ct=SEX, ct_map={"Male": "M", "Female": "F"})
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="dob")
    .date("RFSTDTC", source="first_dose")
    .to_frame()
)

A --DTC column is text (pl.String) in ISO 8601. .date() keeps a partial value partial (2023-01) and never guesses the day (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4). A *DT target (TRTSDT) is a pl.Date.

docs.title: EX (Exposure) and the reference dates
docs.text:
ex = (
    raw_ex.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="EX")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .date("EXSTDTC", source="start")
    .date("EXENDTC", source="end")
    .to_frame()
)

RFXSTDTC and RFXENDTC are the first and last exposure dates in EX. The subject-level verbs first_date and last_date take them from EX. On a *DTC target they keep the text of the earliest (or latest) record. A partial value is left out with a warning, so S002 gets no RFXSTDTC:

dm = (
    dm.adam.adsl.first_date("RFXSTDTC", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXSTDTC")
    .last_date("RFXENDTC", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXENDTC")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: VS (Vital Signs) — with a cross-domain pin
docs.text:
study_day() needs DM's RFSTDTC; instead of merging DM in, pin it — the reference stays beside the frame and the output stays clean:

vs = (
    raw_vs.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="VS")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign(
        "VSTESTCD",
        source="test_name",
        ct=VSTESTCD,
        ct_map={"Weight": "WEIGHT", "Heart Rate": "HR"},
    )
    .assign("VSSTRESN", source="result")
    .assign("VSSTNRLO", source="low")
    .assign("VSSTNRHI", source="high")
    .date("VSDTC", source="date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("VSDY", date_col="VSDTC")  # resolves DM.RFSTDTC via the pin
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: AE (Adverse Events)
docs.text:
ae = (
    raw_ae.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign("AEDECOD", source="ae_term")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: ADSL (Subject-Level Analysis)
docs.text:
TRTSDT is the date of first exposure, so it comes from EX, not from another domain (ADaMIG 1.3, ADSL). The EX start of S002 is partial. With impute="first" (the rule of the SAP) first_date imputes the day and writes TRTSDTF; with no impute= the partial value is left out:

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl.source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "ARM", "SEX")
    .assign("TRT01P", source="ARM")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXSTDTC", impute="first")
    .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXENDTC")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: ADVS (BDS) — pin ADSL, carry columns, derive baseline
docs.text:
BNRIND is the ANRIND of the baseline record. baseline() carries any column, text included:

advs = (
    vs.adam.pin("ADSL", adsl)
    .source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "VSTESTCD")
    .assign("PARAMCD", source="VSTESTCD")
    .assign("AVAL", source="VSSTRESN")
    .assign("ANRLO", source="VSSTNRLO")
    .assign("ANRHI", source="VSSTNRHI")
    .nrind("ANRIND", value="AVAL", low="ANRLO", high="ANRHI")
    .join_adsl("TRT01P", "TRTSDT")  # carry forward on the ADSL pin's key
    # the last pre-dose record per subject and parameter
    .flag(
        "ABLFL",
        criteria="last",
        order_by="VSDTC",
        where='pl.col("VSDY") <= 1',
        by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
    )
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .baseline("BNRIND", aval="ANRIND", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 5. Prove traceability — .trail()
docs.text:
Drop .trail() anywhere in a chain (typically just before .to_frame()) and Fleet prints the origin of every derived variable — including cross-domain pin reads, attributed as DOMAIN.COLUMN:

advs_ns = (
    vs.adam.pin("ADSL", adsl)
    .source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "VSTESTCD")
    .assign("AVAL", source="VSSTRESN")
    .join_adsl("TRTSDT")
    .trail()  # ← prints the table below; the pipeline continues
)

Variable trail (4 derivation(s)):
┌───┬──────────┬────────┬──────────┐
│ # ┆ Variable ┆ Verb   ┆ Origin   │
╞═══╪══════════╪════════╪══════════╡
│ 1 ┆ STUDYID  ┆ source ┆ STUDYID  │
│ 2 ┆ USUBJID  ┆ source ┆ USUBJID  │
│ 3 ┆ VSTESTCD ┆ source ┆ VSTESTCD │
│ 4 ┆ AVAL     ┆ assign ┆ VSSTRESN │
└───┴──────────┴────────┴──────────┘

join_adsl does not record a trail row yet: the pin itself is recorded, and TRTSDT does not show in this table.

This is the machine-checkable answer to "where did this number come from" — the same lineage feeds to_spec_yaml() (pipeline → define.yaml round-trip) and the Define-XML method descriptions.

docs.title: 6. Validate — are we CDISC compliant?
docs.text:
Validation is a verb — chain .validate() right where the dataset is born and the CDISC Rules Engine report prints without breaking the pipeline (fleet install-engine once, first). Revisiting the AE chain from step 3:

ae = (
    raw_ae.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="STUDY01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign("AEDECOD", source="ae_term")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
    .validate("AE")  # ← CORE report prints here; the chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

======================================================================
CDISC Validation Report: AE
======================================================================
Standard:     SDTMIG (namespace)
IG version:   3.4 (default)
...
Dataset Type: sdtmig v3.4
Status: FAIL
Rules (engine run, official): 75 executed, 340 skipped, 15 could not run
Total Issues: 19
  Errors: 17, Warnings (accepted): 0, Info: 2
----------------------------------------------------------------------

ERRORS (9 unique, 17 total):

1. [CORE-000182] (official) Variable name length is greater than 8.
   Variable: variable_name
...
3. [CORE-000355] (official) At least one required variable is missing from dataset
   Variable: AESEQ, AETERM
...

This is a real run (CORE 0.15.0). The toy AE has no AESEQ and no AETERM, and it keeps the raw columns (subject_id is longer than 8 characters), so CORE reports them. The report is a warning: the chain continues.

For a CI pipeline, make compliance a hard gate — on_fail="raise" turns a finding that validation.accepted does not list into a ValidationError instead of a warning:

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl.source("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "ARM", "SEX")
    .assign("TRT01P", source="ARM")
    .date("TRTSDT", source="RFSTDTC")
    .validate("ADSL", on_fail="raise")  # ← a finding not accepted stops the build
    .to_frame()
)

The full ValidationResult stays retrievable via the namespace's last_validation property when you need programmatic access to findings. To sweep every written dataset at once (e.g. a nightly job), the batch equivalent is uv run fleet validate --report outputs/validation.html. (Note: official executable ADaMIG rules are not yet published by CDISC — ADaM datasets run your custom rules; see Validation with CORE.)

docs.title: 7. Define-XML with an annotated CRF
docs.text:
Declare the aCRF once (it edits metadata/sdtm/define.yaml in place — point --href at your real annotated CRF; blankcrf.pdf is the conventional placeholder name in a submission package):

uv run fleet add-acrf --href blankcrf.pdf --standard both

Tag CRF-collected variables with their page numbers in the define.yaml (origin: Collected + crf_pages: "8" — see CRF Page References), then generate:

uv run fleet define-xml --standard sdtm
uv run fleet define-xml --standard adam

Each Derived variable gets a <MethodDef> with its method text: a verifiable link between the submission metadata and the exact code above. Add --strict to refuse a define with a gap (a Derived variable with no method text, or a numeric variable with no length:).

docs.title: 8. Bonus: read the dependency graph
docs.text:
The same define.yaml files describe the dependency graph. Fleet gives it as data that an orchestrator can read. Fleet does not write a Snakefile or an Airflow DAG file: each step of a study run is fleet run --dataset ....

from fleet import build_dag

dag = build_dag("metadata/sdtm/define.yaml", "metadata/adam/define.yaml")
dag.execution_order()  # → ["dm_raw", "DM", ..., "ADSL", ...]
dag.to_airflow()  # → {"ADSL": ["DM", ...], ...}: upstream datasets per dataset
dag.generate("dag.json")  # → the graph as JSON

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: One workspace bootstrap, ~60 lines of pipeline code, and four CLI commands took us from raw EDC extracts to validated SDTM/ADaM datasets with variable-level traceability and a Define-XML — with every path resolved from study_config.yaml, so the same flow runs unchanged in any company folder structure.

docs.title: A study that fleet run builds end to end (MINIPILOT)
docs.text:
examples/minipilot is a small synthetic study. Its define files drive every dataset, from the raw CSV files to ADaM, so one command builds the whole study:

uv run fleet run --config examples/minipilot/study_config.yaml --out out/minipilot

docs.title: Why this study exists
docs.text:
• The CDISCPILOT01 example is script-driven. Its define files read raw columns that only examples/cdiscpilot01_spec_driven.py creates, and the script derives some variables inline. So fleet run cannot build its ADVS, ADAE or ADEX (finding c1-347).
  • MINIPILOT holds no code. Every variable is either derived in a define file or carried from an input that the inputs: block names. What fleet run writes is what the define files say.
  • It is a template. Copy the folder to start a study that fleet run builds, and replace the raw files and the variables.
  • A test keeps it working. tests/unit/test_minipilot_study.py runs it with fleet run and checks every declared variable.

docs.title: What is in the folder
docs.text:
Path Content study_config.yaml Study id, IG versions, where the define files are raw/*.csv 3 subjects: demographics, adverse events, vital signs, exposure sdtm/define.yaml DM, AE, VS and EX, each from one raw file adam/define.yaml ADSL from DM and EX; ADVS, ADAE and ADEX from their SDTM domain and ADSL

The run order comes from the type: dataset inputs: ADSL runs before ADVS, ADAE and ADEX, because they read it.

docs.title: The clinical rules it shows
docs.text: Variable Rule ADSL.SAFFL Y when the subject has an EX record with EXDOSE > 0, or EXDOSE = 0 and EXTRT contains PLACEBO; else N. Subject 003 had no dose: N. ADVS.AVAL VSSTRESN. ADVS.ABLFL The last record, by ADT then VISITNUM, with a non-missing AVAL and ADT on or before TRTSDT, per USUBJID and PARAMCD. Subject 002 has no DAY 1 value, so its baseline is the screening record. ADVS.CHG, PCHG Only on post-baseline records (ADT after TRTSDT); null on the baseline record and before it. ADAE.TRTEMFL Start on or after TRTSDT and on or before TRTEDT. ADEX.EXDURD AENDT - ASTDT + 1.

docs.title: 1. Check the study
docs.text:
fleet check reads the study config and checks each define file against its schema, before any dataset is built:

uv run fleet check --config examples/minipilot/study_config.yaml

docs.title: 2. Build the datasets
docs.text:
Build every dataset, then only some of them:

uv run fleet run --config examples/minipilot/study_config.yaml --out out/minipilot
uv run fleet run --config examples/minipilot/study_config.yaml --out out/minipilot \
    --dataset ADSL --dataset ADVS

out/minipilot then holds one parquet file per dataset: dm.parquet to adex.parquet.

docs.title: 3. QC a dataset with inline verbs
docs.text:
A QC programmer writes ADVS a second time, with the inline verbs, from the SDTM VS and the ADSL that fleet run wrote. Each verb is one rule of the define file:

import polars as pl

import fleet

vs = fleet.frame(pl.read_parquet("out/minipilot/vs.parquet"))
adsl = pl.read_parquet("out/minipilot/adsl.parquet").select("USUBJID", "TRT01A", "TRTSDT", "SAFFL")

advs = (
    vs.adam.merge(dataset=adsl, on="USUBJID", how="left")
    .assign("PARAMCD", source="VSTESTCD")
    .assign("PARAM", source="VSTEST")
    .assign("AVAL", source="VSSTRESN")
    .assign("AVALU", source="VSSTRESU")
    .date("ADT", source="VSDTC")
    .flag(
        "ABLFL",
        criteria="last",
        by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
        order_by=["ADT", "VISITNUM"],
        where="pl.col('AVAL').is_not_null() & (pl.col('ADT') <= pl.col('TRTSDT'))",
    )
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE", post_baseline="pl.col('ADT') > pl.col('TRTSDT')")
    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE", post_baseline="pl.col('ADT') > pl.col('TRTSDT')")
    .to_frame()
    # keep= of SAS: the ADVS variables of the define, without the SDTM VS ones
    .select(
        "STUDYID",
        "USUBJID",
        "TRT01A",
        "TRTSDT",
        "SAFFL",
        "PARAMCD",
        "PARAM",
        "AVAL",
        "AVALU",
        "VISITNUM",
        "VISIT",
        "ADT",
        "ADTF",
        "ABLFL",
        "BASE",
        "CHG",
        "PCHG",
    )
)
advs.write_parquet("out/minipilot/advs_qc.parquet")

Then fleet compare, the PROC COMPARE of Fleet, checks every variable of the two datasets:

uv run fleet compare out/minipilot/advs.parquet out/minipilot/advs_qc.parquet \
    --keys USUBJID,PARAMCD,VISITNUM

The verdict is EQUAL: no differences found. and the exit code is 0.

docs.title: When a variable is missing
docs.text:
A variable with no derivation: is carried from the inputs. When no input has it, fleet run stops and names the variable, so a dataset is never written without it (ADR 0053). There are two ways out:

  • optional: true on the variable in the define, for a variable the study does not collect. A reviewer sees it in the define.
  • fleet run --no-strict, for one draft run: the stop becomes a warning.

docs.title: One file. One domain. Raw to Render.
docs.text:
The Raw-to-Render (R2R) strategy collapses the traditional multi-program pharma workflow into a single, self-contained script that takes raw source data all the way to a rendered clinical table:

flowchart LR
    RAW["Raw AE CSV"] --> SDTM["SDTM AE<br/>df.sdtm"]
    SDTM --> ADAE["ADaM ADAE<br/>df.adam · df.adam.occds"]
    ADSL[("ADSL<br/>pre-built, governed")] -.-> ADAE
    ADAE --> QC["QC<br/>.compare()"]
    QC --> VAL["Validate<br/>.validate()"]
    VAL --> TLG["AE summary table<br/>df.tlg.ae → HTML"]

DM and ADSL are assumed to already exist — they are governed, shared artefacts produced by separate programs. The R2R script focuses on one domain end-to-end: raw AE data through SDTM, ADaM, QC, validation, and table rendering.

Instead of maintaining separate programs for each layer — with hand-offs, naming conventions to remember, and scattered data lineage — an R2R script keeps the complete derivation chain for a single domain visible in one place.

docs.title: The traditional model
docs.text:
In conventional clinical programming, the AE deliverable involves at least four separate programs, often written by different people. The last column is the R2R layer that replaces each:

Program Input Output Owner R2R layer ae.sas Raw AE extract SDTM AE SDTM prog. 1 — df.sdtm adae.sas SDTM AE + ADSL ADaM ADAE ADaM prog. 2 — df.adam.occds adae_qc.sas SDTM AE + ADSL PROC COMPARE listing QC prog. 3 — .compare() t_ae.sas ADAE + ADSL AE summary table TLG prog. 5 — df.tlg.ae

Each program runs independently. Context about why a particular derivation exists often lives only in the developer's head or in a Word document. When the table looks wrong, you debug backwards across four files, hoping the variable names haven't drifted.

docs.title: The R2R model
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph R2R["r2r_ae.py — one script, one review"]
        direction LR
        L1["Layer 1<br/>SDTM AE"] --> L2["Layer 2<br/>ADAE"]
        L2 --> L3["Layer 3<br/>QC compare"]
        L3 --> L4["Layer 4<br/>Validate"]
        L4 --> L5["Layer 5<br/>Render HTML"]
    end
    RAWAE["Raw AE"] --> L1
    ADSL[("ADSL<br/>pre-built input")] -.-> L2

One script. One review. When cell (3, 2) in the table looks wrong, scroll up — the derivation that produced it is in the same file.

DM and ADSL remain separate, governed programs — they are shared by many domains. The R2R script consumes ADSL as a pre-built input and owns everything else.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• Full lineage visibility — every transformation from raw value to table cell is traceable in a single scroll.
  • Faster debugging — no need to run four programs and cross-reference intermediate datasets; breakpoints anywhere in the chain.
  • Atomic reviews — a reviewer sees the complete picture; intent and implementation live together.
  • Agent-native — an AI coding agent can reason about the entire pipeline in one context window, generate it end-to-end, and fix issues without switching files.
  • Reproducible — one command (uv run python r2r_ae.py) regenerates everything from source.

docs.title: When to use R2R
docs.text:
R2R shines when:

  • You need to prototype fast — get a table on screen from raw data in minutes.
  • The domain is self-contained — AE, VS, LB, CM — where the analysis dataset depends only on its own SDTM domain plus ADSL.
  • You're working with an AI agent that benefits from seeing the full pipeline in one prompt.
  • You want a living specification — the code is the documentation of how raw data becomes a regulatory table.

docs.title: When NOT to use R2R
docs.text:
• Shared derivations — ADSL is consumed by many domains; it deserves its own program with governed outputs. The R2R script loads ADSL as an input — it does not derive it.
  • Large teams — when SDTM and ADaM are programmed by different people on different timelines, separation makes sense.
  • Validated production — regulatory submissions may require individual program-level sign-off; R2R is ideal for exploratory and rapid development before refactoring into governed programs.

docs.title: The Layers
docs.text: An R2R script is organised into clearly labelled layers. Each layer uses a different Fleet namespace:

docs.title: Layer 0 — Inputs
docs.text:
Load the pre-built ADSL and the raw AE extract:

import polars as pl
import fleet  # registers .sdtm / .adam / .tlg namespaces

# ADSL is produced by a separate governed program; it holds the arm as TRT01A
adsl = pl.read_csv("outputs/cdiscpilot01/adsl_admiral.csv", try_parse_dates=True)

# Raw AE — the only raw data this script owns (your study's file)
ae_raw = pl.read_csv("data/raw/ae_raw.csv")

docs.title: Layer 1 — SDTM (.sdtm namespace)
docs.text:
Standardise raw columns into CDISC-compliant SDTM variables:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .assign("AEENDTC", source="ae_end_date")
    .assign("AESEV", source="ae_severity")
    .assign("AESER", source="ae_serious")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Layer 2 — ADaM ADAE (.adam / .adam.occds namespaces)
docs.text:
Merge ADSL treatment dates into SDTM AE, then derive analysis dates, treatment-emergent flags, and worst-severity flags:

# Merge ADSL treatment dates & population flags into SDTM AE
_adsl_trt = adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT", "TRTEDT", "TRT01A", "SAFFL"])
ae_with_trt = ae.join(_adsl_trt, on="USUBJID", how="left")

adae = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.source("STUDYID")
    .source("USUBJID")
    .source("AETERM")
    .assign("TRTA", source="TRT01A")  # parallel design: TRTA is the ADSL actual arm
    .source("SAFFL")
    .date("ASTDT", source="AESTDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ASTDT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
    .adam.occds.treatment_emergent(
        "TRTEMFL",
        start_date="ASTDT",
        end_date="AEENDTC",
        trtsdt="TRTSDT",
        trtedt="TRTEDT",
        end_window=0,  # the SAP decides the window after the last dose
    )
    .recode("AESEVN", source="AESEV", recode_map={"MILD": 1, "MODERATE": 2, "SEVERE": 3})
    .flag(
        "ANL01FL",
        criteria="max",
        value_col="AESEVN",
        by=["USUBJID", "AETERM"],
    )
    .seq("ASEQ", by=["USUBJID"])
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Layer 3 — QC (.compare())
docs.text:
This is adae_qc.sas. A second programmer re-derives the analysis variables from the same SDTM AE and ADSL inputs — in plain Polars expressions rather than the first-class verbs the production chain used — and ends the chain in .compare(), Fleet's PROC COMPARE. The chain is the candidate, the production ADAE is the base, and on_fail="raise" turns a difference into a stopped script:

adae_qc = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.occds("ADAE")
    .derivation("ASTDT", expression=pl.col("AESTDTC").str.to_date(strict=False))
    .derivation(
        "TRTEMFL",
        expression=pl.when(
            pl.col("AESTDTC")
            .str.to_date(strict=False)
            .is_between(
                pl.col("TRTSDT").str.to_date(strict=False),
                pl.col("TRTEDT").str.to_date(strict=False),
            )
        ).then(pl.lit("Y")),
    )
    # ... AENDT, ADY, ANL01FL, ASEQ, AEDECOD and AEBODSYS likewise
    .compare(
        adae,
        keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"],
        variables=["ASTDT", "AENDT", "ADY", "TRTEMFL", "ANL01FL", "ASEQ", "AEDECOD", "AEBODSYS"],
        base_name="ADAE (production)",
        candidate_name="ADAE (QC)",
        on_fail="raise",
    )
    .to_frame()
)

variables= states the QC scope, so production's imputation-flag by-products are neither compared nor reported as missing. The report is printed and kept on the namespace as last_comparison:

Comparison report: ADAE (production) vs ADAE (QC)
======================================================================

Data set summary
----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Base:      ADAE (production)  (5 observations, 37 variables)
  Candidate: ADAE (QC)  (5 observations, 34 variables)
  Keys:      USUBJID, AESEQ
  Variables: ASTDT, AENDT, ADY, TRTEMFL, ANL01FL, ASEQ, AEDECOD, AEBODSYS  (restricted)
  Settings:  exact

Verdict
----------------------------------------------------------------------
  EQUAL: no differences found.

docs.title: Layer 4 — Validate
docs.text:
Call .validate() directly in the pipeline chain — it prints the conformance report and returns the namespace unchanged so derivations can continue:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .assign("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .assign("AEENDTC", source="ae_end_date")
    .assign("AESEV", source="ae_severity")
    .assign("AESER", source="ae_serious")
    .validate("AE")  # ← prints report, chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

adae = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.source("STUDYID")
    .source("USUBJID")
    .source("AETERM")
    .assign("TRTA", source="TRT01A")
    .source("SAFFL")
    .date("ASTDT", source="AESTDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ASTDT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
    .adam.occds.treatment_emergent(
        "TRTEMFL",
        start_date="ASTDT",
        end_date="AEENDTC",
        trtsdt="TRTSDT",
        trtedt="TRTEDT",
        end_window=0,
    )
    .recode("AESEVN", source="AESEV", recode_map={"MILD": 1, "MODERATE": 2, "SEVERE": 3})
    .flag(
        "ANL01FL",
        criteria="max",
        value_col="AESEVN",
        by=["USUBJID", "AETERM"],
    )
    .seq("ASEQ", by=["USUBJID"])
    .validate("ADAE")  # ← prints report, chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

The report printed to stdout makes conformance issues immediately visible. examples/r2r_ae_example.py gives this report (CORE engine 0.15.0). The example sends a copy of AE with a planted AESER "YES" to the SDTM check only, so CORE-000087 reports it; ADAE and the table use the clean AE.

======================================================================

Status: FAIL
Rules (engine run, official): 82 executed, 334 skipped, 14 could not run
Total Issues: 13
  Errors: 11, Warnings (accepted): 0, Info: 2

ERRORS (11):
  [CORE-000087] (official) AESER: AESER is completed, but not equal to "N" or "Y"
  [CORE-000266] (official) AESER, AESCAN, AESCONG, AESDISAB, AESDTH, AESHOSP, AESLIFE, AESOD, AESMIE: If AESER = "N" then none of the seriousness criteria (AESCAN, AESCONG, AESDISAB, AESDTH, AESHOSP, AESLIFE, AESOD, AESMIE) could be equal to "Y".

  [CORE-000334] (official) AEBDSYCD, AEBODSYS, AEHLGT, AEHLGTCD, AEHLT, AEHLTCD, AELLT, AELLTCD, AEPTCD, AESOC, AESOCCD: At least one expected variable is missing from dataset

Every CORE finding blocks until the study config accepts it with a reason (validation.accepted, ADR-0017). An accepted finding gives Status: FINDINGS (1) and shows its reason.

docs.title: Layer 4b — Trace an issue back to its verb
docs.text:
.validate() cross-links each finding to the chain's own variable lineage, so the report says not just what failed but which verb produced it. Nothing extra to call — .trail() shows the same lineage on demand:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.assign("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .trail()  # ← the lineage .validate() reads from
    .validate("AE")
    .to_frame()
)

The join is name-exact: each name in ValidationIssue.variable is matched against VariableNode.name, so an issue only gains a Producing verb when the chain derived that same column. A finding that names several variables (AESEQ, USUBJID, POOLID) gets each verb with the variables it made (assign (AESEQ, USUBJID)). A finding that names more than five variables gets none. A finding on AETERM carries its origin — the verb name plus the dotted path to its implementation:

2. [SDTM.AE.R0004] AETERM must not be empty
   Variable: AETERM
   Row: 7 (1 occurrence)
   Producing verb: assign (fleet.sdtm.namespace.SDTMNamespace.assign)

AEBODSYS above stays bare: nothing in the chain derives it, so there is no lineage node to match.

docs.title: Layer 5 — Render (.tlg.ae namespace)
docs.text:
Compute the Analysis Results Dataset and render to HTML:

from fleet.tlg import (
    AESummarySpec,
    Row,
    Statistic,
    RenderMetadata,
    ard_to_table_model,
    render_html,
)

spec = AESummarySpec(
    rows=[
        Row(field="AEBODSYS", label="System Organ Class"),
        Row(field="AEDECOD", label="Preferred Term"),
    ],
    statistics=[Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT],
    adsl_group_col="TRT01A",  # ADAE arm is TRTA, ADSL arm is TRT01A
)

ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)

meta = RenderMetadata(
    title="Table 14.3.1.1",
    subtitle="AE Summary by SOC and PT",
    footnotes=["Source: ADAE", "Population: Safety"],
)
html = render_html(ard_to_table_model(ard, meta))
Path("outputs/ae_r2r.html").write_text(html)

docs.title: R2R and Agentic Coding
docs.text:
R2R was designed for a reviewable human workflow — one file, one reading order, one visible output. AI agents happen to need exactly the same things, which is why they do well with it:

  1. Single-context reasoning — The entire derivation fits in one file (and one prompt). An agent doesn't need to discover dependencies across a file tree.

  2. End-to-end generation — Given a raw dataset schema and a target table shell, an agent can generate a complete R2R script in one pass — no multi-turn orchestration.

  3. Instant feedback — The script produces a visible output (HTML table). The agent (or user) can inspect the result and iterate without leaving the file.

  4. Self-documenting — The layered structure doubles as executable documentation. An agent reading the file can explain every derivation decision from raw to table.

  5. Deterministic re-execution — One uv run python r2r_ae.py reproduces the full artefact. No DAG scheduler, no Makefile, no external state.

docs.title: Agent prompt pattern
docs.text:
"Using Fleet's R2R pattern, write a single Python script that takes ae_raw.csv and a pre-built ADSL (adsl_admiral.csv) and produces an HTML AE summary table (Table 14.3.1.1). Include SDTM AE, ADAE with treatment-emergent flags, pre-validation, and a rendered HTML output."

The agent returns a complete, runnable script — no follow-up questions needed.

docs.title: Running the Example
docs.text:
The full working example is at examples/r2r_ae_example.py:

uv run python examples/r2r_ae_example.py

Output:

━━ Layer 0 · Inputs ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ADSL (pre-built) : 5 subjects × 33 variables
  ae_raw           :   5 rows × 9 cols

━━ Layer 1 · SDTM AE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  AE : 5 records × 21 variables

━━ Layer 2 · ADaM ADAE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ADAE : 5 records × 37 variables

━━ Layer 3 · QC ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  EQUAL: no differences found.

━━ Layer 4 · Validate ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ✓ TLG pre-validation passed

━━ Layer 5 · Render ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ARD: 155 rows × 15 cols → ae_r2r.html

━━ R2R Complete ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  ADaM → QC        : 8 variables compared → EQUAL
  One file. One domain. Raw to Render.

docs.title: Trial Design, Fully Offline
docs.text: Trial Design is the one corner of a study you can build before any data exists — and in Fleet it needs no API key either: SDTMIG 3.4 structures for the seven Trial Design domains, plus the subject-level SV and SE, ship with the package. This walkthrough goes from a design definition to audited, submission-shaped datasets in five steps. The runnable script is examples/tdd_example.py.

docs.title: 1. Define the design once
docs.text:
Arms are element paths — TAETORD, ELEMENT, EPOCH, and TABRANCH (at the randomization branch) are derived, never typed by hand:

import fleet
from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialVisits

design = fleet.StudyDesign(
    study_id="MYSTUDY01",
    elements=[
        {
            "etcd": "SCRN",
            "element": "Screening",
            "tedur": "P14D",
            "epoch": "SCREENING",
            "testrl": "INFORMED CONSENT",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "TRTA",
            "element": "Drug A Treatment",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "TRTB",
            "element": "Drug B Treatment",
            "tedur": "P84D",
            "epoch": "TREATMENT",
            "testrl": "RANDOMIZATION",
        },
        {
            "etcd": "FU",
            "element": "Follow-up",
            "tedur": "P28D",
            "epoch": "FOLLOW-UP",
            "testrl": "END OF TREATMENT + 1",
        },
    ],
    arms={"DRGA": ["SCRN", "TRTA", "FU"], "DRGB": ["SCRN", "TRTB", "FU"]},
    arm_names={"DRGA": "Drug A", "DRGB": "Drug B"},
    visits=TrialVisits.from_schedule(
        [("Screening", -14), ("Baseline", 0), ("Week 4", 28), ("Week 8", 56)],
        anchor="RANDOMIZATION",
        window=3,
    ).visits,
)

docs.title: 3. Audit before anyone else does
docs.text:
design.audit() runs the P21-style conformance battery offline — findings carry the public rule IDs, and a missing FDA-required TS parameter is flagged before a validator ever sees the data:

findings = design.audit()
print(findings.head(3))

┌─────────┬──────────┬────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ rule_id ┆ severity ┆ domain ┆ message                                        │
╞═════════╪══════════╪════════╪════════════════════════════════════════════════╡
│ SD2213  ┆ error    ┆ TS     ┆ Required TS parameter 'TITLE' is missing       │
│ SD2214  ┆ error    ┆ TS     ┆ Required TS parameter 'TPHASE' is missing      │
│ SD2232  ┆ error    ┆ TS     ┆ Required TS parameter 'SSTDTC' is missing      │
│         ┆          ┆        ┆ (FDA rejection criterion 1734)                 │
└─────────┴──────────┴────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 4. Fill TS from ClinicalTrials.gov
docs.text:
The registry already knows most of the FDA-required TS parameters — seed them straight from the study's NCT registration:

uv run fleet tdd ctgov NCT04280705 --write   # merge into trial_design.yaml

28 parameter(s) from NCT04280705 merged into metadata/sdtm/trial_design.yaml (2 already present).

docs.title: 5. Build (and re-audit) from the CLI
docs.text:
Persist the design as YAML next to your study metadata, then let the CLI do the rest — inside a study workspace, spec and output paths resolve from study_config.yaml:

design.to_yaml("metadata/sdtm/trial_design.yaml")

uv run fleet tdd audit                # conformance pre-check, exit 1 on errors
uv run fleet tdd build --format xpt   # audit + write te/ta/tv/ts/... to <sdtm_data>

docs.title: Bonus: the design is a diagram
docs.text:
to_mermaid() renders the arm/element/epoch structure for protocol review decks. StudyDesign.from_mermaid() reads the arm paths, ETCD, ELEMENT, TEDUR and the epochs back. The diagram does not carry ARM, TESTRL, TEENRL, TABRANCH, TATRANS or a crossover, so to_mermaid() warns when a design cannot be read back. YAML (design.to_yaml()) is the lossless round trip:

print(design.to_mermaid())

flowchart TD
    subgraph EP0[SCREENING]
        SCRN["Screening<br/>P14D"]
    end
    subgraph EP1[TREATMENT]
        TRTA["Drug A Treatment<br/>P84D"]
        TRTB["Drug B Treatment<br/>P84D"]
    end
    subgraph EP2[FOLLOW-UP]
        FU["Follow-up<br/>P28D"]
    end
    SCRN -->|DRGA| TRTA
    TRTA --> FU
    SCRN -->|DRGB| TRTB
    TRTB --> FU

USDM imports (StudyDesign.from_usdm()), the subject-level SV/SE verbs, and the full rule table are covered in the Trial Design concepts page.

docs.title: TLG from a Spec
docs.text: One YAML file defines a clinical table; the same file drives the batch render, the interactive explorer, and the QC trail. This walkthrough takes the shipped aet01 (Overview of Adverse Events) spec from definition to rendered outputs.

docs.title: 1. The spec is the table
docs.text:
examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml, abbreviated — every knob is a plain spec field:

template: aet01                # resolves spec class + df.tlg.ae method
schema_version: 1

adsl_filter: 'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"'   # safety population (N and n)

header_rows:
  - label: Subjects with at least one adverse event
  - label: Subjects with at least one serious adverse event
    filter: 'pl.col("AESER") == "Y"'
  - label: Subjects with at least one adverse event leading to discontinuation
    filter: 'pl.col("AEACN") == "DRUG WITHDRAWN"'

statistics: [n_subjects, n_pct]

Discover the available templates and their spec schemas from the registry:

uv run fleet tlg list                 # every registered template
uv run fleet tlg schema aet01         # the spec's JSON Schema (editor validation)

docs.title: 2. Batch render
docs.text:
Inside a study workspace the datasets and output directory resolve from study_config.yaml — ADAE and ADSL are found by name in the configured adam_data directory and the table lands in the outputs directory:

uv run fleet tlg run examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml --format html

aet01.yaml → outputs/aet01.html  (aet01, table, 9 rows)

Outside a study (or to override), pass paths explicitly:

uv run fleet tlg run examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml \
  --data ADAE=adae.parquet --adsl adsl.parquet --adsl-groupby TRT01A \
  -o out/ --format rtf --rows-per-page 40

ADAE holds the arm as TRTA and a conformant ADSL holds it as TRT01A: --adsl-groupby TRT01A names the ADSL arm for the big N. Without it the CLI stops and names the flag.

--format selects the display format — html, rtf, pdf, or pptx (PDF/PPTX need the tlg-pdf / tlg-pptx extras).

docs.title: 3. The same spec, interactive
docs.text:
Declare degrees of freedom in an interactive: block (population presets, dataset filters, statistics variants) and render one self-contained HTML explorer — no server, every variant pre-computed by the same engine:

uv run fleet tlg explore examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml

The batch output is byte-identical to the explorer's default variant, so there is no second implementation to drift — see Interactive Explorer.

docs.title: 4. The same spec, from Python
docs.text:
import polars as pl
import fleet.tlg as tlg

adae = pl.read_parquet("data/adam/adae.parquet")
adsl = pl.read_parquet("data/adam/adsl.parquet")

spec = tlg.load_spec("examples/tlg_specs/aet01.yaml")
ard = tlg.run_spec(spec, adae, adsl=adsl)  # Analysis Results Dataset

The ARD is a long-format Polars DataFrame holding every computed statistic — rendering (HTML/RTF/PDF/PPTX) is a separate, display-only step, so QC compares numbers, not formatting. For ad-hoc summaries without a spec file, fleet tlg export --domain ae --format pdf renders a domain's t_summary directly from the configured datasets.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Add the table to a one-file raw-to-render script: R2R Strategy
  • Sanctioned interactivity and the variant-space limits: Interactive Explorer
  • Dataset (not display) outputs: Exporting Datasets

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Fleet ships the fleet command-line tool for bootstrapping studies, executing derivation pipelines, validating datasets, generating Define-XML, managing CDISC Controlled Terminology, and rendering TLGs. Commands that query the CDISC Library require a valid CDISC_API_KEY — set it in a .env file at your project root or as an environment variable. Fleet reads only this key from .env; set CDISC_BASE_URL, proxies and FLEET_* variables in the shell.

.env
CDISC_API_KEY=your-api-key-here

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Config discovery — every command that needs study_config.yaml finds it git-style: the current directory first, then each parent. Pass --config <path> to override.
  • Exit codes — 0 success, 1 on a Fleet error (a single clean message on stderr), 2 on a usage error (missing/unknown command or flag). fleet compare turns its verdict into the exit code: 0 equal, 1 different, 2 the comparison could not run. fleet doctor exits 1 when the study config or the rules engine has a cross.
  • Errors go to stderr; results go to stdout. A bad YAML file, a corrupt input file or a folder that cannot be written gives one line. Set FLEET_DEBUG=1 to see the Python traceback.
  • Comments — fleet add-acrf and fleet tdd ctgov --write edit the YAML file as text, so its comments stay. When no parameter is new, fleet tdd ctgov --write does not write the file. A layout that the text edit does not handle (a flow-style block) is written again through YAML, with a warning that counts the comment lines that are lost.
  • Run log — keep the output of a run in a file: fleet run > run.log 2>&1.
  • fleet --version prints the installed version.

Run fleet <command> --help for the authoritative, always-current usage.

docs.title: Command inventory
docs.text: Command What it does fleet init Bootstrapping pipeline: cfg → define → ct → rules. fleet run Execute define.yaml derivation pipelines and write datasets. fleet validate Validate datasets with the CDISC Rules Engine, one engine run per standard. Every finding blocks unless validation.accepted lists it (exit 0 nothing blocks, 1 a finding blocks, 2 a dataset could not run). fleet check CI gate: config parse + define.yaml schema + codelists.py + run setup + custom-rule YAMLs. fleet compare Compare a candidate dataset against a base on keys (exit 0 equal, 1 different, 2 could not run). fleet new Bootstrap a study: init cfg → define → ct → rules, one confirmation. fleet migrate Rewrite removed pre-alpha spellings: Python verbs and kwargs (libcst), or, with --spec, define.yaml algorithms and keys (ADR-0008). fleet tdd Trial design workflow: build/audit TDD datasets from trial_design.yaml. fleet tlg TLG workflow: list templates, run/explore YAML specs, export summaries. fleet define-xml Generate Define-XML 2.1 from a define.yaml specification. fleet add-acrf Declare the annotated CRF document (study.documents block) in define.yaml. fleet add-ct Add domains to an existing codelists.py (preserves existing). fleet add-rule Scaffold a new custom validation rule YAML. fleet check-rule Validate a custom rule YAML (syntax, structure, schema). fleet install-engine Download the CDISC Rules Engine binary for validation. fleet uninstall-engine Remove the managed CDISC Rules Engine binary. fleet doctor Check Fleet setup: engine, API key, codelists.py, optional extras. fleet derivation Scaffold and manage study-specific derivations. fleet mcp Serve Fleet tools to MCP-capable assistants (requires the 'mcp' extra). fleet lsp Language server for define.yaml files (requires the 'lsp' extra).

docs.title: fleet init
docs.text: Run one step of the study bootstrap: cfg, then define, then ct, then rules. Use it to continue a study that fleet new started, to run a step again with --force, or to build a study one step at a time. For a new study in one command, use fleet new.

docs.title: fleet init cfg
docs.text: Option Default Description --study-id (required) Study identifier (e.g. CDISCPILOT01). --company (none) Originator / company name (study.originator in define.yaml). --description (none) Study description (study.description in define.yaml). --domains (none) Comma-separated SDTM domains (e.g. DM,AE,VS,EX). --adam-datasets (none) Comma-separated ADaM datasets (e.g. ADSL,ADVS,ADAE). --ig 3-4 SDTM IG version (default: 3-4). --adam-ig 1-3 ADaM IG version (default: 1-3). --package sdtmct-2023-12-15 SDTM CT package version (default: sdtmct-2023-12-15). --adam-package (none) ADaM CT package, for the codelists only ADaM CT holds (DTYPE). Default with ADaM datasets: adamct-2023-06-30, the latest on or before the default SDTM package; required with another --package. --root / -r . Study root directory (default: current directory).

docs.title: fleet init define
docs.text: Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style). --sdtm-only (none) Generate SDTM define.yaml only (skip ADaM). --adam-only (none) Generate ADaM define.yaml only (skip SDTM). --force (none) Overwrite existing define.yaml files.

docs.title: fleet init ct
docs.text: Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style). --no-docs (none) Omit definitions and preferred terms from generated code. --force (none) Overwrite existing codelists.py.

docs.title: fleet init rules
docs.text: Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style). --sdtm-only (none) Fetch SDTM rules only (skip ADaM). --adam-only (none) Fetch ADaM rules only (skip SDTM). --force (none) Overwrite existing rule files.

docs.title: fleet run
docs.text: Option Default Description --dataset (none) Dataset to build (repeatable). Default: every dataset in the define files. --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style). --out / --output / -o (none) Output directory for every dataset. Default: the configured data/sdtm and data/adam directories. Fleet only writes here: inputs are read from the run, a declared path:, the raw directory (type: raw) or the data directory of the input's standard (type: dataset). --format (none) Output format of every dataset. Default: the output_format of the dataset, else of define.yaml, else parquet (the rule of the Define-XML leaf). Choices: parquet, xpt, dataset-json. --strict / --no-strict (on) Raise on unknown spec algorithms and on a declared variable with no derivation that no input has (default). --no-strict warns and skips both. --overwrite (none) Let a spec derivation replace a column that the input already has. Default off, so a QC run keeps the guard. --check (none) Stop before the write when a variable's values do not match its define type (for CI). Without it the mismatch is a warning on stderr.

docs.title: fleet validate
docs.text: Argument Description paths Dataset files or directories (parquet / csv / xpt / sas7bdat). Default: the configured sdtm_data and adam_data directories. Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style). --standard (none) Force the standard. Default: the configured data directory that holds the dataset, else AD* datasets → adam, others → sdtm. Choices: sdtm, adam. --version (none) IG version. It applies to every dataset of the run, SDTM and ADaM. Default: the sdtm/adam ig_version declared in the discovered study_config.yaml (3.4 / 1.3 outside a study). --define (none) Define-XML file that CORE checks with the datasets (CORE -dxp). Opt-in: Fleet never passes a define by default. --custom-rules (none) Directory of custom validation rule YAML files, relative to the working directory. Default: validation.custom_rules from the discovered study_config.yaml. --timeout (none) Seconds before an engine run is stopped. Default: validation.timeout from the discovered study_config.yaml, else 300. --report (none) Write an HTML findings report to PATH. --encoding (none) Text encoding of the CSV and SAS files, e.g. iso-8859-1 for files from a WLATIN1 SAS session (default: UTF-8).

docs.title: fleet check
docs.text:
CI gate: parse the study config, check each define.yaml against its schema, check codelists.py against ct.package, ct.adam_package and the define.yaml files, build the validation run setup for SDTM and ADaM with no datasets, and check each custom rule YAML. An unsupported sdtm.ig_version or adam.ig_version and a configured validation.custom_rules directory that does not exist fail the gate. A missing rules engine and an unset CDISC_API_KEY are warnings only, because CI installs no engine. Exit 1 on any failure, else 0.

Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style).

docs.title: fleet compare
docs.text:
PROC COMPARE analogue: pair the two datasets on --keys, match variables by name and print the comparison report. --pairs compares variables named differently on each side and --variables restricts the comparison to the ones that matter. Equality is exact unless --abs-tol, --rel-tol or --ignore-trailing-whitespace widens it. --by sections the report per group and --allow-duplicates pairs duplicate keys by position. Exit 0 when the datasets are equal, 1 when they differ, 2 when the comparison could not run (unreadable file, missing keys, duplicate keys without --allow-duplicates, a negative tolerance, a --variables list of keys only, --out or --report not writable or naming an input file, an internal error; FLEET_DEBUG=1 prints its traceback).

Argument Description base The reference dataset (parquet / csv / xpt / sas7bdat; SAS formats need the io extra). candidate The dataset measured against the base (same formats). Option Default Description --keys (required) Comma-separated variables that identify one observation on each side, e.g. USUBJID,AESEQ. Required; keys are never looked up. --by (none) Comma-separated variables to section the report by, e.g. TRT01P. They are prepended to --keys automatically, so they need not be repeated there. The observation and values summaries are also reported per group, and a group present on one side only is flagged and listed; the verdict stays global. --pairs (none) Comma-separated variable pairs whose sides carry different names, e.g. WEIGHT=WT. Applied on top of the automatic name matching, so a renamed column is compared rather than reported missing; the report names it after the base. A pair whose candidate variable is absent reports the base one as missing from the candidate. --variables (none) Comma-separated variables to restrict the comparison to, in base names, so a work-in-progress candidate is checked on the columns that are finished. A variable outside the list is ignored on both sides: neither compared nor reported as missing. --abs-tol 0.0 Absolute tolerance on the numeric variables (default: 0, exact). A numeric pair differs when the absolute difference exceeds max(--abs-tol, --rel-tol x |base|). --rel-tol 0.0 Relative tolerance on the numeric variables, as a fraction of the base value (default: 0, exact). It anchors on the base because the base is the reference, as in SAS: 0.01 is one percent of the base. --ignore-trailing-whitespace (none) Strip trailing whitespace from both sides of a string before comparing, so a legacy SAS dataset's padded character values equal Fleet's stripped ones. Leading whitespace still differs. --blank-is-missing (none) Read an empty string as missing on both sides, keys included, as SAS does. Use it when one side comes from a tool that kept blanks as empty strings (an R data frame without convert_blanks_to_na). A SAS file always reads a blank as missing. --text (none) Comma-separated CSV columns to read as text, the equivalent of a SAS $ informat, e.g. LBORRES. A CSV file holds no types: a column is text when a value on either side has a leading zero or is not a number, a number otherwise, and the other side's type when that side is not a CSV file. --encoding (none) Text encoding of a CSV or SAS file, e.g. iso-8859-1 for a file from a WLATIN1 SAS session (default: UTF-8). --allow-duplicates (none) Pair duplicate keys by their position within each key group instead of refusing to run. The report then counts the duplicates per side, raises the duplicate_keys flag and warns at the top: order within a key group decides which observations pair. --all (none) Print every unequal value (default: 50 per variable, 500 overall). --format text Output format: the text report, or one JSON document (verdict, flags, summaries, listing within the print limits, settings, Fleet version) and nothing else on stdout (default: text). Choices: text, json. --out (none) Also write the complete value listing (never truncated) to PATH as parquet, e.g. differences.parquet. --report (none) Also write a self-contained HTML report to PATH for a reviewer without Python: structural findings as chips, then every mismatched observation with the base and candidate values side by side, one collapsible block per variable.

docs.title: fleet new
docs.text:
Create a new study in the folder ./STUDY_ID: the study_config.yaml and the folders, then the define.yaml files, codelists.py and the cached rules from the CDISC Library. Use it once, at the start of a study. To run one step again, or to continue after a missing CDISC_API_KEY, use fleet init.

Argument Description study_id Study identifier (e.g. STUDY01). Option Default Description --domains (none) Comma-separated SDTM domains (e.g. DM,AE,VS,EX). --adam-datasets (none) Comma-separated ADaM datasets (e.g. ADSL,ADVS,ADAE). --company (none) Originator / company name (study.originator in define.yaml). --description (none) Study description (study.description in define.yaml). --ig 3-4 SDTM IG version (default: 3-4). --adam-ig 1-3 ADaM IG version (default: 1-3). --package sdtmct-2023-12-15 SDTM CT package version (default: sdtmct-2023-12-15). --adam-package (none) ADaM CT package, for the codelists only ADaM CT holds (DTYPE). Default with ADaM datasets: adamct-2023-06-30, the latest on or before the default SDTM package; required with another --package. --root / -r (none) Study root directory (default: ./STUDY_ID). Pass --root . to use the current one. --yes / -y (none) Skip the confirmation prompt.

A PDF loads no external resource: a logo or style sheet the wrapper links is left out, with a warning.

docs.title: fleet define-xml
docs.text:
Generate Define-XML 2.1 from a define.yaml specification. This imports the spec's derivations_module (study Python code) to describe callable: derivations: run it only on a study you trust.

Option Default Description --spec / -s (none) Path to the define.yaml specification file. Default: /define.yaml from the discovered study_config.yaml (per --standard). --output / -o (none) Output path for the Define-XML file. Default: /define_.xml from the discovered study_config.yaml. --standard sdtm Which define.yaml to use for the config-based defaults (default: sdtm). Choices: sdtm, adam. --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style). --no-preview (none) Skip generating the HTML preview alongside the XML. --enrich-methods (none) Kept for old scripts: MethodDefs are on by default. Every Derived variable with a comment: or a derivation: gets a MethodDef. This imports the spec's derivations_module (study Python code). --strict (none) Refuse to write the file when the define has gaps: a Derived variable with no method text, a text, integer or float variable with no length, a float with no significant_digits. Without it the gaps are warnings. --watch (none) Re-generate whenever the spec file changes (requires the 'watch' extra).

docs.title: fleet add-acrf
docs.text: Option Default Description --href blankcrf.pdf aCRF file path in the submission package (default: blankcrf.pdf). --title (none) Display title (default: "Annotated Case Report Form"). --page-map (none) External DOMAIN.VARIABLE → pages YAML file, relative to define.yaml. --standard sdtm Which define.yaml to update (default: sdtm). Choices: sdtm, adam, both. --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style).

docs.title: fleet add-ct
docs.text: Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style). --domains (required) Comma-separated SDTM domain abbreviations to add. --ig (none) SDTM IG version. Default: sdtm.ig_version from the discovered study_config.yaml (3-4 outside a study). --package (none) CT package version. Default: ct.package from the discovered study_config.yaml, else the package of the existing codelists.py, else sdtmct-2023-12-15. Refused when it differs from the package an existing codelists.py was generated from. --output / -o (none) Path to the existing codelists.py. Default: /codelists.py from the discovered study_config.yaml (./codelists.py outside a study). --no-docs (none) Omit definitions and preferred terms from generated code.

docs.title: fleet add-rule
docs.text: Option Default Description --domain (required) SDTM/ADaM domain code (e.g. AE, DM, VS). --description (required) Human-readable description of the rule. --prefix FLEET Rule ID prefix (default: FLEET). --id (none) Explicit rule ID (e.g. ACME-AE-042). Skips auto-increment. --output / -o (none) Output directory for the rule YAML. Defaults to validation.custom_rules from study_config.yaml. --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style).

docs.title: fleet check-rule
docs.text: Argument Description rule_file Path to the custom rule YAML file to validate.

docs.title: fleet install-engine
docs.text: Option Default Description --version v0.15 Release tag to download (default: v0.15, the CORE release that Fleet is tested with). 'latest' gets the newest release and warns. --force (none) Re-download even if already installed.

docs.title: fleet doctor
docs.text:
Check the Fleet setup: the study config, codelists.py, the rules engine, CDISC_API_KEY and the optional extras. Exit 1 when the study config or the rules engine has a cross; the API key and the extras are information only.

Option Default Description --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style).

docs.title: fleet derivation add
docs.text: Argument Description name Variable name to create (e.g. AGEGR1). Option Default Description --dataset ADSL Target dataset name (default: ADSL). --kind column Derivation kind: column / frame (default: column). For a new parameter row, use .adam.derive_param(). Choices: column, frame. --config / -c (none) Path to study_config.yaml. Default: discovered by walking up from the current directory (git-style).

docs.text: Option Default Description --stdio (none) Serve over stdio (the only supported transport; accepted for explicitness). --trust-study-engine (none) Let fleet_validate start the engine that validation.engine_path of a study config names. Without it, such a run could not run.
