docs.title: Coming from SAS
docs.text: This page maps common SAS DATA step and PROC statements to Fleet verbs. It also shows where a missing value gives a result other than SAS. Read the null rules before you port a flag or a category.

docs.title: Statement map
docs.text:
SAS Fleet PROC SORT NODUPKEY; BY USUBJID PARAMCD ADT; .nodup(subset=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "ADT"], sort_by=[...], keep="first") BY USUBJID PARAMCD; IF FIRST.PARAMCD THEN ... .flag("FIRSTFL", criteria="first", order_by="ADT", by=[...]) IF LAST.PARAMCD THEN ... .flag("LASTFL", criteria="last", order_by="ADT", by=[...]) MERGE A(IN=A) B(KEEP=USUBJID TRT01A); BY USUBJID; IF A; .merge(b, on="USUBJID", keep=["TRT01A"]) IF ... THEN ...; ELSE IF ...; ELSE ...; .case_when("VAR", when=[...], else_=...) VAR = OLDVAR; / VAR = "TEXT"; .assign("VAR", source="oldvar") / .assign("VAR", value="TEXT") KEEP STUDYID USUBJID ...; .keep("STUDYID", "USUBJID", ...) WHERE AESER = "Y"; .whereclauses(where='pl.col("AESER") == "Y"') (ADaM namespaces) PROC COMPARE BASE=PROD COMPARE=QC; ID USUBJID; .compare(prod, keys=["USUBJID"])

A BY group with FIRST. and LAST. on one record:

import polars as pl

import fleet  # noqa: F401  (registers df.sdtm and df.adam)

vs = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬─────────┬────────────┬───────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ PARAMCD ┆ ADT        ┆ AVAL  │
│ ---     ┆ ---     ┆ ---        ┆ ---   │
│ str     ┆ str     ┆ date       ┆ f64   │
╞═════════╪═════════╪════════════╪═══════╡
│ S1      ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 2024-01-01 ┆ 120.0 │
│ S1      ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 2024-01-08 ┆ 118.0 │
└─────────┴─────────┴────────────┴───────┘
""")

out = (
    vs.adam.flag("FIRSTFL", criteria="first", order_by="ADT", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .flag("LASTFL", criteria="last", order_by="ADT", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Nulls are not SAS missing values
docs.text:
In SAS, a missing numeric value is lower than every number, so IF AGE < 65 is true when AGE is missing. In Polars, a comparison with a null gives null, and a filter or a when treats null as false.

Expression, AGE missing SAS Fleet AGE < 65 true null .flag("YNGFL", criteria=...) Y null (false_value="N" gives N) case_when with else_=">=65" <65 (first branch) >=65 (no branch matches, so the else_ value) AGE = . / AGE IS MISSING missing(AGE) pl.col("AGE").is_null() PROC SORT (ascending) missing sorts first sort() puts nulls first; nulls_last=True puts them last

Write the null case on purpose, so that the code states the rule of the SAP:

adsl = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬──────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ AGE  │
│ ---     ┆ ---  │
│ str     ┆ i64  │
╞═════════╪══════╡
│ S1      ┆ 70   │
│ S2      ┆ null │
└─────────┴──────┘
""")

adsl = adsl.adam.adsl.case_when(
    "AGEGR1",
    when=[
        {"condition": 'pl.col("AGE").is_null()', "value": "Missing"},
        {"condition": 'pl.col("AGE") < 65', "value": "<65"},
    ],
    else_=">=65",
).to_frame()

docs.title: Two more differences
docs.text:
• Lazy frames. Most verbs add a step to a plan. Polars runs the plan at .to_frame(), as SAS runs a DATA step at RUN;. Some verbs read the data before the chain continues (a check, a join on records, nodup); the chain does not break.
  • No update in place. A verb returns a new frame and never changes its input, as a DATA step writes a new data set. Assign the result (adsl = ...to_frame()) to keep it.

docs.title: IDE & AI Tooling
docs.text: Fleet ships three optional layers of editor/assistant integration. None of them change what a pipeline does: each one exposes the workflow Fleet already has — its verbs, arguments and validation — to the editor or to an assistant, so the intended path is more obvious and the wrong path fails sooner. Pipelines run identically with or without them.

docs.title: Typed entry — fleet.frame() (optional)
docs.text:
df.sdtm / df.adam / df.tlg are registered on Polars frames at runtime, which static type checkers cannot see (pola-rs/polars#27795). Pipelines work either way — the only difference is what your editor reports:

import fleet
import polars as pl

# Without frame(): runs fine, but Pyright/Pylance flag `.sdtm` as unknown.
dm = pl.read_csv("dm_raw.csv").sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM").to_frame()

# With frame(): fully typed, zero runtime cost (returns its input unchanged).
raw = fleet.frame(pl.read_csv("dm_raw.csv"))
dm = raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM").to_frame()  # -> fleet.DataFrame
dm.tlg.ae  # typed downstream too, since to_frame() returns fleet.DataFrame

fleet.DataFrame / fleet.LazyFrame are plain aliases of the Polars classes at runtime (isinstance behaves normally); the namespace properties exist only for type checkers. Wrap loads at IO boundaries. A verb chain and to_frame() keep the typed view. A plain Polars step (filter, join, with_columns) returns the plain Polars type, so wrap its result again:

safety = fleet.frame(dm.filter(pl.col("ARM") != "Screen Failure"))
safety.adam.adsl  # typed again

docs.title: Language server — fleet lsp (define.yaml intelligence)
docs.text:
uv add "fleet-cdisc[lsp]"      # adds pygls
fleet lsp --stdio              # spoken by any LSP client

Capabilities on define.yaml files, all discovered live from the installed Fleet package (never hardcoded):

Capability Source of truth Diagnostics on open/change generated JSON schema (define_spec_schema.json); a key only fleet define-xml needs (a study key, a dataset or variable label) is a warning Unexpected keys, each on its own line; a refused derivation: block in the words of from_spec() JSON schema, per-algorithm models Unknown algorithm: did-you-mean (case ignored); a pre-ADR-0008 name names fleet migrate --spec spec-algorithm registry Completions: algorithm ids and per-algorithm parameter keys registry (required params first; keys the block holds are left out) Completions: codelist OIDs the file's own codelists: section Hover: algorithm docs, codelist name + terms verb docstrings / inline codelists

VS Code: the client ships from its own repository, RealSlimMahdi/fleet-vscode (installation, settings, and the development loop are documented there). It finds the server via the fleet.server.path setting, then the FLEET_LSP env var, then .venv/bin/fleet, then uv run fleet. Other editors: point any LSP client at fleet lsp --stdio for YAML files. The server checks only files named define*.yaml (or .yml); every other YAML file gets an empty list of diagnostics.

docs.title: AI assistants — fleet mcp (Model Context Protocol)
docs.text: The MCP server lets any MCP-capable assistant (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, ...) call Fleet's pipeline intelligence as tools instead of guessing from source code.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv add "fleet-cdisc[mcp]"
# Claude Code (run from the study root — see note below):
claude mcp add fleet -- uv run fleet mcp --stdio

Any other MCP client uses the same stdio command. For JSON-config clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, a project .mcp.json):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fleet": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": ["run", "fleet", "mcp", "--stdio"],
      "cwd": "/path/to/your/study"
    }
  }
}

Launch from the study root. The tools take dataset/spec paths as arguments; registering the server with the study workspace as its working directory (cwd above, or running claude mcp add inside the study) lets the assistant pass the same relative paths your study_config.yaml uses (data/sdtm/ae.parquet, metadata/sdtm/define.yaml, ...).

docs.title: Exposed tools
docs.text:
Each is a thin wrapper over a public Fleet API:

Tool Does fleet_execution_order(spec_paths) topological dataset build order from define.yaml fleet_impacted_by(spec_paths, node) what must re-run if a dataset changes fleet_lineage(dag_json_path, dataset) variable-level lineage from a pipeline DAG export (call dag.inject_lineage(ns, "ADSL") before dag.generate(path), or the record has no variables) fleet_validate(dataset_path, standard?, version?, custom_rules?) CDISC Rules Engine validation from the run setup fleet_ct_terms(codelist, ct_path?) valid terms for a codelist (ct_path is a local CT file, never a URL) fleet_tlg_catalog() all registered TLG templates fleet_tlg_run(spec_path, data_path, adsl_path?, groupby?, adsl_groupby?) run a TLG spec YAML, return rendered HTML; a table that uses ADSL needs adsl_path, as fleet tlg run needs --adsl fleet_dataset_check(data_path, define_yaml, dataset) conformance check against the spec fleet_code_to_spec(source) derivation blocks reverse-mapped from a program's verb calls, without running it fleet_spec_to_code(define_yaml, dataset) an inline program skeleton rendered from a dataset's spec

fleet_validate builds the same run setup as fleet validate. It looks for the study_config.yaml from the directory of the dataset, not from the working directory of the server. So a dataset inside a study uses the study's IG version, custom rules and engine. When standard is not given, the configured data directory that holds the file names it, else the file stem (adsl.parquet is ADaM). The result lists each input with its source:

{
  "outcome": "pass",
  "dataset": "ADSL",
  "standard": "adam",
  "is_valid": true,
  "setup": {
    "standard": {"value": "adam", "source": "data directory"},
    "ig_version": {"value": "1.3", "source": "study config"},
    "custom_rules": {"value": "/study/metadata/custom_rules", "source": "study config"},
    "engine": {"value": "/home/me/.fleet/cdisc-rules-engine/core/core", "source": "default"},
    "engine_version": "0.15.0",
    "study_config": "/study/study_config.yaml"
  },
  "issues": []
}

A refused run setup does not raise. The tool returns {"outcome": "could not run", "reason": ...}: for example a standard conflict (data/adam/dm.parquet), an unsupported IG version, a custom rules directory that does not exist, or no engine found.

Each issue names its dataset. A study-level finding of the engine (dataset STUDY, for example "EX is not present in study") is listed as information, as fleet validate lists it, and does not change is_valid.

An error inside a tool reaches the assistant with its reason, for example "codelist 'Sex' is not in cdisc_ct_sample.yaml. It holds 12 codelists: C170010, ...".

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text: The tools run with your file rights, and there is no sandbox. An assistant can pass any path that you can read: a tool reads that file. The server does not fetch URLs (ct_path must be a local file), fleet_lineage reads only a pipeline_dag.json, and fleet_validate starts an engine that a study config names only when you start the server with fleet mcp --trust-study-engine. Connect the server only to an assistant that you let read your study files.

docs.title: What to ask your assistant
docs.text:
Once connected, these workflows stop being copy-paste-the-error loops and become one question each:

  • "In what order do I need to build the datasets in metadata/adam/define.yaml?" → fleet_execution_order
  • "If I change DM, which downstream datasets must re-run?" → fleet_impacted_by
  • "Where does ADSL.TRTSDT come from?" → fleet_lineage (on a DAG export written after inject_lineage)
  • "Validate data/sdtm/ae.parquet and summarise the errors." → fleet_validate
  • "Is 'INTERVENTIONAL' a valid term for C99077 in metadata/ct/sdtm_ct.yaml? What are the others?" → fleet_ct_terms
  • "Which TLG template covers an AE overview table, and run it against my ADAE." → fleet_tlg_catalog + fleet_tlg_run
  • "Does data/sdtm/dm.parquet conform to its define.yaml spec?" → fleet_dataset_check
  • "Turn this inline AE pipeline into define.yaml derivations." → fleet_code_to_spec
  • "Write me the ADSL program that metadata/adam/define.yaml describes." → fleet_spec_to_code

Combined with llms.txt (the machine-readable API summary shipped at the repo root), an assistant can both write Fleet pipelines and verify their outputs without leaving the conversation.

fleet doctor reports whether the lsp and mcp extras are installed.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Fleet is pre-alpha. Only pre-release versions are on PyPI, so tell the installer to accept them.

uv (recommended)pip 
uv init my-study && cd my-study
uv add fleet-cdisc --prerelease=allow

pip install --pre fleet-cdisc

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
Extra Installs When to use io pyreadstat Reading SAS files (.xpt, .sas7bdat) and writing XPT tlg-pdf weasyprint TLG PDF export tlg-pptx python-pptx TLG PowerPoint export migrate libcst fleet migrate (old spellings to new) watch watchfiles --watch on fleet define-xml and tlg lsp pygls fleet lsp --stdio language server mcp mcp fleet mcp --stdio MCP server all All extras above Full feature set docs MkDocs + plugins Building this documentation dev pytest, ruff, io Contributing to Fleet 
# SAS XPT support
uv add "fleet-cdisc[io]"

# Development
uv add "fleet-cdisc[dev]"

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
import fleet

print(fleet.__version__)  # e.g. 0.2.0a1

Save this as a file and run it with uv run python <file>.py, or run uv run python -c "import fleet; print(fleet.__version__)".

After the import, .sdtm, .adam and .tlg are on every polars.DataFrame. The ADSL and OCCDS verbs are under .adam.adsl and .adam.occds.

docs.title: 1. SDTM domain from raw data
docs.text:
import fleet
import polars as pl
from fleet.ct import import_codelists

import_codelists()  # metadata/sdtm/codelists.py, made by: fleet init ct
from codelists import SEX

raw = pl.from_repr("""
┌────────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
│ patient_id ┆ sex_raw ┆ birth_date │
│ ---        ┆ ---     ┆ ---        │
│ str        ┆ str     ┆ str        │
╞════════════╪═════════╪════════════╡
│ 001        ┆ M       ┆ 1970-04-15 │
│ 002        ┆ F       ┆ 1985-11-02 │
│ 003        ┆ M       ┆ 1960-07-30 │
└────────────┴─────────┴────────────┘
""")

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"M": "M", "F": "F"})
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 2. ADaM BDS dataset
docs.text:
vs_sdtm = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────────┬────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ VISITNUM ┆ VSTESTCD ┆ VSSTRESN ┆ VSDTC      ┆ TRTSDT     │
│ ---     ┆ ---      ┆ ---      ┆ ---      ┆ ---        ┆ ---        │
│ str     ┆ i64      ┆ str      ┆ f64      ┆ str        ┆ str        │
╞═════════╪══════════╪══════════╪══════════╪════════════╪════════════╡
│ 001-01  ┆ 1        ┆ SYSBP    ┆ 120.0    ┆ 2024-01-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 2        ┆ SYSBP    ┆ 115.0    ┆ 2024-02-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 3        ┆ SYSBP    ┆ 118.0    ┆ 2024-03-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
└─────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴────────────┴────────────┘
""")

advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam.source("USUBJID")
    .assign("PARAMCD", source="VSTESTCD")
    .assign("AVAL", source="VSSTRESN")
    .date("ADT", source="VSDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ADT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VISITNUM") == 1')
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 3. ADSL (one row per subject)
docs.text:
# Exposure rule of the admiral template (ad_adsl.R): a placebo dose of 0 is exposure.
# The SAP decides. Change this if placebo is not coded EXDOSE = 0 with PLACEBO in EXTRT.
treated = (
    '(pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0) | '
    '((pl.col("EXDOSE") == 0) & pl.col("EXTRT").str.to_uppercase().str.contains("PLACEBO"))'
)

adsl = (
    dm_sdtm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID", "AGE", "SEX")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXSTDTC", where=treated)
    .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXENDTC", where=treated)
    .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")
    .flag("SAFFL", criteria='pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null()', false_value="N")
    .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae_sdtm)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 4. define.yaml-driven pipeline
docs.text:
Fleet can read a define.yaml specification and execute the whole pipeline without hand-writing verbs:

import polars as pl
import fleet  # noqa: F401

dm = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/dm.parquet")
ex = pl.read_parquet("outputs/sdtm/ex.parquet")

adsl = (
    dm.adam.pin("EX", ex)
    .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml", dataset="ADSL")
    .to_frame()
)

from_spec is the execution entry point: pin any datasets the spec references by name, then materialise with .to_frame(). See How define.yaml works for the full spec format.

docs.title: 5. Generate Define-XML
docs.text:
One CLI command — inside a study workspace both paths default from study_config.yaml (--spec, --output, and --standard sdtm|adam override):

uv run fleet define-xml --standard adam

The same generation from Python, for notebooks or custom scripts:

from fleet import DefineSpecGenerator

DefineSpecGenerator("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml").generate(
    "outputs/cdiscpilot01/define_adam.xml"
)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 to 3.14
  • Fleet installed — see Installation
  • Coming from SAS? Read Coming from SAS first: a null in a condition does not behave as a SAS missing value.

docs.title: Your first SDTM domain — zero setup
docs.text:
No API key, no config file, no network. Import fleet and chain verbs on any Polars DataFrame. fleet.frame() returns its input unchanged; it only lets the editor see .sdtm and .adam (see IDE tooling):

import fleet
import polars as pl

raw = fleet.frame(pl.from_repr("""
┌────────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
│ patient_id ┆ sex_raw ┆ birth_date │
│ ---        ┆ ---     ┆ ---        │
│ str        ┆ str     ┆ str        │
╞════════════╪═════════╪════════════╡
│ 001        ┆ Male    ┆ 1970-04-15 │
│ 002        ┆ Female  ┆ 1985-11-02 │
│ 003        ┆ Male    ┆ 1960-07-30 │
└────────────┴─────────┴────────────┘
"""))

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)
print(dm)

┌────────────┬─────────┬────────────┬────────┬───────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
│ patient_id ┆ sex_raw ┆ birth_date ┆ DOMAIN ┆ STUDYID   ┆ USUBJID ┆ BRTHDTC    │
│ 001        ┆ Male    ┆ 1970-04-15 ┆ DM     ┆ MYSTUDY01 ┆ 001     ┆ 1970-04-15 │
│ …          ┆         ┆            ┆        ┆           ┆         ┆            │
└────────────┴─────────┴────────────┴────────┴───────────┴─────────┴────────────┘

assign is the one assignment verb: source= copies a column, value= hardcodes a literal. Most verbs append to one lazy plan, and Polars runs it at .to_frame(). date to a DTC variable first reads a few rows to check the raw date layout.

More zero-setup wins

The Trial Design domains work fully offline too — SDTMIG 3.4 structures ship with Fleet, so fleet tdd build and the whole Trial Design walkthrough run without an API key.

docs.title: Add controlled terminology
docs.text:
CT is where the CDISC Library comes in. Put an API key in a .env file at your project root:

.env
CDISC_API_KEY=your-key-here

Then bootstrap typed codelist constants for your study's domains:

uv run fleet add-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output codelists.py

This queries the SDTM Implementation Guide to discover every codelist referenced by variables in those domains, downloads the term definitions from the CDISC Library, and generates a typed Python module with IDE auto-completion. Now the same pipeline validates and recodes against real CT:

from codelists import SEX  # generated above

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=SEX, ct_map={"Male": "M", "Female": "F"})
    .date("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)

ct= (a generated codelist class or an NCI concept ID) turns on controlled-terminology validation — no need to look up concept IDs. ct_map recodes collected values to CT submission values (here "Male" → "M"); omit it when the raw data already matches the codelist — values are then passed through and validated as-is.

docs.title: Your first ADaM BDS dataset
docs.text:
vs_sdtm = fleet.frame(pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────┬────────────┬────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ VISITNUM ┆ PARAMCD ┆ AVAL  ┆ ADT        ┆ TRTSDT     │
│ ---     ┆ ---      ┆ ---     ┆ ---   ┆ ---        ┆ ---        │
│ str     ┆ i64      ┆ str     ┆ f64   ┆ str        ┆ str        │
╞═════════╪══════════╪═════════╪═══════╪════════════╪════════════╡
│ 001-01  ┆ 1        ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 120.0 ┆ 2024-01-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 2        ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 115.0 ┆ 2024-02-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
│ 001-01  ┆ 3        ┆ SYSBP   ┆ 118.0 ┆ 2024-03-10 ┆ 2024-01-10 │
└─────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────┴────────────┴────────────┘
"""))

advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam.source("USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVAL")
    .study_day("ADY", date_col="ADT", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VISITNUM") == 1')
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL", by=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

The flag → baseline → chg chain runs in one pipeline — no intermediate .to_frame(). study_day uses the CDISC algorithm (+1 when on/after the reference date, no day 0).

docs.title: ADSL — one row per subject
docs.text:
dm_sdtm = fleet.frame(pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬─────┬─────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ AGE ┆ SEX │
│ ---     ┆ --- ┆ --- │
│ str     ┆ i64 ┆ str │
╞═════════╪═════╪═════╡
│ 001-01  ┆ 63  ┆ F   │
│ 001-02  ┆ 71  ┆ M   │
└─────────┴─────┴─────┘
"""))
ex_sdtm = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬────────────┬────────┬────────────┬────────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ EXTRT      ┆ EXDOSE ┆ EXSTDTC    ┆ EXENDTC    │
│ ---     ┆ ---        ┆ ---    ┆ ---        ┆ ---        │
│ str     ┆ str        ┆ f64    ┆ str        ┆ str        │
╞═════════╪════════════╪════════╪════════════╪════════════╡
│ 001-01  ┆ PLACEBO    ┆ 0.0    ┆ 2024-01-10 ┆ 2024-03-10 │
│ 001-02  ┆ XANOMELINE ┆ 54.0   ┆ 2024-01-12 ┆ 2024-03-12 │
└─────────┴────────────┴────────┴────────────┴────────────┘
""")
ae_sdtm = pl.from_repr("""
┌─────────┬──────────┐
│ USUBJID ┆ AETERM   │
│ ---     ┆ ---      │
│ str     ┆ str      │
╞═════════╪══════════╡
│ 001-02  ┆ HEADACHE │
│ 001-02  ┆ NAUSEA   │
└─────────┴──────────┘
""")

# Exposure rule of the admiral template (ad_adsl.R): a placebo dose of 0 is exposure.
# The SAP decides. Change this if placebo is not coded EXDOSE = 0 with PLACEBO in EXTRT.
treated = (
    '(pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0) | '
    '((pl.col("EXDOSE") == 0) & pl.col("EXTRT").str.to_uppercase().str.contains("PLACEBO"))'
)

adsl = (
    dm_sdtm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID", "AGE", "SEX")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXSTDTC", where=treated)
    .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXENDTC", where=treated)
    .duration("TRTDURD", start="TRTSDT", end="TRTEDT")
    .flag("SAFFL", criteria='pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null()', false_value="N")
    .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae_sdtm)
    .to_frame()
)

A population flag is never blank (ADaMIG 1.3), so false_value="N" gives N to the subjects outside the safety population.

Fleet also provides Admiral-parity verbs for advanced BDS derivations — bsa(), map(), qtc(), derive_summary_records(), derive_locf_records(), and derive_param() — as well as ADSL helpers age_years() and derive_period(). See the Cheat Sheet for the full list.

docs.title: Initialising a new study workspace
docs.text:
The bootstrapping pipeline is the recommended way to set up a new study. It creates the folder tree, queries the CDISC Library IG to generate define.yaml specs, and downloads the referenced codelists:

# Step 1 — create study_config.yaml + directory structure
uv run fleet init cfg --study-id MYSTUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./studies/MYSTUDY01
cd studies/MYSTUDY01

# Step 2 — generate define.yaml from the CDISC Library IG
uv run fleet init define

# Step 3 — generate codelists.py from define.yaml codelist references
uv run fleet init ct

See the CLI Reference for full argument details and standalone commands like fleet add-ct.

The same first step can be done programmatically with StudyContext.init():

from fleet import StudyContext
from fleet.core.study_context import ADAMConfig, SDTMConfig

ctx = StudyContext.init(
    "./studies/MYSTUDY01",
    study_id="MYSTUDY01",
    company="Acme Pharma",
    sdtm=SDTMConfig(ig_version="3-4", domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]),
    adam=ADAMConfig(ig_version="1-1", datasets=["ADSL", "ADVS"]),
)

This creates:

studies/MYSTUDY01/
  study_config.yaml        ← load later with load_study_context()
  data/
    raw/
    sdtm/
    adam/
  metadata/
    sdtm/                  ← define.yaml created by `fleet init define`
    adam/                   ← define.yaml created by `fleet init define`
  outputs/

If study_config.yaml already exists, StudyContext.init() raises a StudyConfigError without touching anything — protecting in-progress work.

To reload an existing workspace in subsequent sessions:

from pathlib import Path
from fleet import load_study_context

ctx = load_study_context(Path("./studies/MYSTUDY01/study_config.yaml"))

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: When you build SDTM or ADaM pipelines in Fleet, an error comes from the data or from the pipeline code. This page shows the common messages, what they mean and how to fix them.

docs.title: UserWarning: ... contains values not in codelist ...
docs.text:
What it means: .assign(ct=...) found values that are not submission terms of the codelist. It is a warning, not an error. The pipeline continues and writes the values as they are:

SEX: column 'sex' contains values not in codelist 'C66731': ['Q']. Valid values: ['F', 'INTERSEX', 'M', 'U']. Consider providing a ct_map parameter.

How to fix it:

  1. Look at the raw values: df.select("raw_column").unique().
  2. Add the missing raw value to ct_map={...}. A raw value that is not in ct_map is kept as text, as SAS PUT with no OTHER= keeps it.
  3. Or correct the data upstream.

To make warnings stop the run while you develop, use warnings.simplefilter("error").

docs.title: DerivationError: ... column '...' not found in the frame
docs.text:
What it means: A verb reads a column that is not in the frame yet. For example, chg reads AVAL and BASE before you derive them:

chg('CHG'): column 'AVAL' not found in the frame. Available columns: ['patient_id', 'sex_raw']

DerivationError is a FleetError and a ValueError. The message names the verb and the columns that are available.

How to fix it: Order matters in a Fleet pipeline. Derive a variable before the verbs that read it. For example, .source("AVAL") must come before .baseline(aval="AVAL", ...).

docs.title: SpecError: ... unknown algorithm '...'
docs.text:
What it means: In a spec-driven pipeline, an algorithm: in define.yaml is not a verb name:

define.yaml → dataset ADSL → variable X: unknown algorithm 'asign' for the adam spec path. Did you mean 'assign'? Pass strict=False to warn and skip instead.

How to fix it: Use the verb name that the message suggests, or one from the Namespace Pipeline tables. An editor that reads the JSON Schema (define_spec_schema.json) marks an unknown algorithm before you run the pipeline. See Validating define.yaml below.

docs.title: Debugging Lazy Evaluation
docs.text:
Each verb adds one step to the plan of one Polars LazyFrame. Nothing runs until .to_frame(). So a stack trace can point to .to_frame() and not to the verb that caused the problem.

Two chainable verbs show the pipeline before it runs:

  • .explain() prints the Polars query plan.
  • .trail() prints one row per derived variable: the verb and the origin.
import polars as pl

import fleet

dm = pl.from_repr("""
┌────────────┐
│ patient_id │
│ ---        │
│ str        │
╞════════════╡
│ P1         │
└────────────┘
""")

pipeline = dm.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM").assign("USUBJID", source="patient_id")

pipeline.explain()
#  WITH_COLUMNS:
#  ["DM".alias("DOMAIN"), col("patient_id").alias("USUBJID")]
#   DF ["patient_id"]; PROJECT */1 COLUMNS
pipeline.trail()
# Variable trail (2 derivation(s)):
# │ 1 ┆ DOMAIN  ┆ assign ┆ (literal)  ┆ — │
# │ 2 ┆ USUBJID ┆ assign ┆ patient_id ┆ DM │

You can also stop the chain early and look at the intermediate frame:

debug_df = (
    dm.sdtm.assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    # .assign("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct=...)  <-- commented out to isolate the bug
    .to_frame()
)
print(debug_df.head())

docs.title: Validating define.yaml
docs.text:
If you are using the spec-driven approach, validate your define.yaml file against the Fleet schema before running pipelines. This ensures you don't waste time tracing runtime errors that are actually typos in the specification.

The Fleet VS Code extension does this with no setup: fleet lsp loads the schema from the installed package, so it can never drift from the Fleet that runs your pipeline.

Without the extension, a generic YAML language server can read the same schema from a comment at the top of the file:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=<path to define_spec_schema.json>

fleet init define prints that line with the path already resolved against your install. Scaffolded specs no longer carry it by default, because running both validators reports every schema error twice.
